% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
% Pure-Lua base64 decoder. Reads this very source, finds each marked block,
% strips the comment prefixes, decodes, and writes the archive to the build
% directory. No shell escape, no external decoder, no adjacent ZIP.
%
% The Lua below deliberately uses no backslash, no percent sign and no hash.
% TeX tokenises the argument of \directlua before Lua ever sees it, so those
% three characters are the escape, the comment and the macro-parameter
% characters respectively, and any of them would be consumed or would raise a
% TeX error. Hence string.char(10) for a newline, string.char(37) for a per
% cent sign, string.len instead of the length operator, math.fmod instead of
% the modulo operator, and plain (non-pattern) string.find throughout.
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
\directlua{
local NL = string.char(10)
local PCT = string.char(37)
local B64 = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
local rev = {}
for i = 1, 64 do rev[string.sub(B64, i, i)] = i - 1 end

local function decode(payload)
  local out, n, bits, nbits = {}, 0, 0, 0
  for i = 1, string.len(payload) do
    local c = string.sub(payload, i, i)
    if c == "=" then break end
    bits = bits * 64 + rev[c]
    nbits = nbits + 6
    if nbits >= 8 then
      nbits = nbits - 8
      local shift = 2 ^ nbits
      local byte = math.floor(bits / shift)
      bits = bits - byte * shift
      n = n + 1
      out[n] = string.char(byte)
    end
  end
  return table.concat(out)
end

local function source_text()
  local names = { tex.jobname .. ".tex" }
  local found = kpse.find_file(tex.jobname .. ".tex", "tex")
  if found then names[2] = found end
  for _, name in ipairs(names) do
    local fh = io.open(name, "rb")
    if fh then
      local text = fh:read("*a")
      fh:close()
      if string.find(text, "NPZ" .. "_BEGIN", 1, true) then return text, name end
    end
  end
  error("mnn supplement: cannot read the compiling source file. Expected "
        .. tex.jobname .. ".tex in the working directory, carrying the NPZ blocks.")
end

local text, where = source_text()
local OPEN = "<NPZ" .. "_BEGIN name=" .. string.char(34)
local SHUT = string.char(34) .. ">"
local STOP = PCT .. "<NPZ" .. "_END>"
local pos, count, report = 1, 0, {}

while true do
  local a, b = string.find(text, OPEN, pos, true)
  if not a then break end
  local c, d = string.find(text, SHUT, b + 1, true)
  if not c then
    error("mnn supplement: a block header is malformed -- no closing quote after "
          .. "character " .. b .. ".")
  end
  local name = string.sub(text, b + 1, c - 1)
  local e, f = string.find(text, STOP, d + 1, true)
  if not e then
    error("mnn supplement: the block for " .. name .. " has no end marker.")
  end
  local block = string.sub(text, d + 1, e - 1)

  local buf, k = {}, 0
  for i = 1, string.len(block) do
    local ch = string.sub(block, i, i)
    if rev[ch] ~= nil or ch == "=" then
      k = k + 1
      buf[k] = ch
    elseif ch ~= PCT and ch ~= NL and ch ~= " " and ch ~= string.char(13) then
      error("mnn supplement: the block for " .. name .. " contains a character that is "
            .. "neither base64 nor a comment prefix, at offset " .. i .. ".")
    end
  end
  local payload = table.concat(buf)
  if string.len(payload) == 0 then
    error("mnn supplement: the block for " .. name .. " is empty.")
  end
  if math.fmod(string.len(payload), 4) ~= 0 then
    error("mnn supplement: the block for " .. name .. " is truncated -- its payload is "
          .. string.len(payload) .. " characters, which is not a multiple of 4.")
  end
  local bytes = decode(payload)
  if string.sub(bytes, 1, 2) ~= "PK" then
    error("mnn supplement: " .. name .. " did not decode to a zip container (an .npz "
          .. "begins PK), so the block is corrupt.")
  end
  local fh = io.open(name, "wb")
  if not fh then
    error("mnn supplement: cannot write " .. name .. " into the build directory.")
  end
  fh:write(bytes)
  fh:close()
  count = count + 1
  report[count] = name .. " (" .. string.len(bytes) .. " bytes)"
  pos = f + 1
end

if count == 0 then
  error("mnn supplement: no NPZ blocks were found in " .. where
        .. ". The evidence blocks are required; the document cannot attach them.")
end
texio.write_nl("mnn supplement: reconstructed " .. count .. " archives: "
               .. table.concat(report, ", "))
}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\section{Package scope and reconstruction}
This document is the complete source of the software supporting Chapter~6, together with the
numerical evidence its reported results are computed from. It is self-contained: every listing
below is printed in full, and the four deposited archives are embedded as base64 at the end of
the file.

The companion \texttt{mnn-torch-release.zip} beside this document is the same software as an
executable tree, and is the convenient way to run it. It is not needed to compile or read this
supplement.

\subsection{What is printed, and what is not}
Printed verbatim: every Python file under \texttt{src/}, \texttt{tools/} and \texttt{tests/};
\texttt{README.md}, \texttt{THIRD\_PARTY\_DATA.md} and \texttt{LICENSE}; \texttt{pyproject.toml}
and \texttt{uv.lock}; every JSON sidecar; and every notebook markdown and code cell in execution
order.

Not printed: notebook image payloads and the rendered figure PDFs. Every figure is drawn by the
plotting code printed in Section~\ref{sec:plotting} from the arrays embedded here, so the
pictures carry no information the source and the evidence do not. Together they are four fifths
of the archive.

\subsection{Reconstructing the evidence}
Compiling this file with LuaLaTeX writes the four archives into the build directory and attaches
them to the resulting PDF:
\begin{quote}
\texttt{latexmk -lualatex mnn-torch-supplement.tex}
\end{quote}
The decoder is pure Lua, embedded in the preamble. It locates this source, finds each marked
block, strips the comment prefixes, decodes the payload, and stops with a stated reason if a
block is missing, empty, truncated or not a zip container. Reconstruction therefore needs no
shell escape, no network access, no external tool and no adjacent ZIP.

The attachments below are the reconstructed files. Saving one and loading it needs nothing but
NumPy:
\begin{quote}
\texttt{python -c "import numpy; print(numpy.load('mnn-device.npz', allow\_pickle=False).files)"}
\end{quote}
\subsection{Attached archives}
The four archives, reconstructed during compilation and attached here:

\textattachfile{mnn-device.npz}{\texttt{mnn-device.npz}} \quad 301,709 bytes, from \texttt{data/device.npz}.

\textattachfile{mnn-static.npz}{\texttt{mnn-static.npz}} \quad 5,756 bytes, from \texttt{data/static.npz}.

\textattachfile{mnn-substitution.npz}{\texttt{mnn-substitution.npz}} \quad 30,199 bytes, from \texttt{data/substitution.npz}.

\textattachfile{mnn-all-volatile.npz}{\texttt{mnn-all-volatile.npz}} \quad 9,555 bytes, from \texttt{data/all\_volatile.npz}.

\section{Environment and third-party data}
\subsection{README.md}
\index{README.md}
\begin{Verbatim}
# mnn-torch

Simulation code and recorded data for spiking networks whose synapses carry a measured memristive
device response: a steady-state one, and a volatile one that fades over seconds.

`data/` holds the recorded data: the measured device traces, the training results and the
delayed-classification results, each with the axes it varies over. The code is the library those
results came from, the plotting that turns them into figures, and the training pipeline.

## Getting started

```bash
uv sync                                    # library, plotting, training code (PyTorch included)
uv run python tools/reproduce.py           # the figures and reported summaries, from data/
```

That second command trains nothing and needs no dataset: if it passes, the code and the data agree.

`uv sync` installs no extras, so ask for what you need — or `pip install -e ".[test,notebooks]"`:

| extra | for |
|---|---|
| `test` | the unit tests — `uv run pytest -q` |
| `notebooks` | opening the notebooks — `uv run jupyter lab notebooks/` |
| `datasets` | downloading the datasets — **both** training profiles need it |

## Three profiles

| profile | inputs | trains | reportable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `archived` (default) | `data/` only | no | yes — these are the recorded results |
| `reduced` | small prepared subsets | yes, in about a minute | no |
| `published` | the full splits | yes, in hours | yes — as a fresh run of its own |

```bash
uv run python tools/reproduce.py             # archived: no dataset needed

uv sync --extra datasets                     # both training profiles need this
uv run python tools/prepare_data.py reduced
uv run python tools/reproduce.py reduced

uv run python tools/prepare_data.py published
uv run python tools/reproduce.py published geometry   # check the caches
uv run python tools/reproduce.py published
```

**Both training profiles need `prepare_data.py` first.** The datasets are third-party and none is
distributed here, so `reproduce.py` never reaches the network: it either finds prepared inputs or
names the command that builds them.

**`prepare_data.py` builds four of the five datasets automatically. DVS128 Gesture must be fetched
by hand** — tonic's download URL for it is dead, so the command stops on it and prints the two
archive names, their checksums and where to put them. See [Datasets](#datasets). The other four
build first and are kept, so nothing is lost. To run everything that does not depend on it
meanwhile:

```bash
uv run python tools/reproduce.py reduced geometry static homeostasis kernel_fit \
    substitution_nmnist all_volatile_nmnist all_volatile_shd
```

The `geometry` gate checks only the datasets the stages in a given run read, so naming stages this
way needs no DVS Gesture present.

**`reduced` and `published` are the same pipeline** — same stages, same drivers, same output
schema. The only difference is `SCALE` in `tools/experiments/pipeline.py`: the inputs each stage
gets, and how many seeds, epochs and delays it runs. Every full-scale setting there is the recorded
one, from `data/static.json`, the delay instrument's `PROTOCOL`, and `breadth_cohort.SEEDS`.

`published` is a fresh run, not a replay: its numbers are its own and will not match the recorded
ones exactly. Reproducing those is `archived`'s job.

**Only `archived` draws figures**, because the figure code reads the deposited archives. `reduced`
and `published` write their run outputs under `outputs/<profile>/`; `pipeline.json` summarises the
complete run. Nothing writes into `data/`.

## The pipeline

Eight stages, run in this order by both `reduced` and `published`:

| stage | driver |
|---|---|
| `geometry` | the inputs against the dataset registry |
| `static` | `training.run_static_classification` — both architectures, ideal and Poole-Frenkel |
| `homeostasis` | `training.run_dense_homeostasis` — the paired regulariser-off/on benefit |
| `kernel_fit` | `volatile.fit_kww` — the stretched exponential, refitted to the measured traces |
| `substitution_nmnist` | `tools/profile_matched.py` — train, freeze, replay under each decay kernel, both architectures |
| `all_volatile_nmnist`, `all_volatile_shd`, `all_volatile_dvsgesture` | `tools/breadth_cohort.py` — every synaptic layer volatile, cleared layer by layer |

Each experiment runs on the datasets it is deposited on. The substitution archive carries no dataset
axis and its reportable cohorts are `mcsnn|F` and `msnn|F`, so a default run replays kernels on
N-MNIST alone; `all_volatile` is deposited on all three, its `matched_v2` cohort being the SHD and
DVS128 Gesture pair. `substitution_shd` and `substitution_dvsgesture` are registered and run when
named, and reproduce nothing deposited.

`geometry` is a **gate**: missing or wrongly shaped inputs stop the run there rather than after
hours of training. Each stage's controls run inside it — `all_volatile` asserts the clearing
identity per delay, `substitution` the realised 4.0725 s hold. Run a subset by naming it:
`python tools/reproduce.py reduced static homeostasis`.

## What is in `data/`

| archive | holds |
|---|---|
| `device` | the measured multistate sweeps, the conduction model fitted over the screened states, and the ITO relaxation traces the volatile kernel comes from |
| `static` | training with the measured nonidealities against an ideal control, and the paired firing-rate homeostasis result |
| `substitution` | networks replayed under different relaxation kernels, with their controls and endpoints |
| `all_volatile` | networks in which every synaptic layer is volatile, and what clearing state layer by layer costs |
| `datasets.json` | the public event datasets: how each frame cache is binned and what it holds |

Each `.npz` carries dense arrays; the `.json` beside it names their axes, and marks any sparsity
with its reason, so a cell that was never measured is never a zero.

There is no stored ledger of results: every number a figure or a notebook sentence quotes is
computed from these arrays by `tools/quantities.py`, and the unit tests pin several directly.

## Notebooks

Three, one per subject: `01_static`, `02_retention`, `03_spiking`. Each displays every figure it
owns inline, saves that same object under `figures/`, and follows each measurement figure with a
sentence computed from the arrays when the cell runs. **They train nothing** — training is
`tools/reproduce.py reduced` or `published`.

```bash
uv sync --extra notebooks && uv run jupyter lab notebooks/
```

## Datasets

**No third-party dataset samples are distributed with this package.** MNIST, Fashion-MNIST,
N-MNIST, SHD and DVS128 Gesture each carry their own upstream terms, which this project's MIT
licence does not grant. `tools/prepare_data.py` downloads them from their own sources into
`~/.cache/mnn-torch` — outside the tree, and never copied back into it.

`archived` needs none of them. See **[THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md](THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md)** for each source,
its terms and the selection rules; `--list` prints what a command would build, and where:

```bash
uv sync --extra datasets
uv run python tools/prepare_data.py reduced --list
```

The subsets are defined by a rule, not by a stored list of indices: images take the first 100
training and 50 test examples of each class; the event datasets take the first 20 test examples of
each class, split 12 train / 8 test. `data/datasets.json` keeps the preprocessing dimensions — bin
counts, frame geometry, class counts — which describe the transformation rather than the data.

| cache | frame shape | binning | `published` train | test | read densely or convolutionally |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nmnist_frames.npz` | 8x2x17x17 | 8 bins, 17x17 at spatial_factor 0.5 | 10000 | 5000 | both |
| `shd_frames.npz` | 50x700 | 50 bins, 700 channels | 6000 | 2000 | densely |
| `dvsgesture_frames.npz` | 12x2x32x32 | 12 bins, 32x32 | 1176 | 288 | convolutionally |

**DVS128 Gesture must be fetched by hand**: tonic 1.6.0's URL for it is dead. `prepare_data.py`
prints the two archive names, their checksums and where to put them. Its stages cannot run until it
is supplied; nothing else is affected, because the geometry gate checks only the datasets the
stages in that run read.

Frames are `uint8` and **binary** (presence per bin per channel, not counts), bit-packed with
`numpy.packbits`, which the loader reverses; the loader applies `10*log1p(x)/log(256)` on read, and
that encoding is not stored. The `geometry` stage checks whatever it finds against the registry
before anything trains.

## Scope

The device records come from single contacts measured in single sessions, so their spread bounds
repeatability within a session and says nothing about variation between devices. The networks are
simulated. No classification was performed in hardware. Where a result depends on a criterion, a
readout rule or a delay grid, that dependence is a property of the measurement and is reported
with it.
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{THIRD\_PARTY\_DATA.md}
\index{THIRD\_PARTY\_DATA.md}
\begin{Verbatim}
# Third-party datasets

> No third-party dataset samples are distributed with this package. Preparation commands download
> them from their respective sources, after which each dataset remains subject to its upstream
> terms.

The MIT licence in `LICENSE` covers this project's code and its own recorded data — the measured
device traces and the training and delayed-classification results in `data/`. It does not and cannot
grant any right over the datasets below.

## What the training profiles use

| Dataset | Downloader | Upstream source and terms |
|---|---|---|
| MNIST | `torchvision.datasets.MNIST` | the MNIST source Torchvision selects — see [`torchvision/datasets/mnist.py`](https://github.com/pytorch/vision/blob/main/torchvision/datasets/mnist.py) |
| Fashion-MNIST | `torchvision.datasets.FashionMNIST` | [Zalando Research](https://github.com/zalandoresearch/fashion-mnist), MIT — the MIT terms must travel with any redistributed copy, which is one reason this package redistributes none ([licence](https://github.com/zalandoresearch/fashion-mnist/blob/master/LICENSE)) |
| N-MNIST | `tonic.datasets.NMNIST` | the dataset accompanying Orchard et al., *Converting Static Image Datasets to Spiking Neuromorphic Datasets Using Saccades* ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/1507.07629v1), [Front. Neurosci.](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2015.00437/full)) |
| SHD | `tonic.datasets.SHD` | [Zenke Lab](https://zenkelab.org/resources/spiking-heidelberg-datasets-shd/), CC BY 4.0 |
| DVS128 Gesture | `tonic.datasets.DVSGesture` | [IBM Research](https://www.research.ibm.com/dvsgesture/) |

Consult each source for its own citation requirements and terms of use before publishing anything
derived from it.

All five are used. The pipeline has a stage per event dataset, on the architecture each admits:
N-MNIST and DVS128 Gesture are read convolutionally, SHD densely — a 700-channel stream has no
spatial structure for a convolution to use.

### DVS128 Gesture needs fetching by hand

As of tonic 1.6.0 its download URL returns nothing, so `prepare_data.py` stops and tells you exactly
what to supply rather than failing obscurely. Put either the archives or the extracted data where
tonic looks, under `<cache>/raw/DVSGesture/`:

| file | md5 | tonic fetches it from |
|---|---|---|
| `ibmGestureTest.tar.gz` | `56070e45dadaa85fff82e0fbfbc06de5` | `https://figshare.com/ndownloader/files/38020584` |
| `ibmGestureTrain.tar.gz` | `3a8f0d4120a166bac7591f77409cb105` | `https://figshare.com/ndownloader/files/38022171` |

Extracted data works too: tonic walks `<cache>/raw/DVSGesture/{ibmGestureTest,ibmGestureTrain}` for
`*.npy`. The underlying dataset is IBM's, linked in the table above; the two archives are tonic's
repackaging of it, and the checksums let you confirm whatever you obtain is that repackaging.

Until it is supplied, the DVS Gesture stages cannot run. The others are unaffected — the geometry
gate checks only the datasets the stages in **that** run read, so
`reproduce.py reduced substitution_shd all_volatile_shd` works with no DVS Gesture present.

## How they are obtained

```bash
uv sync --extra datasets
uv run python tools/prepare_data.py reduced      # or: published
```

The downloaders write into `~/.cache/mnn-torch` — outside this package — or wherever
`MNN_DATA_CACHE` points. Nothing is ever copied back into the tree, and `.gitignore` and the
packaging step both exclude anything built from a downloaded dataset.

Downloading is a separate, explicit command. `tools/reproduce.py` never reaches the network: a run
either finds prepared inputs or tells you which command builds them.

## What is built locally, and by what rule

The subsets are defined by a rule rather than by a stored list of indices, so nothing about which
examples were selected has to be distributed:

| profile | selection |
|---|---|
| `reduced`, images | the first **100 training** and first **50 test** examples of each class |
| `reduced`, events | the first **20 test** examples of each class; the first **12** become reduced training data, the remaining **8** reduced test data |
| `published`, events | the first N of each official split, at the counts `data/datasets.json` declares |

`data/datasets.json` keeps the preprocessing dimensions — bin counts, frame geometry, channel
counts, class counts — which is a description of the transformation, not dataset content. The
downloader versions are pinned in `pyproject.toml` (`torchvision`, and `tonic==1.6.0` in the
`datasets` extra), so the same rule applied to the same upstream data gives the same subset.
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{pyproject.toml}
\index{pyproject.toml}
\begin{Verbatim}
[project]
name = "mnn-torch"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Memristive spiking neural networks in PyTorch: a measured ITO relaxation as the fading synaptic state of a simulated SiOx crossbar"
readme = "README.md"
license = { text = "MIT" }
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.13"
authors = [
    { name = "Viet Cuong Vu", email = "viet.vu.14@ucl.ac.uk" },
    { name = "Anak Agung Ngurah Arymurti Santosa" },
    { name = "Wing H. Ng" },
    { name = "Adnan Mehonic" },
    { name = "Anthony J. Kenyon" },
]
keywords = [
    "memristive", "neural-networks", "pytorch", "spiking-neural-networks",
    "hardware-acceleration", "neuromorphic", "memristor",
    "volatile-memory", "stretched-exponential",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Physics",
]

# Pinned to the versions the recorded numbers were produced under. numpy is capped below 2.0
# because torch 2.12.1 was resolved against a numpy-1.x environment.
dependencies = [
    "numpy==1.26.4",
    "scipy==1.15.3",
    "matplotlib==3.10.9",
    "snntorch==1.0.0",
    "torch==2.12.1",
    "torchvision==0.27.1",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = ["pytest>=8.0.0"]
notebooks = [
    "jupyterlab==4.6.3",
    "nbclient==0.11.0",
    "nbformat==5.10.4",
    "ipykernel==7.3.0",
]
# Only tools/prepare_event_data.py needs this. tonic 1.6.0 is the version the shipped cache
# geometry was binned with.
datasets = ["tonic==1.6.0"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/hyperionx/mnn-torch"
Repository = "https://github.com/hyperionx/mnn-torch"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# The wheel is the library alone. tools/ resolves its paths relative to this file and reads data/
# and figures/ beside it, none of which exists next to an installed package, so it ships in the
# sdist instead.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/mnn_torch"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "/src",
    "/notebooks",
    "/tools",
    "/tests",
    "/figures",
    "/data",
    "/pyproject.toml",
    "/uv.lock",
    "/README.md",
]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/*.py[cod]",
    "**/.DS_Store",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# The default run uses only what this package ships, so it neither downloads nor skips. One test
# needs a downloaded dataset; run it with `pytest -m integration`.
addopts = "-m 'not integration'"
markers = ["integration: needs a dataset this package does not ship"]

[tool.black]
line-length = 88
target-version = ["py310"]
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{uv.lock}
\index{uv.lock}
\begin{Verbatim}
version = 1
revision = 3
requires-python = ">=3.10, <3.13"
resolution-markers = [
    "python_full_version >= '3.12'",
    "python_full_version == '3.11.*'",
    "python_full_version < '3.11'",
]

[[package]]
name = "anyio"
version = "4.14.2"
source = { registry = "https://pypi.org/simple" }
dependencies = [
    { name = "exceptiongroup", marker = "python_full_version < '3.11'" },
    { name = "idna" },

\section{Deposited numerical evidence}
\label{sec:evidence}
Four archives hold every number the reported results are computed from. Each is
pickle-free: \texttt{numpy.load} opens them with \texttt{allow\_pickle=False}. The tables below
describe every stored array; the JSON sidecars that follow give the axis meanings, the protocol
each cohort ran under, and the provenance of each block. The base64 payloads are at the end of
this document.

For a text array no minimum or maximum is reported, because its ordering carries no meaning; the
finite count is its size. For a floating array the count is of finite entries, so a shortfall
against the shape is the absent cells the sidecar flags rather than a defect.

{
 "about": "The public event datasets the temporal protocols train on: how each frame cache is binned, what it contains, and the checksum a rebuild must match. The caches are not shipped.",

   ],
   "frame_values": [
    0,
    1
   ],

    "train": 1176
   },
   "stored_as": "bit-packed",
   "why_not_shipped": "a binned derivative of a public dataset: reconstructible from it, larger than the rest of the archive together, and carrying upstream terms this archive does not restate"

 "how_to_check_a_rebuild": "Compatibility is structural, not by file identity: a cache is accepted if its arrays, shapes, dtypes, split sizes, class range and binary frame values match this description. mnn_torch.datasets.validate_cache performs exactly that check and reports every problem it finds.",
 "how_to_supply": "Not shipped. Put the three files below in one directory and point MNN_DATA_CACHE at it, or place them under data/caches/, which the loader also checks. README.md states what each must contain.",
 "inherited_provenance": {
  "binned_with": "1.6.0",

\section{Library source}
\label{sec:library}
\subsection{src/mnn\_torch/\_\_init\_\_.py}
\index{src/mnn\_torch/\_\_init\_\_.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""Mnn-Torch: memristive and volatile-synapse spiking networks in PyTorch.

Seven modules, each named for what it holds:

  ``devices``     the measured SiO_x device: multistate loading, the Poole--Frenkel
                  conduction model and its per-device variability, the stuck-fault
                  disturbances, and the memristive crossbar layers built on them.
  ``volatile``    the volatile-synapse primitive: a measured relaxation used as a fading
                  synaptic state that carries information across an input-free interval.
  ``networks``    the spiking architectures and their neurons.
  ``training``    the declared training protocols and campaigns.
  ``datasets``    dataset resolution, caching and spike encoding.
  ``archives``    where canonical evidence lives and how it is read; the write guard.
  ``estimators``  the statistics the results are quoted with.

Figure style and figure I/O are deliberately not here. They live in
``tools/plotting/common.py``, outside the installed package, because they are how results
are presented rather than how they are produced.
"""

from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version

try:
    __version__ = version("mnn-torch")
except PackageNotFoundError:                                        # Pragma: no cover
    __version__ = "unknown"
finally:
    del version, PackageNotFoundError

from . import archives, datasets, devices, estimators, networks, training, volatile
from .archives import (ARCHIVES, archive, archive_dir, data_dir, device_data_mat, load_result,
                       repo_root, results_dir, save_result)
from .datasets import (SPEC, batches, encode, ensure_images, ensure_mnist,
                       image_loaders, load_arrays, load_encoded, mnist_loaders)
from .devices import (HomeostasisDropout, HomeostaticRegulariser, MemristiveConv2d,
                      MemristiveLinearLayer, clean_experimental_data,
                      compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch,
                      compute_PooleFrenkel_parameters,
                      compute_PooleFrenkel_regression_parameters,
                      load_SiOx_curves, load_SiOx_multistate,
                      sample_PooleFrenkel_parameters_torch)
from .networks import MCSNN, MSNN, BaseSNN, LayerBuilder
from .training import (dose_response, gate_homeostasis_sweep, isolate_collapse,
                       precompute_device_params, run_condition)
from .volatile import (ITO_REFERENCE, KohlrauschTrace, TransientProfile, VolatileSynapse,
                       fit_kww, holdout_validate, ito_reference_profile,
                       kohlrausch_modes)

__all__ = [
    "__version__",
    # Modules
    "archives", "datasets", "devices", "estimators", "networks", "training", "volatile",
    # Devices: the measured SiO_x device and the crossbar layers over it
    "load_SiOx_multistate", "load_SiOx_curves", "clean_experimental_data",
    "compute_PooleFrenkel_parameters", "compute_PooleFrenkel_regression_parameters",
    "compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch", "sample_PooleFrenkel_parameters_torch",
    "MemristiveLinearLayer", "MemristiveConv2d",
    "HomeostasisDropout", "HomeostaticRegulariser",
    # Volatile: a measured relaxation as a fading synaptic state
    "TransientProfile", "fit_kww", "kohlrausch_modes", "KohlrauschTrace",
    "VolatileSynapse", "holdout_validate", "ito_reference_profile", "ITO_REFERENCE",
    # Networks
    "MSNN", "MCSNN", "BaseSNN", "LayerBuilder",
    # Training
    "run_condition", "gate_homeostasis_sweep", "dose_response", "isolate_collapse",
    "precompute_device_params",
    # Datasets
    "mnist_loaders", "image_loaders", "ensure_mnist", "ensure_images", "load_arrays",
    "encode", "load_encoded", "batches", "SPEC",
    # Archives
    "ARCHIVES", "archive", "archive_dir", "repo_root", "data_dir", "results_dir",
    "device_data_mat", "save_result", "load_result",
]

\subsection{src/mnn\_torch/archives.py}
\index{src/mnn\_torch/archives.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""Where everything on disk lives, resolved in one place.

The deposited archives in ``data/``, the figures in ``figures/``, the working output under
``outputs/``, and the event frame caches -- which are not shipped and are found either under
``data/caches/`` or wherever ``MNN_DATA_CACHE`` points.

One resolver, so the notebooks and the command line agree. Both reach the same files regardless of
the working directory they were started from, which they find by walking up to ``pyproject.toml``.

Filesystem paths for the recorded archives, generated figures and result grids.

This module is the one place that resolves ``data/``, so the notebooks and the command line agree
on where the archives, the fixtures and the caches live regardless of the working directory they
were started from.  Result grids a training run writes go under ``data/results``; nothing in
``data/`` itself is ever written by a run.

Because the package is installed editable, ``__file__`` resolves inside the real
repository ``src/`` tree, so the repository root -- and its sibling ``data/`` -- is
discoverable from the module location. Set ``MNN_DATA_DIR`` to override (e.g. for a
wheel install or CI where ``data/`` lives elsewhere).

The root is found by walking up to a SENTINEL (``pyproject.toml``), not by counting
parents. A fixed ``parents[2]`` keeps returning a directory
after a file changes depth in the tree; it just returns the wrong one, silently, and the
caller then reads or writes somewhere unintended. :func:`repo_root` raises instead.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

__all__ = [
    "repo_root",
    "data_dir",
    "results_dir",
    "device_data_mat",
    "save_result",
    "load_result",
    "ARCHIVES",
    "cache_dir",
    "reduced_dir",
    "PROFILES",
    "DEFAULT_PROFILE",
    "profile",
    "output_dir",
    "guard_not_shipped",
    "ShippedDataWriteError",
]

#: the file whose presence marks the repository / release root
SENTINEL = "pyproject.toml"

# ==========================================================================
# Execution profiles
#
# ``archived``     renders every figure from the shipped ``.npz`` archives and
#                  trains nothing. The default, because that is what a reader
#                  who just unpacked this package can actually run.
# ``reduced``      executes every producer on the compact fixtures, so the code
#                  paths are exercised without a publication-scale run.
# ``published``    runs the same pipeline on the full splits. Its outputs go
#                  under ``outputs/published/``, never into ``data/``.
#
# No profile may write into the shipped ``data/`` tree; :func:`guard_not_shipped`
# makes an attempt a raise rather than a surprise.
# ==========================================================================

#: The three execution profiles, in order of how much they run. These are the names
#: ``tools/reproduce.py`` takes on the command line, so there is one vocabulary.
PROFILES = ("archived", "reduced", "published")

#: Rendering from the archives is the default: it needs no data beyond this package
#: and cannot overwrite anything.
DEFAULT_PROFILE = "archived"


class ShippedDataWriteError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when something tries to write inside the shipped ``data/`` tree."""


def profile() -> str:
    """The active profile from ``MNN_PROFILE``; ``archived`` when unset.

    Raises on an unrecognised value rather than falling back, because silently
    defaulting would make a mistyped ``publishd`` look like a successful
    no-training run.
    """
    p = os.environ.get("MNN_PROFILE", DEFAULT_PROFILE).strip().lower()
    if p not in PROFILES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"MNN_PROFILE={p!r} is not a profile; expected one of {PROFILES}")
    return p


def guard_not_shipped(path) -> Path:
    """Return ``path``, or raise if it lands inside the shipped ``data/`` tree.

    Call this on every write destination: ``data/`` holds the recorded results, and a run that
    overwrote one would destroy what the package exists to carry.
    """
    p = Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
    shipped = data_dir().resolve()
    if p == shipped or shipped in p.parents:
        raise ShippedDataWriteError(
            f"refusing to write to {p}: it is inside the shipped data directory "
            f"({shipped}). Generated output belongs under output_dir() -- see MNN_WORK_DIR.")
    return p


def output_dir(create: bool = True) -> Path:
    """Where the active profile may write. Never inside ``data/``.

    Every profile gets one, including ``archived``. What none of them gets is write access to
    the recorded archives.
    """
    d = work_dir() / profile()
    guard_not_shipped(d)
    if create:
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def repo_root() -> Path:
    """Root of the installed tree, found by sentinel; raises if there is none.

    Honours ``MNN_REPO_ROOT`` for wheel installs, where there is no source tree to
    walk up through.
    """
    env = os.environ.get("MNN_REPO_ROOT")
    if env:
        return Path(env).expanduser().resolve()
    here = Path(__file__).resolve()
    for cand in here.parents:
        if (cand / SENTINEL).is_file():
            return cand
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"Could not locate the repository root: no {SENTINEL!r} above {here}. Set "
        "MNN_REPO_ROOT (or MNN_DATA_DIR) to say where data/ lives."
    )


def data_dir() -> Path:
    """Absolute path to the package ``data/`` directory (created if absent).

    Honours the ``MNN_DATA_DIR`` environment variable; otherwise resolves to
    ``<repo-root>/data`` from this module's location (editable install).
    """
    env = os.environ.get("MNN_DATA_DIR")
    if env:
        d = Path(env).expanduser().resolve()
    else:
        d = repo_root() / "data"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def results_dir() -> Path:
    """``outputs/<profile>/results`` -- where a sweep's grids and tables go.

    Under ``outputs/``, not under ``data/``: everything a run generates belongs with the run, and
    ``data/`` holds only what was deposited.
    """
    p = guard_not_shipped(output_dir() / "results")
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return p


def device_data_mat() -> Path:
    """Path to the bundled SiOx multistate device fixture ``SiO_x-multistate-data.mat``.

    Resolves to ``data_dir()/SiO_x-multistate-data.mat`` when that exists. When
    ``MNN_DATA_DIR`` relocates the *writable* data dir (for MNIST downloads and
    result grids) the shipped fixture is not there, so we fall back to the
    repository-relative ``<repo-root>/data`` (discoverable from this module's
    location under the editable ``src/`` tree). The fixture is read-only, so it
    always ships with the repo even when results live elsewhere.
    """
    primary = data_dir() / "SiO_x-multistate-data.mat"
    if primary.exists():
        return primary
    repo_data = repo_root() / "data" / "SiO_x-multistate-data.mat"
    if repo_data.exists():
        return repo_data
    return primary


def archive_dir() -> Path:
    """``data/`` -- where the three shipped evidence archives live.

    The release ships exactly ``static``, ``retention`` and ``spiking`` as
    ``.npz`` + ``.json`` pairs. This is a read path: the ``publication`` profile
    writes elsewhere (see :func:`work_dir`) and consolidation into these files is
    a separate, validated step that never happens implicitly.
    """
    return data_dir()


#: The archives this package ships, by stem.
ARCHIVES = ("device", "static", "substitution", "all_volatile")


def archive(name: str) -> Path:
    """Path to one shipped archive by stem, e.g. ``archive("device")``."""
    if name not in ARCHIVES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown archive {name!r}; this package ships {ARCHIVES}")
    return archive_dir() / f"{name}.npz"


def cache_dir() -> Path:
    """Where third-party datasets are downloaded to. Outside this package, always.

    No sample of MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, N-MNIST, SHD or DVS128 Gesture is distributed here: each
    carries its own upstream terms, which this package's licence does not and cannot grant. The
    preparation commands fetch them from their own sources into this directory, and nothing ever
    copies them back into the tree.

    ``MNN_DATA_CACHE`` overrides it; otherwise ``~/.cache/mnn-torch``.
    """
    env = os.environ.get("MNN_DATA_CACHE")
    d = Path(env).expanduser().resolve() if env else Path.home() / ".cache" / "mnn-torch"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def reduced_dir() -> Path:
    """Where ``prepare_data.py reduced`` writes the small locally built subsets."""
    d = cache_dir() / "reduced"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d




def work_dir() -> Path:
    """Where the ``publication`` profile writes fresh records.

    Deliberately outside the repository by default, so a full campaign cannot
    overwrite a shipped archive by accident. Honours ``MNN_WORK_DIR``.
    """
    env = os.environ.get("MNN_WORK_DIR")
    d = Path(env).expanduser().resolve() if env else repo_root() / "outputs"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def save_result(name: str, obj) -> Path:
    """Save ``obj`` as ``.npy`` under :func:`output_dir`, returning the path.

    Writes under :func:`output_dir`, never into ``data/``. That is where the shipped
    evidence lives, so a sweep writing there could overwrite a deposited record -- and
    the sidecar digests would then certify the overwritten file as authentic. The
    destination is guarded, not merely relocated.
    """
    path = guard_not_shipped(output_dir() / name)
    np.save(path, obj, allow_pickle=True)
    return path


def load_result(name: str):
    """Load a grid written by :func:`save_result`, or a shipped one.

    Looks in :func:`output_dir` first (a fresh run supersedes for the caller who
    just produced it), then in the shipped ``data/results``, which still carries
    read-only records such as the homeostasis sample archive.
    """
    for cand in (output_dir(create=False) / name, output_dir(create=False) / "results" / name):
        if cand.exists():
            return np.load(cand, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tried = [output_dir(create=False) / name, output_dir(create=False) / "results" / name]
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"{name} not found. Looked, in order, at:\n  "
        + "\n  ".join(str(t) for t in tried))
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{src/mnn\_torch/datasets.py}
\index{src/mnn\_torch/datasets.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""Every input this package trains on, and the one registry that describes them.

Two kinds. The image datasets, MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, loaded through torchvision. And the
pre-binned event frame caches -- N-MNIST, SHD, DVS128 Gesture -- which are not shipped: they are
binned derivatives of public datasets, and :data:`DATASETS` states the geometry a supplied cache
must have. ``torch``/``torchvision`` are imported lazily inside the functions, so importing this
module costs nothing.

Dataset loading and preparation helpers for the mnn-torch experiments.

Two dataset paths feed the memristive spiking-network studies:

* **MNIST** -- the fault-recovery / homeostasis sweeps.
  :func:`ensure_mnist` downloads it once (into :func:`mnn_torch.archives.data_dir`
  by default) so that pooled worker processes can open it with ``download=False``;
  :func:`mnist_loaders` builds seeded train/test ``DataLoader`` pairs, optionally
  subsetting for a fast smoke run.

* **Fashion-MNIST** -- the second dataset for the paired homeostasis comparison.
  Same loaders, selected with ``dataset="fashion-mnist"``.

* **The pre-binned temporal caches** -- N-MNIST, SHD and DVS128 Gesture, plus
  sequential MNIST. :func:`load_arrays`, :func:`encode`, :func:`load_encoded` and
  :func:`batches` are verified bit-exact against the loader that produced the
  deposited caches.

``torch``/``torchvision`` are imported *lazily* inside the
functions so that importing :mod:`mnn_torch.data` (and hence :mod:`mnn_torch`)
never drags in those heavy trees; only the caller who actually needs a loader
pays for the import.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

import numpy as np

from . import archives as paths

__all__ = [
    "ensure_images", "ensure_mnist", "image_loaders", "mnist_loaders",
    "SPEC", "DATASETS", "load_arrays", "encode", "load_encoded", "batches",
    "class_balanced_indices", "resolve_subset", "blank_like",
    "pack_frames", "unpack_frames",
]


#: torchvision class name per supported image dataset.
_IMAGE_DATASETS = {"mnist": "MNIST", "fashion-mnist": "FashionMNIST"}


def _tv_dataset(dataset: str):
    """The torchvision class for ``dataset``, with a specific error if unknown."""
    import torchvision
    try:
        return getattr(torchvision.datasets, _IMAGE_DATASETS[dataset])
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown image dataset {dataset!r}; supported: "
                         f"{sorted(_IMAGE_DATASETS)}") from None



# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MNIST (fault-recovery / homeostasis sweeps)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def ensure_images(dataset="mnist", data_dir=None):
    """Download ``dataset`` once (train + test) so workers can use ``download=False``.

    ``data_dir`` defaults to :func:`mnn_torch.archives.data_dir`. Returns the
    resolved data directory as a string so callers can thread it to workers.
    """
    import torchvision.transforms as T

    cls = _tv_dataset(dataset)
    data_dir = str(paths.cache_dir()) if data_dir is None else str(data_dir)
    tfm = T.Compose([T.ToTensor()])
    cls(data_dir, train=True, download=True, transform=tfm)
    cls(data_dir, train=False, download=True, transform=tfm)
    return data_dir


def ensure_mnist(data_dir=None):
    """Back-compatible alias for ``ensure_images("mnist", data_dir)``."""
    return ensure_images("mnist", data_dir)


def image_loaders(
    data_dir=None,
    seed=0,
    batch_size=64,
    train_subset=None,
    test_subset=None,
    *,
    num_workers=0,
    pin_memory=None,
    persistent_workers=False,
    dataset="mnist",
):
    """Build seeded MNIST train/test ``DataLoader`` pairs.

    Lifted from ``gate_homeostasis_recovery._data_loaders``: the train loader is
    shuffled under a per-run ``torch.Generator`` seed and drops the last partial
    batch; the test loader is deterministic. ``train_subset`` / ``test_subset``
    (if given) take the leading ``n`` examples for a fast smoke run. ``pin_memory``
    defaults to cuda availability and the worker controls are optional, preserving
    single-process behaviour. Assumes MNIST is already present (see
    :func:`ensure_mnist`); opens with ``download=False``.
    """
    import torch
    import torchvision.transforms as T
    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Subset

    cls = _tv_dataset(dataset)
    data_dir = str(paths.cache_dir()) if data_dir is None else str(data_dir)
    tfm = T.Compose([T.ToTensor(), T.Normalize((0,), (1,))])
    train = cls(data_dir, train=True, download=False, transform=tfm)
    test = cls(data_dir, train=False, download=False, transform=tfm)
    if train_subset:
        train = Subset(train, range(train_subset))
    if test_subset:
        test = Subset(test, range(test_subset))
    if pin_memory is None:
        pin_memory = bool(torch.cuda.is_available())
    num_workers = int(num_workers)
    persistent_workers = bool(persistent_workers and num_workers > 0)
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    train_loader = DataLoader(train, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True,
                              drop_last=True, generator=g, num_workers=num_workers,
                              pin_memory=pin_memory,
                              persistent_workers=persistent_workers)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False,
                             drop_last=True, num_workers=num_workers,
                             pin_memory=pin_memory,
                             persistent_workers=persistent_workers)
    return train_loader, test_loader


def mnist_loaders(*args, **kw):
    """Back-compatible alias for :func:`image_loaders` on MNIST."""
    kw.setdefault("dataset", "mnist")
    return image_loaders(*args, **kw)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The pre-binned temporal caches (N-MNIST, SHD, DVS128 Gesture, seq-MNIST)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verified bit-exact against the loader that produced the deposited caches.
#
# Encoding (event caches only):  x -> 10 * log1p(x) / log(256)
#     a binary cache {0, 1}  ->  {0, 1.25}  exactly, because log(2)/log(256) = 1/8.
# Do not "simplify" this to {0, 1}: the Poole-Frenkel forward map is nonlinear,
# so a 1.25x change in drive is a different network, not a rescaled one.

# The single dataset registry. It agrees with the specification the deposited
# caches were built under on source/T/shape/classes/kind for all three event
# datasets, and additionally carries seq-MNIST plus the architecture and subset
# fields the temporal models need. ``SPEC`` below is a derived view, not a second
# source of truth, so the two cannot drift apart.
DATASETS = {'seqmnist': {'kind': 'dense',
              'source': 'torchvision.datasets.MNIST(download=False)',
              'T': 28,
              'num_inputs': 28,
              'num_hidden': 64,
              'num_outputs': 10,
              'n_train_full': 60000,
              'n_test_full': 10000,
              'train_subset': 12000,
              'test_subset': None,
              'encode': 'x/255',
              'chance': 10.0},
 'nmnist': {'kind': 'conv',
            'source': 'nmnist_frames.npz',
            'T': 8,
            'input_shape': (2, 17, 17),
            'num_outputs': 10,
            'num_kernels': 3,
            'num_conv1': 4,
            'num_conv2': 8,
            'max_pooling': 2,
            'n_train_full': 10000,
            'n_test_full': 5000,
            'train_subset': None,
            'test_subset': None,
            'encode': '10*log1p(x)/log(256)',
            'chance': 10.0},
 'shd': {'kind': 'dense',
         'source': 'shd_frames.npz',
         'T': 50,
         'num_inputs': 700,
         'num_hidden': 64,
         'num_outputs': 20,
         'n_train_full': 6000,
         'n_test_full': 2000,
         'train_subset': None,
         'test_subset': None,
         'encode': '10*log1p(x)/log(256)',
         'chance': 5.0},
 'dvsgesture': {'kind': 'conv',
                'source': 'dvsgesture_frames.npz',
                'T': 12,
                'input_shape': (2, 32, 32),
                'num_outputs': 11,
                'num_kernels': 3,
                'num_conv1': 4,
                'num_conv2': 8,
                'max_pooling': 2,
                'n_train_full': 1176,
                'n_test_full': 288,
                'train_subset': None,
                'test_subset': None,
                'encode': '10*log1p(x)/log(256)',
                'chance': 9.090909090909092}}


def _spec_view():
    """``{name: (file, T, shape, classes, kind)}`` derived from :data:`DATASETS`.

    Event caches only -- seq-MNIST has no cache file. Kept because it is the
    shape the encoding helpers below were written against.
    """
    out = {}
    for name, d in DATASETS.items():
        src = d.get("source", "")
        if not src.endswith(".npz"):
            continue
        shape = tuple(d["input_shape"]) if d.get("input_shape") else (d["num_inputs"],)
        out[name] = (src, d["T"], shape, d["num_outputs"], d["kind"])
    return out


SPEC = _spec_view()


def load_arrays(dataset, data_root=None):
    """``(Xtr, ytr, Xte, yte)`` as numpy, unconverted (uint8 stays uint8: 8x memory).

    ``data_root`` defaults to :func:`mnn_torch.archives.cache_dir`, since the event
    caches are fetched rather than shipped.
    """
    import numpy as np

    root = paths.cache_dir() if data_root is None else data_root
    if dataset == "seqmnist":                       # Dense 28x28, encode x/255
        import torchvision
        tr = torchvision.datasets.MNIST(str(root), train=True, download=False)
        te = torchvision.datasets.MNIST(str(root), train=False, download=False)
        return (tr.data.numpy(), tr.targets.numpy(),
                te.data.numpy(), te.targets.numpy())
    from pathlib import Path
    name = SPEC[dataset][0]
    return _load_frames(name, root, data_root)


#: Suffixes the bit-packed frame caches use. See :func:`pack_frames`.
PACKED_SUFFIX = "_packed"
SHAPE_SUFFIX = "_shape"


def pack_frames(arrays: dict) -> dict:
    """Bit-pack the binary frame tensors of an event cache.

    The event frames are strictly ``{0, 1}`` yet stored as ``uint8``, i.e. eight
    bits per bit. ``np.packbits`` removes that, and it is worth doing even though
    the container is already deflate-compressed: measured over the three shipped
    caches the total falls from 27.76 MB to 20.77 MB, a 25% saving. The gain is
    well under the naive 8x because deflate was already exploiting the byte-level
    redundancy that packing removes.

    Lossless and exactly invertible by :func:`unpack_frames`. Non-binary and 1-D
    arrays (labels, shape scalars) pass through untouched.
    """
    out = {}
    for k, a in arrays.items():
        a = np.asarray(a)
        if a.dtype == np.uint8 and a.ndim > 1:
            uniq = np.unique(a)
            if not set(uniq.tolist()) <= {0, 1}:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{k!r} is uint8 but not binary (values {uniq[:5]}...); "
                    "bit-packing would be lossy")
            out[f"{k}{PACKED_SUFFIX}"] = np.packbits(a.reshape(-1))
            out[f"{k}{SHAPE_SUFFIX}"] = np.asarray(a.shape, dtype=np.int64)
        else:
            out[k] = a
    return out


def unpack_frames(z, key):
    """Read ``key`` from a frame cache, unpacking it if it was bit-packed.

    Accepts both layouts, so a cache written before packing still loads.
    """
    if key in getattr(z, "files", ()):
        return z[key]
    pk, sh = f"{key}{PACKED_SUFFIX}", f"{key}{SHAPE_SUFFIX}"
    if pk not in z.files:
        raise KeyError(f"{key!r} absent, packed or otherwise; have {list(z.files)}")
    shape = tuple(int(v) for v in z[sh])
    n = int(np.prod(shape))
    return np.unpackbits(z[pk])[:n].reshape(shape).astype(np.uint8)


def _load_frames(name, root, data_root):
    """Locate and read one event frame cache, packed or plain."""
    from pathlib import Path
    # The three event frame caches are shipped, under data/caches/, so look there
    # as well as in the download cache. Resolving only to cache_dir() sent every
    # event-dataset call to an empty directory and then reported "the event caches
    # are not shipped", which was false and made netbench.main() unrunnable on a
    # complete checkout.
    # The caller's root is tried first, so an explicit override still wins, but the
    # shipped location is always a fallback. Gating the fallback on
    # ``data_root is None`` was too narrow: run_capability passes
    # ``data_root=str(paths.cache_dir())`` explicitly, so every event-dataset
    # capability cell failed with "not found" while the file sat in data/caches/.
    candidates = [Path(root) / name]
    shipped = paths.data_dir() / "caches" / name
    if shipped not in candidates:
        candidates.append(shipped)
    for p in candidates:
        if p.exists():
            with np.load(p) as z:
                return (unpack_frames(z, "Xtr"), z["ytr"],
                        unpack_frames(z, "Xte"), z["yte"])
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"{name} not found. Looked, in order, at:\n  "
        + "\n  ".join(str(c) for c in candidates)
        + "\nSet MNN_DATA_CACHE to point at a directory holding it.")


def encode(dataset, xb, device="cpu"):
    """Batch -> ``(T, B, ...)`` float32 tensor with the dataset's exact encoding.

    Seq-MNIST streams one 28-pixel row per timestep. The event caches use
    ``10*log1p(x)/log(256)``; all three are measured binary and
    ``log(2)/log(256) = 1/8``, so that map sends ``{0, 1}`` to ``{0, 1.25}``
    exactly.

    Do not "simplify" it to ``{0, 1}`` to make the layers' binary fast paths
    fire. The Poole-Frenkel map is nonlinear, so cutting the drive by 1.25x cuts
    the per-synapse current by 1.46-3.74x (measured over the fitted conductance
    grid, mean 1.79), takes the layer-1 output magnitude down 2.37x, and takes
    the fraction of hidden units driven over threshold from 13.6% to 3.2% -- a
    different network, not a rescaled one. The guard was relaxed instead
    (``layers.py``: ``single_nonzero_value``), so the drive stays exactly as
    encoded.

    Verified bit-exact on all three caches against the loader that produced
    them.
    """
    import math

    import numpy as np
    import torch

    x = torch.as_tensor(np.ascontiguousarray(xb), dtype=torch.float32)
    if dataset == "seqmnist":
        return x.div(255.0).permute(1, 0, 2).to(device)          # (28, B, 28)
    x = 10.0 * torch.log1p(x) / math.log(256.0)                  # {0,1} -> {0,1.25}
    if SPEC[dataset][4] == "dense":
        return x.permute(1, 0, 2).to(device)                     # (T, B, 700)
    return x.permute(1, 0, 2, 3, 4).to(device)                   # (T, B, C, H, W)


def load_encoded(dataset, data_root=None, n_train=None, n_test=None, device="cpu"):
    """Fully encoded ``(x_train, y_train, x_test, y_test)``; x is ``(T, N, ...)`` float32.

    Memory warning: SHD float32 full train is 6000*50*700*4 = 840 MB. Pass
    ``n_train``/``n_test``, or keep the uint8 arrays and call :func:`encode` per batch.
    """
    import torch

    Xtr, ytr, Xte, yte = load_arrays(dataset, data_root)
    if n_train is not None:
        Xtr, ytr = Xtr[:n_train], ytr[:n_train]
    if n_test is not None:
        Xte, yte = Xte[:n_test], yte[:n_test]
    return (encode(dataset, Xtr, device), torch.as_tensor(ytr, dtype=torch.long),
            encode(dataset, Xte, device), torch.as_tensor(yte, dtype=torch.long))


def batches(dataset, X, y, batch_size, shuffle=False, seed=0, device="cpu"):
    """Lazy encoder: yields ``(xs (T,B,...) float32, yb (B,) long)`` from uint8 arrays."""
    import numpy as np
    import torch

    idx = np.arange(len(X))
    if shuffle:
        np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle(idx)
    for i in range(0, len(idx), batch_size):
        j = idx[i:i + batch_size]
        yield encode(dataset, X[j], device), torch.as_tensor(y[j], dtype=torch.long)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deterministic class-balanced subsets
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
#: Seed salt shared by every deterministic selection, so a subset drawn in a
#: spawned worker matches the parent's. Absorbed with the selection code that
#: uses it -- it is not a free parameter.
SUBSET_SALT = 20260803

#: Split identifier folded into the seed, so the train and test selections of one
#: dataset cannot collide.
SPLIT_ID = {"train": 0, "test": 1}


def class_balanced_indices(y, subset_seed: int, split: str, per_class):
    """Deterministic, spawn-stable, class-balanced index selection.

    ``np.random.default_rng`` is seeded from a list of plain ints, so nothing is
    inherited from the parent interpreter's global RNG state and a spawn child
    reproduces the parent's selection exactly (verified). ``per_class=None``
    returns every index (used for the test splits, so reproduced accuracies land
    on the archive's integer ``100/N`` lattice).

    The selection is nested in ``per_class``: the k=20 prefix of a class is the
    first 20 of its k=50 permutation, so shrinking a subset never reshuffles it.
    """
    import numpy as np

    y = np.asarray(y)
    out = []
    for c in np.unique(y):
        idx = np.flatnonzero(y == c)
        if per_class is None:
            out.append(idx)
            continue
        rng = np.random.default_rng(
            [SUBSET_SALT, int(subset_seed), SPLIT_ID[split], int(c)])
        out.append(np.sort(rng.permutation(idx)[:int(per_class)]))
    return np.concatenate(out)


def resolve_subset(y, n_target, subset_seed, split):
    """Turn a target total sample count into class-balanced indices."""
    import numpy as np

    if not n_target:
        return class_balanced_indices(y, subset_seed, split, None)
    n_classes = int(np.unique(y).size)
    per_class = max(1, int(n_target) // n_classes)
    return class_balanced_indices(y, subset_seed, split, per_class)


def blank_like(xs):
    """A stimulus-free continuation of the same shape as one streamed batch."""
    import torch

    return torch.zeros_like(xs[:1])
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{src/mnn\_torch/devices.py}
\index{src/mnn\_torch/devices.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""The measured device: its records, its conduction model, and the layers built on it.

Three groups. The measured multistate sweeps as they are read off the measurement; the conduction
model fitted over them, including the Poole-Frenkel forward map and the nonidealities that ride on
it; and the memristive layers that put a conductance pair behind a weight.
"""


# ============================================================================
# Measured device records
# ============================================================================
import numpy as np
from scipy.io import loadmat


def load_SiOx_multistate(data_path) -> np.array:
    experimental_data = loadmat(data_path)["data"]
    experimental_data = np.flip(experimental_data, axis=2)
    experimental_data = np.transpose(experimental_data, (1, 2, 0))
    experimental_data = experimental_data[:2, :, :]

    return experimental_data


def load_SiOx_curves(
    experimental_data, max_voltage=0.5, voltage_step=0.005, clean_data=True
):
    num_points = int(max_voltage / voltage_step) + 1

    data = experimental_data[:, :, :num_points]
    if clean_data:
        data = clean_experimental_data(data)
    voltages = data[1, :, :]
    currents = data[0, :, :]

    return voltages, currents


def clean_experimental_data(experimental_data, threshold=0.1):
    accepted_curves = []
    for idx in range(experimental_data.shape[1]):
        curve = experimental_data[0, idx, :]
        d2y_dx2 = np.gradient(np.gradient(curve))
        ratio = d2y_dx2 / np.mean(curve)
        if ratio.max() < threshold:
            accepted_curves.append(idx)

    return experimental_data[:, accepted_curves, :]


# ============================================================================
# Conduction model and nonidealities
# ============================================================================
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde, truncnorm
import scipy.constants as const
import torch
from .estimators import sort_multiple_arrays, compute_multivariate_linear_regression, predict_with_multivariate_linear_regression


def disturb_conductance_fixed(G, fixed_conductance, true_probability=0.5):
    """
    Disturbs the conductance by randomly replacing values with a fixed conductance.

    Args:
    - G: The original conductance array (tensor).
    - fixed_conductance: The fixed conductance value to replace randomly selected entries.
    - true_probability: The probability of replacing an entry with the fixed conductance.

    Returns:
    - G: The disturbed conductance array (tensor).
    - mask: The boolean mask indicating which values were replaced.
    """
    mask = torch.rand(*G.shape, device=G.device) < true_probability
    G = torch.where(mask, fixed_conductance, G)
    return G, mask


def disturb_conductance_device(G, G_on, G_off, true_probability=0.1):
    """
    Models stuck devices by probabilistically fixing their conductance to G_off or G_on.

    Args:
    - G (torch.Tensor): Original conductance tensor.
    - G_on (float or torch.Tensor): Maximum conductance value.
    - G_off (float or torch.Tensor): Minimum conductance value.
    - true_probability (float): Proportion of devices to be stuck (0 to 1).

    Returns:
    - torch.Tensor: Updated conductance tensor with probabilistic stuck behavior.
    """
    device = G.device
    G_on = torch.tensor(G_on, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    G_off = torch.tensor(G_off, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)

    # Calculate conductance range and median range
    conductance_range = G_on - G_off
    median_range = torch.median(conductance_range)

    # Identify potentially stuck devices based on range criteria
    stuck_mask = (G - G_off).abs() < (0.5 * median_range)

    # Generate a PDF for stuck values using kde
    G_flat = G[~stuck_mask].detach().cpu().numpy()  # Non-stuck conductance values
    kde = gaussian_kde(G_flat)
    kde_samples = kde.resample(len(G_flat)).flatten()

    # Apply truncated normal distribution to mitigate bias near zero
    a, b = (0 - kde_samples.mean()) / kde_samples.std(), float("inf")
    truncated_samples = truncnorm(
        a, b, loc=kde_samples.mean(), scale=kde_samples.std()
    ).rvs(len(G_flat))
    truncated_samples = torch.tensor(
        truncated_samples, device=device, dtype=torch.float32
    )

    # Map stuck devices probabilistically to G_off or G_on
    stuck_values = torch.where(torch.rand_like(G, device=device) < 0.5, G_off, G_on)

    # Generate a random mask to select which devices are stuck
    random_stuck_mask = torch.rand_like(G, device=device) < true_probability

    # Incorporate device-to-device variability using a lognormal distribution
    # (Eq. lognormal). The lognormal model is defined on positive conductance, so
    # operate on |G| to stay valid when G carries a sign (e.g. conv kernels where
    # G = G_pos - G_neg); a positive floor avoids log(0)/NaN that would make the
    # sampling std non-finite. The original sign is restored after sampling.
    G_sign = torch.sign(G)
    G_mag = torch.clamp(torch.abs(G), min=1e-8)
    log_var = torch.clamp(torch.var(torch.log(G_mag)), min=0.0)
    log_std = torch.sqrt(log_var)
    log_mu = torch.log(G_mag) - (0.5 * log_var)
    # Sample per element: draw standard normals and scale by the (scalar) std so
    # the call is shape-safe across backends (mps rejects a 0-dim std against a
    # full-shaped mean), then exponentiate. Equivalent to N(log_mu, log_std**2).
    noise = torch.randn_like(log_mu) * log_std
    variability_samples = G_sign * torch.exp(log_mu + noise)

    # Combine stuck and non-stuck conductance values out-of-place: stuck devices
    # take the fixed stuck value, the rest take the lognormal-perturbed value.
    # An out-of-place select (rather than in-place index assignment) is required
    # because G may be part of an autograd graph when the conductance feeds the
    # differentiable Poole-Frenkel forward map.
    G = torch.where(random_stuck_mask, stuck_values, variability_samples)

    return G


def sample_device_fault(shape, G_on, G_off, true_probability=0.1, sigma_g=0.5,
                        device="cpu", generator=None, stuck_polarity="split"):
    """Draw a *fixed* device-fault realisation, once, for a conductance array.

    This implements the declared fault protocol, in which the
    stuck-device pattern and the device-to-device (D2D) programming spread are
    sampled once per training run and then held fixed, exactly as a physically
    programmed crossbar would behave: a device that is stuck, or programmed off
    its target, stays that way for the rest of training. This is distinct from
    :func:`disturb_conductance_device`, which re-rolls a fresh random fault on
    every forward pass and therefore injects a new, destabilising perturbation at
    every time step rather than a fixed hardware fault.

    The realisation is independent of the live weight values: it records *which*
    devices are stuck (``stuck_mask``), the conductance they are stuck at
    (``stuck_values``), and a per-device multiplicative lognormal D2D factor
    (``d2d_factor``, Eq. lognormal). It is applied later by
    :func:`apply_device_fault` to whatever conductance the current weights map to.

    The ``stuck_polarity`` argument follows the Joksas et al. nonideality
    taxonomy (``StuckAtGOff`` / ``StuckAtGOn``), which separates the two failure
    modes that the symmetric default blends together:

    * ``"off"`` -- stuck-at-G_off: dead / open synapses (cannot conduct). The
      presynaptic line goes silent; a firing-rate homeostat has nothing to act
      on, so this is the natural *negative control* for the homeostasis claim.
    * ``"on"``  -- stuck-at-G_on: shorted / saturated synapses that drive their
      postsynaptic line hyperactive. This is exactly the regime the sigmoidal
      firing-rate regulariser (Eq. homeo) is designed to suppress, so it is
      where homeostatic recovery should be largest.
    * ``"split"`` (default) -- each stuck device is G_off or G_on with equal
      probability, the original symmetric behaviour.

    Args:
    - shape (tuple): Shape of the conductance tensor the fault applies to.
    - G_on, G_off (float): Conductance bounds; stuck devices take one of these.
    - true_probability (float): Fraction of devices that are stuck.
    - sigma_g (float): Lognormal width of the D2D programming spread (Eq. lognormal).
    - device: Torch device for the realisation tensors.
    - generator (torch.Generator, optional): For reproducible realisations.
    - stuck_polarity (str): ``"split"`` | ``"off"`` | ``"on"`` (see above).

    Returns:
    - dict: {"stuck_mask", "stuck_values", "d2d_factor"} torch tensors of `shape`,
      all detached (a fixed hardware realisation, not a function of the weights).
    """
    G_on_t = torch.as_tensor(G_on, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    G_off_t = torch.as_tensor(G_off, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)

    def _rand(s):
        return torch.rand(s, device=device, generator=generator)

    def _randn(s):
        return torch.randn(s, device=device, generator=generator)

    stuck_mask = _rand(shape) < true_probability
    if stuck_polarity == "off":
        stuck_values = G_off_t.expand(shape).clone()
    elif stuck_polarity == "on":
        stuck_values = G_on_t.expand(shape).clone()
    elif stuck_polarity == "split":
        stuck_values = torch.where(_rand(shape) < 0.5, G_off_t, G_on_t)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"stuck_polarity must be 'split', 'off' or 'on'; got {stuck_polarity!r}"
        )
    # Multiplicative lognormal D2D spread, mean-preserving (median at the target):
    # G_observed = G_target * exp(N(0, sigma_g^2)).
    d2d_factor = torch.exp(sigma_g * _randn(shape))
    return {
        "stuck_mask": stuck_mask.detach(),
        "stuck_values": stuck_values.detach(),
        "d2d_factor": d2d_factor.detach(),
    }


def apply_device_fault(G, fault):
    """Apply a *fixed* device-fault realisation (from :func:`sample_device_fault`).

    Stuck devices take their fixed stuck conductance; all other devices keep their
    programmed conductance scaled by the fixed per-device lognormal D2D factor. The
    operation is out-of-place so it is safe inside an autograd graph (the surviving
    devices' gradient still flows through ``G``), while the stuck devices and the
    D2D factors are constants that do not move during training.

    Args:
    - G (torch.Tensor): Live conductance tensor from the current weights.
    - fault (dict): Realisation from :func:`sample_device_fault`.

    Returns:
    - torch.Tensor: Conductance with the fixed fault realisation applied.
    """
    sign = torch.sign(G)
    perturbed = sign * torch.abs(G) * fault["d2d_factor"]
    return torch.where(fault["stuck_mask"], fault["stuck_values"], perturbed)


def compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch(V, c, d_epsilon):
    r"""Differentiable Poole-Frenkel current (Torch), the declared forward map.

    Implements Eq. ``forward-g`` / Eq. ``pf``:

    .. math::
        I = c\, V \exp\!\left( \frac{2e}{k_B T} \sqrt{\frac{e |V|}{4\pi d\varepsilon}} \right)

    At ``T = 20 degC``, with the sign of ``V`` preserved so the map is valid for
    both bias polarities. All operations are Torch ops, so gradients flow through
    ``V``, ``c`` and ``d_epsilon``; this is the differentiable replacement for the
    NumPy :func:`compute_PooleFrenkel_current` used in offline fitting.

    Args:
        V (Tensor): Voltage.
        c (Tensor): Conductance-like prefactor (broadcastable to ``V``).
        d_epsilon (Tensor): Effective oxide-thickness--permittivity product
            (broadcastable to ``V``).

    Returns:
        Tensor: Poole-Frenkel current, same shape as the broadcast of the inputs.
    """
    e = const.elementary_charge
    kT = const.Boltzmann * (const.zero_Celsius + 20.0)
    V_abs = torch.abs(V)
    V_sign = torch.sign(V)
    # The poole-frenkel exponent: (2e/kT) * sqrt(e|V| / (4 pi d_epsilon)). This is
    # algebraically identical to the NumPy reference's (e/kT)*sqrt(e|V|/(pi d_eps))
    # since 2*sqrt(1/4) = 1. Clamp the radicand for numerical stability.
    term = torch.clamp(e * V_abs / (4.0 * np.pi * d_epsilon), min=1e-18)
    exponent = (2.0 * e / kT) * torch.sqrt(term)
    # Clamp the exponent: when a synapse's sampled conductance falls outside the
    # fitted resistance range, the regression can predict an unphysically small
    # d_epsilon and the raw exp() overflows to inf. Bounding the exponent keeps
    # the forward map finite and differentiable without distorting the in-range
    # Response (exp(50) already exceeds any realistic current scale here).
    exponent = torch.clamp(exponent, max=50.0)
    return V_sign * c * V_abs * torch.exp(exponent)


def cholesky_factor_from_covariance(covariance_matrix, device="cpu", dtype=torch.float32):
    """Cholesky factor ``L`` of the PF residual covariance, with pd jitter.

    Precomputing this once (e.g. at layer construction) avoids recomputing a
    ``torch.linalg.cholesky`` on the constant covariance at every forward pass,
    which is the dominant redundant cost in the per-timestep PF sampling.
    """
    Sigma = torch.as_tensor(covariance_matrix, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    jitter = 1e-12 * torch.eye(2, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    return torch.linalg.cholesky(Sigma + jitter)


def sample_PooleFrenkel_parameters_torch(
    G, slopes, intercepts, covariance_matrix, stochastic=True, generator=None,
    cholesky_factor=None, residual=None, return_residual=False,
):
    r"""Sample per-synapse Poole-Frenkel parameters ``(c, d_epsilon)`` from conductance.

    Implements the declared bivariate regression (``pf-regression``):

    .. math::
        [\ln c, \ln(d\varepsilon)]^\top = -\mathbf{m}\,\ln R + \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{E},
        \quad \mathbf{E} \sim \mathcal{N}_2(0, \Sigma)

    With ``R = 1/G``. The regression mean depends on the (trainable) conductance
    ``G`` and so carries gradient; the Gaussian residual ``E`` is treated as
    injected noise and is detached from the graph (stop-gradient), matching the
    declared gradient-flow description. Returns ``c`` and ``d_epsilon`` as
    Torch tensors on ``G``'s device.

    Args:
        G (Tensor): Per-synapse conductance, any shape.
        slopes (array-like): Regression slopes ``m`` for ``[ln c, ln d_epsilon]``.
        intercepts (array-like): Regression intercepts ``b``.
        covariance_matrix (array-like): Residual covariance ``Sigma`` (2x2).
        stochastic (bool): If True, add the ``N(0, Sigma)`` residual; if False,
            return the regression mean only (deterministic).
        generator (torch.Generator, optional): RNG for reproducible sampling.
        cholesky_factor (Tensor, optional): Precomputed Cholesky factor of the
            residual covariance (see :func:`cholesky_factor_from_covariance`). When
            given, the per-call ``cholesky`` is skipped; ``covariance_matrix`` is
            then unused. Pass this from a layer that caches it once at construction.
        residual (Tensor, optional): A frozen ``(*G.shape, 2)`` device-to-device
            residual to reuse instead of drawing a fresh one. Models the variability
            as a fixed per-synapse property (sampled once per run), which also avoids
            the per-timestep ``randn``/matmul. ``cholesky_factor`` is then unused.
        return_residual (bool): If True, also return the residual that was used, so
            a caller can cache it for subsequent forward passes.

    Returns:
        tuple[Tensor, Tensor]: ``(c, d_epsilon)`` with the same shape as ``G``; or
        ``(c, d_epsilon, residual)`` when ``return_residual`` is True.
    """
    device = G.device
    dtype = G.dtype
    m = torch.as_tensor(slopes, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    b = torch.as_tensor(intercepts, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    ln_R = torch.log(1.0 / torch.clamp(G, min=1e-12))
    # Mean of [ln c, ln d_epsilon]: shape (*G.shape, 2).
    # Note: slopes/intercepts come from scipy.linregress (compute_multivariate_
    # linear_regression), whose convention is y = slope*x + intercept, so the
    # prediction uses +slopes here. This is the signed form of the declared
    # Eq. pf-regression (-m ln R + b), where the code's slope already carries the
    # sign; the +convention yields physical d_epsilon ~1e-18 matching the fit.
    mean = ln_R.unsqueeze(-1) * m + b

    drawn_residual = None
    if stochastic:
        if residual is not None:
            # Frozen device-to-device residual (sampled once per run): the
            # variability is a fixed property of each fabricated synapse, so it is
            # not re-rolled every timestep. The weight-dependent mean still updates,
            # so gradients and training-time conductance changes are preserved.
            drawn_residual = residual.to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
        else:
            # Use a precomputed Cholesky factor when supplied (constant across
            # forward passes); otherwise compute it from the covariance. Computing
            # it once at layer construction removes a linalg op from the timestep loop.
            if cholesky_factor is not None:
                L = cholesky_factor.to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
            else:
                L = cholesky_factor_from_covariance(covariance_matrix, device, dtype)
            z = torch.randn(*G.shape, 2, device=device, dtype=dtype, generator=generator)
            drawn_residual = z @ L.T
        ln_params = mean + drawn_residual.detach()  # Stop-gradient on the noise
    else:
        ln_params = mean

    c = torch.exp(ln_params[..., 0])
    d_epsilon = torch.exp(ln_params[..., 1])
    if return_residual:
        return c, d_epsilon, drawn_residual
    return c, d_epsilon


def compute_PooleFrenkel_current(V, c, d_epsilon):
    """
    Computes the Poole-Frenkel current for a given voltage.

    Args:
    - V: The voltage array.
    - c: A coefficient related to the current.
    - d_epsilon: A parameter related to the material's dielectric properties.

    Returns:
    - I: The calculated current array.
    """
    V_abs = np.abs(V)
    V_sign = np.sign(V)
    term = np.maximum(const.elementary_charge * V_abs / (const.pi * d_epsilon), 1e-18)
    I = (
        V_sign
        * c
        * V_abs
        * np.exp(
            const.elementary_charge
            * np.sqrt(term)
            / (const.Boltzmann * (const.zero_Celsius + 20.0))
        )
    )
    return I


def compute_PooleFrenkel_total_current(V, G, slopes, intercepts, covariance_matrix):
    """
    Computes the total Poole-Frenkel current, including deviations based on the regression parameters.

    Args:
    - V: The voltage array.
    - G: The conductance array.
    - slopes: The slopes from the regression model.
    - intercepts: The intercepts from the regression model.
    - covariance_matrix: The covariance matrix for the regression.

    Returns:
    - I: The total current.
    - I_ind: The individual current components.
    """
    R = 1 / G
    ln_R = np.log(R)

    # Predict regression results for ln(R)
    fit_data = predict_with_multivariate_linear_regression(
        ln_R, slopes, intercepts, covariance_matrix
    )

    # Extract coefficients for the Poole-Frenkel equation
    c = np.exp(fit_data[0])
    d_epsilon = np.exp(fit_data[1])

    # Compute individual currents
    I_ind = compute_PooleFrenkel_current(V, c, d_epsilon)

    # Sum currents along the bit lines
    I = np.sum(I_ind, axis=1)
    return I, I_ind


def compute_PooleFrenkel_relationship(V, I, voltage_step=0.005, ref_voltage=0.1):
    """
    Computes the relationship between voltage and current for the Poole-Frenkel model.

    Args:
    - V: Voltage array.
    - I: Current array.
    - voltage_step: Step size for voltage.
    - ref_voltage: The reference voltage to compute resistance.

    Returns:
    - R, c, d_epsilon: The computed resistance, c, and d_epsilon values.
    - V, I: The sorted voltage and current arrays.
    """
    num_curves = V.shape[0]
    R = np.zeros(num_curves)
    c = np.zeros(num_curves)
    d_epsilon = np.zeros(num_curves)

    ref_idx = int(ref_voltage / voltage_step)

    for idx in range(num_curves):
        v = V[idx, :]
        i = I[idx, :]

        # Compute resistance at the reference voltage
        if i[ref_idx] == 0:  # Avoid division by zero
            R[idx] = np.inf
        else:
            R[idx] = v[ref_idx] / i[ref_idx]
