__all__ = ["TransientProfile", "fit_kww", "kohlrausch_modes", "KohlrauschTrace",
]


# ==========================================================================
# Profile
# ==========================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TransientProfile:
    """One measured relaxation, with the provenance needed to defend it.

    ``tau_kww`` is the KWW scale parameter, deliberately not called a time constant;
    :attr:`mean_lifetime` is the quantity a membrane model would need.  ``bias_regime``
    separates near-zero-bias from held-bias fits because the ``eq:floorrate`` correction
    ``tau_0 = tau_hb/(1-rho)`` does real work under bias and adds pure fit noise at
    near-zero bias, where ``f -> 0`` already (measured: applying it at 1 mV turns 4.32 s
    into 7.9 s through an unreliable rho).
    """

    tau_kww: float
    beta: float
    amplitude: float          # A
    floor: float              # I_0  (== I_static in the composed model)
    v_read: float             # Volts
    polarity: str             # "decay" | "rise"
    r2: float
    n_samples: int
    window_s: float
    source: str
    bias_regime: str          # "near_zero" | "held"
    qc_pass: bool
    qc_reasons: tuple = field(default_factory=tuple)

    @property
    def mean_lifetime(self) -> float:
        r"""$\langle t\rangle = (\tau/\beta)\Gamma(1/\beta)$ -- not ``tau_kww``."""
        return (self.tau_kww / self.beta) * math.gamma(1.0 / self.beta)

    @property
    def rho(self) -> float:
        """Floor ratio ``I_0/(A+I_0)`` = ``f/(f+g)`` of ``eq:floorrate``."""
        d = self.amplitude + self.floor
        return float(self.floor / d) if d != 0 else float("nan")

    @property
    def emission_rate(self) -> float:
        """``g = (1-rho)/tau_hb`` -- the field-free emission rate of ``eq:taufree``."""
        return (1.0 - self.rho) / self.tau_kww

    def tau_field_free(self) -> float:
        """``eq:taufree``.  Identity at near-zero bias, where the correction is noise."""
        if self.bias_regime == "near_zero":
            return self.tau_kww
        return self.tau_kww / (1.0 - self.rho)

    def summary(self) -> str:
        f = "PASS" if self.qc_pass else "FAIL(" + ",".join(self.qc_reasons) + ")"
        return (f"{self.source:<26s} V={self.v_read*1e3:7.2f}mV {self.polarity:<5s} "
                f"tau={self.tau_kww:10.4g}s beta={self.beta:6.3f} <t>={self.mean_lifetime:10.4g}s "
                f"rho={self.rho:7.4f} R2={self.r2:7.4f} win={self.window_s:8.2f}s {f}")


# ==========================================================================
# Fitting
# ==========================================================================
def fit_kww(t, I, polarity="auto", min_window_tau=2.0, beta_max=1.0,
            require_positive_floor=True, floor_fixed=None):
    """Fit ``I = floor + A*q`` (decay) or ``floor + A*(1-q)`` (rise), with physical gates.

    Returns ``(params, r2, qc_pass, reasons, polarity)`` where ``params`` is
    ``(A, tau, beta, floor, sign)``.  Gates are applied after fitting so a rejected fit
    still reports its numbers -- silently dropping them is how unidentifiable fits survive.

    The trace is fitted in magnitude (``sign*I``, ``sign`` taken from the median current),
    because the trap population relaxes regardless of the polarity of the sensing bias.
    Without this a negative-bias trace fits a negative floor and is rejected by the
    ``floor<0`` gate -- which would silently discard every held-bias measurement.

    ``floor_fixed`` pins the settled current instead of fitting it.  The floor is an
    asymptote a truncated window never reaches, so it is the unidentifiable parameter in
    a held-out test; supplying it from the tail of the full trace treats it as the
    separate settled-current measurement it physically is, and validates only kinetics.
    measured: at the split the model is still 3.3-4.1% of a above a floor that is 4.9-5.8% of
    A, so a floor taken from the train half instead is biased +65% to +94%.  Be honest about
    what this costs: in a first-half/second-half protocol a full-trace tail floor leaks the end
    of the held-out half into the fit, so such a result is "kinetics validated given an
    independently measured settled current", not a clean held-out test.
    """
    from scipy.optimize import curve_fit

    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    I = np.asarray(I, float)
    m = np.isfinite(t) & np.isfinite(I)
    t, I = t[m], I[m]
    if t.size < 12:
        return None, float("nan"), False, ("too_few_samples",), polarity

    sign = 1.0 if np.nanmedian(I) >= 0 else -1.0
    I = sign * I

    if polarity == "auto":
        i0 = np.interp(min(1.0, t[-1] * 0.1), t, np.abs(I))
        polarity = "rise" if abs(I[-1]) > 1.2 * i0 else "decay"

    def decay(tt, A, tau, beta, fl):
        return fl + A * np.exp(-np.power(np.clip(tt / tau, 1e-12, None), beta))

    def rise(tt, A, tau, beta, fl):
        return fl + A * (1.0 - np.exp(-np.power(np.clip(tt / tau, 1e-12, None), beta)))

    fn = rise if polarity == "rise" else decay
    span = float(abs(I[-1] - I[0])) or float(abs(I).max()) or 1.0
    p0 = [span, max(t[-1] / 4.0, 1e-6), 0.7, float(I[0] if polarity == "rise" else I[-1])]
    if floor_fixed is not None:
        fl0 = float(sign * floor_fixed)
        fn3, p0 = (lambda tt, A, tau, beta: fn(tt, A, tau, beta, fl0)), p0[:3]
    else:
        fn3 = None
    try:
        p, _ = curve_fit(fn3 or fn, t, I, p0=p0, maxfev=40000)
    except Exception as exc:                                   # Pragma: no cover
        return None, float("nan"), False, (f"fit_failed:{type(exc).__name__}",), polarity
    if fn3 is not None:
        p = list(p) + [fl0]

    resid = I - fn(t, *p)
    denom = np.sum((I - I.mean()) ** 2)
    r2 = float(1.0 - np.sum(resid ** 2) / denom) if denom > 0 else float("nan")

    A, tau, beta, floor = (float(x) for x in p)
    window = float(t[-1] - t[0])
    reasons = []
    if not np.isfinite(r2) or r2 < 0.80:
        reasons.append("r2<0.80")
    if beta > beta_max:
        reasons.append(f"beta>{beta_max:g}")
    if beta <= 0:
        reasons.append("beta<=0")
    if require_positive_floor and floor < 0:
        reasons.append("floor<0")
    if not (tau > 0):
        reasons.append("tau<=0")
    elif window < min_window_tau * tau:
        reasons.append(f"window<{min_window_tau:g}tau")
    return (A, tau, beta, floor, sign), r2, (not reasons), tuple(reasons), polarity


# ==========================================================================
# Kernel
# ==========================================================================
def kohlrausch_modes(tau, beta, k=12, span_decades=(-1.5, 1.15), n_grid=400, tmax_tau=21.0):
    """``k`` positive modes with ``q(t) = sum w_i exp(-t/tau_i) ~= exp[-(t/tau)^beta]``.

    ``tau`` is forced into the mode grid, so ``beta == 1`` collapses onto a single mode and
    reproduces the single exponential exactly -- the control that validates the kernel.
    Weights come from non-negative least squares, so every mode is a decaying positive
    contribution and the trace can never grow of its own accord.

    The defaults are the measured ones.  The coarse-and-wide alternative ``k=4,
    (-3.0, 1.5), tmax_tau=8`` breaks the reference profile's own held-out criterion: at those
    values only **1 of 124** ITO transients survive :func:`holdout_validate` and the nine
    reference runs score ``r2_kernel_out`` of **-2.65 to -13.90**, recovering to **13 of 124**
    and **+0.14 to +0.73** at ``k=12, (-1.5, 1.15), tmax_tau=21``.  The mechanism is a mode at
    ``tau*10^1.5 = 507 s``, 2.2x beyond the 226 s measurement window and left unconstrained by
    a grid that stops at ``8 tau = 128 s``: worst in-window excess over the exact KWW at
    ``tau=16.033, beta=0.6225`` is **10.2x** (k=4) and **3.17x** (k=6) against **1.019x** here.
    caveat: the clamped span is a mitigation, not a cure -- ``tau*10^1.15 = 226.5 s`` still
    puts the longest mode at the window edge (inside the window for only 3 of the nine
    reference traces), and the nnls target grid runs past every window.  Two grid ends, both
    real: the rounded default ``tmax_tau=21`` used here ends at ``21 tau = 337 s``, while the
    benchmark scales ``tmax_tau = 1.5*226/16.033 = 21.14`` and so ends at **339 s** -- 339 s is
    the figure to quote for the reported runs, 337 s only for this rounded default.
    """
    from scipy.optimize import nnls

    tau = float(tau)
    if not np.isfinite(tau) or tau <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"kohlrausch_modes: tau must be finite and positive, got {tau}")
    beta = float(np.clip(beta, 1e-3, 1.0))
    exps = np.linspace(span_decades[0], span_decades[1], int(k))
    exps[int(np.argmin(np.abs(exps)))] = 0.0          # <- tau itself is a mode
    taus = tau * np.power(10.0, exps)
    tg = np.logspace(np.log10(tau * 1e-3), np.log10(tau * tmax_tau), n_grid)
    basis = np.exp(-tg[:, None] / taus[None, :])
    target = np.exp(-np.power(tg / tau, beta))
    if not (np.all(np.isfinite(basis)) and np.all(np.isfinite(target))):
        raise ValueError("kohlrausch_modes: non-finite basis/target (tau out of range)")
    w, _ = nnls(basis, target)
    approx = basis @ w
    ss = np.sum((target - target.mean()) ** 2)
    r2 = float(1.0 - np.sum((target - approx) ** 2) / ss) if ss > 0 else float("nan")
    return taus, w, r2


class KohlrauschTrace:
    """Stateful KWW trace as ``k`` positive exponential modes.  Device kernel, not a neuron.

    State is threaded explicitly (``q, z = trace(u, z)``) and never stored on the object,
    so batched sequences cannot contaminate one another and a hold phase is an ordinary
    call with zero drive.  ``hold(z, duration)`` advances the state without input, which is
    what a delay period is -- and note that reading it out requires a probe pulse, because
    zero-field trapped charge is not observable without a sensing bias.
    """

    def __init__(self, tau, beta, k=12, dt=1.0, span_decades=(-1.5, 1.15), tmax_tau=21.0):
        """``span_decades``/``tmax_tau`` are forwarded to :func:`kohlrausch_modes`.

        The defaults are not ``k=4, (-3.0, 1.5), tmax_tau=8``, because those values fail the
        reference profile's own held-out criterion:
        **1 of 124** ITO transients survive :func:`holdout_validate` at them and the nine
        reference runs score ``r2_kernel_out`` of **-2.65 to -13.90**, versus **13 of 124** and
        **+0.14 to +0.73** at ``k=12, (-1.5, 1.15), tmax_tau=21``.  Mechanism: ``(-3.0, 1.5)``
        places a mode at ``tau*10^1.5 = 507 s``, 2.2x beyond the 226 s measurement window, and
        ``tmax_tau=8`` (grid to 128 s) leaves that mode's weight unconstrained over the range a
        long-delay sweep scores.  measured excess of the k-mode kernel over the exact KWW at
        ``tau=16.033, beta=0.6225``: worst factor **10.2x** with the old default k=4 and 3.17x
        with ``k=6, (-3.0, 1.5), tmax_tau=8``, versus **1.019x** at the new defaults.
        This is a mitigation, not a cure: ``tau*10^1.15 = 226.5 s`` leaves the longest mode at
        the window edge, and the nnls grid still runs past the window -- to ``21 tau = 337 s``
        at this rounded default, and to **339 s** at the benchmark's scaled
        ``tmax_tau = 1.5*226/16.033 = 21.14``.  Callers that need the old numbers must now pass
        them explicitly.
        """
        self.tau_kww, self.beta, self.dt, self.k = float(tau), float(beta), float(dt), int(k)
        self.span_decades, self.tmax_tau = tuple(span_decades), float(tmax_tau)
        taus, w, self.mode_r2 = kohlrausch_modes(
            tau, beta, k=k, span_decades=span_decades, tmax_tau=tmax_tau)
        self.mode_taus = taus
        self.weights = w
        s = w.sum()
        self.norm = float(s) if s > 0 else 1.0
        self.decays = np.exp(-self.dt / self.mode_taus)

    @property
    def mean_lifetime(self):
        return (self.tau_kww / self.beta) * math.gamma(1.0 / self.beta)

    def init_state(self, shape, xp=np):
        return xp.zeros(tuple(shape) + (self.k,))

    def step(self, u, z):
        """One timestep.  ``u`` is the drive (e.g. a presynaptic spike), broadcast over modes."""
        z = z * self.decays + np.asarray(u)[..., None]
        q = (z * self.weights).sum(-1) / self.norm
        return q, z

    def hold(self, z, duration):
        """Advance ``duration`` steps with no drive -- a delay period."""
        n = int(round(duration / self.dt))
        return z * np.power(self.decays, n)

    def read(self, z):
        return (z * self.weights).sum(-1) / self.norm


# ==========================================================================
# Loaders
# ==========================================================================


# ==========================================================================
# Stateful (volatile) synapse
# ==========================================================================
class VolatileSynapse:
    r"""Wraps a memristive layer so each synapse carries a measured relaxation.

    .. math::  I_{ij}(t) = I_\mathrm{static}(V_i, G_{ij}) + A(V_i, G_{ij})\, q_i(t)

    ``I_static`` is :func:`mnn_torch.devices.compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch` evaluated
    per device, and the amplitude is tied to it by the measured floor ratio of
    ``eq:floorrate``, ``A = I_static (1-rho)/rho`` -- so there is no free amplitude.

    Both devices of each pair are kept separate.  The trace multiplies each device's own
    current before the pos/neg subtraction, so a mismatch between the two devices of a pair
    survives into the output.  Applying one trace after subtraction would cancel exactly the
    residual that makes an unsilenced bias row imitate retention.

    State is explicit.  ``out, z = layer(x, z, phase=...)`` and ``z = layer.hold(z, dt)``;
    nothing is stored on the object, so batched sequences cannot contaminate one another.
    ``phase`` records intent and selects the drive voltage: a ``"hold"`` carries no drive,
    and a ``"read"`` needs a probe pulse because zero-field trapped charge is not
    observable without a sensing bias.

    Kinetics are shared across the row (one profile per layer) while ``A`` differs per
    device through ``G``.  Per-device kinetics -- true device-to-device tau -- is the
    natural extension and needs state of shape ``(B, n_in+1, 2*n_out, k)`` instead of
    ``(B, n_in+1, k)``.
    """

    def __init__(self, base_layer, profile, k=12, dt=1.0, rho=None, polarity=None,
                 span_decades=(-1.5, 1.15), tmax_tau=21.0):
        """``k``/``span_decades``/``tmax_tau`` build the :class:`KohlrauschTrace`.

        The defaults are not ``k=4, (-3.0, 1.5), tmax_tau=8``, which fail the
        reference profile's own held-out criterion (**1/124** traces and ``r2_kernel_out``
        **-2.65 to -13.90** on the nine reference runs, against **13/124** and **+0.14 to
        +0.73** here) and over-predict the exact KWW by **10.2x** inside the 226 s measurement
        window at ``tau=16.033, beta=0.6225``, versus **1.019x** at these values.  A network
        run at the old defaults therefore held far more charge at long delay than the device
        does, which inflates exactly the retention a delay sweep measures.  note that even
        here the longest mode sits at ``tau*10^1.15 = 226.5 s``, i.e. at the window edge, so
        any delay beyond ~226 s is extrapolating that mode; ``netbench`` instead scales
        ``tmax_tau = 1.5*max_delay/tau`` so the slow mode is constrained over what it scores.
        """
        self.base = base_layer
        self.profile = profile
        self.trace = KohlrauschTrace(profile.tau_kww, profile.beta, k=k, dt=dt,
                                     span_decades=span_decades, tmax_tau=tmax_tau)
        r = profile.rho if rho is None else float(rho)
        if not (0.0 < r < 1.0):
            raise ValueError(f"rho must be in (0,1) to set A from eq:floorrate; got {r}")
        self.rho = r
        self.gain = (1.0 - r) / r                       # A = I_static * gain
        self.polarity = polarity or profile.polarity
        self.k = int(k)

    # -- state ------------------------------------------------------------
    def n_rows(self):
        return int(self.base.weights.shape[1]) + 1      # + bias row

    def init_state(self, batch, device=None, dtype=None):
        import torch
        return torch.zeros(int(batch), self.n_rows(), self.k,
                           device=device, dtype=dtype or torch.float32)

    def hold(self, z, duration):
        """Advance ``duration`` (seconds) with NO drive -- a delay period."""
        import torch
        n = max(int(round(duration / self.trace.dt)), 0)
        d = torch.as_tensor(self.trace.decays, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        return z * torch.pow(d, n)

    def read_trace(self, z):
        import torch
        w = torch.as_tensor(self.trace.weights, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        return (z * w).sum(-1) / self.trace.norm

    # -- forward ----------------------------------------------------------
    def __call__(self, x, z, phase="read", drive=None, gate_bias_row=False,
                 compute_out=True, return_parts=False):
        """``(out, z)``.  ``gate_bias_row=True`` physically disconnects the bias row.

        Measured: with mismatch present, zeroing the digital bias weight leaves a standing
        offset on every output (mean 0.0656, max 0.2321 on N-MNIST fc1), and it is exactly
        0.000000 when the row is gated.  A digital zero is not a gate.

        ``compute_out=False`` returns ``(None, z)`` and skips the conductance grid and the
        Poole-Frenkel map entirely.  This is exact, not an approximation: the trace update
        ``z <- z*dec + u`` contains no weights, so a write/hold step whose output is
        discarded contributes nothing to any gradient.  It is what makes a T=50 write phase
        affordable -- it replaces T evaluations of the ``(B, n_in+1, 2*n_out)`` PF map with
        one at the read.

        ``return_parts=True`` returns ``(out, z, (out_static, out_trace))`` with the pos/neg
        difference taken separately on the static and the trace accumulators before they are
        summed.  Algebraically identical, numerically not: the static parts of a pos/neg pair
        very nearly cancel, so forming ``I_static*(1+gain*q)`` first destroys a small trace
        term in that cancellation.  measured motivation: at ``D = 226 s`` the ``beta=1``
        control has ``gain*q = 1.3e-5``, only 1.1x above ``100*eps32``.
        """
        import torch
        from .devices import compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch

        dev = x.device
        ones = torch.ones(x.shape[0], 1, device=dev, dtype=x.dtype)
        bias_col = torch.zeros_like(ones) if gate_bias_row else ones
        xin = torch.cat([x, bias_col], dim=1)                      # (B, n_in+1)

        # Trace update: the drive is the row's own input unless overridden
        u = xin if drive is None else drive
        if phase == "hold":
            u = torch.zeros_like(xin)
        dec = torch.as_tensor(self.trace.decays, device=dev, dtype=z.dtype)
        z = z * dec + u.unsqueeze(-1).to(z.dtype)
        if not compute_out:
            return (None, z, (None, None)) if return_parts else (None, z)
        q = self.read_trace(z)                                      # (B, n_in+1)

        G, k_I, c, d_epsilon = self.base._grid_and_params(dev)
        if c is None:                                               # Linear (ideal) rung
            I_dev = (self.base.k_V * xin).unsqueeze(-1) * G.unsqueeze(0)
        else:
            V = (self.base.k_V * xin).unsqueeze(-1)                 # (B, n_in+1, 1)
            I_dev = compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch(V, c, d_epsilon)
        if I_dev.dim() == 4:                                        # (1,B,r,c) -> (B,r,c)
            I_dev = I_dev.squeeze(0)

        qq = q.unsqueeze(-1).to(I_dev.dtype)
        trace_term = qq if self.polarity == "decay" else (1.0 - qq)
        if return_parts:
            a_s = I_dev.sum(dim=1)                                  # (B, 2*n_out) static
            a_t = (I_dev * (self.gain * trace_term)).sum(dim=1)      #             Trace
            o_s = (a_s[:, 0::2] - a_s[:, 1::2]) / k_I
            o_t = (a_t[:, 0::2] - a_t[:, 1::2]) / k_I
            return o_s + o_t, z, (o_s, o_t)
        I_tot = I_dev * (1.0 + self.gain * trace_term)              # Per device
        acc = I_tot.sum(dim=1)                                      # (B, 2*n_out)
        out = (acc[:, 0::2] - acc[:, 1::2]) / k_I
        return out, z


def holdout_validate(t, I, profile_kwargs=None, split=0.5, k=12,
                     span_decades=(-1.5, 1.15), tmax_tau=21.0):
    """Fit KWW + kernel on the first ``split`` of a trace, score on the held-out remainder.

    Reports in-sample and out-of-sample R^2 for the k-mode kernel, not just the closed-form
    KWW -- the kernel is what a network would actually run, so it is what must generalise.

    The kernel grid is part of what is being tested, so it must not be hard-coded to values
    this test rejects.  measured over the 124-transient corpus: ``k=4,
    (-3.0, 1.5), tmax_tau=8`` passes **1 of 124** and gives the nine reference runs
    ``r2_kernel_out`` of **-2.65 to -13.90**; ``k=12, (-1.5, 1.15), tmax_tau=21`` passes
    **13 of 124** and **+0.14 to +0.73**.  The defaults are the latter.

    Read ``r2_kernel_out`` with care.  On an almost-flat second half it ranks traces by how
    much decay is left rather than by predictive accuracy, so it understates accuracy on the
    best-settled traces; report out-of-sample rmse relative to ``A`` alongside it (for the
    nine reference runs: 0.78-2.49% out-of-sample against a 0.97-1.98% in-sample residual rms,
    i.e. all nine predict the held-out half to within measurement noise).  Note also that
    ``profile_kwargs["floor_fixed"]``, if taken from the tail of the full trace, leaks the end
    of the held-out half into the fit; see :data:`ITO_REFERENCE` for what the leak-free
    variants give.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, float); I = np.asarray(I, float)
    n = int(len(t) * split)
    if n < 12 or len(t) - n < 6:
        return None
    p, r2_in, ok, why, pol = fit_kww(t[:n], I[:n], **(profile_kwargs or {}))
    if p is None:
        return None
    A, tau, beta, floor, sign = p
    tr = KohlrauschTrace(tau, min(beta, 1.0), k=k, dt=float(np.median(np.diff(t))),
                         span_decades=span_decades, tmax_tau=tmax_tau)
    taus, w = tr.mode_taus, tr.weights

    def kernel_q(tt):
        return (w[None, :] * np.exp(-tt[:, None] / taus[None, :])).sum(1) / tr.norm

    # ``floor``/``A`` come back from fit_kww in magnitude space, so ``I`` must be passed in
    # the same convention (callers pass ``np.abs(I)``); a signed negative-bias trace scored
    # here would fail on the sign alone, not on the kinetics.
    def score(tt, II):
        pred = floor + A * (kernel_q(tt) if pol == "decay" else (1.0 - kernel_q(tt)))
        ss = np.sum((II - II.mean()) ** 2)
        r2 = float(1.0 - np.sum((II - pred) ** 2) / ss) if ss > 0 else float("nan")
        rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((II - pred) ** 2)))
        return r2, (rmse / abs(A) if A else float("nan"))

    r2_in_k, rmse_in = score(t[:n], I[:n])
    r2_out_k, rmse_out = score(t[n:], I[n:])
    # Rmse/A is reported beside R^2 because R^2 on an almost-flat held-out tail measures how
    # much decay is left, not how accurate the prediction is (see the docstring).
    return dict(tau=tau, beta=beta, r2_kww_in=r2_in, r2_kernel_in=r2_in_k,
                r2_kernel_out=r2_out_k, rmse_over_A_in=rmse_in, rmse_over_A_out=rmse_out,
                qc=ok, reasons=why, polarity=pol, n_in=n, n_out=len(t) - n)


# ==========================================================================
# Reference profile
# ==========================================================================
#: The measured ITO relaxation this module builds on.
#:
#: The cohort.  Nine near-zero-bias runs from one session (06-30-2026; runs 545-551, 553, 555),
#: one pad, one protocol.  Windows **223.5-228.5 s** at tau ~ 16 s, so window/tau ~ 14, and
#: ``R^2`` 0.9869-0.9966.  The SDs recorded below are within-session repeat scatter at n=9, not
#: device-to-device spread: there is one coherent replicate block, so between-block variance is
#: not estimable from this corpus.
#:
#: The gates.  :func:`fit_kww` applies physical QC -- ``beta <= 1``, ``floor >= 0``,
#: ``window >= 2 tau`` -- and appends ``r2 < 0.80`` to the same reasons tuple, so a "62 of 124"
#: pass rate is the compound gate and "78 of 124" the physics alone.  Of 124 traces, 123 return
#: parameters and 103 yield a finite ``R^2``; the 20 non-finite ones are current-stress files in
#: which the current is the forced quantity, so its variance is zero and ``R^2`` is undefined by
#: construction rather than failed.  These nine were selected on fit quality (session,
#: span > 150 s, ``R^2 > 0.95``), which is not predictive validation.
#:
#: Window dependence.  ``tau_kww`` is window-dependent -- **16.03 s** fitted over 226 s against
#: **9.49 s** over 30 s -- so it is only comparable between traces at a matched window.  ``beta``
#: is the magnitude-invariant parameter: across the nine the fitted amplitude drifts **1.867x**
#: monotonically while the elasticity ``d ln y / d ln A`` is **+0.0127 [-0.088, +0.114]** for
#: ``beta`` and **+0.0839 [-0.156, +0.324]** for ``tau``, i.e. the exponent is well determined
#: and the time constant is not.
#:
#: Interpretation limits.
#:   * The floor is not identifiable from half a trace.  With it free, 1 of 124 traces survives
#:     corpus-wide and 0 of 34 in the near-zero regime; a floor estimated from the first half is
#:     biased **+65% to +94%**, because the model is still 3.3-4.1% of ``A`` above a floor worth
#:     4.9-5.8% of ``A`` at the split.  Quote the kinetics as validated GIVEN an independently
#:     measured settled current.
#:   * On an almost-flat tail ``R^2`` ranks traces by how much decay is left, not by accuracy,
#:     which is why :func:`holdout_validate` also returns ``rmse_over_A_out``: all nine predict
#:     the held-out half to within measurement noise (out-of-sample **0.78-2.49%** of ``A``
#:     against an in-sample residual of 0.97-1.98%).  Report both.
#:   * No ``tau(V)`` law is supported.  The held-bias ladder is from Jan 2025 and every
#:     near-zero trace from mid-2026, so bias regime is collinear with session and any
#:     difference cannot be attributed to field rather than to ageing; no law fits the ladder
#:     anyway (best ``R^2`` 0.43 for a power law, 0.28 for Poole-Frenkel ``sqrt(V)``).
ITO_REFERENCE = dict(
    # The SDs below are within-session repeat scatter (n=9, one pad, one protocol, one
    # session), not a device-to-device or between-session uncertainty -- see the cv paragraph
    # above: random 9-draws from the near-zero pool give a median tau cv of 43.7%.
    tau_kww=16.033, tau_sd=0.938,          # s   (CV 5.85%; window-dependent: 13.05 s at 60 s)
    beta=0.6225, beta_sd=0.0148,           #     (CV 2.38%; the magnitude-invariant parameter)
    rho=0.0531, rho_sd=0.0032,             #     Floor/(A+floor) -- a separate settled-current
                                           #     Measurement; not identifiable from a half-fit
    mean_lifetime=23.031, mean_lifetime_sd=0.842,   # s -- (tau/beta)*Gamma(1/beta)
    v_read=1e-3, n_runs=9, window_s=226.0,          # Windows 223.5-228.5 s
    window_over_tau=14.1,
    session="06-30-2026", r2_range=(0.9869, 0.9966),
    runs=(545, 546, 547, 548, 549, 550, 551, 553, 555),   # 552 does not exist; 554 R^2=0.8812
)


def ito_reference_profile(k_gate=2.0):
    """The nine-replicate near-zero-bias profile -- one session, one pad, one protocol.

    Prefer this over any single trace, but not because it was predictively validated: it was
    selected on fit quality (session, span > 150 s, ``R^2 > 0.95``), and only 5 of the 9 pass
    :func:`holdout_validate` -- itself an R^2 artefact, since all nine predict the held-out
    half to within measurement noise (out-of-sample rmse/A 0.78-2.49%).  Read the
    :data:`ITO_REFERENCE` provenance comment before quoting any of these numbers, in
    particular that ``tau_kww`` is window-dependent (16.03 s at 226 s, 9.49 s at 30 s) while
    ``beta`` is the magnitude-invariant one.  ``beta = 0.6225`` supersedes the ``0.569`` in
    ``models.py``'s docstring, which came from a field law the ladder does not support.
    """
    r = ITO_REFERENCE
    return TransientProfile(
        tau_kww=r["tau_kww"], beta=r["beta"],
        amplitude=1.0 - r["rho"], floor=r["rho"],   # Normalised: A + I_0 = 1
        v_read=r["v_read"], polarity="decay",
        r2=float(np.mean(r["r2_range"])), n_samples=0, window_s=r["window_s"],
        source=f"ITO_REFERENCE n={r['n_runs']} {r['session']}",
        bias_regime="near_zero", qc_pass=True, qc_reasons=(),
    )


# ============================================================================
# The convolutional volatile synapse
# ============================================================================
# Volatile relaxation on a convolutional memristive layer.
#
# :class:`~mnn_torch.volatile.VolatileSynapse` wraps a dense crossbar. This is the same physics
# on :class:`~mnn_torch.devices.MemristiveConv2d`, which is what an all-layer volatile network
# needs and what the reported single-layer study deliberately never used.
#
# The algebra that makes it cheap. The trapped-charge state is indexed by crossbar row, not by
# crosspoint: the dense equation is
# :math:`I_{ij}(t) = I_\mathrm{static}(V_i, G_{ij}) + A(V_i, G_{ij})\,q_i(t)`, with ``q`` carrying
# only ``i``. Both devices of a pos/neg pair therefore see the same factor, so it survives the
# differential subtraction as a per-row scalar:
#
# .. math::
#     \frac{I^{+}_{io}(1 + g q_i) - I^{-}_{io}(1 + g q_i)}{k_I} = (1 + g q_i)\,W^\mathrm{eff}_{io}
#
# That is why no per-crosspoint or per-position state is required. The state is ``(B, K, k)`` with
# ``K = C_in \cdot k_h \cdot k_w`` unrolled kernel rows, exactly analogous to the dense
# ``(B, n_in+1, k)``, and it is shared across all output positions because one physical crossbar
# computes every position.
#
# Why the write drive is a mean over positions, not a sum. A convolution reuses one crossbar for
# every output position. The frame period ``dt`` is fixed, so ``L`` positions share it and each
# receives ``dt/L`` of drive time. Injected charge per position is therefore proportional to
# ``(dt/L) x``, and the total over the frame to ``dt \cdot \mathrm{mean}_\ell(x)``. Summing instead
# would model ``L`` independent crossbars each given the full frame, which is not the hardware
# being simulated, and would scale the injected charge by ``L`` -- 225x at conv1 -- saturating the
# trace on the first frame. ``aggregate="sum"`` is available for that alternative reading and is
# not the default.
#
# NO bias row. The dense layer carries bias as crossbar row ``n_in+1`` and can gate it physically;
# ``MemristiveConv2d`` adds its bias digitally after the array, so there is no row to gate and no
# row to relax. ``SpikingCell`` already zeroes and freezes every memristive bias, which is what
# keeps "array output under zero input is exactly zero" true on this path too. The state therefore
# has ``K`` rows and not ``K+1``, and :meth:`n_rows` says so.
#
# Two paths, and the fast one is the one the network actually takes. When the input carries at
# most one distinct non-zero value ``v``, Poole-Frenkel takes only two values, ``PF(0) = 0`` and
# ``PF(k_V v)``, so it can be evaluated once on the conductance grid and reduced to a matrix that
# depends on neither batch nor output position:
#
# .. math::
#     W^\mathrm{eff}_{io} = \frac{I^{+}_{io} - I^{-}_{io}}{k_I}, \qquad
#     \mathrm{out}_{bo\ell} = \sum_i \mathrm{drive}_{bi\ell}\, f_{bi}\, W^\mathrm{eff}_{io}
#
# With ``f = 1 + g q`` the per-row factor. This is exact, not an approximation, and it is only
# possible because ``q`` is row-indexed and so factors out of the differential pair. It drops the
# Poole-Frenkel evaluation count from ``B L K 2C_out`` to ``K 2C_out``, a factor of ``B L`` --
# 14,400 at conv1 scale.
#
# Both convolutional layers of the reported network qualify: conv1 is fed encoded event frames,
# and the encoding maps a binary event cache onto ``{0, 1.25}`` exactly, while conv2 is fed LIF
# Spike output on ``{0, 1}``. The general per-element path is kept for continuous input, where the
# map genuinely depends on each patch value, and the two are asserted equal on one-valued input --
# That equivalence is the only thing standing between the fast path and a silently different
# Convolution.

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from .devices import single_nonzero_value


class ConvVolatileSynapse:
    """Wraps a :class:`MemristiveConv2d` so each unrolled kernel row carries a relaxation.

    Mirrors :class:`~mnn_torch.volatile.VolatileSynapse`'s interface: explicit state,
    ``out, z = syn(x, z, phase=...)``, ``z = syn.hold(z, seconds)``, and nothing stored on the
    object, so batched sequences cannot contaminate one another.
    """

    def __init__(self, base_layer, profile, k=12, dt=1.0, rho=None, polarity=None,
                 span_decades=(-1.5, 1.15), tmax_tau=21.0, aggregate="mean"):
        self.base = base_layer
        self.profile = profile
        self.trace = KohlrauschTrace(profile.tau_kww, profile.beta, k=k, dt=dt,
                                     span_decades=span_decades, tmax_tau=tmax_tau)
        r = profile.rho if rho is None else float(rho)
        if not (0.0 < r < 1.0):
            raise ValueError(f"rho must be in (0,1) to set A from eq:floorrate; got {r}")
        self.rho = r
        self.gain = (1.0 - r) / r
        self.polarity = polarity or profile.polarity
        self.k = int(k)
        if aggregate not in ("mean", "sum"):
            raise ValueError(f"aggregate must be 'mean' or 'sum', got {aggregate!r}")
        self.aggregate = aggregate

    # -- state ------------------------------------------------------------
    def n_rows(self):
        """``C_in * k_h * k_w`` unrolled rows. NO bias row: see the module docstring."""
        # MemristiveConv2d follows the nn.Conv2d name ``weight``; the dense layer uses
        # ``weights``. Mixing them up is silent until a shape check fires.
        w = self.base.weight
        return int(w.shape[1] * w.shape[2] * w.shape[3])

    def init_state(self, batch, device=None, dtype=None):
        return torch.zeros(int(batch), self.n_rows(), self.k,
                           device=device, dtype=dtype or torch.float32)

    def hold(self, z, duration):
        """Advance ``duration`` seconds with NO drive, exactly as the dense synapse does."""
        n = max(int(round(duration / self.trace.dt)), 0)
        d = torch.as_tensor(self.trace.decays, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        return z * torch.pow(d, n)

    def read_trace(self, z):
        w = torch.as_tensor(self.trace.weights, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        return (z * w).sum(-1) / self.trace.norm

    # -- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _patches(self, x):
        """``(B, K, L)`` unfolded input patches -- the voltage each row sees per position."""
        return F.unfold(x, kernel_size=self.base.kernel_size,
                        stride=self.base.stride, padding=self.base.padding)

    def _row_drive(self, patches):
        """``(B, K)`` drive per row, aggregated over output positions."""
        return patches.mean(-1) if self.aggregate == "mean" else patches.sum(-1)

    def out_hw(self, x):
        kh, kw = self.base.kernel_size
        sh, sw = self.base.stride
        ph, pw = self.base.padding
        return ((x.shape[2] + 2 * ph - kh) // sh + 1,
                (x.shape[3] + 2 * pw - kw) // sw + 1)

    # -- forward ----------------------------------------------------------
    def __call__(self, x, z, phase="read", drive=None, compute_out=True, no_write=False):
        """``(out, z)`` with ``out`` shaped ``(B, C_out, H_out, W_out)``.

        ``compute_out=False`` returns ``(None, z)`` and skips the conductance grid and the
        Poole-Frenkel map entirely. That is exact and not an approximation: ``z <- z*dec + u``
        contains no weights, so a write step whose output is discarded contributes nothing to
        any gradient -- the same property that makes a long write phase affordable on the dense
        path.
        """
        patches = self._patches(x)                                  # (B, K, L)
        u = self._row_drive(patches) if drive is None else drive
        if phase == "hold":
            u = torch.zeros_like(u)
        if no_write:
            # Global non-writing read. The sense voltage still comes from the propagated
            # input, so the layer reports what its state does to that input, but nothing is
            # injected: the state only decays. This is the separation the model already
            # assumes between sensing voltage and state-writing drive, and it is what makes a
            # read non-disturbing on the dense path too.
            #
            # Expressed as a flag, not a zero tensor the caller builds. Passing drive=zeros
            # requires knowing the state's row count, and sizing it from the probe instead of
            # from the state is a real bug this project already shipped once.
            u = torch.zeros(z.shape[0], z.shape[1], device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        dec = torch.as_tensor(self.trace.decays, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        z = z * dec + u.unsqueeze(-1).to(z.dtype)
        if not compute_out:
            return None, z

        q = self.read_trace(z)                                      # (B, K)
        trace_term = q if self.polarity == "decay" else (1.0 - q)
        factor = (1.0 + self.gain * trace_term)                     # (B, K)

        G, k_I, c, d_epsilon = self.base._grid_and_params(x.device)

        # -- fast path: one PF evaluation, then a pre-computed (K, C_out) matrix ----------
        # The guard mirrors MemristiveConv2d's own: for v != 1 the drive becomes a 0/1 mask,
        # which carries no gradient in x, so that branch is only safe when none is needed.
        v, one_valued = single_nonzero_value(x)
        unit_drive = v is None or bool(v == 1)
        if one_valued and (unit_drive or not x.requires_grad):
            K = self.n_rows()
            Cout = self.base.out_channels
            drive_p = patches if unit_drive else (patches != 0).to(patches.dtype)
            k_V_full = torch.full((1, 1, K, 2 * Cout), self.base.k_V,
                                  device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
            if not unit_drive:
                k_V_full = k_V_full * v
            if c is None:
                I_on = (k_V_full * G[None, None, :, :]).reshape(K, 2 * Cout)
            else:
                from .devices import compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch
                I_on = compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch(
                    k_V_full, c, d_epsilon).reshape(K, 2 * Cout)
            W_eff = (I_on[:, 0::2] - I_on[:, 1::2]) / k_I           # (K, C_out)
            scaled = drive_p * factor.unsqueeze(-1).to(drive_p.dtype)   # (B, K, L)
            y_cols = torch.einsum("bkl,ko->blo", scaled, W_eff.to(scaled.dtype))
            oh, ow = self.out_hw(x)
            out = y_cols.permute(0, 2, 1).reshape(x.shape[0], Cout, oh, ow)
            return out + self.base.bias.view(1, -1, 1, 1), z
        V = self.base.k_V * patches                                 # (B, K, L)
        # (B, L, K, 1) matches MemristiveConv2d._current_tile's own tile layout
        V_tile = V.permute(0, 2, 1).unsqueeze(-1)
        if c is None:
            I_ind = V_tile * G[None, None, :, :]
        else:
            from .devices import compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch
            I_ind = compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch(V_tile, c, d_epsilon)
        # Per-row differential contribution, before the Kirchhoff sum, so the row-indexed
        # trace can be applied to it. _current_tile sums over rows first, which would make
        # the per-row factor inapplicable.
        r_row = (I_ind[..., 0::2] - I_ind[..., 1::2]) / k_I          # (B, L, K, C_out)
        r_row = r_row * factor[:, None, :, None].to(r_row.dtype)
        y_cols = r_row.sum(dim=2)                                   # (B, L, C_out)

        oh, ow = self.out_hw(x)
        out = y_cols.permute(0, 2, 1).reshape(x.shape[0], self.base.out_channels, oh, ow)
        return out + self.base.bias.view(1, -1, 1, 1), z


def cost_note(base_layer, x_shape):
    """What the general path costs against the fast path it declines to use.

    Returned rather than printed, so a caller can record it instead of a reader having to
    trust a comment.
    """
    kh, kw = base_layer.kernel_size
    K = base_layer.weight.shape[1] * kh * kw
    ph, pw = base_layer.padding
    sh, sw = base_layer.stride
    oh = (x_shape[2] + 2 * ph - kh) // sh + 1
    ow = (x_shape[3] + 2 * pw - kw) // sw + 1
    L = oh * ow
    return {"K": int(K), "L": int(L), "out_channels": int(base_layer.out_channels),
            "pf_evaluations_general": int(x_shape[0] * L * K * 2 * base_layer.out_channels),
            "pf_evaluations_fast_path": int(K * 2 * base_layer.out_channels),
            "ratio": float(x_shape[0] * L)}
\end{Verbatim}
\section{Training and experiment drivers}
\label{sec:drivers}
\subsection{tools/all\_volatile\_cohort.py}
\index{tools/all\_volatile\_cohort.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""An all-layer volatile TemporalMCSNN, for the feasibility cohort.

What this is for, and what it cannot support. The substitution experiment makes exactly one layer
volatile, so that substituting the decay profile can be attributed to the profile. This cell makes
every memristive layer volatile and trains from initialisation with the measured KWW dynamics
active. It therefore answers a different question -- whether such a network is trainable at all,
and whether the delayed decision draws on state at more than one depth -- and it cannot support a
KWW-versus-exponential shape attribution, because its weights are KWW-adapted. That attribution
stays with the substitution experiment.

Read mode: global non-writing read. Probing is input-only. Activity propagates normally, each
layer senses its own propagated input, and every volatile layer receives zero drive, so states
decay but are never recharged. That is the separation the model already assumes between sensing
voltage and state-writing drive, and it is the same mechanism the single-layer read uses; if it
were not physically available, the single-layer non-disturbing probe would need the same
qualification. No mid-network probe is injected, because none can be.

The write phase cannot skip its output here, and that is the dominant cost. With one volatile
layer, ``compute_out=False`` makes a write free: the state update carries no weights, so a
discarded output contributes nothing. With every layer volatile, conv1's output is conv2's input,
so each of the T write frames is a full forward pass through all three volatile layers. The cell
reports that cost rather than leaving it to be discovered.

Attribution is by snapshot and restore. Every layer's end-of-hold state is captured, and restored
before each intervention, so conditions are independent rather than cumulative. Clearing a layer
individually tests its necessity; preserving one while clearing the others tests its sufficiency.
"Distributed" requires at least two layers to show a causal contribution -- one layer carrying
everything is single-site retention with volatile hardware attached elsewhere.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import torch

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))

import netbench as NB                                    # Noqa: E402
import profile_matched as PM                             # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.volatile import ConvVolatileSynapse        # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.volatile import VolatileSynapse             # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.networks import MemristiveConv2d                      # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.devices import single_nonzero_value                   # Noqa: E402



# ===========================================================================
# Per-layer calibration
# ===========================================================================
def _stats(t):
    """Per-unit mean and spread of a pre-LIF tensor, flattened over batch and space."""
    flat = t.detach().transpose(0, 1).reshape(t.shape[1], -1) if t.dim() > 2 else \
        t.detach().transpose(0, 1)
    return flat.mean(1), flat.std(1).clamp_min(1e-8)


class LayerCalibrationMixin:
    #: target fraction of units above threshold after calibration
    CAL_FIRE = 0.15

    """A frozen, label-free affine per volatile layer, so its output reaches the next LIF in range.

    Why this is needed at all, and why the reported study does not need it. The trace multiplies
    each device's current by ``1 + gain*q`` with ``gain = (1-rho)/rho = 17.83`` from the measured
    floor ratio, and ``q`` exceeds 1 because it accumulates across the write frames. measured on
    the all-layer convolutional network: conv1 applies a mean factor of 30, conv2 of 111, fc1 of
    36. The reported study puts its one volatile layer directly in front of a calibrated reader
    (``mu``, ``A``, ``C`` and a shared scale) which absorbs exactly this, but there is no
    equivalent between layers -- so conv2's output arrives about 111x off-scale and the next LIF
    saturates. Measured consequence: the all-layer convolutional network sits at 9.67% against a
    10% chance rate, flat from epoch 0, i.e. dead before optimisation starts.

    What is fitted, and why it is label-free. For each volatile layer, the pre-LIF output is
    measured twice on the same unlabelled inputs: once with the trace suppressed (``gain = 0``,
    which is exactly the ordinary non-volatile layer) and once with it active. The affine that
    maps the second onto the first's per-unit mean and spread is stored and frozen. No labels are
    used and no target accuracy is involved; the reference is the network's own non-volatile
    statistics.

    It is fitted before training, which differs from the reported order. There, calibration comes
    after training because the weights are mapped in already trained. Here training happens with
    the kernel active, so a network that cannot pass signal cannot be trained at all: calibration
    has to precede it. The weights then move under a fixed calibration, which is a real
    limitation and is reported as one rather than hidden.
    """

    def calibrate_sequential(self, xs, tag=""):
        """Fit layer by layer, freezing each before the next is measured, on the probe path.

        Why sequentially. Calibrating conv1 changes what conv2 receives, so a joint fit would
        measure conv2 against an input that no longer exists once conv1 is corrected. Each layer
        is therefore fitted with ``self.cal`` already set for the layers upstream of it.

        Why on the probe path. The delayed decision is read through the uniform probe with a
        non-writing read, not through the write frames. Fitting on the write phase calibrates the
        wrong distribution -- measured symptom: 75% of conv1 units firing on every probe tick, a
        saturated and spatially constant code.

        The target for each layer is its own output with the trace suppressed, given upstream
        already corrected -- i.e. the ordinary non-volatile layer in the network it now sits in.
        Label-free throughout.
        """
        # The target is not the non-volatile layer. On the probe path, suppressing the trace
        # leaves a uniform input driving a fixed layer, so its output is identical for every
        # sample -- zero sample variance, which is exactly the probe-only control being at
        # Chance. Matching that reference is therefore degenerate: measured spread ratios of
        # 3.7e9, and a transform that collapsed every unit onto a constant.
        #
        # The target is instead the one the reported reader uses: standardise per unit, then
        # place the firing fraction. A LIF fed a standardised signal fires when it crosses
        # threshold, so the offset is chosen from the empirical quantile to put a stated
        # fraction of units above it. Label-free, and it targets the thing that was actually
        # broken -- 75% of conv1 units firing on every tick.
        n = len(self.synapses)
        self.cal = [None] * n
        report = []
        for i in range(n):
            ma, sa = self._probe_prelif(xs, i)
            thr = float(getattr(self.net.lif1, "threshold", 1.0))
            raw = self._probe_prelif_raw(xs, i)                  # Standardised sample
            zstd = ((raw - ma.view(self._bshape(raw, ma))) /
                    sa.view(self._bshape(raw, sa))).flatten()
            q = torch.quantile(zstd, 1.0 - self.CAL_FIRE)
            b = thr - float(q)
            st = torch.ones_like(sa)
            mt = torch.full_like(ma, b)
            self.cal[i] = (ma, sa, st, mt)
            report.append({"layer": self.LAYERS[i], "offset": b,
                           "raw_spread": float(sa.mean())})
        return report

    def calibrate_layers(self, xs):
        gains = [s.gain for s in self.synapses]
        for s in self.synapses:
            s.gain = 0.0
        target = self._collect_prelif(xs)          # The ordinary, non-volatile statistics
        for s, g in zip(self.synapses, gains):
            s.gain = g
        actual = self._collect_prelif(xs)          # What the volatile layers actually emit
        self.cal = [(ma, sa, st, mt) for (mt, st), (ma, sa) in zip(target, actual)]
        return [{"layer": n, "gain_seen": float((sa / st).mean())}
                for n, (ma, sa, st, mt) in zip(self.LAYERS, self.cal)]

    @staticmethod
    def _bshape(h, v):
        return [1, -1] + [1] * (h.dim() - 2)

    def _apply_cal(self, h, i):
        cal = getattr(self, "cal", None)
        if not cal or i >= len(cal) or cal[i] is None:
            return h
        ma, sa, st, mt = cal[i]
        shape = [1, -1] + [1] * (h.dim() - 2)
        return (h - ma.view(shape)) / sa.view(shape) * st.view(shape) + mt.view(shape)


class AllVolatileMCSNN(LayerCalibrationMixin, PM.OutputVolatileCell):
    """Conv1, conv2 and fc1 all volatile; three explicit states threaded through the network."""

    LAYERS = ("conv1", "conv2", "fc1")

    def __init__(self, arm, n_in, ncls, a, seed, **kw):
        # ``nat`` and ``delays`` are keywords on SpikingCell; the sixth positional slot is
        # ``gain_override``. Passing nat positionally silently set the gain to a tuple.
        super().__init__(arm, n_in, ncls, a, seed, **kw)
        net = self.net
        for name in ("conv1", "conv2"):
            m = getattr(net, name)
            if not isinstance(m, MemristiveConv2d):
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"{name} is {type(m).__name__}, not MemristiveConv2d -- this cell needs a "
                    f"config WITHOUT conv_ideal, or there is nothing to make volatile")
        prof = self.vs.profile
        mk = dict(k=self.vs.k, dt=self.vs.trace.dt, rho=self.vs.rho,
                  polarity=self.vs.polarity,
                  span_decades=tuple(self.args.span),
                  tmax_tau=self.vs.trace.tmax_tau if hasattr(self.vs.trace, "tmax_tau") else 21.0)
        self.cvs1 = ConvVolatileSynapse(net.conv1, prof, **mk)
        self.cvs2 = ConvVolatileSynapse(net.conv2, prof, **mk)
        self.synapses = (self.cvs1, self.cvs2, self.vs)
        self.write_forwards = 0            # Measured cost, not asserted

    # -- state -------------------------------------------------------------
    def init_states(self, B):
        return [s.init_state(B) for s in self.synapses]

    def hold_all(self, zs, seconds):
        return [s.hold(z, seconds) for s, z in zip(self.synapses, zs)]

    def snapshot(self, zs):
        """Detached clones, so an intervention cannot write back into the snapshot."""
        return [z.detach().clone() for z in zs]

    def restore(self, snap):
        return [z.clone() for z in snap]

    def clear(self, zs, which=None):
        """Zero the named layers' states. ``which=None`` clears all of them."""
        names = set(self.LAYERS if which is None else which)
        return [torch.zeros_like(z) if n in names else z
                for n, z in zip(self.LAYERS, zs)]

    def preserve_only(self, zs, name):
        """Keep one layer's state, clear the others -- the sufficiency condition."""
        return self.clear(zs, which=[n for n in self.LAYERS if n != name])

    # -- forward -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _propagate(self, x_frame, zs, *, no_write):
        """One pass: conv1 -> lif1 -> conv2 -> lif2 -> fc1, carrying all three states."""
        net = self.net
        z1, z2, z3 = zs
        # Pool before the LIF, matching TemporalMCSNN.forward:
        #   Cur = F.max_pool2d(conv(x), pool); spk, mem = lif(cur, mem)
        # pooling after the LIF instead computes a different network, and nothing downstream
        # would have complained.
        F = torch.nn.functional
        pool = net.max_pooling
        h1, z1 = self.cvs1(x_frame, z1, phase="read", no_write=no_write)
        s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), pool), self._m1)
        h2, z2 = self.cvs2(s1, z2, phase="read", no_write=no_write)
        s2, self._m2 = net.lif2(F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h2, 1), pool), self._m2)
        s2 = s2.flatten(1)
        out, z3 = self.vs(s2, z3, phase="read" if no_write else "write",
                          gate_bias_row=self.args.gate,
                          drive=(torch.zeros(z3.shape[0], z3.shape[1],
                                             device=z3.device, dtype=z3.dtype)
                                 if no_write else None))
        return self._apply_cal(out, 2), [z1, z2, z3]

    def state_after_write(self, xs):
        """Stream the sample. Every frame is a full forward, because each layer feeds the next."""
        B = xs.shape[1]
        zs = self.init_states(B)
        self._m1 = self.net.lif1.init_leaky()
        self._m2 = self.net.lif2.init_leaky()
        for t in range(xs.shape[0]):
            _, zs = self._propagate(xs[t], zs, no_write=False)
            self.write_forwards += 1
        return zs

    def reads(self, zs, steps=None):
        """``R`` non-writing reads. Neuronal membranes are re-initialised, as on the dense path."""
        R = steps or self.R
        self._m1 = self.net.lif1.init_leaky()
        self._m2 = self.net.lif2.init_leaky()
        probe = torch.full_like(self._probe_like, self.v_probe) if False else None
        outs = []
        for _ in range(R):
            out, zs = self._propagate(self._probe_for(zs[0].shape[0]), zs, no_write=True)
            outs.append(out)
        return outs, zs


class AllVolatileMSNN(LayerCalibrationMixin, PM.OutputVolatileCell):
    """Fc1 and fc2 both volatile; two explicit states threaded through the dense network.

    The cost inverts relative to the reported cohort. There, MSNN was the cheap architecture
    because its single volatile layer is ``fc2`` at 64->10. Making ``fc1`` volatile too puts a
    579x128 Poole-Frenkel map in the read path -- the largest layer in either network -- so
    all-layer MSNN is expected to cost more than all-layer MCSNN, whose conv layers reduce to
    small pre-computed matrices. Measured, not assumed: see :func:`epoch_cost`.

    No change is made to ``VolatileSynapse``. The non-writing read is obtained by passing a zero
    drive sized from the state, which is what the reported cell already does. Adding a flag to
    the dense synapse would mean editing the module every reported number depends on, for a
    feasibility-only cohort.
    """

    LAYERS = ("fc1", "fc2")

    def __init__(self, arm, n_in, ncls, a, seed, **kw):
        super().__init__(arm, n_in, ncls, a, seed, **kw)
        if self.kind != "dense":
            raise AssertionError(f"AllVolatileMSNN needs the dense path, got kind={self.kind!r}")
        net = self.net
        prof = self.vs.profile
        # vs2 IS the inherited output synapse on fc2; only fc1 needs wrapping.
        self.vs1 = VolatileSynapse(net.fc1, prof, k=self.vs.k, dt=self.vs.trace.dt,
                                      rho=self.vs.rho, polarity=self.vs.polarity,
                                      span_decades=tuple(self.args.span),
                                      tmax_tau=getattr(self.vs.trace, "tmax_tau", 21.0))
        self.synapses = (self.vs1, self.vs)
        self.write_forwards = 0

    # -- state -------------------------------------------------------------
    def init_states(self, B):
        return [s.init_state(B) for s in self.synapses]

    def hold_all(self, zs, seconds):
        return [s.hold(z, seconds) for s, z in zip(self.synapses, zs)]

    def snapshot(self, zs):
        return [z.detach().clone() for z in zs]

    def restore(self, snap):
        return [z.clone() for z in snap]

    def clear(self, zs, which=None):
        names = set(self.LAYERS if which is None else which)
        return [torch.zeros_like(z) if n in names else z for n, z in zip(self.LAYERS, zs)]

    def preserve_only(self, zs, name):
        return self.clear(zs, which=[n for n in self.LAYERS if n != name])

    # -- forward -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _dense_read(self, syn, x, z, *, no_write):
        """A dense volatile read using a pre-computed (rows, n_out) matrix.

        Same algebra as the conv case: ``q`` is row-indexed, so it factors out of the pos/neg
        subtraction as a per-row scalar and the Poole-Frenkel map can be evaluated once at the
        single drive voltage instead of once per (sample, synapse) element. On ``fc1`` that is a
        (B, 579, 128) map replaced by a (579, 128) one -- 64x fewer evaluations at B=64, which
        is what makes all-layer MSNN affordable at all.

        Falls through to the shipped synapse whenever the input is not single-valued, so this is
        an accelerator for the case the network is actually in, never a substitute for the model.
        """
        v, one_valued = single_nonzero_value(x)
        if not one_valued or (v is not None and x.requires_grad and not bool(v == 1)):
            return syn(x, z, phase="read" if no_write else "write",
                       gate_bias_row=self.args.gate,
                       drive=self._zero_drive(z) if no_write else None)
        ones = torch.ones(x.shape[0], 1, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        bias_col = torch.zeros_like(ones) if self.args.gate else ones
        xin = torch.cat([x, bias_col], dim=1)                       # (B, rows)
        u = self._zero_drive(z) if no_write else xin
        dec = torch.as_tensor(syn.trace.decays, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        z = z * dec + u.unsqueeze(-1).to(z.dtype)
        q = syn.read_trace(z)
        term = q if syn.polarity == "decay" else (1.0 - q)
        factor = 1.0 + syn.gain * term                              # (B, rows)

        G, k_I, c, d_epsilon = syn.base._grid_and_params(x.device)
        rows = z.shape[1]
        cols = G.shape[1]
        vv = 1.0 if v is None else float(v)
        Vone = torch.full((rows, cols), syn.base.k_V * vv, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        if c is None:
            I_on = Vone * G
        else:
            from mnn_torch.devices import compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch
            I_on = compute_PooleFrenkel_current_torch(Vone, c, d_epsilon)
        # c is (1, rows, cols), so the PF call returns a leading singleton dim; slicing before
        # collapsing it slices the row axis instead of the pos/neg column pairs.
        I_on = I_on.reshape(rows, cols)
        W_eff = (I_on[:, 0::2] - I_on[:, 1::2]) / k_I                # (rows, n_out)
        drive_x = xin if (v is None or bool(v == 1)) else (xin != 0).to(xin.dtype)
        out = (drive_x * factor.to(drive_x.dtype)) @ W_eff.to(drive_x.dtype)
        return out, z

    @staticmethod
    def _zero_drive(z):
        """Sized from the state, never from the input: that mismatch is a shipped bug here."""
        return torch.zeros(z.shape[0], z.shape[1], device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)

    def _propagate(self, x_frame, zs, *, no_write):
        """Fc1 -> lif1 -> fc2, matching TemporalMSNN.forward (no pooling on this path)."""
        net = self.net
        z1, z2 = zs
        h1, z1 = self._dense_read(self.vs1, x_frame, z1, no_write=no_write)
        s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), self._m1)
        out, z2 = self._dense_read(self.vs, s1, z2, no_write=no_write)
        return self._apply_cal(out, 1), [z1, z2]

    def state_after_write(self, xs):
        B = xs.shape[1]
        zs = self.init_states(B)
        self._m1 = self.net.lif1.init_leaky()
        for t in range(xs.shape[0]):
            _, zs = self._propagate(xs[t], zs, no_write=False)
            self.write_forwards += 1
        return zs

    def reads(self, zs, steps=None):
        R = steps or self.R
        self._m1 = self.net.lif1.init_leaky()
        outs = []
        for _ in range(R):
            out, zs = self._propagate(self._probe_for(zs[0].shape[0]), zs, no_write=True)
            outs.append(out)
        return outs, zs




# ===========================================================================
# The final spiking readout
# ===========================================================================
class SpikingReadoutMixin:
    """Integer spike counts over the probe ticks, ties resolved on the final membrane.

    Why this replaces mean-then-argmax. The development runs averaged the twelve raw read
    currents and took an argmax. That is neither this readout nor a spiking one,
    so its accuracies are not comparable to anything and -- more importantly -- calibration fitted
    against it targets the wrong signal. The output LIF is what turns current into a decision, so
    the firing fraction that calibration places has to be measured on this path.

    The tie rule is the reported primary. Maximise the spike count, then among the tied classes
    only take the largest final output-membrane potential. A class losing on count can never win
    on membrane. Deterministic and label-free; no claim is made that the membrane recovers
    sub-threshold information.
    """

    def _out_lif(self):
        """The output LIF.

        Not named ``out_lif``: ``OutputVolatileCell.__init__`` already binds that as an
        attribute holding the module, so a method of the same name is shadowed and calling it
        invokes the LIF with no input. The parent's attribute is preferred when present.
        """
        got = getattr(self, "out_lif", None)
        if isinstance(got, torch.nn.Module):
            return got
        return self.net.lif3 if hasattr(self.net, "lif3") and self.kind != "dense" \
            else self.net.lif2

    def spike_counts(self, outs):
        """``(counts, final_membrane)`` from the calibrated read currents."""
        lif = self._out_lif()
        mem = lif.init_leaky()
        counts = None
        for cur in outs:
            s, mem = lif(cur, mem)
            counts = s if counts is None else counts + s
        return counts, mem

    def classify(self, outs):
        """Predicted class under the primary membrane tie rule."""
        cnt, mem = self.spike_counts(outs)
        best = cnt.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
        tied = cnt >= best                       # ">=" so exact ties are all admitted
        masked = mem.masked_fill(~tied, float("-inf"))
        return masked.argmax(dim=1), cnt, mem

    def set_probe_frame(self, like):
        """Record the per-sample probe shape, not a batch-sized tensor.

        Defined once, on the mixin, so both cells share one definition and a batch-size fix
        cannot reach only one of them: a probe pinned to the batch its cell was created with
        fails on any other. Storing the tensor is the error this avoids. The probe is uniform
        and label-independent, so only its per-sample
        shape and amplitude carry information.
        """
        self._probe_shape = tuple(like.shape[1:])
        self._probe_dtype = like.dtype
        return self._probe_for(like.shape[0])

    def _probe_for(self, batch):
        p = torch.full((int(batch),) + self._probe_shape, self.v_probe,
                       dtype=self._probe_dtype)
        assert p.unique().numel() == 1, "probe frame must be uniform"
        return p

    def output_firing_fraction(self, outs):
        """Fraction of output units spiking per tick -- the diagnostic calibration targets."""
        lif = self._out_lif()
        mem = lif.init_leaky()
        tot = n = 0.0
        for cur in outs:
            s, mem = lif(cur, mem)
            tot += float(s.mean()); n += 1
        return tot / max(n, 1)


for _c in (AllVolatileMCSNN, AllVolatileMSNN):
    _c.__bases__ = (SpikingReadoutMixin,) + _c.__bases__


# ===========================================================================
# The calibration controller
# ===========================================================================
def _layer_firing_mcsnn(self, xs, idx):
    """Firing fraction of the LIF immediately downstream of volatile layer ``idx``.

    Measured on the probe path with the non-writing read, because that is the path the delayed
    decision is read through and therefore the one calibration must place.
    """
    import torch.nn.functional as F
    net = self.net
    zs = self.hold_all(self.state_after_write(xs), PM.MEMORY_DELAY_S)
    self._m1 = net.lif1.init_leaky(); self._m2 = net.lif2.init_leaky()
    m_out = self._out_lif().init_leaky()
    pool = net.max_pooling
    tot = n = 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(self.R):
            z1, z2, z3 = zs
            h1, z1 = self.cvs1(self._probe_for(z1.shape[0]), z1, phase="read", no_write=True)
            s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), pool), self._m1)
            if idx == 0: tot += float(s1.mean()); n += 1
            h2, z2 = self.cvs2(s1, z2, phase="read", no_write=True)
            s2, self._m2 = net.lif2(F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h2, 1), pool), self._m2)
            if idx == 1: tot += float(s2.mean()); n += 1
            o, z3 = self.vs(s2.flatten(1), z3, phase="read", gate_bias_row=self.args.gate,
                            drive=torch.zeros(z3.shape[0], z3.shape[1]))
            so, m_out = self._out_lif()(self._apply_cal(o, 2), m_out)
            if idx == 2: tot += float(so.mean()); n += 1
            zs = [z1, z2, z3]
    return tot / max(n, 1)


def _layer_firing_msnn(self, xs, idx):
    net = self.net
    zs = self.hold_all(self.state_after_write(xs), PM.MEMORY_DELAY_S)
    self._m1 = net.lif1.init_leaky()
    m_out = self._out_lif().init_leaky()
    tot = n = 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(self.R):
            z1, z2 = zs
            h1, z1 = self._dense_read(self.vs1, self._probe_for(z1.shape[0]), z1, no_write=True)
            s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), self._m1)
            if idx == 0: tot += float(s1.mean()); n += 1
            o, z2 = self._dense_read(self.vs, s1, z2, no_write=True)
            so, m_out = self._out_lif()(self._apply_cal(o, 1), m_out)
            if idx == 1: tot += float(so.mean()); n += 1
            zs = [z1, z2]
    return tot / max(n, 1)


AllVolatileMCSNN._layer_firing = _layer_firing_mcsnn
AllVolatileMSNN._layer_firing = _layer_firing_msnn


def calibrate_iterative(self, xs, target=0.15, tol=0.02, max_iter=12, span=8.0, verbose=False):
    """Sequential calibration with the offset found by bisection on measured firing.

    Why iteration is necessary, not defensive. The single static placement used during development
    sets the offset from a quantile of the standardised pre-LIF signal, which would be right for a
    memoryless threshold. The output LIF integrates across twelve probe ticks, so firing is a
    dynamic quantity and the static quantile does not predict it: measured 0.328 and 0.188 against
    a 0.15 target. The offset therefore has to be found by measuring the firing it actually
    produces.

    Why bisection. It is deterministic given fixed inputs, needs no step size, and converges
    monotonically because firing is monotone in the offset -- raising the offset can only add
    spikes. A gradient or secant step would be faster and would depend on the local slope, which
    is exactly the quantity the static placement got wrong.

    Layers are calibrated in order and frozen before the next is measured, so each is placed
    against the upstream it will actually see. Label-free throughout: only firing fractions and
    training-split inputs are used.

    Returns one record per layer with the achieved firing, the iterations used, and whether it
    landed inside tolerance. A layer outside tolerance is not retried and its target is not
    relaxed -- the caller fails that seed.
    """
    n = len(self.synapses)
    self.cal = [None] * n
    records = []
    for i in range(n):
        ma, sa = self._probe_prelif(xs, i)
        st = torch.ones_like(sa)

        def set_offset(b):
            self.cal[i] = (ma, sa, st, torch.full_like(ma, float(b)))
            return self._layer_firing(xs, i)

        lo, hi = -span, span
        f_lo, f_hi = set_offset(lo), set_offset(hi)
        used, f, b = 0, None, 0.0
        if not (f_lo <= target <= f_hi):
            # Target unreachable within the bracket: take the closer end and report it
            b = lo if abs(f_lo - target) < abs(f_hi - target) else hi
            f = set_offset(b)
        else:
            for used in range(1, max_iter + 1):
                b = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
                f = set_offset(b)
                if abs(f - target) <= tol:
                    break
                if f > target:
                    hi = b
                else:
                    lo = b
        set_offset(b)                                   # Freeze the accepted offset
        ok = abs(f - target) <= tol
        records.append({"layer": self.LAYERS[i], "offset": float(b), "firing": float(f),
                        "iterations": int(used), "in_tolerance": bool(ok),
                        "bracket_firing": [float(f_lo), float(f_hi)]})
        if verbose:
            print(f"    {self.LAYERS[i]:6} f={f:.4f} b={b:+.3f} iters={used} ok={ok}", flush=True)
    return records


AllVolatileMCSNN.calibrate_iterative = calibrate_iterative
AllVolatileMSNN.calibrate_iterative = calibrate_iterative


# ===========================================================================
# Pre-lif sampling (restored: an over-greedy edit removed these)
# ===========================================================================
def _collect_prelif_mcsnn(self, xs):
    """Pre-LIF statistics of every volatile layer over the write phase."""
    import torch.nn.functional as F
    net, B = self.net, xs.shape[1]
    zs = self.init_states(B)
    self._m1 = net.lif1.init_leaky(); self._m2 = net.lif2.init_leaky()
    pool = net.max_pooling
    acc = [[], [], []]
    with torch.no_grad():
        for t in range(xs.shape[0]):
            z1, z2, z3 = zs
            h1, z1 = self.cvs1(xs[t], z1, phase="write")
            acc[0].append(h1)
            s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), pool), self._m1)
            h2, z2 = self.cvs2(s1, z2, phase="write")
            acc[1].append(h2)
            s2, self._m2 = net.lif2(F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h2, 1), pool), self._m2)
            o, z3 = self.vs(s2.flatten(1), z3, phase="write", gate_bias_row=self.args.gate)
            acc[2].append(o)
            zs = [z1, z2, z3]
    return [_stats(torch.cat(a, 0)) for a in acc]


def _collect_prelif_msnn(self, xs):
    net, B = self.net, xs.shape[1]
    zs = self.init_states(B)
    self._m1 = net.lif1.init_leaky()
    acc = [[], []]
    with torch.no_grad():
        for t in range(xs.shape[0]):
            z1, z2 = zs
            h1, z1 = self._dense_read(self.vs1, xs[t], z1, no_write=False)
            acc[0].append(h1)
            s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), self._m1)
            o, z2 = self._dense_read(self.vs, s1, z2, no_write=False)
            acc[1].append(o)
            zs = [z1, z2]
    return [_stats(torch.cat(a, 0)) for a in acc]


def _probe_prelif_mcsnn(self, xs, idx):
    """Layer ``idx``'s pre-LIF output over the non-writing probe ticks, upstream calibration on."""
    import torch.nn.functional as F
    net = self.net
    zs = self.hold_all(self.state_after_write(xs), PM.MEMORY_DELAY_S)
    self._m1 = net.lif1.init_leaky(); self._m2 = net.lif2.init_leaky()
    pool = net.max_pooling
    acc = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(self.R):
            z1, z2, z3 = zs
            h1, z1 = self.cvs1(self._probe_for(z1.shape[0]), z1, phase="read", no_write=True)
            c1 = F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), pool)
            if idx == 0: acc.append(c1)
            s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(c1, self._m1)
            h2, z2 = self.cvs2(s1, z2, phase="read", no_write=True)
            c2 = F.max_pool2d(self._apply_cal(h2, 1), pool)
            if idx == 1: acc.append(c2)
            s2, self._m2 = net.lif2(c2, self._m2)
            o, z3 = self.vs(s2.flatten(1), z3, phase="read", gate_bias_row=self.args.gate,
                            drive=torch.zeros(z3.shape[0], z3.shape[1]))
            if idx == 2: acc.append(self._apply_cal(o, 2))
            zs = [z1, z2, z3]
    t = torch.cat(acc, 0)
    if getattr(self, "_raw_capture", None) is not None:
        self._raw_capture.append(t)
    return _stats(t)


def _probe_prelif_msnn(self, xs, idx):
    net = self.net
    zs = self.hold_all(self.state_after_write(xs), PM.MEMORY_DELAY_S)
    self._m1 = net.lif1.init_leaky()
    acc = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(self.R):
            z1, z2 = zs
            h1, z1 = self._dense_read(self.vs1, self._probe_for(z1.shape[0]), z1, no_write=True)
            if idx == 0: acc.append(self._apply_cal(h1, 0))
            s1, self._m1 = net.lif1(self._apply_cal(h1, 0), self._m1)
            o, z2 = self._dense_read(self.vs, s1, z2, no_write=True)
            if idx == 1: acc.append(self._apply_cal(o, 1))
            zs = [z1, z2]
    t = torch.cat(acc, 0)
    if getattr(self, "_raw_capture", None) is not None:
        self._raw_capture.append(t)
    return _stats(t)


def _probe_prelif_raw_generic(self, xs, idx):
    keep, self._raw_capture = getattr(self, "_raw_capture", None), []
    self._probe_prelif(xs, idx)
    out = torch.cat(self._raw_capture, 0) if self._raw_capture else torch.zeros(1, 1)
    self._raw_capture = keep
    return out


AllVolatileMCSNN._collect_prelif = _collect_prelif_mcsnn
AllVolatileMSNN._collect_prelif = _collect_prelif_msnn
AllVolatileMCSNN._probe_prelif = _probe_prelif_mcsnn
AllVolatileMSNN._probe_prelif = _probe_prelif_msnn
AllVolatileMCSNN._probe_prelif_raw = _probe_prelif_raw_generic
AllVolatileMSNN._probe_prelif_raw = _probe_prelif_raw_generic
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/attribution\_sweep.py}
\index{tools/attribution\_sweep.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The delayed sweep and the attribution harness for an all-layer volatile network.

What this measures, and why each piece is here. The feasibility-only claim is that an all-layer
volatile network "uses distributed device state for delayed classification". Four things have to
be shown, and none of them is visible at zero hold:

  1. accuracy remains above chance after a positive input-free hold;
  2. clearing all states removes the performance;
  3. clearing layers individually shows more than one layer contributing;
  4. probe-only returns to chance.

Snapshot at end of hold, restore before every intervention. Conditions must be independent, not
cumulative: clearing conv1 and then clearing conv2 from the already-cleared state would measure
something else entirely. Every condition therefore starts from a restored copy of the same
end-of-hold state, which is also why the snapshot is taken after the hold rather than after the
write.

Necessity and sufficiency are different questions. Clearing one layer while keeping the others
tests whether that layer is necessary. Keeping one while clearing the others tests whether it is
sufficient. A layer can be neither, either, or both, and "distributed" is only earned when at
least two layers show a causal contribution -- one layer carrying everything is single-site
retention with volatile hardware attached elsewhere, and :func:`verdict` says so.

Probe-only is the floor, not a control of convenience. It skips the write entirely and holds a
zero state over the same interval, then applies the identical probe. If it does not sit at chance,
the probe is carrying the answer and nothing else in this file means anything.

The chance bound is the upper one-sided 95% clopper-pearson limit on the majority-class rate of
the test split, not 1/n_classes: a finite split is not perfectly balanced, so the naive rate would
credit a curve that had decayed to guessing the commonest class.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))

import netbench as NB                                    # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch import estimators as A                     # Noqa: E402


def conditions_for(layers):
    """``intact``, ``cleared_all``, one ``cleared_<l>`` and one ``only_<l>`` per layer, ``probe_only``."""
    out = ["intact", "cleared_all"]
    out += [f"cleared_{n}" for n in layers]
    out += [f"only_{n}" for n in layers]
    out += ["probe_only"]
    return out


def _state_for(cell, cond, snap):
    """A fresh state for ``cond``, always restored from the same end-of-hold snapshot."""
    zs = cell.restore(snap)
    if cond == "intact":
        return zs
    if cond == "cleared_all":
        return cell.clear(zs)
    if cond.startswith("cleared_"):
        return cell.clear(zs, which=[cond[len("cleared_"):]])
    if cond.startswith("only_"):
        return cell.preserve_only(zs, cond[len("only_"):])
    raise ValueError(cond)


def _scorers():
    """The declared tie rules, from the one place they are defined.

    ``tie_rules.score_tie_rules`` implements the primary membrane rule, the mandatory uniform
    random-tie expectation and the recorded class-share rule, and returns per-sample scores. Only the
    all-layer attribution path lacked them, so they are imported rather than reimplemented -- a
    second copy of a scoring rule is how the two drift apart.
    """
    import tie_rules
    return tie_rules.score_tie_rules


#: Reported rules. ``membrane`` is the locked primary, ``uniform`` the mandatory sensitivity, and
#: the class-share rule -- a tie earns ``1 / n_classes`` -- is recorded and never interpreted. Its
#: key keeps the archive's spelling, ``legacy_1_over_n``.
RULE_NAMES = ("membrane", "uniform", "legacy_1_over_n")


def sweep(cell, xte, yte, delays, ncls, bs=64, shape=None):
    """``(accs, floor, cp95)`` with ``accs[cond][delay]`` a fraction correct.
