no weights), so no membrane is driven during the stimulus and every LIF state is
initialised to zero after the hold.  Asserted operationally by control C22: permuting
``z`` across the batch permutes the logits identically, so nothing else can be carrying
the sample.

The one frozen quantity, and why it is the only one that matters (trap 1).  Read noise is
injected as a fixed fraction of ``sigma0``, the between-sample signal spread measured once
at D = 0 and never re-derived.  Everything downstream of that injection point -- the
analog level's trainable ``nn.Linear`` weight+bias, and the spiking level's frozen
per-neuron reference current and gain -- multiplies signal and noise identically, so it is
snr-neutral and cannot manufacture retention.  Re-deriving ``sigma0`` per delay is exactly
trap 1 and is what makes retention look unbounded: measured here, a closed-form ridge
probe that standardises its own features scores 32.17% at D = 0, 45 and 128 s, i.e.
identically, because the hold is very nearly a pure scalar multiply.

Arms.  ``kww`` is the measured ITO profile (tau = 16.033 s KWW scale, beta = 0.6225).
``exp_meanlife`` is a single exponential at the matched mean lifetime <t> = 23.031 s and is
the fair control: it is the arm a reviewer will say the device is no better than.
``exp_tau`` is a single exponential at the matched scale, which is the unfair-to-the-control
comparison and is reported only to show the difference the matching makes.  ``no_trace``
sets gain = 0 and must sit at the empirical chance floor at every delay.

Where the scout reports conflict, and what was done (per instruction: timescale wins on
protocol, leak wins on controls):

  * dt.  Timescale scout: dt_stim = 0.4525 s, one measurement sampling interval, because
    below that the KWW arm's state composition is set by modes nothing measured.  Leak
    scout used dt = 1.0 s.  protocol -> 0.4525 s.  The leak scout's dt objections are then
    enforced as controls on top: hold-quantisation injectivity, and no mode faster than dt.
  * Kernel grid.  Timescale scout: k = 12, span_decades = (-1.5, 1.15) (kills the
    fabricated 507 s mode).  Leak scout: keep k = 6 but widen the nnls target to
    tmax_tau = 30 so the slow mode is constrained over the scored range.  both are adopted:
    the timescale scout's grid is the protocol, and the leak scout's widening is applied to
    it (tmax_tau = 1.5*max_delay/tau) because it is what makes the leak scout's
    kernel-fidelity assertion pass.  measured: worst |q_kernel/q_KWW - 1| over the delay
    grid is 217% for the module default, 54% for k=6/tmax=30, and 1.8% here.
  * Full-scale calibration point.  Task requirement: calibrate at zero delay.  Leak scout:
    calibrate at D = dt so sub-dt modes cannot inflate the KWW arm's full scale only.
    The requirement wins, and the leak scout's concern is instead closed at the source --
    with span_lo = -1.5 the fastest mode is 0.507 s > dt = 0.4525 s, so NO mode is faster
    than one step and there is nothing to inflate.  That is asserted (control C18).
  * Static floor.  Data scout: subtract a matched no-trace baseline because the
    class-independent static read swamps the signal.  Not subtracted -- a real array cannot
    erase its own trace mid-trial -- but the objection is answered instead by calibrating
    the read-noise full scale on the between-sample signal spread at D = 0 rather than on
    |read|, so a constant offset no longer inflates the noise.  Both scales are reported;
    ``--scale-mode absmean`` reproduces the older convention.

What this benchmark cannot claim (timescale scout's risk 1, restated because it survives).
The hold is very nearly a pure scalar multiply for every arm, so ~90% of any arm difference
is retained amplitude against a fixed noise floor and is computable from the lab retention
curve with no dataset at all.  The honest claim is "the measured retention curve converted
into a task-level delay budget on real data", not "the device enables a capability".  The
arm ordering is also threshold-dependent and flips below ~90% of ceiling, so ``--dmax-frac``
is pre-registered at 0.75 and every threshold in {0.95, 0.90, 0.75, 0.50} is printed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import pathlib as _pathlib
import sys as _sys

_sys.path.insert(0, str(_pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "src"))

import numpy as np                                                    # Noqa: E402
import torch                                                          # Noqa: E402
import torch.nn as nn                                                 # Noqa: E402
import torch.nn.functional as F                                       # Noqa: E402

from mnn_torch.volatile import (VolatileSynapse, TransientProfile,              # Noqa: E402
                        ito_reference_profile, ITO_REFERENCE,
                        kohlrausch_modes)
from mnn_torch.networks import MemristiveLinearLayer                            # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.networks import hold_conductance, delayed_readout                # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch import datasets as TD                                           # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch import archives as paths, training                                          # Noqa: E402

torch.set_num_threads(int(os.environ.get("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "3")))

REF = ITO_REFERENCE


def default_out() -> str:
    """Default results path, resolved at call time.

    Pinning it to a module-level ``OUTDIR`` at import would make the destination
    depend on where the interpreter started, so it is a function and
    ``MNN_WORK_DIR`` / ``MNN_PROFILE`` are honoured.

    Resolves under the profile's output directory, and is guarded, so a sweep run with
    default arguments cannot write among the deposited records inside the shipped tree.
    """
    return str(paths.guard_not_shipped(paths.output_dir() / "netbench.json"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-registration.  Fixed before any accuracy is computed and hashed into every
# results record, so no per-arm tuning and no post-hoc threshold can hide.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PREREG = dict(
    dt_stim=0.4525,                 # s per network step = 1 measurement sample interval
    delays_s=[0, 2, 4, 8, 16, 23, 32, 45, 64, 90, 128, 180, 226],
    k_modes=12,
    span_decades=(-1.5, 1.15),
    dmax_frac=0.75,                 # Of (D=0 accuracy - empirical floor)
    v_probe=1.25,                   # = the datasets' own encoded drive, 10*log1p(1)/log256*10
    noise_frac=0.05,                # Of the frozen D=0 signal spread
    pf_variability="frozen",
    gate_bias_row=True,
    scale_mode="spread",
    probe_steps=8,                  # Spiking level: R read steps -> counts 0..R
    lif_tau_leak=8.0,               # The archive's own temporal-box membrane leak, in steps
    tau_kww=REF["tau_kww"], beta=REF["beta"], mean_lifetime=REF["mean_lifetime"],
    rho=REF["rho"],
)
# Measured real trial durations (timescale scout), for the re-timing declaration
REAL_DUR_S = {"nmnist": 0.3063, "shd": 0.7148, "dvsgesture": 6.5315, "seqmnist": None}
THRESH_GRID = (0.95, 0.90, 0.75, 0.50)
ARMS_ALL = ("kww", "exp_meanlife", "exp_tau", "no_trace")


def cfg_hash(d) -> str:
    return hashlib.blake2b(json.dumps(d, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode(),
                           digest_size=8).hexdigest()


def thash(t) -> str:
    if t is None:
        return "none"
    if isinstance(t, dict):
        return "|".join(f"{k}:{thash(v)}" for k, v in sorted(t.items()))
    if not torch.is_tensor(t):
        return str(t)
    return hashlib.blake2b(t.detach().cpu().numpy().tobytes(),
                           digest_size=6).hexdigest()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Profiles + kernel
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def profile_for(arm, tau=None, beta=None, rho=None):
    """``kww`` = measured; exp_meanlife = beta 1 at matched <t>; exp_tau = beta 1 at tau.

    ``exp:<tau>`` is an extra single-exponential arm at an arbitrary time constant.  Its only
    purpose is to put more than two points on the exponential-family line D_max = tau*ln(1/q*),
    so the retention equivalence is read off a measured line instead of a two-point slope --
    which is the first thing a referee attacks.  Nothing else about the run changes.
    """
    p = ito_reference_profile()
    t0 = REF["tau_kww"] if tau is None else float(tau)
    b0 = REF["beta"] if beta is None else float(beta)
    r0 = REF["rho"] if rho is None else float(rho)
    ml = (t0 / b0) * math.gamma(1.0 / b0)
    if arm.startswith("exp:"):
        tt, bb = float(arm.split(":", 1)[1]), 1.0
    elif arm == "kww":
        tt, bb = t0, b0
    elif arm == "exp_meanlife":
        tt, bb = ml, 1.0
    else:                                       # exp_tau and no_trace share the geometry
        tt, bb = t0, 1.0
    return TransientProfile(
        tau_kww=tt, beta=bb, amplitude=1.0 - r0, floor=r0, v_read=p.v_read,
        polarity="decay", r2=(p.r2 if arm == "kww" else float("nan")), n_samples=0,
        window_s=p.window_s, source=f"{arm}(tau={tt:.4g},beta={bb:.4g})",
        bias_regime="near_zero", qc_pass=True, qc_reasons=())


def q_exact(d, tau, beta):
    d = np.asarray(d, float)
    return np.exp(-np.power(np.clip(d / tau, 1e-30, None), beta))


def q_kernel(d, taus, w, norm):
    d = np.asarray(d, float)
    return (w[None, :] * np.exp(-d[:, None] / taus[None, :])).sum(1) / norm


def tmax_tau_for(delays, tau):
    """Leak-scout fix: the nnls target must cover the delays actually scored.

    Widened by the pre-registered grid, never by the run's own grid, so that scoring a
    subset of delays cannot silently change the kernel -- and therefore the physics -- being
    compared.  A smoke test and the full sweep run the identical device.
    """
    d = list(delays) + [float(x) for x in PREREG["delays_s"]]
    return max(8.0, 1.5 * float(max(d)) / float(tau))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_flat(dataset, n_train, n_test):
    """``(xtr (T,N,n_in), ytr, xte, yte, T, n_in, ncls, nat)``.

    Always flat, so one code path feeds both readouts; ``nat`` is the natural per-sample
    shape, and the spiking level reshapes back to it so the real conv stack sees frames,
    not a flattened vector.
    """
    xtr, ytr, xte, yte = TD.load_encoded(dataset, n_train=n_train, n_test=n_test)
    # The loader always returns float32.  Under --float64 the model's parameters are
    # Float64, and MemristiveConv2d's conv2d refuses the mix ("expected Float, found
    # double"), so the numerical cross-check has to carry the data in float64 too --
    # Otherwise it silently only ever ran on the dense path.
    dt_ = torch.get_default_dtype()
    if xtr.dtype != dt_:
        xtr, xte = xtr.to(dt_), xte.to(dt_)
    T = xtr.shape[0]
    nat = tuple(xtr.shape[2:])
    xtr = xtr.reshape(T, xtr.shape[1], -1).contiguous()
    xte = xte.reshape(T, xte.shape[1], -1).contiguous()
    ncls = int(max(ytr.max().item(), yte.max().item())) + 1
    if dataset in TD.SPEC:
        ncls = TD.SPEC[dataset][3]
    elif dataset == "seqmnist":
        ncls = 10
    assert torch.isfinite(xtr).all() and torch.isfinite(xte).all(), "non-finite input"
    return xtr, ytr, xte, yte, T, int(xtr.shape[2]), ncls, nat


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scoring
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def cp_upper(k, n, alpha=0.05):
    """Upper one-sided (1-alpha) Clopper-Pearson bound on a binomial proportion."""
    from scipy.stats import beta as B
    if k >= n:
        return 1.0
    return float(B.ppf(1.0 - alpha, k + 1, n - k))


def empirical_floor(y, ncls):
    c = torch.bincount(y, minlength=ncls)
    return float(c.max().item()) / float(len(y)), c.tolist()


def score(o, y, ncls):
    """Tie-aware, NaN-hard accuracy.

    A degenerate all-equal output scores 1/ncls (not class 0), and any non-finite row is a
    hard failure returning NaN -- both of those otherwise land on exactly chance and are
    then read as a clean control.
    """
    nonfinite = int((~torch.isfinite(o)).any(1).sum().item())
    if nonfinite:
        return float("nan"), nonfinite, -1, [0] * ncls
    mx = o.max(1, keepdim=True).values
    ntie = (o == mx).sum(1)
    pred = o.argmax(1)
    hit = ((pred == y) & (ntie == 1)).float() + (ntie > 1).float() / ncls
    hist = torch.bincount(pred[ntie == 1], minlength=ncls).tolist()
    return float(hit.sum().item()) / len(y), 0, int((ntie > 1).sum().item()), hist


def iso_dec(y):
    """Pool-adjacent-violators non-increasing fit (equal weights)."""
    blocks = [[float(v), 1] for v in y]
    i = 0
    while i < len(blocks) - 1:
        if blocks[i][0] < blocks[i + 1][0] - 1e-15:
            s = blocks[i][0] * blocks[i][1] + blocks[i + 1][0] * blocks[i + 1][1]
            n = blocks[i][1] + blocks[i + 1][1]
            blocks[i:i + 2] = [[s / n, n]]
            i = max(i - 1, 0)
        else:
            i += 1
    out = []
    for v, n in blocks:
        out += [v] * n
    return np.asarray(out)


def dmax_interp(delays, accs, floor, frac, cp=None):
    """D_max by interpolation on the monotone fit -- NO first-failure break.

    Returns (dmax, censored).  Threshold is ``floor + frac*(acc[D=0] - floor)``, i.e. a
    fraction of the arm's own above-floor ceiling, so a small ceiling difference between
    arms cannot masquerade as a retention difference.

    ``cp`` is the upper 95% bound on the empirical chance floor.  An arm that never gets
    above it has NO retention to measure, and must report 0 rather than a flat at-chance
    curve censored at the grid edge -- which is how a null arm otherwise reports the largest
    D_max in the table.
    """
    d = np.asarray(delays, float)
    a = iso_dec(accs)
    if cp is not None and a[0] <= cp:
        return 0.0, False
    th = floor + frac * (a[0] - floor)
    if a[0] < th or not np.isfinite(th):
        return 0.0, False
    below = np.where(a < th)[0]
    if below.size == 0:
        return float(d[-1]), True                      # Censored at the grid edge
    i = int(below[0])
    if i == 0:
        return 0.0, False
    a0, a1 = a[i - 1], a[i]
    f = 0.0 if a0 == a1 else (a0 - th) / (a0 - a1)
    return float(d[i - 1] + f * (d[i] - d[i - 1])), False


def dmax_boot(delays, per_seed, floor, frac, n_boot=2000, rng=None, cp=None):
    """Bootstrap CI over the (seed x noise-rep) accuracy replicates at each delay."""
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng(12345)
    R = np.asarray(per_seed, float)                    # (n_rep, n_delay)
    if R.shape[0] < 2:
        return (float("nan"), float("nan"))
    out = []
    for _ in range(n_boot):
        j = rng.integers(0, R.shape[0], R.shape[0])
        dm, _c = dmax_interp(delays, np.nanmean(R[j], axis=0), floor, frac, cp=cp)
        out.append(dm)
    return (float(np.percentile(out, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(out, 97.5)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cell
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_RTS = [None]
_DEV = [None]
_CFG = {}


def rts_module():
    """Back-compatible shim: the model builder, dataset registry and temporal
    config now live in the package, so nothing is loaded from a sibling file.

    Loading it through ``importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`` would create a
    private module object distinct from anything ``import`` returns, so patching the
    imported one has no effect at all. Returning a namespace built from the package
    removes that trap.
    """
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    # The three old modules are two new ones. data -> datasets, and models and temporal were
    # both merged into networks, which is where build_temporal_model and build_cfg now live.
    from mnn_torch import datasets as _d
    from mnn_torch import networks as _n
    if _RTS[0] is None:
        _RTS[0] = SimpleNamespace(DATASETS=_d.DATASETS,
                                  build_model=_n.build_temporal_model,
                                  build_cfg=_n.build_cfg)
    return _RTS[0]


def device_params():
    """The fitted device: the deposited fit where it is available, else a refit.

    The deposit is preferred, and not as a fallback for a missing file. ``precompute_device_params``
    re-reads and re-fits the raw multistate measurement, which this release does not ship -- so
    without this the instrument cannot run here at all. It is also the more faithful choice: a
    refit could land on slightly different parameters than the ones the deposited results were
    measured under, and a rerun that trains against a different device reproduces nothing. The
    refit is kept for a tree that has the raw file and wants to re-derive from it.
    """
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    try:
        from experiments.static import deposited_device_params
        return deposited_device_params()
    except Exception:                                    # Noqa: BLE001
        return training.precompute_device_params()


def make_cfg(pf_variability, sigma_g=0.5, fault_prob=0.0):
    """Cached: :func:`device_params` is called once per cell. Caching is safe because it
    consumes no torch RNG and the result is a deterministic function of the deposit -- and
    every Cell re-seeds torch immediately afterwards anyway."""
    key = (pf_variability, sigma_g, fault_prob)
    if key not in _CFG:
        if _DEV[0] is None:
            _DEV[0] = device_params()
        _CFG[key] = rts_module().build_cfg(
            "pf_healthy", PREREG["lif_tau_leak"], _DEV[0], pf_variability=pf_variability,
            fault_prob=fault_prob, stuck_polarity="split", sigma_g=sigma_g)
    return dict(_CFG[key])


class Cell:
    """One (arm, delay, seed) network with the analog readout: a digital ``nn.Linear`` on
    the analog column current.  Everything arm-independent is seeded identically."""

    readout_kind = "analog"

    def __init__(self, arm, n_in, ncls, args, seed, gain_override=None,
                 tau=None, beta=None, rho=None, delays=None, nat=None):
        self.arm, self.args, self.seed, self.ncls = arm, args, seed, ncls
        self.dt = float(args.dt)
        self.nat = tuple(nat or ())
        self.diag = {}
        cfg = make_cfg(args.pf_variability)
        # Control: pf_variability must be frozen/off or the device is re-rolled between the
        # write and the read (leak scout: 'read out of a physically different device').
        assert (not cfg.get("pf_stochastic")) or cfg.get("pf_frozen_variability"), \
            "pf variability must be frozen"
        self.cfg_id = cfg_hash({k: v for k, v in cfg.items() if not torch.is_tensor(v)})

        torch.manual_seed(seed)                          # Weights: arm-independent
        self.layer = MemristiveLinearLayer(n_in, args.cols, cfg)
        self.n_syn_in = int(self.layer.weights.shape[1])
        self.v_probe = float(args.v_probe)
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.layer.bias.zero_()
        self.layer.bias.requires_grad_(False)            # Keep it out of max|weights_and_bias|

        # Device realisation sampled eagerly from a dedicated stream, so no arm-specific
        # RNG consumption can hand one arm a different physical device.
        with torch.random.fork_rng():
            torch.manual_seed(seed + 7777)
            self.layer._grid_and_params(torch.device("cpu"))
        self.dev_id = thash({"pf": self.layer._pf_residual,
                             "fault": self.layer._device_fault})

        prof = profile_for(arm, tau=tau, beta=beta, rho=rho)
        dl = delays if delays is not None else args.delays
        self.vs = VolatileSynapse(self.layer, prof, k=args.k, dt=self.dt,
                                  span_decades=tuple(args.span),
                                  tmax_tau=tmax_tau_for(dl, prof.tau_kww))
        self.gain_nominal = self.vs.gain
        if arm == "no_trace":
            self.vs.gain = 0.0
        if gain_override is not None:
            self.vs.gain = float(gain_override)

        torch.manual_seed(seed + 31337)                  # Readout: arm-independent
        self.readout = nn.Linear(args.cols, ncls)
        assert not any("Norm" in type(m).__name__ for m in self.readout.modules()), \
            "no batch-dependent statistic is allowed in the readout"
        self.gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + 9991)
        self.scale = None                                # Frozen float, set once
        self.scale_absmean = None
        self.w0 = None
        self.params = [self.layer.weights] + list(self.readout.parameters())

    # -- physics -----------------------------------------------------------
    def state_after_write(self, xs):
        """Write the sample over its natural timesteps.  Output discarded, so the PF map is
        skipped: z has no weight dependence, making the skip exact rather than an
        approximation (verified in transient.py's compute_out docstring)."""
        z = self.vs.init_state(xs.shape[1])
        for t in range(xs.shape[0]):
            _, z = self.vs(xs[t], z, phase="write",
                           gate_bias_row=self.args.gate, compute_out=False)
        self._last_write_u = xs[-1].detach()      # For the power test's leak probe only
        return z

    def probe(self, B, n_in=None):
        p = torch.full((B, n_in or self.n_syn_in), self.v_probe)
        # Control C3: the probe is label-independent by construction.  measured power of
        # this control (leak scout): a probe that is the sample scores 100% at D = 400 s
        # with gain = 0, i.e. with no device memory at all -- so a probe derived from x
        # would carry the whole answer.  Never pass drive= at the read step.
        assert p.unique().numel() == 1, "probe must be uniform"
        return p

    def read(self, z, n_in=None, gen=None):
        out, z, (o_s, o_t) = self.vs(self.probe(z.shape[0], n_in), z, phase="read",
                                     gate_bias_row=self.args.gate, return_parts=True)
        return out, o_s, o_t

    def _logits_from_state(self, z, gen=None, want_parts=False):
        """Everything after the hold.  Kept separate so control C22 can prove that ``z``
        is the only thing crossing the delay: permuting z permutes the logits."""
        out, o_s, o_t = self.read(z)
        raw = out
        out = out / self.scale
        if self.args.noise > 0:
            g = gen if gen is not None else self.gen
            out = out + self.args.noise * torch.randn(out.shape, generator=g)
        logits = self.readout(out)
        if want_parts:
            return logits, raw, o_s, o_t
        return logits

    def forward(self, xs, delay, gen=None, want_parts=False):
        z = self.state_after_write(xs)
        if delay > 0:
            # One exact tensor op.  Never loop a delay: 400x slower for an identical result,
            # and a stepped delay with the row open recharges the bias row instead of
            # decaying it (leak scout, measured q growing 12.9 -> 26.5 with delay).
            z = self.vs.hold(z, delay)
        return self._logits_from_state(z, gen=gen, want_parts=want_parts)

    # -- calibration -------------------------------------------------------
    def calibrate(self, xs, n_cal=256, scale_from=None, delay=0.0):
        """Frozen full scale at zero delay.  Never a per-batch statistic (trap 1).

        ``delay`` is accepted and ignored at this level: the analog readout's trainable
        ``nn.Linear`` (weight and bias) is fitted at the cell's own delay by training, so
        it absorbs the delay-dependent pedestal itself.  The spiking level has no
        trainable map on that path and so must be given the same freedom explicitly --
        see :meth:`SpikingCell.calibrate`.

        ``scale_from`` pins the scale to another cell's frozen value.  Required for the gain
        dose-response: recalibrating the scale at each gain divides the signal by its own
        amplitude, which is trap 1 applied along the dose axis and flattens the very
        response the control is trying to measure (measured: with per-gain calibration the
        response saturates above gain/4 and is non-monotone).
        """
        assert self.scale is None, "scale is calibrated exactly once"
        with torch.no_grad():
            xc = xs[:, :min(n_cal, xs.shape[1])]
            z = self.state_after_write(xc)
            out, o_s, o_t = self.read(z)
            spread = float(out.std(0).mean().item())
            absmean = float(out.abs().mean().item()) or 1.0
            self.scale_absmean = absmean
            self.static_absmean = float(o_s.abs().mean().item())
            self.trace_absmean = float(o_t.abs().mean().item())
            self.spread0 = spread
            # --scale-force: one absolute noise floor shared by every arm.  Noise is injected
            # as noise_frac of `scale`, so per-arm calibration gives arms with a smaller D=0
            # Spread a smaller absolute floor -- measured: kww 201 vs exp_meanlife 235, i.e.
            # The stretched kernel ran at a 14% lower floor because the 3.62 s write already
            # decays it.  Forcing a common value equalises snr across arms.  measured at
            # 246.5243 (the largest per-arm D=0 spread, so it disadvantages kww): the D=90 gap
            # goes 33.11 -> 30.70 pp, i.e. the advantage is not a calibration artefact.
            forced = float(getattr(self.args, "scale_force", 0.0) or 0.0)
            if forced > 0:
                self.scale = forced
                self.scale_src = "forced-shared"
            elif scale_from is not None:
                self.scale = float(scale_from)
                self.scale_src = "frozen-from-reference"
            elif self.args.scale_mode == "spread" and spread > 0:
                self.scale = spread
                self.scale_src = "spread"
            else:
                self.scale = absmean
                self.scale_src = "absmean" + ("(no-signal)" if spread <= 0 else "")
            self.w0 = float(self.layer.weights.abs().max().item())
        return self

    def regauge(self):
        """Max|weights| is a pure gauge: it leaves G bit-identical and scales the output by
        exactly the same factor, so leaving it free lets training raise snr against a frozen
        noise calibration without changing any physics.  Project it back every step."""
        with torch.no_grad():
            m = float(self.layer.weights.abs().max().item())
            if m > 0:
                self.layer.weights.mul_(self.w0 / m)

    # -- train / eval ------------------------------------------------------
    def loss_logits(self, logits):
        """Identity here.  The spiking level rescales its integer spike counts for the
        loss only -- a monotone, per-sample-constant-free rescaling, so every argmax and
        therefore every reported accuracy is bit-identical either way."""
        return logits

    def _snap(self):
        return [p.detach().clone() for p in self.params]

    def _restore(self, snap):
        with torch.no_grad():
            for p, q in zip(self.params, snap):
                p.copy_(q)

    def val_loss(self, xv, yv, delay, bs):
        """Validation loss + decision degeneracy, with a deterministic noise draw so the
        early-stopping signal is not itself noise (the generator is re-seeded identically at
        every evaluation).

        The degeneracy statistics are what make the plateau gate trustworthy.  measured:
        the N-MNIST/spiking cell at D = 45 s sat at validation loss 2.279 against
        ln 10 = 2.303 -- inside any loss-only margin one would dare to set -- while
        1000/1000 of its test predictions were argmax ties, i.e. it had made no decision at
        all.  A loss threshold cannot separate those two; a tie rate can.

        Returns ``(loss, tie_fraction, max_predicted_class_share)``.
        """
        lossf = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        tot, n, nties = 0.0, 0, 0
        hist = np.zeros(self.ncls, int)
        with torch.no_grad():
            g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(self.seed + 424242)
            for i in range(0, xv.shape[1], bs):
                lo = self.forward(xv[:, i:i + bs], delay, gen=g)
                if not torch.isfinite(lo).all():
                    return float("nan"), 1.0, 1.0
                tot += float(lossf(self.loss_logits(lo),
                                   yv[i:i + bs]).item()) * lo.shape[0]
                nt = (lo == lo.max(1, keepdim=True).values).sum(1)
                nties += int((nt > 1).sum().item())
                hist += np.bincount(lo.argmax(1)[nt == 1].numpy(),
                                    minlength=self.ncls)
                n += lo.shape[0]
        n = max(n, 1)
        share = (hist.max() / hist.sum()) if hist.sum() else 1.0
        return tot / n, nties / n, float(share)

    def train(self, xs, y, delay, epochs, bs, lr, shuffle_labels=False,
              xval=None, yval=None, patience=8):
        """Train with early stopping on A held-out validation split, restoring the best
        parameters.

        A training-loss plateau is the wrong convergence target here and using it was a real
        defect.  measured on SHD (n_train=1200, kww): going from 60 to 150 epochs drives the
        training loss from 0.486 to 0.089 while test accuracy at D=0 falls from 46.40% to
        41.20%, and simultaneously lifts the D=180 s cell from 5.80% (chance) to 16.80%
        (above the floor).  The budget was setting the answer in both directions at once --
        the undertrained-comparator trap and its overfitting mirror image.  Stopping every
        cell at its own validation optimum makes the arms comparable and makes 'D_max is
        unchanged when the budget is quadrupled' a test the design can actually pass.
        """
        opt = torch.optim.Adam(self.params, lr=lr)
        lossf = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        uniform = math.log(self.ncls)          # The loss of the uniform predictor
        N = xs.shape[1]
        yy = y
        if shuffle_labels:
            perm = torch.randperm(N, generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(self.seed + 5))
            yy = y[perm]
        traj, vtraj = [], []
        nan_step, best, best_ep, bad = -1, float("inf"), -1, 0
        best_informative, best_stats = False, (float("nan"),) * 3
        snap = self._snap()
        stopped = False
        for ep in range(epochs):
            order = torch.randperm(N, generator=self.gen)
            for i in range(0, N, bs):
                j = order[i:i + bs]
                if len(j) < 2:
                    continue
                opt.zero_grad()
                logits = self.forward(xs[:, j], delay)
                loss = lossf(self.loss_logits(logits), yy[j])
                if not torch.isfinite(loss):
                    nan_step = len(traj)
                    traj.append(float("nan"))
                    return traj, nan_step, dict(converged=False, best_epoch=ep,
                                                val=vtraj, nan=True, stopped=False)
                loss.backward()
                torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.params, 1.0)
                opt.step()
                self.regauge()
                traj.append(float(loss.item()))
            if xval is not None:
                v, tiefrac, share = self.val_loss(xval, yval, delay, bs)
                vtraj.append(v)
                # Degenerate = no decision made: (almost) every sample an argmax tie, or
                # every prediction the same class.  Either way the cell is the trivial
                # predictor and its flat loss is the collapse plateau, not an optimum.
                degenerate = (tiefrac > 0.5) or (share > 0.9)
                informative = (np.isfinite(v) and v < uniform - 0.02
                               and not degenerate)
                if informative:
                    best_informative = True
                if np.isfinite(v) and v < best - 1e-4 and (
                        informative or not best_informative):
                    best, best_ep, bad, snap = v, ep, 0, self._snap()
                    best_stats = (v, tiefrac, share)
                else:
                    bad += 1
                    # Never early-stop at the trivial solution.  A cell whose validation
                    # loss is still ln(ncls) is the uniform predictor: it has learned
                    # nothing, and the flat stretch it is sitting on is the collapse
                    # plateau, not an optimum.  measured on N-MNIST/spiking at D = 45 s:
                    # Patience 40 fired at epoch 30 with val loss 2.279 vs ln 10 = 2.303
                    # And the cell was recorded as "converged at chance" -- a manufactured
                    # Null.  Stopping is therefore gated on having left the plateau, and a
                    # Cell that reaches the epoch cap without leaving it is reported as not
                    # Converged (so its D_max is not reportable) rather than as a null.
                    # ... except for the no_trace arm, whose whole purpose is to sit at
                    # the floor: it has no optimum to find, so the plateau is its answer
                    # and forcing it to the epoch cap would only burn compute.
                    # A shuffled-label cell is also supposed to sit at the floor, so it is
                    # exempt too -- otherwise the leakage control burns the whole epoch cap
                    # on every cell to confirm the very thing it is asserting.
                    if bad >= patience and (self.arm == "no_trace" or shuffle_labels
                                            or best_informative):
                        stopped = True
                        break
        left = bool(best_informative) or self.arm == "no_trace" or shuffle_labels
        if xval is not None:
            self._restore(snap)                       # The validation optimum, not the last step
        return traj, nan_step, dict(converged=bool(stopped and left), best_epoch=best_ep,
                                    best_val=best, val=vtraj, nan=False, stopped=stopped,
                                    left_plateau=left, uniform_loss=uniform,
                                    val_tie_frac=best_stats[1], val_max_share=best_stats[2],
                                    epochs_run=ep + 1)

    def evaluate(self, xs, y, delay, bs, noise_reps=1):
        accs, ties, nonf, hists = [], 0, 0, np.zeros(self.ncls, int)
        with torch.no_grad():
            for r in range(noise_reps):
                g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(self.seed * 1000 + r + 777)
                hit, n = 0.0, 0
                for i in range(0, xs.shape[1], bs):
                    logits = self.forward(xs[:, i:i + bs], delay, gen=g)
                    a, nf, nt, h = score(logits, y[i:i + bs], self.ncls)
                    if not np.isfinite(a):
                        nonf += nf
                        return float("nan"), nonf, -1, hists.tolist()
                    hit += a * logits.shape[0]
                    n += logits.shape[0]
                    ties += nt
                    hists += np.asarray(h, int)
                accs.append(hit / n)
        return float(np.mean(accs)), nonf, ties, hists.tolist(), accs


class SpikingCell(Cell):
    """The real model, with only its dense synapse made volatile.

    ``run_temporal_sweep.build_model`` builds the archive's own ``TemporalMCSNN`` /
    ``TemporalMSNN`` from the archive's own dataset dims and config; its conv layers, its
    LIF neurons (a configured leak, ``beta = exp(-dt/tau_leak)``) and its rate-coded decision
    ``spk.sum(0)`` are untouched.  Only ``fc1`` -- which is a ``MemristiveLinearLayer`` in
    both models -- is wrapped as a :class:`VolatileSynapse`, so on the conv path the
    volatile current feeds ``lif3`` directly (the hard test: a spiking threshold, not a
    linear readout) and on the dense path it feeds ``lif1 -> fc2 -> lif2``.

    Why a probe window of R steps.  A single read step yields one binary spike per output
    neuron, which is a degenerate decision (every sample an argmax tie).  R steps give a
    rate code in ``0..R``.  Every one of those steps must carry the sensing bias, because
    with zero drive ``PF(0) = 0`` and the read is exactly zero -- trapped charge is not
    observable without a bias.  The probe is uniform and class-independent, so the charge
    it adds is common-mode; it dilutes the class-dependent part but cannot carry a label.

    The operating point is a frozen calibration, and it is necessary, not a tuning knob.
    measured: the read is a large class-independent pedestal plus a small signal
    (|read|/spread = 7.3 on N-MNIST, 2.8 on SHD), so a fixed threshold either saturates
    (measured 47/48 of the maximum possible spikes, spread over samples 0.035 -> every
    sample an argmax tie) or falls silent.  A threshold readout of a volatile synapse
    therefore needs a reference current, exactly as a real sense amplifier does.  Three
    numbers are fitted once, before training, and then frozen for the whole cell:
    per-neuron reference ``mu`` (per read step), per-neuron gain ``A``, per-neuron offset
    ``C``, chosen so the D=0 count distribution has mean R/2 and sd R/4.  All three sit
    after the noise injection, so they scale signal and noise identically -- snr-neutral,
    hence not trap 1.  ``sigma0``, the noise reference, is still measured at D = 0 only.
    They are the exact counterpart of the analog level's trainable ``nn.Linear``
    weight+bias, which is likewise fitted at the cell's own delay; the difference is that
    here they are frozen and do no cross-neuron mixing, so this is still a spiking
    threshold readout and not a linear classifier.

    Measured consequence of getting this wrong, recorded so it is not re-derived: with the
    calibration re-run every epoch it fights the optimiser (11.9% on N-MNIST); with it
    frozen at D = 0 and used at D = 45 s the readout is out of band and collapses; frozen
    at the cell's own delay it trains to 41.0% at D = 0 (chance 10.0%) over 200 epochs and
    was still improving.
    """

    readout_kind = "spiking"

    def __init__(self, arm, n_in, ncls, args, seed, gain_override=None,
                 tau=None, beta=None, rho=None, delays=None, nat=None):
        self.arm, self.args, self.seed, self.ncls = arm, args, seed, ncls
        self.dt = float(args.dt)
        self.nat = tuple(nat or ())
        self.diag = {}
        cfg = make_cfg(args.pf_variability)
        assert (not cfg.get("pf_stochastic")) or cfg.get("pf_frozen_variability"), \
            "pf variability must be frozen"
        self.cfg_id = cfg_hash({k: v for k, v in cfg.items() if not torch.is_tensor(v)})

        rts = rts_module()
        torch.manual_seed(seed)                          # Weights: arm-independent
        # ``force_dense`` routes a conv dataset through the dense model. It is an
        # explicit argument threaded to the builder, never a mutation of the shared
        # registry, and both the network and ``self.kind`` must honour it or the read
        # path would be selected for the wrong architecture.
        _kind = ("dense" if getattr(args, "force_dense", False)
                 else rts.DATASETS[args.dataset]["kind"])
        self.net = rts.build_model(args.dataset, cfg, args.bs, kind=_kind)
        self.model_name = type(self.net).__name__
        self.kind = _kind
        self.layer = self.net.fc1                        # The dense synapse -> volatile
        assert isinstance(self.layer, MemristiveLinearLayer), \
            f"fc1 must be the memristive dense synapse, got {type(self.layer).__name__}"
        self.n_syn_in = int(self.layer.weights.shape[1])
        self.n_syn_out = int(self.layer.weights.shape[0])
        if self.kind == "conv":
            self.out_lif = self.net.lif3
            self.hold_layers = [self.net.conv1, self.net.conv2, self.net.fc1]
            assert self.n_syn_out == ncls, "on the conv path fc1 IS the output layer"
        else:
            self.out_lif = self.net.lif2
            self.hold_layers = [self.net.fc1, self.net.fc2]
        # The probe equals the largest amplitude this synapse's own input can take during
        # the write: a spike (1.0) on the conv path, the encoded drive on the dense path
        self.v_probe = float(args.v_probe_spk) if args.v_probe_spk is not None else (
            1.0 if self.kind == "conv" else float(args.v_probe))
        self.R = int(args.probe_steps)

        # Every in-array bias row is zeroed and frozen: it is a real crossbar row
        # (layers.py:184/:315) and it also enters max|weights_and_bias|, so a trainable
        # bias could silently become the layer's global gain (leak scout, medium).
        for m in self.net.modules():
            if isinstance(m, MemristiveLinearLayer):
                with torch.no_grad():
                    m.bias.zero_()
                m.bias.requires_grad_(False)
        for p in self.net.parameters():
            if p.ndim == 1:                              # Conv biases: digital, PF(0)=0
                p.requires_grad_(False)

        with torch.random.fork_rng():
            torch.manual_seed(seed + 7777)
            self.layer._grid_and_params(torch.device("cpu"))
        self.dev_id = thash({"pf": self.layer._pf_residual,
                             "fault": self.layer._device_fault})

        prof = profile_for(arm, tau=tau, beta=beta, rho=rho)
        dl = delays if delays is not None else args.delays
        self.vs = VolatileSynapse(self.layer, prof, k=args.k, dt=self.dt,
                                  span_decades=tuple(args.span),
                                  tmax_tau=tmax_tau_for(dl, prof.tau_kww))
        self.gain_nominal = self.vs.gain
        if arm == "no_trace":
            self.vs.gain = 0.0
        if gain_override is not None:
            self.vs.gain = float(gain_override)

        # Only fc1 is gauge-projected during training (see Cell.regauge), and that is
        # sufficient: the gauge concern is a free gain sitting between the signal and the
        # frozen noise reference.  fc1 is the only layer in that position.  The conv layers
        # feed the trace with binary spikes, so their gain cannot scale the trace amplitude;
        # Fc2 (dense path) sits after the noise injection, so its gain scales signal and
        # noise together and is snr-neutral.
        self.readout = nn.Identity()                     # There is NO digital readout
        self.gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + 9991)
        self.scale = None
        self.scale_absmean = None
        self.w0 = None
        self.mu = torch.zeros(1)
        self.A = torch.ones(self.n_syn_out)
        self.C = torch.zeros(self.n_syn_out)
        self.params = [p for p in self.net.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
        assert any(p is self.layer.weights for p in self.params)
        # No homeostasis anywhere on the path (leak scout, low)
        assert not any(any(s in type(m).__name__ for s in ("Homeo", "Norm"))
                       for m in self.net.modules()), "no homeostat/Norm may sit on the path"

    # -- physics -----------------------------------------------------------
    def state_after_write(self, xs):
        """Stream the sample through the model's own stack; its spikes drive the trace.

        ``compute_out=False`` at every write step, so no output current is formed, no
        membrane downstream of the synapse is driven, and the PF map is evaluated once at
        the read instead of T times.  exact, not an approximation: the trace update
        ``z <- z*dec + u`` contains no weights.
        """
        B = xs.shape[1]
        z = self.vs.init_state(B)
        if self.kind == "dense":
            for t in range(xs.shape[0]):
                _, z = self.vs(xs[t], z, phase="write",
                               gate_bias_row=self.args.gate, compute_out=False)
            self.diag["hidden_rate"] = float("nan")
            self._last_write_u = xs[-1].detach()
            return z
        net = self.net
        x = xs.reshape(xs.shape[0], B, *self.nat)
        mem1, mem2 = net.lif1.init_leaky(), net.lif2.init_leaky()
        rate = 0.0
        for t in range(x.shape[0]):
            spk1, mem1 = net.lif1(F.max_pool2d(net.conv1(x[t]), net.max_pooling), mem1)
            spk2, mem2 = net.lif2(F.max_pool2d(net.conv2(spk1), net.max_pooling), mem2)
            rate += float(spk2.detach().mean().item())
            u = spk2.reshape(B, -1)
            self._last_write_u = u.detach()
            _, z = self.vs(u, z, phase="write",
                           gate_bias_row=self.args.gate, compute_out=False)
        # Trap 5: a hidden layer at rate ~0 makes everything chance by construction.
        self.diag["hidden_rate"] = rate / x.shape[0]
        return z

    def reads(self, z):
        """The R raw analog probe reads -- the only thing the spiking head ever sees."""
        outs, parts = [], []
        for _r in range(self.R):
            out, z, (o_s, o_t) = self.vs(self.probe(z.shape[0]), z, phase="read",
                                         gate_bias_row=self.args.gate, return_parts=True)
            outs.append(out)
            parts.append((o_s, o_t))
        return outs, parts

    def spike_head(self, outs, gen=None, A=None, C=None, want_driven=False):
        """``want_driven`` returns the counts of the neurons the volatile current drives
        directly (``lif3`` on the conv path, where they are also the output neurons;
        ``lif1`` on the dense path, where they are the hidden layer).  Those are the
        neurons whose operating point the calibration sets, and they are ``n_syn_out``
        wide -- the output layer on the dense path is a different width, which is why the
        two cannot be conflated."""
        net = self.net
        A = self.A if A is None else A
        C = self.C if C is None else C
        if self.kind == "conv":
            mem = net.lif3.init_leaky()
        else:
            m1, m2 = net.lif1.init_leaky(), net.lif2.init_leaky()
        rec, driven = [], []
        for r, out in enumerate(outs):
            cur = out if self.scale is None else (out - self.mu[r]) / self.scale
            if gen is not None and self.args.noise > 0:
                # Noise injection point: immediately after the array, before anything that
                # could act as a gain.  Everything after this line scales signal and noise
                # together, which is what keeps the frozen-scale guard meaningful.
                cur = cur + self.args.noise * torch.randn(cur.shape, generator=gen)
            cur = A * cur + C
            if self.kind == "conv":
                s, mem = net.lif3(cur, mem)
                driven.append(s)
            else:
                s1, m1 = net.lif1(cur, m1)
                driven.append(s1)
                s, m2 = net.lif2(net.fc2(s1), m2)
            rec.append(s)
        if want_driven:
            return delayed_readout(torch.stack(driven), self.R)
        # The model's own rate-coded decision (training.py: loss_fn(spk.sum(dim=0), y))
        return delayed_readout(torch.stack(rec), self.R)

    def loss_logits(self, logits):
        """Spike counts run 0..R, so at init the logit magnitudes are large and the
        cheapest descent direction is to become uninformative (all neurons saturate ->
        uniform softmax -> loss = ln(ncls)).  measured: initial CE 3.9 > ln 10 = 2.303, and
        the net duly collapsed to 7.8/8 spikes on every neuron and sat at chance.  Dividing
        by the calibrated count spread R/4 removes that trap.  It is a positive scalar, so
        it changes no argmax and no reported accuracy."""
        return logits * (4.0 / self.R)

    # -- calibration -------------------------------------------------------
    def _fit_operating_point(self, outs, iters=40):
        """Bounded feedback controller for the spiking reference (mu, A, C).

        Why it is bounded.  The original rule scaled the gain by ``(ts/s)**0.5`` with no
        damping and no check on the mean.  A saturated neuron has a small count spread for
        the wrong reason -- not "signal too weak" but "already pinned at R" -- so the rule
        amplified, which deepened the saturation, which kept the spread small.  measured at
        D = 45 s: s = 0.03 against ts = 6 gives (6/0.03)**0.5 = 14.1x per iteration, twelve
        iterations, straight into the 1e9 clamp; the cell landed at mean 22.94 / sd 0.03 of
        R = 24 with all 5000 test samples tied, identically at R = 8 and R = 24.

        The fix.  Judge usability by the mean, not the spread: outside a usable band the
        spread carries no information at all, so centre hard and shrink the gain instead of
        growing it.  In band, keep the same target but clamp the per-iteration factor so no
        runaway is representable.  More iterations, because every step is now damped.
        """
        tm, ts = self.R / 2.0, self.R / 4.0
        lo_band, hi_band = 0.15 * self.R, 0.85 * self.R
        A, C = self.A.clone(), self.C.clone()
        m = s = None
        for _ in range(iters):
            with torch.no_grad():
                cnt = self.spike_head(outs, gen=None, A=A, C=C,
                                      want_driven=True).float()
            m, s = cnt.mean(0), cnt.std(0)
            oob = (m < lo_band) | (m > hi_band)
            # Centre first, with a full step when out of band
            C = C + torch.where(oob, torch.ones_like(m), torch.full_like(m, 0.5)) \
                * (tm - m) / max(self.R, 1)
            grow = torch.clamp((ts / s.clamp(min=1e-6)) ** 0.5, 0.5, 2.0)
            grow = torch.where(oob, torch.full_like(grow, 0.7), grow)
            A = torch.clamp(A * grow, 1e-9, 1e9)
        self.A, self.C = A, C
        return float(m.mean()), float(s.mean())

    def calibrate(self, xs, n_cal=256, scale_from=None, delay=0.0):
        """``sigma0`` at D = 0 (frozen, the noise reference); ``(mu, A, C)`` at the cell's
        own delay (frozen, snr-neutral, label-independent).  Called exactly once."""
        assert self.scale is None, "scale is calibrated exactly once"
        xc = xs[:, :min(n_cal, xs.shape[1])]
        with torch.no_grad():
            with hold_conductance(*self.hold_layers):
                z0 = self.state_after_write(xc)
                outs0, parts0 = self.reads(z0)
            O0 = torch.stack(outs0)                      # (R, B, n_out) at D = 0
            spread = float(O0.std(1).mean().item())
            absmean = float(O0.abs().mean().item()) or 1.0
            self.scale_absmean = absmean
            self.static_absmean = float(parts0[0][0].abs().mean().item())
            self.trace_absmean = float(parts0[0][1].abs().mean().item())
            self.spread0 = spread
            # --scale-force: one absolute noise floor shared by every arm.  Noise is injected
            # as noise_frac of `scale`, so per-arm calibration gives arms with a smaller D=0
            # Spread a smaller absolute floor -- measured: kww 201 vs exp_meanlife 235, i.e.
            # The stretched kernel ran at a 14% lower floor because the 3.62 s write already
            # decays it.  Forcing a common value equalises snr across arms.  measured at
            # 246.5243 (the largest per-arm D=0 spread, so it disadvantages kww): the D=90 gap
            # goes 33.11 -> 30.70 pp, i.e. the advantage is not a calibration artefact.
            forced = float(getattr(self.args, "scale_force", 0.0) or 0.0)
            if forced > 0:
                self.scale = forced
                self.scale_src = "forced-shared"
            elif scale_from is not None:
                self.scale = float(scale_from)
                self.scale_src = "frozen-from-reference"
            elif self.args.scale_mode == "spread" and spread > 0:
                self.scale = spread
                self.scale_src = "spread"
            else:
                self.scale = absmean
                self.scale_src = "absmean" + ("(no-signal)" if spread <= 0 else "")
            self.w0 = float(self.layer.weights.abs().max().item())
            # Operating point at this cell's delay
            with hold_conductance(*self.hold_layers):
                z = self.state_after_write(xc)
                if delay > 0:
                    z = self.vs.hold(z, delay)
                outs, _p = self.reads(z)
            self.mu = torch.stack(outs).mean(1).detach().clone()   # (R, n_out)
            assert self.mu.dim() == 2 and self.mu.shape[0] == self.R
        m, s = self._fit_operating_point(outs)
        with torch.no_grad():
            oc = self.spike_head(outs, gen=None).float()
        self.diag.update(op_out_mean=float(oc.mean().item()),
                         op_out_sd=float(oc.std(0).mean().item()),
                         op_out_zerofrac=float((oc.sum(1) == 0).float().mean().item()),
                         op_count_mean=m, op_count_sd=s,
                         op_A=float(self.A.mean().item()), op_C=float(self.C.mean().item()),
                         pedestal_over_spread=absmean / max(self.scale, 1e-30))
        self.calib_delay = float(delay)
        return self

    # -- forward -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _logits_from_state(self, z, gen=None, want_parts=False):
        outs, parts = self.reads(z)
        lo = self.spike_head(outs, gen=gen if gen is not None else self.gen)
        with torch.no_grad():
            c = lo.detach().float()
            n = self.diag.get("_n", 0) + 1
            self.diag["_n"] = n
            for k, v in (("out_spk_mean", float(c.mean().item())),
                         ("out_spk_sd", float(c.std(0).mean().item())),
                         ("zero_spk_frac", float((c.sum(1) == 0).float().mean().item()))):
                self.diag[k] = self.diag.get(k, 0.0) * (n - 1) / n + v / n
        if want_parts:
            return lo, outs[0], parts[0][0], parts[0][1]
        return lo

    def forward(self, xs, delay, gen=None, want_parts=False):
        # One hold_conductance scope for the whole trial, exactly as the real model's own
        # forward does -- which also guarantees G is identical at write and at read (C12c).
        with hold_conductance(*self.hold_layers):
            z = self.state_after_write(xs)
            if delay > 0:
                z = self.vs.hold(z, delay)              # One exact tensor op
            return self._logits_from_state(z, gen=gen, want_parts=want_parts)


def make_cell(arm, n_in, ncls, args, seed, **kw):
    """The readout factor, dispatched in one place so nothing else has to know."""
    klass = SpikingCell if args.readout == "spiking" else Cell
    return klass(arm, n_in, ncls, args, seed, **kw)


def split_val(x, y, frac, seed):
    """Held-out validation split for early stopping.  The permutation is seeded by seed0
    only, so every arm, delay and seed sees the identical split -- the split cannot become a
    per-arm confound."""
    n = x.shape[1]
    nv = max(int(round(n * frac)), 2)
    p = torch.randperm(n, generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + 606))
    return x[:, p[nv:]].contiguous(), y[p[nv:]], x[:, p[:nv]].contiguous(), y[p[:nv]]


def converged(traj, tail=0.2, tol=0.02):
    """Loss-plateau criterion: relative decrease over the final `tail` of the run < tol."""
    t = np.asarray([x for x in traj if np.isfinite(x)], float)
    if t.size < 20:
        return False, float("nan")
    w = max(int(t.size * tail), 5)
    a, b = t[-2 * w:-w].mean(), t[-w:].mean()
    rel = float((a - b) / abs(a)) if a != 0 else float("nan")
    return bool(rel < tol), rel


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structural controls (no training; every one is an assert or a printed diagnostic)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def structural_controls(args, data, out):
    xtr, ytr, xte, yte, T, n_in, ncls, nat = data
    ok = True
    P = lambda tag, good, msg: print(f"  [{'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'}] {tag:<34s} {msg}",
                                     flush=True)
    rec = {}

    # --- C17 pre-registration: does the pre-registered grid span the cliff for every arm? ---
    # The gate is on PREREG["delays_s"], because that is what "pre-registered" means: the
    # grid was fixed before any accuracy was looked at.  A run may legitimately score a
    # subset of it (a smoke test, a refinement), which is declared and warned about; a grid
    # containing delays that are not in the pre-registered set is a hard failure, because
    # that is the garden-of-forking-paths move this control exists to stop.
    pre = [float(d) for d in PREREG["delays_s"]]
    dmin, dmax_pre = min(d for d in pre if d > 0), max(pre)
    span_ok = True
    for arm in ARMS_ALL[:3]:
        p = profile_for(arm)
        q0 = q_exact([dmin], p.tau_kww, p.beta)[0]
        q1 = q_exact([dmax_pre], p.tau_kww, p.beta)[0]
        span_ok &= (q0 > 0.5) and (q1 < 0.05)
        rec[f"span_{arm}"] = (float(q0), float(q1))
    P("C17 prereg grid spans the cliff", span_ok,
      f"q({dmin:g}s)>0.5 and q({dmax_pre:g}s)<0.05 for kww/exp_meanlife/exp_tau")
    ok &= span_ok
    extra = sorted(set(args.delays) - set(pre))
    P("C17b run grid is within prereg", not extra,
      "run grid == prereg grid" if set(args.delays) == set(pre) else
      (f"DECLARED SUBSET {sorted(args.delays)} of the {len(pre)}-point prereg grid -- "
       f"D_max from a subset is NOT the headline number"
       if not extra else f"OFF-PREREG delays {extra}"))
    ok &= not extra
    rec["run_grid_is_prereg"] = set(args.delays) == set(pre)
    dmax = max(args.delays)

    # --- C7 in-window scope ---
    win = ito_reference_profile().window_s
    good = dmax <= win + 1e-9
    P("C7  delays inside measured window", good, f"max delay {dmax:g}s vs window {win:g}s")
    ok &= good

    # --- C9 hold-quantisation injectivity + dt vs delay spacing ---
    ns = [int(round(d / args.dt)) for d in args.delays]
    inj = len(set(ns)) == len(ns)
    dd = np.diff(sorted(args.delays))
    # a single-delay run (cost probe, dose mode) has no spacing to check
    minsp = float(dd.min()) if dd.size else float("inf")
    sp_ok = args.dt <= minsp / 2.0 + 1e-12
    P("C9  hold quantisation injective", inj and sp_ok,
      f"n={ns} distinct={len(set(ns))}/{len(ns)}, dt={args.dt:g}<=min spacing/2="
      + ("n/a (single delay)" if not dd.size else f"{minsp/2:g}"))
    ok &= inj and sp_ok
    rec["realised_delays_s"] = [n * args.dt for n in ns]

    # --- C5/C6/C18 kernel fidelity, numerical headroom, no sub-dt modes ---
    eps = float(torch.finfo(torch.float64 if args.float64 else torch.float32).eps)
    print(f"  kernel + headroom  (k={args.k}, span={tuple(args.span)}, "
          f"tmax_tau={tmax_tau_for(args.delays, REF['tau_kww']):.2f}, eps={eps:.3g})")
    kern_ok = head_ok = subdt_ok = True
    for arm in ARMS_ALL[:3]:
        p = profile_for(arm)
        tmx = tmax_tau_for(args.delays, p.tau_kww)
        taus, w, r2 = kohlrausch_modes(p.tau_kww, p.beta, k=args.k,
                                       span_decades=tuple(args.span), tmax_tau=tmx)
        nz = int((w > 1e-12).sum())
        qk = q_kernel(args.delays, taus, w, w.sum())
        qe = q_exact(args.delays, p.tau_kww, p.beta)
        worst = float(np.abs(qk / qe - 1).max())
        gain = (1.0 - REF["rho"]) / REF["rho"]
        # Headroom over the nonzero delays (at D=0 every arm has q=1 by construction).
        # Indexed by a mask, not by qk[1:], so a single-delay run does not reduce an
        # empty array.
        nzm = np.asarray(args.delays, float) > 0
        qh = qk[nzm] if nzm.any() else qk
        hmarg = float((gain * qh).min() / (100 * eps))
        fast = float(w[taus < args.dt].sum() / w.sum())
        kern_ok &= worst < 0.05
        head_ok &= hmarg > 1.0
        subdt_ok &= fast <= 1e-12
        print(f"    {arm:<13s} nnz={nz:2d} r2={r2:.6f} worst|q_k/q_KWW-1|={worst*100:5.2f}% "
              f"headroom(min gain*q)/(100 eps)={hmarg:8.2f}x  amp in modes faster than dt="
              f"{fast:.3g}")
        rec[f"kernel_{arm}"] = dict(nnz=nz, r2=r2, worst_excess=worst,
                                    headroom_x=hmarg, subdt_amp=fast)
    P("C5  kernel fidelity <5%", kern_ok, "per arm, per scored delay")
    thin = [a_ for a_ in ARMS_ALL[:3] if rec[f"kernel_{a_}"]["headroom_x"] < 10.0]
    P("C6  float headroom gain*q>100eps", head_ok,
      "margin printed above; <1.0x means the control is annihilated by rounding"
      + (f"\n         *** THIN (<10x): {thin} -- cross-check with --float64 before "
         f"reporting the longest delay ***" if thin else ""))
    P("C18 no mode faster than dt", subdt_ok,
      "so the frozen D=0 full scale cannot be inflated for one arm only")
    ok &= kern_ok and head_ok and subdt_ok

    # --- build two arms at the same seed for the runtime controls ---
    mk = lambda a: make_cell(a, n_in, ncls, args, args.seed0, nat=nat)
    c_k, c_e, c_n = mk("kww"), mk("exp_meanlife"), mk("no_trace")

    # --- C13 config identity / C14 device identity across arms ---
    good = (c_k.cfg_id == c_e.cfg_id == c_n.cfg_id)
    P("C13 config hash identical across arms", good, c_k.cfg_id)
    ok &= good
    good = (c_k.dev_id == c_e.dev_id == c_n.dev_id)
    P("C12a device realisation identical", good, c_k.dev_id)
    ok &= good
    good = all(torch.equal(a_, b_) for a_, b_ in zip(c_k.params, c_e.params)) and \
        len(c_k.params) == len(c_e.params)
    P("C12b init weights identical", good,
      f"all {len(c_k.params)} trainable tensors, arm vs arm")
    ok &= good

    xb = xtr[:, :8]
    # --- C2 silent input with the row gated must be bitwise 0 ---
    with torch.no_grad():
        z0 = c_k.vs.init_state(4)
        nsyn = c_k.n_syn_in                    # The synapse's own width, not the input's
        o_g, _ = c_k.vs(torch.zeros(4, nsyn), z0, phase="read", gate_bias_row=True)
        o_o, _ = c_k.vs(torch.zeros(4, nsyn), z0, phase="read", gate_bias_row=False)
    good = float(o_g.abs().max().item()) == 0.0
    P("C2  silent-input, row GATED", good,
      f"max|out| = {o_g.abs().max().item():.8f}  (row OPEN: {o_o.abs().max().item():.6f} "
      f"-- a digital zero is not a gate)")
    ok &= good
    rec["silent_gated"] = float(o_g.abs().max().item())
    rec["silent_open"] = float(o_o.abs().max().item())

    # --- C12c grid identical at write and at read within one trial ---
    with torch.no_grad():
        G1 = c_k.layer._grid_and_params(torch.device("cpu"))[0].clone()
        z = c_k.state_after_write(xb)
        G2 = c_k.layer._grid_and_params(torch.device("cpu"))[0]
    good = torch.equal(G1, G2)
    P("C12c G(write) == G(read)", good, "bitwise, within a trial")
    ok &= good

    # --- C8 hold exactness  /  C10 monotone decay  /  C11 bias row silent ---
    with torch.no_grad():
        n = 7
        zh = c_k.vs.hold(z, n * args.dt)
        zs = z
        mono = True
        for _ in range(n):
            zn, prev = None, zs
            _, zs = c_k.vs(torch.zeros(xb.shape[1], c_k.n_syn_in), zs, phase="hold",
                           gate_bias_row=True, compute_out=False)
            mono &= bool((zs <= prev + 1e-7).all().item())
        dif = float((zh - zs).abs().max().item())
        zmag = float(zs.abs().max().item())
        qbias = float(c_k.vs.read_trace(zh)[:, -1].abs().max().item())
        zbias = float(zh[:, -1, :].abs().max().item())
    # Relative tolerance: float32 carries ~1.2e-7 relative precision, so an absolute
    # threshold is a statement about the state magnitude, not about hold()'s exactness.
    rel = dif / max(zmag, 1e-30)
    good = rel < 1e-5
    P("C8  hold() == stepped hold", good,
      f"max|diff| = {dif:.3g} at max|z| = {zmag:.4g} -> relative {rel:.2e} "
      f"(< 1e-5 = float32 noise) over {n} steps")
    ok &= good
    rec["hold_rel_err"] = rel
    P("C10 z non-increasing in hold", mono, "element-wise, every step")
    ok &= mono
    good = (qbias == 0.0) and (zbias == 0.0)
    P("C11 bias-row trace exactly 0", good, f"max|z_bias| = {zbias:g}, max|q_bias| = {qbias:g}")
    ok &= good

    # --- C1 no-trace arm has exactly zero between-sample spread ---
    # The load-bearing control.  With gain = 0 nothing about the sample can reach the
    # output, so the between-sample spread must be bitwise zero -- at the array and at
    # whatever readout sits on top of it.  If any downstream state (a membrane, an
    # accumulator, a stale calibration) were carrying the sample, this is what would
    # catch it.
    with torch.no_grad():
        zn_ = c_n.state_after_write(xb)
        on_, os_, ot_ = c_n.read(zn_)
        spread = float(on_.std(0).max().item())
        zk_ = c_k.state_after_write(xb)
        ok_, oks, okt = c_k.read(zk_)
    good = spread == 0.0
    P("C1  no_trace between-sample spread", good,
      f"max std over samples = {spread:g} (kww arm: {ok_.std(0).max().item():.4g})")
    ok &= good
    rec["no_trace_spread"] = spread
    rec["kww_spread"] = float(ok_.std(0).max().item())
    print(f"       static |read| = {oks.abs().mean().item():.4g}, "
          f"trace |read| = {okt.abs().mean().item():.4g}, "
          f"trace/static = {okt.abs().mean().item()/max(oks.abs().mean().item(),1e-30):.3g}")

    # --- C15 batch independence ---
    with torch.no_grad():
        zb = c_k.state_after_write(xb)
        ob, _, _ = c_k.read(zb)
        singles = []
        for i in range(xb.shape[1]):
            zi = c_k.state_after_write(xb[:, i:i + 1])
            oi, _, _ = c_k.read(zi)
            singles.append(oi)
        d = float((ob - torch.cat(singles, 0)).abs().max().item())
    good = d < 1e-5
    P("C15 batch independence", good,
      f"max|batched - one-at-a-time| = {d:.3g} at output scale {ob.abs().mean().item():.3g}")
    ok &= good

    # --- C16 gauge: scaling all weights leaves G identical, scales out by the same factor ---
    with torch.no_grad():
        G_a = c_k.layer._grid_and_params(torch.device("cpu"))[0].clone()
        o_a, _, _ = c_k.read(c_k.state_after_write(xb))
        c_k.layer.weights.mul_(100.0)
        G_b = c_k.layer._grid_and_params(torch.device("cpu"))[0].clone()
        o_b, _, _ = c_k.read(c_k.state_after_write(xb))
        c_k.layer.weights.div_(100.0)
        dG = float((G_a - G_b).abs().max().item())
        ratio = float((o_b / o_a).mean().item())
    good = (dG < 1e-8) and abs(ratio - 100.0) < 1.0
    P("C16 max|w| is a pure gauge", good,
      f"max|dG| = {dG:.3g} at c=100, out ratio = {ratio:.4f} "
      f"(=> it is projected back every step)")
    ok &= good

    # --- C19 empirical chance floor, not 1/ncls ---
    f_te, hist_te = empirical_floor(yte, ncls)
    upper = cp_upper(int(round(f_te * len(yte))), len(yte))
    print(f"  [INFO] C19 chance floor                 1/ncls = {100/ncls:.3f}%, EMPIRICAL "
          f"majority = {f_te*100:.3f}%, upper 95% CP bound = {upper*100:.3f}% "
          f"(n_test={len(yte)})")
    rec.update(floor=f_te, floor_cp95=upper, test_hist=hist_te, n_test=len(yte))

    # --- C22 state sufficiency: z is the only thing that crosses the delay ---
    # Permuting the synapse state across the batch must permute the decisions identically.
    # Any other carrier -- a membrane driven during the write, an accumulator, a per-sample
    # calibration -- breaks this exactly.  Applies to both readouts.
    # Run it noise-free: the read-noise tensor is drawn per row and is not itself
    # permuted, so with noise on this control would compare two different noise
    # realisations and fail by exactly the noise (measured 0.094 at logit scale 3.8).
    _noise_save = args.noise
    args.noise = 0.0
    try:
        c_ = c_k
        c_.calibrate(xtr, n_cal=min(64, xtr.shape[1]), delay=0.0)
        with torch.no_grad():
            zz = c_.state_after_write(xb)
            perm = torch.tensor([3, 0, 1, 2, 7, 4, 5, 6][:xb.shape[1]])
            la = c_._logits_from_state(zz)[perm]
            lb = c_._logits_from_state(zz[perm])
            d22 = float((la - lb).abs().max().item())
    finally:
        args.noise = _noise_save
    good = d22 <= 1e-5 * max(float(la.abs().max().item()), 1.0)
    P("C22 z is the only delay-crossing state", good,
      f"max|logits(z)[perm] - logits(z[perm])| = {d22:.3g} at logit scale "
      f"{float(la.abs().max().item()):.3g}")
    ok &= good
    rec["state_sufficiency_err"] = d22

    # --- C21 nothing undeclared and stateful downstream ---
    # A LIF on the read path is the point of readout='spiking', so the assertion is
    # readout-specific: the analog level must have NO membrane at all; the spiking level
    # must have exactly the model's own LIF neurons and no homeostat/Norm, and its
    # membranes must not span the delay (that is C22 above, plus the structural fact that
    # the hold computes no output and touches no membrane).
    names = [type(m).__name__ for m in list(self_modules(c_k))]
    forbidden = (("Leaky", "Homeo", "Norm", "LIF", "Dropout") if args.readout == "analog"
                 else ("Homeo", "Norm", "Dropout"))
    bad = [n for n in names if any(s in n for s in forbidden)]
    P(f"C21 read path is declared ({args.readout})", not bad,
      f"modules = {sorted(set(names))}"
      + ("" if args.readout == "analog" else
         f"; hold phase drives NO membrane (compute_out=False, LIF init AFTER the hold)"))
    ok &= not bad
    # Trace state is threaded, not stored on the object
    good = not any(torch.is_tensor(v) for v in vars(c_k.vs).values())
    P("C21b synapse holds no tensor state", good, "state is threaded explicitly")
    ok &= good

    if args.readout == "spiking":
        # --- C23 the spiking readout is the real model, and it is not vacuous ---
        lif_is_models_own = (c_k.out_lif is (c_k.net.lif3 if c_k.kind == "conv"
                                             else c_k.net.lif2))
        vol_feeds_lif = c_k.vs.base is c_k.net.fc1
        P("C23 real model, volatile -> LIF", lif_is_models_own and vol_feeds_lif,
          f"{c_k.model_name}.fc1 ({type(c_k.net.fc1).__name__} "
          f"{c_k.n_syn_in}->{c_k.n_syn_out}) wrapped as VolatileSynapse; its current feeds "
          f"{'lif3' if c_k.kind == 'conv' else 'lif1->fc2->lif2'} "
          f"({type(c_k.out_lif).__name__}, beta={float(c_k.out_lif.beta):.4f}, "
          f"thr={float(c_k.out_lif.threshold):.3g}); decision = spk.sum(0) over R="
          f"{c_k.R} probe steps")
        ok &= lif_is_models_own and vol_feeds_lif
        rec["model"] = c_k.model_name
        d = c_k.diag
        hr = d.get("hidden_rate", float("nan"))
        # Both the calibrated interface and the layer the decision is read from must vary.
        nonvac = (float(d.get("op_count_sd", 0.0)) > 0.25
                  and float(d.get("op_out_sd", 0.0)) > 0.02
                  and (np.isnan(hr) or hr > 0.01))
        P("C23b readout is not vacuous", nonvac,
          f"hidden spk rate = {hr:.4f} (nan = dense path, no conv), D=0 driven count "
          f"{d.get('op_count_mean', float('nan')):.2f}+-{d.get('op_count_sd', float('nan')):.2f}"
          f" of {c_k.R}, DECISION count {d.get('op_out_mean', float('nan')):.2f}"
          f"+-{d.get('op_out_sd', float('nan')):.2f} (zero-count frac "
          f"{d.get('op_out_zerofrac', float('nan')):.2f}), "
          f"pedestal/spread = {d.get('pedestal_over_spread', float('nan')):.2f}"
          + ("" if nonvac else "  *** a saturated or silent readout scores the argmax-tie "
             "floor = chance at EVERY delay, which would read as a clean null ***"))
        ok &= nonvac
        rec["spiking_diag"] = {k: v for k, v in d.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
        # --- C24 downstream in-array bias row (dense path only) ---
        if c_k.kind == "dense":
            with torch.no_grad():
                o2 = c_k.net.fc2(torch.zeros(4, c_k.n_syn_out))
            off = float(o2.abs().max().item())
            beta_m = float(c_k.out_lif.beta)
            u_win = off * (1.0 - beta_m ** c_k.R) / (1.0 - beta_m)
            thr = float(c_k.out_lif.threshold)
            good = u_win < thr
            P("C24 downstream bias row sub-threshold", good,
              f"fc2 zero-input offset max = {off:.4g}; over the R={c_k.R} probe window it "
              f"integrates to {u_win:.4g} vs threshold {thr:g}.  It is class-independent "
              f"and common-mode across arms (C1 = 0 proves it carries no label), but above "
              f"threshold it would spike on its own")
            rec["fc2_offset"] = off
            rec["fc2_U_window"] = u_win
            ok &= good

    # --- re-timing declaration ---
    real = REAL_DUR_S.get(args.dataset)
    pres = T * args.dt
    if real:
        print(f"  [INFO] re-timing                        {args.dataset}: T={T} x dt="
              f"{args.dt:g}s = {pres:.3f}s presentation vs {real:.4f}s measured recording "
              f"= {pres/real:.2f}x RE-TIMED (declared, not hidden)")
        rec["retiming_x"] = pres / real
    print(f"  [INFO] device                           tau={REF['tau_kww']}s "
          f"beta={REF['beta']} <t>={REF['mean_lifetime']}s rho={REF['rho']} "
          f"gain=(1-rho)/rho={c_k.gain_nominal:.3f}")
    rec["structural_ok"] = bool(ok)
    out["controls"] = rec
    return ok


def self_modules(cell):
    """Every module the decision passes through, so C21 can inspect it."""
    if cell.readout_kind == "spiking":
        for m in cell.net.modules():
            yield m
        return
    yield cell.readout
    for m in cell.readout.modules():
        yield m


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main curve
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def run_curve(args, data, out, arms=None, delays=None, tag="main",
              gain_override=None, tau=None, beta=None, rho=None,
              shuffle_labels=False, epochs=None):
    xtr, ytr, xte, yte, T, n_in, ncls, nat = data
    arms = arms or args.arms
    delays = delays if delays is not None else args.delays
    epochs = args.epochs if epochs is None else epochs
    xtr, ytr, xva, yva = split_val(xtr, ytr, args.val_frac, args.seed0)
    floor, _h = empirical_floor(yte, ncls)
    cp = cp_upper(int(round(floor * len(yte))), len(yte))
    rows = []
    probe_cell = make_cell(arms[0], n_in, ncls, args, args.seed0, nat=nat,
                           delays=delays)
    width = (f"cols={args.cols}" if args.readout == "analog" else
             f"syn={probe_cell.n_syn_in}->{probe_cell.n_syn_out} "
             f"({probe_cell.model_name}, --cols is IGNORED at this level)")
    print(f"\n{tag.upper()}:  {args.dataset}  readout={args.readout.upper()}  "
          f"n_train={xtr.shape[1]} n_test={xte.shape[1]} "
          f"T={T} n_in={n_in} {width} ncls={ncls}")
    print(f"  dt={args.dt:g}s  k={args.k}  span={tuple(args.span)}  v_probe={args.v_probe} "
          f"noise={args.noise:g} x frozen D=0 {args.scale_mode}  epochs={epochs} "
          f"bs={args.bs} lr={args.lr}  seeds={args.seeds}  noise_reps={args.noise_reps}"
          + (f"  probe_steps={args.probe_steps}" if args.readout == "spiking" else ""))
    print(f"  empirical floor {floor*100:.2f}%  (upper 95% CP bound {cp*100:.2f}%) "
          f"-- accuracy must beat the BOUND, not 1/ncls={100/ncls:.2f}%")
    if args.readout == "spiking":
        # Trap 4, and it is much sharper at this level than at the analog one.  measured on
        # N-MNIST: the spiking cell first collapses (all neurons saturate -> every sample an
        # argmax tie -> exactly chance), sits on that plateau for ~100 epochs, and only then
        # separates: 7.9% at epoch 0, 11.3% at 5, 19.9% at 40, 25.9% at 90, 41.0% at 190 and
        # still rising.  A short budget therefore reports chance for a readout that is not
        # at chance, which would read as "the stretched kernel is invisible to a threshold"
        # -- a conclusion manufactured by the optimiser budget.
        n_upd = epochs * max(int(np.ceil(xtr.shape[1] / args.bs)), 1)
        if n_upd < 1500 or args.patience < 25:
            print(f"  [WARN] SPIKING BUDGET: {n_upd} updates, patience {args.patience}. "
                  f"MEASURED need: >=1500 updates AND patience >=25, because this level "
                  f"plateaus at chance for ~100 epochs before separating. Below that, read "
                  f"the spiking numbers as a LOWER BOUND, never as a null.")
    hdr = f"  {'arm':>13} {'D(s)':>7} {'acc%':>7} {'sd':>5} {'>floor':>6} " \
          f"{'conv':>5} {'bestEp':>6} {'vloss':>6} {'loss0':>6} {'lossN':>6} " \
          f"{'ties':>5} {'nonf':>4} " \
          f"{'collapse':>8} {'scale':>9} {'q(D)':>8}" \
          + (f" {'spk/N':>6} {'spkSD':>6} {'zero%':>6} {'hidR':>6}"
             if args.readout == "spiking" else "")
    print(hdr)
    for arm in arms:
        p = profile_for(arm, tau=tau, beta=beta, rho=rho)
        for D in delays:
            accs_rep, trajs, flags = [], [], []
            for s in range(args.seeds):
                c = make_cell(arm, n_in, ncls, args, args.seed0 + s,
                              gain_override=gain_override, tau=tau, beta=beta, rho=rho,
                              delays=delays, nat=nat).calibrate(xtr, delay=D)
                traj, nan_step, info = c.train(
                    xtr, ytr, D, epochs, args.bs, args.lr, shuffle_labels=shuffle_labels,
                    xval=xva, yval=yva, patience=args.patience)
                _plateau, rel = converged(traj)
                conv = info["converged"]
                gdrift = float(c.layer.weights.abs().max().item()) / c.w0
                assert 0.95 < gdrift < 1.05, f"gauge drift {gdrift}"
                assert float(c.layer.bias.abs().max().item()) == 0.0, "bias must stay 0"
                assert float(c.layer.bias.abs().max().item()) < \
                    float(c.layer.weights.abs().max().item()) + 1e-30
                ev = c.evaluate(xte, yte, D, args.bs, noise_reps=args.noise_reps)
                acc, nonf, ties, hist = ev[0], ev[1], ev[2], ev[3]
                reps = ev[4] if len(ev) > 4 else [acc]
                accs_rep += list(reps)
                trajs.append(traj)
                # Predicted-class distribution.  The failure this detects is a point mass
                # (prior collapse / tie collapse), so the statistic is the max class share,
                # not the min: a 10-class cell at 70% legitimately has small min shares and
                # flagging it would make the diagnostic noise.  min share is kept in the JSON.
                tot = max(sum(hist), 1)
                mx = max(hist) / tot if sum(hist) else 1.0
                mn = min(hist) / tot if sum(hist) else 0.0
                flags.append(dict(seed=args.seed0 + s, conv=conv, rel=rel, nan_step=nan_step,
                                  plateau=_plateau, left_plateau=info.get("left_plateau"),
                                  best_epoch=info["best_epoch"],
                                  best_val=info.get("best_val"), val_traj=info["val"],
                                  epochs_run=info.get("epochs_run"),
