                                  val_tie_frac=info.get("val_tie_frac"),
                                  val_max_share=info.get("val_max_share"),
                                  ties=ties, nonfinite=nonf, pred_hist=hist,
                                  min_pred_rate=mn, max_pred_rate=mx,
                                  gauge=gdrift, scale=c.scale,
                                  scale_src=c.scale_src, spread0=c.spread0,
                                  static=c.static_absmean, trace=c.trace_absmean,
                                  dev_id=c.dev_id, cfg_id=c.cfg_id,
                                  diag={k: v for k, v in c.diag.items()
                                        if not k.startswith("_")}))
            m = float(np.nanmean(accs_rep))
            sd = float(np.nanstd(accs_rep))
            nconv = sum(1 for f in flags if f["conv"])
            ties = sum(f["ties"] for f in flags)
            nonf = sum(max(f["nonfinite"], 0) for f in flags)
            collapse = max(f["max_pred_rate"] for f in flags)
            qd = float(q_exact([D], p.tau_kww, p.beta)[0])
            l0 = np.mean([t[0] for t in trajs if t])
            lN = np.mean([np.mean(t[-max(len(t)//10, 1):]) for t in trajs if t])
            print(f"  {arm:>13} {D:>7g} {m*100:>7.2f} {sd*100:>5.2f} "
                  f"{'YES' if m > cp else 'no':>6} {nconv}/{args.seeds:<3} "
                  f"{np.mean([f['best_epoch'] for f in flags]):>6.1f} "
                  f"{np.mean([f['best_val'] or np.nan for f in flags]):>6.3f} "
                  f"{l0:>6.3f} {lN:>6.3f} {ties:>5d} {nonf:>4d} "
                  f"{collapse:>8.3f}{'!' if collapse > 0.5 else ' '} "
                  f"{flags[0]['scale']:>9.3g} {qd:>8.5f}"
                  + ("" if args.readout != "spiking" else
                     " {:>6.2f} {:>6.2f} {:>6.1f} {:>6.3f}".format(
                         np.mean([f["diag"].get("out_spk_mean", np.nan) for f in flags]),
                         np.mean([f["diag"].get("out_spk_sd", np.nan) for f in flags]),
                         100 * np.mean([f["diag"].get("zero_spk_frac", np.nan)
                                        for f in flags]),
                         np.mean([f["diag"].get("hidden_rate", np.nan) for f in flags]))),
                  flush=True)
            rows.append(dict(tag=tag, arm=arm, D=float(D), acc=m, sd=sd,
                             reps=accs_rep, floor=floor, cp95=cp, q=qd,
                             n_converged=nconv, flags=flags,
                             loss_traj={str(f["seed"]): t for f, t in zip(flags, trajs)}))
    out.setdefault("rows", []).extend(rows)

    # --- C1b the load-bearing control: no_trace must sit at chance at every delay ---
    nt = [r for r in rows if r["arm"] == "no_trace"]
    if nt:
        bad = [(r["D"], round(r["acc"] * 100, 2)) for r in nt if r["acc"] > r["cp95"]]
        print(f"\n  [{'PASS' if not bad else 'FAIL'}] C1b no_trace at chance          "
              f"{len(nt) - len(bad)}/{len(nt)} delays at or below the {cp*100:.2f}% CP bound"
              + (f"\n         *** {bad} ARE ABOVE CHANCE WITH gain=0: the benchmark is "
                 f"BROKEN, some path other than the trace carries the label ***"
                 if bad else ""))
        out["no_trace_ok"] = not bad
    else:
        print("\n  [WARN] C1b no_trace arm was not run -- the benchmark's own null is missing")

    # --- C-conv: an unconverged comparator is the trap that already invalidated a headline ---
    # The null arm is excluded: it is built to sit at the floor, so "did it find an
    # optimum" is not a meaningful question for it (its test is C1b, on accuracy).
    unconv = [(r["arm"], r["D"], r["n_converged"]) for r in rows
              if r["n_converged"] < args.seeds and r["arm"] != "no_trace"]
    all_conv = not unconv
    n_rel = sum(1 for r in rows if r["arm"] != "no_trace")
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if all_conv else 'FAIL'}] C-conv every cell converged      "
          f"{n_rel - len(unconv)}/{n_rel} non-null cells early-stopped at a "
          f"VALIDATION optimum (patience {args.patience})"
          + ("" if all_conv else
             f"\n         *** {len(unconv)} cells hit the epoch cap before validation "
             f"loss stopped improving, so their accuracy is a threshold on the OPTIMISER "
             f"BUDGET, not on physics (this exact trap turned a published 1.67x into an "
             f"artefact). Raise --epochs. ***"))
    stuck = [(r["arm"], r["D"]) for r in rows
             if any(f.get("left_plateau") is False for f in r["flags"])]
    if stuck:
        print(f"         *** {len(stuck)} cells NEVER LEFT the uniform-predictor plateau "
              f"(val loss = ln ncls): {stuck}.  Those are UNDETERMINED, not nulls -- the "
              f"readout may or may not carry the label at that delay, and only a bigger "
              f"budget can tell. ***")
    out[f"stuck_at_uniform_{tag}"] = stuck
    out[f"converged_{tag}"] = bool(all_conv)
    out[f"dmax_reportable_{tag}"] = bool(all_conv and out.get("no_trace_ok", True))

    # --- D_max table, every threshold, with bootstrap CI ---
    banner = ("(REPORTABLE)" if out[f"dmax_reportable_{tag}"]
              else "(*** NOT REPORTABLE: see the FAILs above ***)")
    print(f"\n  D_max {banner} interpolated on a monotone fit, no first-failure break; "
          f"pre-registered frac={args.dmax_frac}")
    print(f"  {'arm':>13} " + " ".join(f"{'frac='+format(f,'.2f'):>22}" for f in THRESH_GRID))
    dtab = {}
    for arm in arms:
        cells = [r for r in rows if r["arm"] == arm]
        dl = [r["D"] for r in cells]
        mean_curve = [r["acc"] for r in cells]
        R = np.array([r["reps"] for r in cells], float).T          # (n_rep, n_delay)
        line = []
        for f in THRESH_GRID:
            dm, cen = dmax_interp(dl, mean_curve, cells[0]["floor"], f,
                                  cp=cells[0]["cp95"])
            lo, hi = dmax_boot(dl, R, cells[0]["floor"], f, cp=cells[0]["cp95"])
            line.append(f"{dm:>7.1f}s[{lo:>5.1f},{hi:>5.1f}]{'C' if cen else ' '}")
            dtab[(arm, f)] = (dm, lo, hi, cen)
        print(f"  {arm:>13} " + " ".join(f"{c:>22}" for c in line))
    out.setdefault("dmax", {})[tag] = {f"{a}|{f}": v for (a, f), v in dtab.items()}
    if "kww" in arms and "exp_meanlife" in arms:
        print("  ratio kww/exp_meanlife: " + "  ".join(
            f"frac={f:.2f}: {dtab[('kww',f)][0]/max(dtab[('exp_meanlife',f)][0],1e-9):.3f}x"
            for f in THRESH_GRID))
        print("  NOTE the ordering is threshold-dependent and can FLIP; only frac="
              f"{args.dmax_frac} is pre-registered.")
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extra control modes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def mode_power(args, data, out):
    """Power test for the probe-independence control: a class-dependent probe with gain=0
    (no device memory at all) must score high.  If it does not, the clean uniform-probe
    result proves nothing, because the test could not have detected leakage."""
    xtr, ytr, xte, yte, T, n_in, ncls, nat = data
    floor, _ = empirical_floor(yte, ncls)
    print("\nPOWER TEST (leak scout): probe = the sample itself, gain = 0.")
    print("  If this does NOT score far above the floor, the probe-independence control is "
          "vacuous.")

    base = SpikingCell if args.readout == "spiking" else Cell

    class Leaky(base):
        """Overrides only the probe, so the leak is the single change under test.

        The probe is the sample's own final write drive -- the encoded input on the dense
        path, the conv stack's own last-frame spikes on the conv path -- so it is exactly
        the maximal leak at the synapse's own input width.  Truncating the flat input
        instead hands the readout only the first 32 of 578 features
        and the test then fails for lack of signal rather than for lack of leakage.
        """

        def probe(self, B, n_in=None):
            p = self._last_write_u                   # Class-dependent: forbidden by design
            assert p.shape[0] == B and p.shape[1] == self.n_syn_in
            return p * 1.0

    for D in (0.0, max(args.delays)):
        c = Leaky("no_trace", n_in, ncls, args, args.seed0, nat=nat)
        c.calibrate(xtr, delay=D)
        traj, _, _info = c.train(xtr, ytr, D, args.epochs, args.bs, args.lr)
        acc = c.evaluate(xte, yte, D, args.bs, noise_reps=1)[0]
        # The criterion is statistical, not a fixed margin: a fixed +15 pp was calibrated
        # on the analog readout, and applying it to the spiking one confuses "the leak is
        # undetectable" with "this readout is weaker" -- which is the very thing the
        # readout factor exists to measure.  measured: the same maximal leak scores 64.00%
        # Behind the analog readout and 16.16% behind the spiking one.
        cpb = cp_upper(int(round(floor * len(yte))), len(yte))
        good = acc > cpb
        strong = acc > floor + 0.15
        print(f"  [{'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'}] C3-power  D={D:>6g}s  gain=0, "
              f"class-dependent probe -> {acc*100:.2f}%  (floor {floor*100:.2f}%, "
              f"CP bound {cpb*100:.2f}%)"
              + ("  => the control CAN detect leakage" if strong else
                 "  => detectable but WEAKLY: a probe leak of this size would clear the "
                 "chance bound yet stay far below the legitimate D=0 accuracy, so on this "
                 "readout the probe-independence assertion carries less power" if good else
                 "  => NO POWER at this budget: the test cannot distinguish 'no leak' from "
                 "'not trained' (readout=spiking needs >=1500 updates)"))
        out.setdefault("power", []).append(dict(D=D, acc=acc, floor=floor, cp95=cpb,
                                               pass_=good, strong=strong))


def mode_shuffle(args, data, out):
    """Shuffled-label control: one assertion that catches every leakage path at once."""
    print("\nSHUFFLED-LABEL CONTROL: every arm retrained on permuted labels; accuracy must "
          "sit inside the chance band at EVERY delay, including D=0.")
    print("  This control needs a LARGE eval set: a permutation of a small train set leaves "
          "residual\n  label-feature correlation.  MEASURED on N-MNIST/kww at D=0: 16.80% vs "
          "a 16.42% bound\n  (marginal FAIL) at n_test=256, and a clean PASS at n_test=2000. "
          "Do not run it below ~2000.")
    if args.n_test < 1000:
        print(f"  [WARN] n_test={args.n_test} is too small for this control to be "
              f"interpretable.")
    rows = run_curve(args, data, out, tag="shuffled", shuffle_labels=True)
    floor = rows[0]["floor"]
    cp = rows[0]["cp95"]
    bad = [(r["arm"], r["D"], r["acc"]) for r in rows if r["acc"] > cp]
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if not bad else 'FAIL'}] C4 shuffled labels          "
          f"{len(bad)} of {len(rows)} cells above the {cp*100:.2f}% CP bound"
          + (f"  -> {bad}" if bad else ""))
    out["shuffle_ok"] = not bad


def mode_dose(args, data, out):
    """Dose-response on the trace amplitude: the one signature no offset, prior, tie or
    normalisation artefact can reproduce."""
    xtr, ytr, xte, yte, T, n_in, ncls, nat = data
    gmax = (1.0 - REF["rho"]) / REF["rho"]
    gains = [0.0, gmax / 8, gmax / 4, gmax / 2, gmax]
    D = args.dose_delay
    floor, _ = empirical_floor(yte, ncls)
    cp = cp_upper(int(round(floor * len(yte))), len(yte))
    print(f"\nDOSE-RESPONSE at D={D:g}s  (gain sweep, all else bitwise identical)")
    if args.readout == "spiking":
        print("  [WARN] readout=spiking needs >=1500 updates per cell here too, or every "
              "gain\n         reads as chance and the dose response is flat for want of "
              "training.")
    print(f"  The noise full scale is FROZEN at the nominal gain and reused at every gain, so")
    print(f"  a smaller trace is measured against the SAME noise floor rather than against a")
    print(f"  floor that shrinks with it.")
    # Frozen reference scale at the nominal (measured) gain
    ref = make_cell("kww", n_in, ncls, args, args.seed0, nat=nat).calibrate(xtr, delay=D)
    S = ref.scale
    print(f"  {'gain':>8} {'acc%':>7} {'sd':>5}   floor={floor*100:.2f}%  "
          f"cp95={cp*100:.2f}%  frozen scale={S:.4g}")
    accs, sds = [], []
    for g in gains:
        a = []
        for s in range(args.seeds):
            c = make_cell("kww", n_in, ncls, args, args.seed0 + s, nat=nat,
                          gain_override=g).calibrate(xtr, scale_from=S, delay=D)
            c.train(xtr, ytr, D, args.epochs, args.bs, args.lr)
            a.append(c.evaluate(xte, yte, D, args.bs, noise_reps=args.noise_reps)[0])
        accs.append(float(np.nanmean(a)))
        sds.append(float(np.nanstd(a)))
        print(f"  {g:>8.3f} {accs[-1]*100:>7.2f} {sds[-1]*100:>5.2f}", flush=True)
    tol = max(0.02, 2 * float(np.max(sds)))
    mono = all(accs[i] <= accs[i + 1] + tol for i in range(len(accs) - 1))
    zero_ok = accs[0] <= cp
    rise = accs[-1] - accs[0]
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if mono else 'FAIL'}] C17-dose monotone in gain      "
          f"(tolerance {tol*100:.2f} pp = max(2 pp, 2 sd))")
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if zero_ok else 'FAIL'}] C17-dose returns to chance at gain=0")
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if rise > 0.15 else 'FAIL'}] C17-dose graded response       "
          f"gain 0 -> {gains[-1]:.3f} lifts accuracy by {rise*100:.2f} pp")
    out["dose"] = dict(gains=gains, accs=accs, sds=sds, monotone=mono, zero_ok=zero_ok,
                       rise=rise, D=D, frozen_scale=S, tol=tol)


def mode_uncertainty(args, data, out):
    """Parameter-uncertainty propagation over the corners of (rho, tau, beta) +- 1 SD."""
    print("\nPARAMETER UNCERTAINTY: D_max recomputed at the corners of rho+-0.0032, "
          "tau+-0.938s, beta+-0.0148")
    corners = []
    for st in (-1, 1):
        for sb in (-1, 1):
            for sr in (-1, 1):
                corners.append((REF["tau_kww"] + st * REF["tau_sd"],
                                REF["beta"] + sb * REF["beta_sd"],
                                REF["rho"] + sr * REF["rho_sd"]))
    for tau, beta, rho in corners:
        tag = f"unc_t{tau:.3f}_b{beta:.4f}_r{rho:.4f}"
        run_curve(args, data, out, arms=["kww", "exp_meanlife"], tag=tag,
                  tau=tau, beta=beta, rho=rho)


def mode_convergence(args, data, out):
    """Convergence assertion: D_max must not move when the step budget is quadrupled."""
    print("\nCONVERGENCE CHECK: the same curve at 1x and 4x the epoch budget.")
    r1 = run_curve(args, data, out, tag="conv1x", epochs=args.epochs)
    r4 = run_curve(args, data, out, tag="conv4x", epochs=args.epochs * 4)
    for arm in args.arms:
        c1 = [r for r in r1 if r["arm"] == arm]
        c4 = [r for r in r4 if r["arm"] == arm]
        d1, _ = dmax_interp([r["D"] for r in c1], [r["acc"] for r in c1],
                            c1[0]["floor"], args.dmax_frac, cp=c1[0]["cp95"])
        d4, _ = dmax_interp([r["D"] for r in c4], [r["acc"] for r in c4],
                            c4[0]["floor"], args.dmax_frac, cp=c4[0]["cp95"])
        step = np.diff(sorted(args.delays)).min()
        good = abs(d4 - d1) <= step
        print(f"  [{'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'}] C6-conv {arm:<14} D_max {d1:.1f}s -> "
              f"{d4:.1f}s  (must move <= one grid step {step:g}s)")
        out.setdefault("convergence", {})[arm] = dict(d1x=d1, d4x=d4, ok=bool(good))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """The instrument's own argument parser, exposed as a normal function.

    Import this rather than recovering the ``ap.add_argument`` block from this file as
    text: a string-sliced copy breaks on any reformatting, and breaks outright when a
    default stops referring to a module-level constant.
    """
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--dataset", default="shd",
                    choices=["shd", "nmnist", "dvsgesture", "seqmnist"])
    ap.add_argument("--arms", default=",".join(ARMS_ALL))
    ap.add_argument("--delays", default=",".join(str(d) for d in PREREG["delays_s"]),
                    help="device SECONDS, not steps")
    ap.add_argument("--noise", type=float, default=PREREG["noise_frac"])
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=40)
    ap.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=PREREG["k_modes"])
    ap.add_argument("--readout", default="analog", choices=["analog", "spiking"],
                    help="THE experimental factor.  'spiking' is the real "
                         "TemporalMCSNN/TemporalMSNN with only fc1 made volatile; "
                         "'analog' is a digital nn.Linear on the column current.")
    ap.add_argument("--probe-steps", type=int, default=PREREG["probe_steps"],
                    help="spiking only: R read steps, so the rate code runs 0..R")
    ap.add_argument("--v-probe-spk", type=float, default=None,
                    help="spiking only: probe amplitude at the SYNAPSE input "
                         "(default: 1.0 = one spike on the conv path, --v-probe on dense)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None,
                    help="results JSON path (default: output_dir()/netbench.json)")
    ap.add_argument("--mode", default="main",
                    choices=["main", "controls", "power", "shuffle", "dose",
                             "uncertainty", "convergence", "all"])
    ap.add_argument("--n-train", type=int, default=1200)
    ap.add_argument("--n-test", type=int, default=1000)
    ap.add_argument("--cols", type=int, default=64, help="analog columns")
    ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-3)
    ap.add_argument("--dt", type=float, default=PREREG["dt_stim"])
    ap.add_argument("--span", default="-1.5,1.15")
    ap.add_argument("--v-probe", type=float, default=PREREG["v_probe"])
    ap.add_argument("--scale-force", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="ONE absolute noise floor for every arm (0 = per-arm calibration, the "
                         "old convention).  Pass 246.5243 for N-MNIST: the largest per-arm D=0 "
                         "spread, which equalises SNR and disadvantages the stretched arm.  "
                         "Recorded in args, so a run is reproducible from argv alone.")
    ap.add_argument("--scale-mode", default=PREREG["scale_mode"],
                    choices=["spread", "absmean"])
    ap.add_argument("--dmax-frac", type=float, default=PREREG["dmax_frac"])
    ap.add_argument("--noise-reps", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--seed0", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--val-frac", type=float, default=0.2,
                    help="held-out fraction of --n-train used for early stopping")
    ap.add_argument("--patience", type=int, default=8,
                    help="epochs of no validation improvement before stopping")
    ap.add_argument("--dose-delay", type=float, default=45.0)
    ap.add_argument("--pf-variability", default=PREREG["pf_variability"],
                    choices=["frozen", "off"])
    ap.add_argument("--gate", type=int, default=1, help="1 = bias row GATED (required)")
    ap.add_argument("--float64", action="store_true",
                    help="numerical cross-check; D_max must be unchanged")
    ap.add_argument("--require-converged", type=int, default=1,
                    help="1 = exit non-zero if any cell failed the loss-plateau criterion. "
                         "Set 0 ONLY for a smoke test, and then D_max is not reportable.")
    return ap


def parse_args(argv=None):
    """Parse ``argv`` with :func:`build_parser` and normalise the list/bool fields.

    The normalisation (``delays``, ``span``, ``gate``) belongs here rather than in every
    caller, because a caller that omits it runs silently with a string where a list of
    floats is expected.
    """
    a = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    a.delays = [float(x) for x in str(a.delays).split(",")]
    a.span = [float(x) for x in str(a.span).split(",")]
    a.gate = bool(a.gate)
    if getattr(a, "out", None) is None:
        a.out = default_out()
    return a


def main():
    a = parse_args()
    # ``arms`` is the only list field parse_args leaves as a string, so it is split
    # here. ``delays``, ``span`` and ``gate`` are normalised inside parse_args, and
    # re-splitting them raised AttributeError on the first call -- main() was dead
    # from the moment the normalisation moved into parse_args during migration.
    a.arms = [s for s in a.arms.split(",") if s]
    assert a.gate, "the bias row must be gated; running with it open is the known artefact"
    if a.float64:
        torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float64)

    t0 = time.time()
    out = dict(prereg=PREREG, prereg_hash=cfg_hash(PREREG),
               argv=sys.argv[1:], args=vars(a).copy(),
               run_hash=cfg_hash({k: v for k, v in vars(a).items()}))
    out["args"]["delays"] = a.delays
    print("=" * 100)
    print(f"NETBENCH  delayed classification on a measured-transient volatile synapse")
    print(f"  prereg hash {out['prereg_hash']}   run hash {out['run_hash']}   "
          f"dtype {'float64' if a.float64 else 'float32'}   READOUT={a.readout.upper()}"
          + (f" (R={a.probe_steps} probe steps)" if a.readout == "spiking" else ""))
    print("=" * 100)
    data = load_flat(a.dataset, a.n_train, a.n_test)

    print("\nSTRUCTURAL CONTROLS")
    ok = structural_controls(a, data, out)
    if not ok and a.mode != "controls":
        print("\n*** STRUCTURAL CONTROLS FAILED -- refusing to report accuracies ***")
        json.dump(out, open(a.out, "w"), indent=1, default=str)
        return 2

    if a.mode in ("main", "all"):
        run_curve(a, data, out, tag="main")
    if a.mode in ("power", "all"):
        mode_power(a, data, out)
    if a.mode in ("shuffle", "all"):
        mode_shuffle(a, data, out)
    if a.mode in ("dose", "all"):
        mode_dose(a, data, out)
    if a.mode in ("uncertainty", "all"):
        mode_uncertainty(a, data, out)
    if a.mode in ("convergence", "all"):
        mode_convergence(a, data, out)

    out["wall_s"] = time.time() - t0
    json.dump(out, open(a.out, "w"), indent=1, default=str)
    print(f"\nwrote {a.out}   ({out['wall_s']:.1f} s)")

    fails = [k for k, v in out.items()
             if k.startswith(("converged_", "dmax_reportable_")) and v is False]
    if out.get("no_trace_ok") is False:
        print("EXIT 4: the gain=0 null beat chance -- fix the benchmark before reading "
              "anything else.")
        return 4
    if a.require_converged and any(k.startswith("converged_") for k in out) and \
            not all(v for k, v in out.items() if k.startswith("converged_")):
        print(f"EXIT 3: unconverged cells ({fails}); D_max is not reportable. Raise --epochs, "
              f"or pass --require-converged 0 to acknowledge a smoke-level budget.")
        return 3
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/prepare\_data.py}
\index{tools/prepare\_data.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Download the third-party datasets and build the inputs a training profile needs.

    python tools/prepare_data.py reduced      the small subsets `reduced` runs on
    python tools/prepare_data.py published    the full frame caches `published` needs
    python tools/prepare_data.py reduced --list        what it would build, and where

Needs the ``datasets`` extra: ``uv sync --extra datasets``.

NO THIRD-PARTY DATASET SAMPLE IS DISTRIBUTED WITH THIS PACKAGE. MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, N-MNIST, SHD
and DVS128 Gesture each carry their own upstream terms, which this package's licence does not grant.
This command fetches them from their own sources into ``~/.cache/mnn-torch`` -- outside the tree,
never copied back into it -- and builds the subsets there. See ``THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md``.

Downloading is explicit on purpose: ``tools/reproduce.py`` never reaches the network, so a run
either finds prepared inputs or says which command builds them.

WHAT EACH PROFILE GETS.

``reduced`` needs small, quick inputs, built by one deterministic rule rather than a stored list of
indices:

  * MNIST and Fashion-MNIST: the first 100 training and first 50 test examples OF EACH CLASS.
  * the event datasets: the first 20 test examples OF EACH CLASS, of which the first 12 become
    reduced training data and the remaining 8 reduced test data.

``published`` needs the full frame caches at the counts ``data/datasets.json`` declares, and the
image datasets in the download cache for torchvision to open. The manifest does not record which
examples its subsets took, so this takes the first N of each official split.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from mnn_torch import archives as paths                                  # noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.datasets import SPEC, pack_frames                         # noqa: E402

#: dataset -> (tonic class, spatial downsample factor or None, whether frames carry channels)
EVENT = {
    "nmnist": ("NMNIST", 0.5, True),
    "shd": ("SHD", None, False),
    "dvsgesture": ("DVSGesture", 0.25, True),
}

#: Every event dataset the pipeline has a stage for, and therefore what a bare invocation builds.
#: N-MNIST and DVS128 Gesture are read convolutionally; SHD is a 700-channel stream with no spatial
#: structure and is read densely.
NEEDED_EVENT = ("nmnist", "shd", "dvsgesture")

#: dataset -> torchvision class name
IMAGE = {"mnist": "MNIST", "fashion-mnist": "FashionMNIST"}

#: The reduced rule, in one place. Changing a number here changes what `reduced` runs on.
PER_CLASS_IMAGE_TRAIN, PER_CLASS_IMAGE_TEST = 100, 50
PER_CLASS_EVENT, PER_CLASS_EVENT_TRAIN = 20, 12


def manifest():
    return json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "datasets.json").read_text())["datasets"]


def _need_tonic():
    try:
        import tonic                                                     # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:
        raise SystemExit("tonic is not installed: `uv sync --extra datasets`, or "
                         "`pip install tonic==1.6.0`.")


def _first_per_class(labels, n_per_class):
    """Indices of the first ``n_per_class`` examples of each class, in dataset order.

    Deterministic and needs no stored index list: the rule reproduces the selection from the
    dataset itself, so nothing about which examples were chosen has to be distributed.
    """
    labels = np.asarray(labels)
    taken, out = {}, []
    for i, y in enumerate(labels):
        y = int(y)
        if taken.get(y, 0) < n_per_class:
            taken[y] = taken.get(y, 0) + 1
            out.append(i)
    return np.asarray(out, dtype=np.int64)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# image datasets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _image_split(dataset, train, root):
    import torchvision

    cls = getattr(torchvision.datasets, IMAGE[dataset])
    ds = cls(root=str(root), train=train, download=True)
    x = ds.data.numpy() if hasattr(ds.data, "numpy") else np.asarray(ds.data)
    y = ds.targets.numpy() if hasattr(ds.targets, "numpy") else np.asarray(ds.targets)
    return x.astype(np.uint8), y.astype(np.int64)


def build_reduced_images(dataset, out_dir, raw_dir):
    xtr, ytr = _image_split(dataset, True, raw_dir)
    xte, yte = _image_split(dataset, False, raw_dir)
    itr = _first_per_class(ytr, PER_CLASS_IMAGE_TRAIN)
    ite = _first_per_class(yte, PER_CLASS_IMAGE_TEST)
    # (n, 1, 28, 28), the shape the dense network's loader takes
    pick = lambda x, i: x[i].reshape(len(i), 1, 28, 28)                  # noqa: E731
    dest = out_dir / f"{dataset}_images.npz"
    np.savez_compressed(dest, Xtr=pick(xtr, itr), ytr=ytr[itr],
                        Xte=pick(xte, ite), yte=yte[ite])
    print(f"  {dataset:14} {len(itr)} train, {len(ite)} test  -> {dest.name} "
          f"({dest.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    return dest


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# event datasets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _download_help(dataset, cls, raw_dir, exc):
    """What to do when an upstream download fails, which is not this package's to fix.

    Concrete on purpose: an instruction to "obtain it from the source" is no use unless it names
    the file, where it goes, and how to tell you got the right one.
    """
    import tonic

    where = raw_dir / cls.__name__
    lines = [f"{dataset}: the downloader could not fetch it ({exc}).",
             f"    This is upstream, not a fault here: the URL tonic {tonic.__version__} carries "
             f"may have moved, or the dataset may require accepting its terms at its source.",
             f"    Fetch it yourself -- see THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md for the source and its terms -- "
             f"and put it where tonic looks:"]
    for split in ("test", "train"):
        fn = getattr(cls, f"{split}_filename", None)
        md5 = getattr(cls, f"{split}_md5", None)
        url = getattr(cls, f"{split}_url", None)
        if fn:
            lines.append(f"        {where / fn}")
            if md5:
                lines.append(f"            md5 {md5}")
            if url:
                lines.append(f"            tonic fetches this from {url}")
    folders = [getattr(cls, f"{sp}_filename", "").removesuffix(".tar.gz").removesuffix(".zip")
               for sp in ("test", "train")]
    folders = [f for f in folders if f]
    if folders:
        lines.append(f"    Already-extracted data works too: tonic walks {where}/"
                     f"{{{','.join(folders)}}} for *.npy.")
    lines.append("    Then run this command again.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _binning(dataset):
    """The transform that takes raw events to the declared frame geometry."""
    import tonic
    import tonic.transforms as TT

    cls_name, spatial, _has_channel = EVENT[dataset]
    cls = getattr(tonic.datasets, cls_name)
    t_bins = int(manifest()[dataset]["binning"]["t_bins"])
    sensor = cls.sensor_size
    steps = []
    if spatial is not None:
        steps.append(TT.Downsample(spatial_factor=spatial))
        sensor = (int(sensor[0] * spatial), int(sensor[1] * spatial), sensor[2])
    steps.append(TT.ToFrame(sensor_size=sensor, n_time_bins=t_bins))
    return cls, t_bins, (TT.Compose(steps) if len(steps) > 1 else steps[0])


def _to_frame(dataset, frame, t_bins):
    """One transformed sample as a binary ``uint8`` frame at the registry geometry."""
    _cls_name, _spatial, has_channel = EVENT[dataset]
    shape = tuple(SPEC[dataset][2])
    f = np.asarray(frame)
    if not has_channel:
        f = f.reshape(t_bins, -1)              # a 1-D sensor returns singleton spatial axes
    # binary, not counts: the representation is presence per bin per channel, and packbits is
    # lossless only on binary frames
    return (f > 0).astype(np.uint8).reshape(t_bins, *shape)


def _event_frames(dataset, train, raw_dir, want=None):
    """One split, binned to the declared geometry and binarised. Returns ``(X, y)``."""
    cls, t_bins, tf = _binning(dataset)

    try:
        ds = cls(save_to=str(raw_dir), train=train, transform=tf)
    except (RuntimeError, OSError) as exc:
        raise SystemExit(_download_help(dataset, cls, raw_dir, exc)) from None
    n = len(ds) if want is None else min(want, len(ds))
    if want is not None and len(ds) < want:
        raise SystemExit(f"{dataset}: the official {'train' if train else 'test'} split has "
                         f"{len(ds)} examples, fewer than the {want} the manifest declares")
    shape = tuple(SPEC[dataset][2])
    X = np.empty((n, t_bins, *shape), dtype=np.uint8)
    y = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    for i in range(n):
        frame, label = ds[i]
        X[i] = _to_frame(dataset, frame, t_bins)
        y[i] = int(label)
        if (i + 1) % 500 == 0:
            print(f"    {dataset} {'train' if train else 'test'}: {i + 1}/{n}", flush=True)
    return X, y


def build_reduced_events(dataset, out_dir, raw_dir):
    """The first 20 test examples per class, split 12 train / 8 test.

    Two passes, because binning is the expensive step and selection does not need it. The first
    reads labels from the untransformed dataset -- about 2 ms a sample -- and STOPS as soon as
    every class has its 20. The second bins only those. Binning the whole split first and then
    discarding 80% of it costs several times as much.
    """
    cls, t_bins, tf = _binning(dataset)
    n_classes = int(SPEC[dataset][3])
    try:
        plain = cls(save_to=str(raw_dir), train=False)          # labels only, no binning
    except (RuntimeError, OSError) as exc:
        raise SystemExit(_download_help(dataset, cls, raw_dir, exc)) from None

    taken, keep = {}, []
    for i in range(len(plain)):
        label = int(plain[i][1])
        if taken.get(label, 0) < PER_CLASS_EVENT:
            taken[label] = taken.get(label, 0) + 1
            keep.append((i, label))
        if len(taken) == n_classes and min(taken.values()) >= PER_CLASS_EVENT:
            break
    short = {k: v for k, v in sorted(taken.items()) if v < PER_CLASS_EVENT}
    if short or len(taken) < n_classes:
        raise SystemExit(f"{dataset}: the test split does not hold {PER_CLASS_EVENT} examples of "
                         f"every class; saw {len(taken)} of {n_classes} classes, short: {short}")
    print(f"    {dataset}: {len(keep)} of {len(plain)} test examples selected, binning those",
          flush=True)

    binned = cls(save_to=str(raw_dir), train=False, transform=tf)
    shape = tuple(SPEC[dataset][2])
    X = np.empty((len(keep), t_bins, *shape), dtype=np.uint8)
    y = np.empty(len(keep), dtype=np.int64)
    seen, is_train = {}, np.zeros(len(keep), dtype=bool)
    for k, (i, label) in enumerate(keep):
        X[k] = _to_frame(dataset, binned[i][0], t_bins)
        y[k] = label
        # within each class, the first PER_CLASS_EVENT_TRAIN go to training
        seen[label] = seen.get(label, 0) + 1
        is_train[k] = seen[label] <= PER_CLASS_EVENT_TRAIN
    dest = out_dir / manifest()[dataset]["cache_file"]
    np.savez_compressed(dest, **pack_frames({"Xtr": X[is_train], "ytr": y[is_train],
                                             "Xte": X[~is_train], "yte": y[~is_train]}))
    print(f"  {dataset:14} {int(is_train.sum())} train, {int((~is_train).sum())} test  "
          f"-> {dest.name} ({dest.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    return dest


def build_published_events(dataset, out_dir, raw_dir):
    entry = manifest()[dataset]
    xtr, ytr = _event_frames(dataset, True, raw_dir, want=int(entry["split"]["train"]))
    xte, yte = _event_frames(dataset, False, raw_dir, want=int(entry["split"]["test"]))
    dest = out_dir / entry["cache_file"]
    np.savez_compressed(dest, **pack_frames({"Xtr": xtr, "ytr": ytr, "Xte": xte, "yte": yte}))
    print(f"  {dataset:14} {len(ytr)} train, {len(yte)} test  -> {dest.name} "
          f"({dest.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    return dest


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def plan(profile):
    """What would be built, as ``(destination directory, description lines)``."""
    m = manifest()
    if profile == "reduced":
        out = paths.reduced_dir()
        rows = [f"{d:14} {PER_CLASS_IMAGE_TRAIN}/class train, {PER_CLASS_IMAGE_TEST}/class test "
                f"-> {d}_images.npz" for d in sorted(IMAGE)]
        rows += [f"{d:14} first {PER_CLASS_EVENT}/class of the test split, "
                 f"{PER_CLASS_EVENT_TRAIN} train / {PER_CLASS_EVENT - PER_CLASS_EVENT_TRAIN} test "
                 f"-> {m[d]['cache_file']}" for d in NEEDED_EVENT]
    else:
        out = paths.cache_dir()
        rows = [f"{d:14} downloaded into {paths.cache_dir()}, where the loaders look"
                for d in sorted(IMAGE)]
        rows += [f"{d:14} {m[d]['split']['train']} train, {m[d]['split']['test']} test "
                 f"-> {m[d]['cache_file']}  frames {m[d]['frame_shape']}" for d in NEEDED_EVENT]
    return out, rows


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("profile", choices=("reduced", "published"))
    ap.add_argument("--dataset", default=None,
                    help="one dataset only (default: every one the profile needs)")
    ap.add_argument("--raw", default=None,
                    help="where the downloads go (default: <cache>/raw)")
    ap.add_argument("--list", action="store_true", help="print what would be built, and stop")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    out_dir, rows = plan(a.profile)
    raw_dir = pathlib.Path(a.raw).expanduser().resolve() if a.raw else paths.cache_dir() / "raw"
    print(f"  {a.profile}: building into {out_dir}")
    print(f"  downloads go to           {raw_dir}")
    for r in rows:
        print(f"    {r}")
    if a.list:
        print("  nothing downloaded. Drop --list to build.")
        return 0

    print("  these datasets are third-party and carry their own terms; see THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md")
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    images = [a.dataset] if a.dataset in IMAGE else ([] if a.dataset else sorted(IMAGE))
    events = [a.dataset] if a.dataset in EVENT else ([] if a.dataset else list(NEEDED_EVENT))
    if a.dataset and not (images or events):
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown dataset {a.dataset!r}; have {sorted(IMAGE) + sorted(EVENT)}")

    if a.profile == "reduced":
        for d in images:
            build_reduced_images(d, out_dir, raw_dir)
        if events:
            _need_tonic()
        for d in events:
            build_reduced_events(d, out_dir, raw_dir)
        print("  now: python tools/reproduce.py reduced")
    else:
        # THE IMAGE DATASETS GO WHERE THE LOADERS LOOK, which is cache_dir() -- not the raw
        # directory tonic uses for its own archives. `image_loaders` and `run_dense_homeostasis`
        # both resolve to `paths.cache_dir()`, so downloading a level deeper would leave the
        # static and homeostasis stages unable to find what this command had just fetched.
        image_root = paths.cache_dir()
        for d in images:
            _image_split(d, True, image_root)  # download only; torchvision opens them itself
            _image_split(d, False, image_root)
            print(f"  {d:14} downloaded into {image_root}")
        if events:
            _need_tonic()
        for d in events:
            build_published_events(d, out_dir, raw_dir)
        print("  now: python tools/reproduce.py published geometry")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/profile\_matched.py}
\index{tools/profile\_matched.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Profile-matched spiking driver: the measured ITO relaxation in the class-output synapse.

The question. Can a measured ITO relaxation, used as the volatile-state kernel of the
class-output synapse, provide the persistent state a spiking network needs after its input
has disappeared?

What "profile-matched" means. Each profile gets its own system: its own trained network and
its own reader, calibrated once at D = 0 before training and then frozen. That is what a
hardware-aware deployment would do. Requiring ITO to use a reader configured for an
exponential is a domain-mismatch stress test, not the primary question; recalibrating at
every delay is too permissive. Both of those already exist in the archive.

The comparison is between profile-adapted systems. Because each profile is trained and
calibrated separately, the two systems differ in more than kernel shape. Nothing here
licenses "kernel shape alone caused the difference".

The volatile layer is the class-output synapse in both architectures, which is what makes
this an architecture replication rather than two unrelated experiments:

    MCSNN   conv1 -> lif1 -> conv2 -> lif2 -> [volatile fc1 32->10] -> lif3
    MSNN    fc1 578->64 -> lif1        ->     [volatile fc2 64->10] -> lif2

``netbench.SpikingCell`` hardcodes ``self.layer = self.net.fc1``, and on the dense path it
streams the input straight into the volatile synapse. Neither is right for MSNN here, so
:class:`OutputVolatileCell` overrides the layer selection, the write path and the probe
amplitude. netbench itself is left untouched -- it is the producer of the deposited arrays.

One consequence of the new placement, recorded. netbench's gauge note says "fc2 (dense path)
sits after the noise injection, so its gain scales signal and noise together and is
snr-neutral". With fc2 now the volatile layer read by the probe, that is no longer true of
it: it sits between the signal and the frozen noise reference, so it is gauge-projected here
exactly as fc1 is on the conv path.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))

import netbench as NB  # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch import estimators as A  # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.networks import MemristiveLinearLayer  # Noqa: E402
from mnn_torch.networks import delayed_readout, hold_conductance  # Noqa: E402

#: The two profiles. `exp_meanlife` is the 23.031 s mean-lifetime-matched exponential.
PROFILES = ("kww", "exp_meanlife")

#: The implemented-mean sensitivity kernel, evaluation-only.
#:
#: why it exists. `exp_meanlife` is matched to the analytic KWW mean lifetime,
#: ``(tau/beta) * Gamma(1/beta) = 23.0323 s``. The 12-mode decomposition the simulation actually
#: integrates does not have that mean: at this study's ``tmax_tau = 1.5 * 226 / 16.033 = 21.1439``
#: it comes out at **23.4285 s**, a **+1.72 %** mismatch. That is easy to miss because
#: ``KohlrauschTrace.mean_lifetime`` (``KohlrauschTrace`` in volatile.py) returns the analytic closed form and never
#: exposes the modes' own first moment, so nothing in the pipeline would ever print the discrepancy.
#:
#: So the primary comparator is described as "matched to the analytic KWW mean", and the mismatch is
#: answered by a real arm rather than a caveat: a single exponential at the implemented mean, swapped
#: in at replay only. `profile_for` accepts ``exp:<tau>`` and sets ``floor = ref["rho"]`` for every
#: arm, so the transient gain ``(1-rho)/rho`` is unchanged and the swap stays clean.
#:
#: It is not a training profile. It never appears on the ``training_profile`` axis, never enters the
#: shared-scale calibration, and is registered only after the reader is frozen.
EXP_MODE_MEAN_TAU = 23.4285
EXP_MODE_MEAN = f"exp:{EXP_MODE_MEAN_TAU:g}"

#: Every kernel a frozen system may be replayed under. The first two are the diagonal/off-diagonal
#: pair; the third is the sensitivity and exists in the confirmation cohort (``B``) only.
EVAL_KERNELS = PROFILES + (EXP_MODE_MEAN,)

#: The declared positive delay at which functional memory is claimed, in realised seconds:
#: the 4 s grid point is 9 hold steps at dt = 0.4525 s, i.e. 4.0725 s. The state-cleared and
#: probe-only controls are scored here and nowhere else in production -- they are delay-invariant by
#: construction (a zeroed tensor does not decay), which the tests assert rather than assume, so a
#: full grid of them would deposit thirteen copies of one number.
MEMORY_DELAY_S = 4.0725

#: The reader, in full. netbench's own `CAL_KEYS` carries only the first four, so two readers
#: differing in probe amplitude or noise fraction would hash identically.
READER_KEYS = ("scale", "mu", "A", "C", "R", "probe_amp", "noise",
               "calib_delay", "calib_cfg")

#: Device tensors that are not in `state_dict` and must be paired explicitly. `dev_id` in
#: netbench hashes these for the volatile layer only.
DEVICE_TENSORS = ("_pf_residual", "_device_fault")


def _digest(obj) -> str:
    """Stable short digest of tensors / arrays / plain values."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()

    def feed(v):
        if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor):
            h.update(np.ascontiguousarray(v.detach().cpu().numpy(),
                                          dtype=np.float64).tobytes())
        elif isinstance(v, dict):
            for k in sorted(v):
                h.update(str(k).encode())
                feed(v[k])
        elif isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
            for x in v:
                feed(x)
        else:
            h.update(repr(v).encode())
    feed(obj)
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]


def volatile_paths(kind: str):
    """``(volatile module name, every memristive module name)`` for an architecture."""
    if kind == "conv":
        return "fc1", ("conv1", "conv2", "fc1")
    return "fc2", ("fc1", "fc2")


def implemented_mean_lifetime(trace) -> float:
    """First moment of the kernel the simulation actually integrates, from its own modes.

    ``KohlrauschTrace.mean_lifetime`` (``KohlrauschTrace`` in volatile.py) returns the analytic
    ``(tau/beta) * Gamma(1/beta)``, which is the mean of the *target* stretched exponential, not of
    the finite mode expansion fitted to it. The two differ by +1.72 % here, and because the analytic
    form is what the property exposes, the difference is invisible unless it is computed like this.
    """
    w = np.asarray(trace.weights, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(trace.mode_taus, dtype=float)
    s = w.sum()
    assert s > 0 and np.isfinite(s), f"mode weights do not sum to a usable value: {s}"
    return float((w * t).sum() / s)


def kernel_crossover(trace, tau_exp: float, t_max: float = 300.0, n: int = 2_000_000):
    """``(t, q)`` where the implemented multi-mode kernel first rises above ``exp(-t/tau_exp)``.

    Computed from the archived mode weights, never from the analytic closed form: the analytic and
    implemented curves cross at materially different places (41.856 s vs 40.963 s against the same
    23.0323 s comparator), and a figure that marks one while plotting the other is simply wrong.
    Returns ``(nan, nan)`` if they never cross inside ``t_max``.
    """
    w = np.asarray(trace.weights, dtype=float)
    mt = np.asarray(trace.mode_taus, dtype=float)
    t = np.linspace(t_max / n, t_max, n)
    q = (w[:, None] * np.exp(-t[None, :] / mt[:, None])).sum(0) / w.sum()
    above = q > np.exp(-t / float(tau_exp))
    if not above.any():
        return float("nan"), float("nan")
    i = int(np.argmax(above))
    return float(t[i]), float(q[i])


def state_age_span(n_frames: int, probe_steps: int, dt: float, delay: float = 0.0):
    """``(youngest, oldest)`` age of sample-dependent state present during the probe.

    This is a span, not a single age, and getting that wrong understates nothing but misstates the
    mechanism. ``VolatileSynapse`` integrates ``z <- z * decays + u``, so with frames written at
    steps ``0..n_frames-1`` and the probe occupying the next ``probe_steps``, the youngest
    contribution is the last frame read at the first probe step (one decay interval) and the oldest
    is the first frame read at the last probe step (``n_frames - 1 + probe_steps`` intervals).
    Note ``n_frames`` frames give ``n_frames - 1`` inter-frame intervals, not ``n_frames``.

    Summing the write and probe windows instead -- ``(n_frames + probe_steps) * dt`` -- treats the
    state as having one age and overstates the oldest contribution.
    """
    assert n_frames >= 1 and probe_steps >= 1, "need at least one frame and one probe step"
    youngest = float(delay) + 1 * float(dt)
    oldest = float(delay) + (int(n_frames) - 1 + int(probe_steps)) * float(dt)
    return youngest, oldest


class OutputVolatileCell(NB.SpikingCell):
    """A ``SpikingCell`` whose volatile synapse is the class-output layer on both paths.

    Three overrides, and nothing else:

    * the volatile layer is ``fc2`` on the dense path, not ``fc1``;
    * ``state_after_write`` runs ``fc1 -> lif1`` on the dense path and writes the volatile
      ``fc2`` state with those hidden spikes, rather than streaming the raw input into it;
    * the probe amplitude is 1, not ``args.v_probe`` -- its 1.25 default belongs to netbench's
      input-side dense placement, not to this one.
    """

    def __init__(self, *a, **kw):
        super().__init__(*a, **kw)
        if self.kind != "dense":
            self.probe_amp = 1.0
            return
        # --- re-point the volatile synapse at fc2, the class-output layer --------------
        self.layer = self.net.fc2
        assert isinstance(self.layer, MemristiveLinearLayer), \
            f"fc2 must be the memristive output synapse, got {type(self.layer).__name__}"
        self.n_syn_in = int(self.layer.weights.shape[1])
        self.n_syn_out = int(self.layer.weights.shape[0])
        assert self.n_syn_out == self.ncls, \
            f"the volatile layer must BE the output layer; got {self.n_syn_out} != {self.ncls}"
        self.out_lif = self.net.lif2
        self.hold_layers = [self.net.fc1, self.net.fc2]
        # The trace was wrapped around fc1 by the base class; re-wrap it on fc2
        self.vs = self._rebuild_vs(self.vs.profile)
        self.gain_nominal = self.vs.gain
        # A and C are per-output-neuron, so they resize with the new layer
        self.A = torch.ones(self.n_syn_out)
        self.C = torch.zeros(self.n_syn_out)
        self.probe_amp = 1.0
        assert any(p is self.layer.weights for p in self.params), \
            "the volatile layer's weights must be trainable parameters"

    def _rebuild_vs(self, prof):
        """Re-wrap the trace around ``self.layer`` using this run's settings."""
        from mnn_torch.volatile import VolatileSynapse
        return VolatileSynapse(self.layer, prof, k=self.args.k, dt=self.dt,
                               span_decades=tuple(self.args.span),
                               tmax_tau=NB.tmax_tau_for(self.args.delays, prof.tau_kww))

    # -- probe -------------------------------------------------------------
    def probe(self, B, n_in=None):
        """A uniform amplitude-1 probe. The 1.25 default belongs to the input-side placement."""
        p = torch.full((B, n_in or self.n_syn_in), float(self.probe_amp))
        assert p.unique().numel() == 1, "probe must be uniform"
        return p

    # -- write -------------------------------------------------------------
    def state_after_write(self, xs):
        """Stream the sample; the spikes that reach the output synapse write its state.

        On the dense path that means ``fc1 -> lif1`` first, and the hidden spikes are what
        drive the volatile ``fc2``. netbench's version streams the raw input straight into
        the volatile layer, which was correct when ``fc1`` was volatile and is wrong now.
        """
        if self.kind != "dense":
            return super().state_after_write(xs)
        net, B = self.net, xs.shape[1]
        z = self.vs.init_state(B)
        with hold_conductance(net.fc1, net.fc2):
            mem1 = net.lif1.init_leaky()          # Hidden membrane, reset per batch
            rate = 0.0
            for t in range(xs.shape[0]):
                spk1, mem1 = net.lif1(net.fc1(xs[t]), mem1)
                rate += float(spk1.detach().mean().item())
                self._last_write_u = spk1.detach()
                _, z = self.vs(spk1, z, phase="write",
                               gate_bias_row=self.args.gate, compute_out=False)
        # Trap 5: a hidden layer at rate ~0 makes everything chance by construction.
        self.diag["hidden_rate"] = rate / xs.shape[0]
        return z

    # -- read --------------------------------------------------------------
    def spike_head(self, outs, gen=None, A=None, C=None, want_driven=False):
        """The volatile current drives the output neurons directly on both paths.

        Netbench routes the dense path through ``lif1 -> fc2 -> lif2`` because ``fc1`` was
        volatile there. Here ``fc2`` IS the read layer, so applying it again downstream
        would double-count it; the read goes straight into ``lif2``.
        """
        if self.kind != "dense":
            return super().spike_head(outs, gen=gen, A=A, C=C, want_driven=want_driven)
        net = self.net
        A = self.A if A is None else A
        C = self.C if C is None else C
        mem = net.lif2.init_leaky()               # Output membrane, reset per call
        rec, driven = [], []
        for r, out in enumerate(outs):
            cur = out if self.scale is None else (out - self.mu[r]) / self.scale
            if gen is not None and self.args.noise > 0:
                cur = cur + self.args.noise * torch.randn(cur.shape, generator=gen)
            cur = A * cur + C
            s, mem = net.lif2(cur, mem)           # Not net.fc2(...) -- fc2 is the read layer
            driven.append(s)
            rec.append(s)
        if want_driven:
            return delayed_readout(torch.stack(driven), self.R)
        return delayed_readout(torch.stack(rec), self.R)


# ===========================================================================
# Device pairing
# ===========================================================================
def materialise(cell, xs, bs=8):
    """Force the lazy device tensors into existence with a write and a read.

    ``_pf_residual`` and ``_device_fault`` are ``None`` until first use (`layers.py:166`,
    `:116`). A write-only pass is not enough: ``state_after_write`` calls the volatile synapse
    with ``compute_out=False``, which deliberately skips the PF map, so the volatile layer's
    residual is still ``None`` afterwards. Measured: pairing on a write-only pass left
    ``fc2._pf_residual`` unset, it was then drawn independently per profile at the first read,
    and the two systems silently diverged in the device realisation the pairing exists to fix.
    So the read is part of materialisation, not an afterthought.

    Legitimately absent is not the same as not materialised, and conflating them made a
    documented configuration unrunnable. ``layers.py:336`` treats the residual as fine to be
    ``None`` when the layer is linear or ``pf_stochastic`` is off, and ``temporal.build_cfg``'s own
    docstring prescribes ``off`` for retention work -- so an unconditional non-None assertion
    killed ``--pf-variability off`` on the first call, blaming the PF map for a setting the
    operator chose deliberately. The guard now asks the layer what it should have.
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        z = cell.state_after_write(xs[:, :bs])
        cell.reads(z)
    vol, _ = volatile_paths(cell.kind)
    m = getattr(cell.net, vol)
    expects_pf = bool(getattr(m, "nonlinear", False) and getattr(m, "pf_stochastic", False))
    if expects_pf:
        assert getattr(m, "_pf_residual", None) is not None, (
            f"{vol} is configured for a stochastic Poole-Frenkel map (nonlinear and "
            f"pf_stochastic), but _pf_residual is still unset after a write+read, so nothing "
            f"can be paired")
    return cell


def device_digest(cell) -> dict:
    """``{module path: digest}`` over every memristive layer, not only the volatile one."""
    _, paths = volatile_paths(cell.kind)
    out = {}
    for name in paths:
        mod = getattr(cell.net, name)
        out[name] = _digest({t: getattr(mod, t, None) for t in DEVICE_TENSORS})
    return out


def pair_devices(canonical, other, xs) -> dict:
    """Copy the canonical system's device realisation into ``other``, path by path.

    Order matters: materialise the canonical system first, copy, assert, and only then
    calibrate and train. A single ``dev_id`` would only prove equality for the volatile
    layer.
    """
    materialise(canonical, xs)
    materialise(other, xs)
    _, paths = volatile_paths(canonical.kind)
    for name in paths:
        src, dst = getattr(canonical.net, name), getattr(other.net, name)
        for t in DEVICE_TENSORS:
            v = getattr(src, t, None)
            if v is None:
                # Legitimately absent (e.g. no faults configured) -- must match on both
                assert getattr(dst, t, None) is None, \
                    f"{name}.{t}: canonical is unset but the pair is set"
                continue
            setattr(dst, t, v.detach().clone() if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) else v)
    a, b = device_digest(canonical), device_digest(other)
    assert a == b, f"device pairing failed: {a} != {b}"
    return a


# ===========================================================================
# Two-stage calibration
# ===========================================================================
def measure_spread(cell, xs, idx, bs=256) -> float:
    """Raw D = 0 spread of the probe read, without noise, on given training indices.

    The reduction axis is the whole quantity, and it is netbench's, not a fresh choice.
    ``torch.stack(outs)`` is ``(R, batch, n_out)``; ``SpikingCell.calibrate`` takes
    ``O0.std(1).mean()`` (`netbench.py:993`) -- the sample-to-sample spread, averaged over probe
    steps and neurons. That is the signal: how much the read moves when the input changes.

    Measured cost of getting it wrong. This function first reduced over ``dim=-1``, the class
    axis, which measures how much the read varies between output neurons within one sample --
    a quantity dominated by the frozen per-synapse Poole-Frenkel pedestal, which is fixed per
    network and carries no signal at all. On MSNN/N-MNIST it returned 945.8 against the correct
    142.0, i.e. 6.66x too large, with the pedestal itself 5.4x the true spread. Since injected
    noise is ``noise_frac * scale``, every accuracy in the campaign would have been scored at
    6.7x the pre-registered noise floor, and three independent reproductions flipped the sign of
    the primary paired difference on the axis alone.
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        z = cell.state_after_write(xs[:, idx[:bs]])
        outs, _ = cell.reads(z)
        return float(torch.stack(outs).std(1).mean().item())


def calibration_ok(v) -> bool:
    """A spread is usable iff it is finite and strictly positive."""
    return bool(np.isfinite(v)) and v > 0.0


def set_operating_point(cell, xs, idx, shared_scale, bs=256):
    """Stage two: fit ``mu``, ``A``, ``C`` against the shared scale, once.

    ``calibrate`` is never called: it asserts ``scale is None`` and would re-derive its own
    denominator, which is the coupling this two-stage split exists to break. But the split is
    meant to change only the denominator -- everything downstream of it is netbench's, reused
    rather than reimplemented:

    * ``mu`` is ``stack(outs).mean(1)``, shape ``(R, n_out)``, per neuron (`netbench.py:1026`,
      including its own shape assertion). A per-step scalar cannot cancel a per-neuron pedestal
      ramp across the probe window; measured, the scalar form inflated the reported paired
      difference by about 4x.
    * ``A`` and ``C`` come from ``_fit_operating_point`` (`netbench.py:1028`), the bounded
      feedback controller that lands the spike counts at the designed ``R/2`` mean and ``R/4``
      spread. Hardcoding ``A = 1`` left the readout at 0.62 spikes of 12 -- the near-silent,
      tie-heavy regime the controller exists to escape -- and the sign of the primary difference
      turned on whether the gain the design says to fit was actually fitted.

    Reimplementing either of those is how the two-stage split silently became a different
    experiment, so this function now derives them from the same code the archive used.
    """
    cell.scale = float(shared_scale)
    with torch.no_grad():
        z = cell.state_after_write(xs[:, idx[:bs]])
        outs, _ = cell.reads(z)
        cell.mu = torch.stack(outs).mean(1).detach().clone()      # (R, n_out), per neuron
        assert cell.mu.dim() == 2 and cell.mu.shape[0] == cell.R, \
            f"mu must be (R, n_out), got {tuple(cell.mu.shape)}"
        cell.calib_delay = 0.0
        cell.scale_src = "shared-max-spread"
        cell.w0 = float(cell.layer.weights.abs().max().item())
    op_mean, op_sd = cell._fit_operating_point(outs)              # Fits a and C
    cell.op_count_mean, cell.op_count_sd = op_mean, op_sd
    bad = [k for k in ("mu", "A", "C")
           if not bool(torch.isfinite(getattr(cell, k)).all())]
    assert not bad, f"non-finite reader parameters after calibration: {bad}"
    return cell


def reader_snapshot(cell) -> dict:
    """The complete operational reader, so two readers cannot hash alike while differing."""
    return {"scale": cell.scale, "mu": cell.mu.detach().clone(),
            "A": cell.A.detach().clone(), "C": cell.C.detach().clone(),
            "R": int(cell.R), "probe_amp": float(cell.probe_amp),
            "noise": float(cell.args.noise), "calib_delay": float(cell.calib_delay),
            "calib_cfg": cell.cfg_id}


def reader_restore(cell, snap):
    for k in ("scale", "mu", "A", "C", "calib_delay"):
        v = snap[k]
        setattr(cell, k, v.detach().clone() if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) else v)
    cell.probe_amp = snap["probe_amp"]
    return cell


# ===========================================================================
# Delays
# ===========================================================================
def realised_delays(delays, dt):
    """``[(requested, steps, realised)]``. ``hold`` rounds, and at dt = 0.4525 s the
    D = 2 s point is realised as 1.81 s -- a 9.5 % error that D_max must not inherit."""
    out = []
    for D in delays:
        n = max(int(round(float(D) / dt)), 0)
        out.append((float(D), n, n * dt))
    return out


# ===========================================================================
# Replay
# ===========================================================================
#: Noise keying base. The key deliberately excludes the profile and the delay, so paired
#: systems draw identical evaluation noise and a profile difference can never be a
#: difference in draws. Including the batch index makes it independent of loop order too.
NOISE_BASE = 777_000


#: Field widths for the evaluation-noise key. The batch field must exceed the batch count, or
#: the fields alias: at the original 100 it took only ``--n-test 10000`` (157 batches at 64) for
#: batch 100 of repetition 0 and batch 0 of repetition 1 to draw the same tensor, so 570 keys
#: collided and the "average over independent repetitions" step would have averaged replicates
#: sharing a third of their draws. Latent at the specified 2,000 samples; one flag away from
#: firing, which is exactly the kind of thing that should not be left to a flag.
NOISE_BI, NOISE_REP = 100_000, 1_000_000


def noise_gen(seed: int, rep: int, bi: int):
    assert 0 <= int(bi) < NOISE_BI, (
        f"batch index {bi} exceeds the noise-key field width {NOISE_BI}; widen NOISE_BI rather "
        f"than let repetitions alias onto each other")
    return torch.Generator().manual_seed(NOISE_BASE + int(seed) * NOISE_REP * 16
                                         + int(rep) * NOISE_REP + int(bi))


def write_cache(cell, xs, bs):
    """One post-write state per batch, in batch order.

    Reused across every delay, every noise repetition and the gain-zero ablation. Sound
    because ``gain`` scales the read (``VolatileSynapse.read`` in volatile.py), so the written state does not
    depend on it -- asserted by :func:`prove_gain_only_affects_read`.
    """
    out = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in range(0, xs.shape[1], bs):
            out.append(cell.state_after_write(xs[:, i:i + bs]))
    return out


def _held(cell, zc, steps, clear_state=False):
    """The per-batch state the probe actually sees, after the hold and any clearing.

    ``clear_state`` implements the state-cleared control: the write and the hold happen exactly as
    normal, and the held volatile tensor is then zeroed immediately before the probe. **Only the held
    tensor is zeroed** -- weights, device tensors, scale, reader and probe inputs are untouched, which
    is what makes this a control on the stored state rather than on the system.

    Zeroing after the hold is deliberately the same object as zeroing before it, so delay-invariance
    of the cleared condition is structural rather than something to hope for; the test asserts it.
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        # Exactly VolatileSynapse.hold's body, device and dtype included, but taking the
        # step count directly so the requested seconds are not rounded a second time.
        def _hold(z):
            if steps <= 0:
                return z
            d = torch.as_tensor(cell.vs.trace.decays, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
            return z * torch.pow(d, steps)
        zs = [_hold(z) for z in zc]
        if clear_state:
            zs = [torch.zeros_like(z) for z in zs]
    return zs


def probe_only_cache(cell, xs, bs):
    """A write cache in which the write never happened: zero initial state, right shapes.

    This is deliberately a different code path from ``clear_state``, which writes normally and then
    zeroes the held tensor. Implementing probe-only as "clear_state by another name" would make the
    required state-cleared/probe-only identity true by construction and therefore untestable -- the
    same mistake as a randomness test that restates the key formula instead of calling it. Here the
    stimulus is genuinely never presented, so the identity is a real check on whether the write
    leaves anything behind outside the volatile tensor.
    """
    out = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in range(0, xs.shape[1], bs):
            out.append(cell.vs.init_state(xs[:, i:i + bs].shape[1]))
    return out


def prespike_currents(cell, zc, steps, clear_state=False, gain=None):
    """Digest and summary of the pre-spike read currents, before the threshold.

    Why accuracy cannot do this job. The state-cleared and gain-zero conditions both land at exactly
    ``1/n_classes`` -- a degenerate all-tie output -- so no accuracy comparison can show that they are
    different interventions. They differ upstream of the threshold: at ``gain = 0`` the trace term is
    suppressed for all R probe steps, whereas a cleared state is *re-charged by the probe itself*,
    which drives the synapse for R*dt seconds. That difference lives in the currents, so the
    non-equivalence test reads the currents.
    """
    nominal = cell.vs.gain
    try:
        if gain is not None:
            cell.vs.gain = float(gain)
        zs = _held(cell, zc, steps, clear_state=clear_state)
        with torch.no_grad():
            outs = [torch.stack(cell.reads(z)[0]) for z in zs]
        flat = torch.cat([o.reshape(-1) for o in outs])
        return {"digest": _digest(flat),
                "abs_mean": float(flat.abs().mean().item()),
                "abs_max": float(flat.abs().max().item()),
                "std": float(flat.std().item())}
    finally:
        cell.vs.gain = nominal


def evaluate_cached(cell, zc, y, steps, bs, noise_reps, clear_state=False):
    """``(mean_acc, per_rep_accs, ties)`` at a delay of ``steps`` hold steps, no gradients.

    ``steps`` is the realised delay in hold steps, not the requested seconds: ``hold``
    rounds, and at dt = 0.4525 s the 2 s point is 4 steps = 1.81 s.

    ``clear_state`` runs the state-cleared control through this identical read path, so the control
    and the reported condition cannot diverge in anything except the state itself.
    """
    accs, ties = [], 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        zs = _held(cell, zc, steps, clear_state=clear_state)
        for r in range(noise_reps):
            hit, n = 0.0, 0
            for bi, z in enumerate(zs):
                outs, _ = cell.reads(z)
                lo = cell.spike_head(outs, gen=noise_gen(cell.seed, r, bi))
                a, nf, nt, h = NB.score(lo, y[bi * bs: bi * bs + lo.shape[0]], cell.ncls)
                if not np.isfinite(a):
                    return float("nan"), [], -1
                hit += a * lo.shape[0]
                n += lo.shape[0]
                ties += nt
            accs.append(hit / n)
    return float(np.mean(accs)), accs, ties


def prove_gain_only_affects_read(cell, xs, bs=8):
    """The written state is gain-independent; only the read changes. Proven, not asserted.

    This is what licenses one write cache serving both the transient-enabled and the
    transient-gain-zero condition.
    """
    nominal = cell.gain_nominal
    with torch.no_grad():
        cell.vs.gain = nominal
        z_on = cell.state_after_write(xs[:, :bs]).clone()
        r_on = torch.stack(cell.reads(z_on)[0]).clone()
        cell.vs.gain = 0.0
        z_off = cell.state_after_write(xs[:, :bs]).clone()
        r_off = torch.stack(cell.reads(z_off)[0]).clone()
        cell.vs.gain = nominal
    same_state = bool(torch.equal(z_on, z_off))
    read_changed = float((r_on - r_off).abs().max().item())
    return {"written_state_identical": same_state,
            "max_read_difference": read_changed}


def probe_only_control(cell, y, bs, noise_reps, floor, cp):
    """Zero written state, probe only: must sit at chance, scored against the real labels.

    What it establishes. The twelve amplitude-1 probe steps are a driven sensing window, not a
    passive read -- they drive and decay the transient for 5.43 s. With no written state, the
    read is the frozen per-synapse Poole-Frenkel pedestal plus that drive, which is fixed per
    network and identical for every sample. If it were nonetheless decodable, part of every
    reported accuracy would be the probe's own signature rather than the stored state.

    It returns an accuracy, scored against ``y`` through the same ``NB.score`` as every other
    cell, which is what makes it a control: a sample-independent read yields one constant
    prediction, so the accuracy must land at the majority-class frequency, at or below the
    Clopper-Pearson bound.
    """
    accs, n_ties = [], 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for r in range(noise_reps):
            hit, n = 0.0, 0
            for i in range(0, len(y), bs):
                b = min(bs, len(y) - i)
                outs, _ = cell.reads(cell.vs.init_state(b))
                lo = cell.spike_head(outs, gen=noise_gen(cell.seed, r, i // bs))
                acc, _nf, nt, _h = NB.score(lo, y[i:i + b], cell.ncls)
                hit += acc * b
                n += b
                n_ties += nt
            accs.append(hit / n)
    mean = float(np.mean(accs))
    return {"acc": mean, "reps": accs, "ties": n_ties, "floor": float(floor),
            "cp95": float(cp), "at_chance": bool(mean <= cp)}


def active_kernel_is(cell, profile: str) -> bool:
    """Is the trace currently installed the one named by ``profile``?

    Checked before every evaluation, so a cell cannot be scored under a kernel other than the
    one it names: a row whose diagonal was evaluated on the off-diagonal kernel would report a
    delta of exactly zero and look like a null result.
    """
    want = NB.profile_for(profile)
    got = cell.vs.profile
    return (abs(got.tau_kww - want.tau_kww) < 1e-9
            and abs(got.beta - want.beta) < 1e-9)


def swap_kernel(cell, profile: str, expect_net: str, expect_reader: str,
                expect_dev: dict) -> None:
    """Substitute the evaluation kernel in a fixed system, and prove it is still that system.

    Only the trace changes. The swap is clean because ``profile_for`` sets ``floor = ref["rho"]``
    for every arm, so ``VolatileSynapse.gain = (1-r)/r`` is identical across profiles: only
    ``tau`` and ``beta`` move, hence the mode decays and weights. That is asserted, not assumed.

    A swap that moved the network, the reader or any device realisation would be a different
    system rather than the same system under a different kernel, so all three are re-checked.
    """
    gain_before = cell.vs.gain
    cell.vs = cell._rebuild_vs(NB.profile_for(profile))
    assert abs(cell.vs.gain - gain_before) < 1e-12, (
        f"the kernel swap moved the transient gain ({gain_before} -> {cell.vs.gain}); rho is "
        f"supposed to be profile-invariant, so this is a confound, not a substitution")
    cell.gain_nominal = cell.vs.gain
    assert net_digest(cell) == expect_net, "the kernel swap moved the network"
    assert _digest(reader_snapshot(cell)) == expect_reader, "the kernel swap moved the reader"
    assert device_digest(cell) == expect_dev, "the kernel swap moved a device realisation"


# ===========================================================================
# One seed: pair -> calibrate -> train -> freeze -> replay
# ===========================================================================
def net_digest(cell) -> str:
    return _digest({k: v for k, v in cell.net.state_dict().items()})


def bias_row_gated(cell) -> dict:
    """The volatile output layer's bias row must be gated and zero.

    This replaces C24, which is not applicable here. C24 fed ``fc2`` a zero input to isolate
    its bias row while it sat downstream of the volatile layer; the volatile layer is now the
    output layer, so nothing is downstream and there is no zero-input configuration to test.
    Reusing C24's "integrate the offset over the probe window and compare to threshold"
    arithmetic on an actively probed layer measures the static probe current, not the bias
    row -- it reported 9.19 vs a threshold of 1.0 and would have failed on every seed.

    The direct check is that the bias row is gated and exactly zero. netbench already zeroes
    every ``MemristiveLinearLayer`` bias in ``SpikingCell.__init__`` (`:809-813`) because the
    row is a real crossbar row that also enters ``max|weights_and_bias|``, where a trainable
    bias could silently become the layer's global gain. The functional controls are separate
    and stronger: the gain-zero condition must give D_max = 0, and the probe-only control must
    sit at chance.
    """
    from mnn_torch.networks import MemristiveLinearLayer as _MLL
    biases = {n: float(m.bias.abs().max().item())
              for n, m in cell.net.named_modules() if isinstance(m, _MLL)}
    with torch.no_grad():
        outs, _ = cell.reads(cell.vs.init_state(4))
        cur = torch.stack([(o - cell.mu[r]) / cell.scale for r, o in enumerate(outs)])
        static = float((cell.A * cur + cell.C).abs().max().item())
    return {"gate_flag": bool(cell.args.gate),
            "bias_abs_max_per_layer": biases,
            "all_bias_rows_zero": all(v == 0.0 for v in biases.values()),
            "probe_amp": float(cell.probe_amp),
            "zero_state_static_current_max": static}


def run_seed(a, data, seed, *, timing_only=0, bs_cache=64, cohort="A", train_profiles=None):
    """One seed, fully paired. Returns a record dict.

    ``train_profiles`` selects which profiles are trained. The confirmation cohort passes
    ``("kww",)``:

        Both profiles are instantiated to preserve shared-scale calibration; only the ITO cell is
        trained, and that cell is replayed under all three evaluation kernels.

    Instantiating both is not optional -- the shared scale is ``max(s_kww, s_exp)`` and needs both
    noiseless D=0 spreads. Skipping the exponential *training* is safe because each cell draws from
    its own ``self.gen``, so the ITO cell's trained digest and replay accuracies do not depend on
    whether or when the other arm trains; the test asserts that rather than trusting it.
    """
    xtr, ytr, xte, yte, T, n_in, ncls, nat = data
    xtr2, ytr2, xva, yva = NB.split_val(xtr, ytr, a.val_frac, a.seed0)
    floor, _ = NB.empirical_floor(yte, ncls)
    cp = NB.cp_upper(int(round(floor * len(yte))), len(yte))
    t0 = time.time()

    cells = {pf: OutputVolatileCell(pf, n_in, ncls, a, seed, delays=a.delays, nat=nat)
             for pf in PROFILES}
    # 1. device pairing, before any calibration or training
    dev = pair_devices(cells[PROFILES[0]], cells[PROFILES[1]], xtr2)
    init_net = {pf: net_digest(c) for pf, c in cells.items()}
    assert init_net[PROFILES[0]] == init_net[PROFILES[1]], \
        "paired systems must start from identical weights"

    # 2. calibration, stage one: raw noiseless D=0 spread on training indices only
    n_cal = min(256, xtr2.shape[1])
    cal_idx = np.arange(n_cal)
    spread = {pf: measure_spread(c, xtr2, cal_idx) for pf, c in cells.items()}
    bad = [pf for pf, v in spread.items() if not calibration_ok(v)]
    if bad:
        return {"seed": seed, "status": "calibration_failed", "profiles_failed": bad,
                "spread": spread, "device_digest": dev}
    shared = float(max(spread.values()))
    # 3. calibration, stage two: operating point against the shared scale
    for c in cells.values():
        set_operating_point(c, xtr2, cal_idx, shared)
    reader = {pf: reader_snapshot(c) for pf, c in cells.items()}
    rhash = {pf: _digest(reader[pf]) for pf in cells}

    # 3b. structural controls, recorded rather than merely documented. Each of these was a
    #     function the driver described as its licence and then never called, so the deposited
    #     record carried no evidence for a control the prose asserted.
    gating = {pf: bias_row_gated(c) for pf, c in cells.items()}
    for pf, g in gating.items():
        assert g["gate_flag"], (
            f"{pf}: --gate is off, so the volatile output layer's bias row is driven at the "
            f"probe amplitude on every read step. Its standing offset imitates retention on the "
            f"very layer whose retention is being measured; this run would be uninterpretable")
        assert g["all_bias_rows_zero"], \
            f"{pf}: a memristive bias row is non-zero: {g['bias_abs_max_per_layer']}"
    # The gain proof and the probe-only control belong to the frozen system (step 5b): both
    # read through the trained weights, so running them here would describe a system that never
    # produced a reported number.

    # 4. train at D = 0. The confirmation cohort trains the ITO arm only; the exponential arm is built and
    #    calibrated above, which is all the shared scale needs from it.
    tp = tuple(PROFILES if train_profiles is None else train_profiles)
    assert set(tp) <= set(PROFILES), f"train_profiles must be a subset of {PROFILES}, got {tp}"
    epochs = timing_only or a.epochs
    train = {}
    for pf in tp:
        c = cells[pf]
        t1 = time.time()
        traj, nan_step, info = c.train(xtr2, ytr2, 0.0, epochs, a.bs, a.lr,
                                       xval=xva, yval=yva, patience=a.patience)
        train[pf] = {"converged": bool(info["converged"]), "best_epoch": info["best_epoch"],
                     "epochs_run": info.get("epochs_run"), "hit_cap":
                         bool(info.get("epochs_run") == epochs),
                     "left_plateau": info.get("left_plateau"), "nan_step": nan_step,
                     "seconds": time.time() - t1,
                     "hidden_rate": c.diag.get("hidden_rate")}
        print(f"    [train] {pf:<13} conv={info['converged']} "
              f"best_epoch={info['best_epoch']} {train[pf]['seconds']:.1f}s", flush=True)
