    # The declared criterion, full height: it is where (a) and (b) read their triangles.
    ax.axvline(FRAC, color=PALETTE["guide"], lw=1.0, ls=(0, (2.4, 1.8)), zorder=1.6,
               label=f"primary criterion $f$ = {FRAC:g} (c)")

    # The intervals are whiskers, not two shaded bands: the two architectures' bands overlap
    # through the middle of the sweep, and at the tint a band needs, which interval had left
    # zero at which fraction could not be attributed. A whisker carries its series' colour at
    # full strength and lands on one fraction. The pair is dodged so they do not overdraw.
    dodge = 0.007
    for sign, (key, text, colour, marker, dash) in zip((-1.0, +1.0), CRIT_SERIES):
        block = table[key]
        ax.errorbar(block["f"] + sign * dodge, block["mean"],
                    yerr=[block["mean"] - block["lo"], block["hi"] - block["mean"]],
                    fmt="none", ecolor=colour, elinewidth=0.9, capsize=1.4, capthick=0.9,
                    alpha=0.85, zorder=3)
        ax.plot(block["f"], block["mean"], color=colour, lw=1.4, ls=dash, marker=marker,
                ms=2.8, mec=colour, mew=0.6, zorder=4, label=text)
        # The declared reading, emphasised on the guide: the same mark, larger, white-edged
        at = int(np.flatnonzero(np.isclose(block["f"], FRAC))[0])
        ax.plot([block["f"][at]], [block["mean"][at]], ls="none", marker=marker, ms=4.9,
                color=colour, mec="white", mew=0.5, zorder=5)

    ax.set_xlabel("criterion fraction $f$", fontsize=L["body"])
    # The label keeps the word. "ITO - exp. (s)" was tried, to buy height back in a narrow
    # Panel, and "exp." is the one abbreviation this figure cannot afford: the chapter's other
    # axes use exp for an exponent.
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\Delta D_{\max}$ = ITO $-$ exponential (s)", fontsize=L["body"])
    ax.tick_params(axis="both", which="both", labelsize=L["tick"])
    ax.set_xlim(0.07, 0.98)
    # Four labels, not nine. Nine "0.1 ... 0.9" labels fit a single-column panel; in a third of
    # this measure, at type set for the reduction, they would touch. The even decades carry the
    # labels and the odd ones stay as minor ticks, so 0.75 is still locatable between 0.7 and
    # the 0.8 label.
    ax.set_xticks([0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8])
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"{v:g}" for v in (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)])
    ax.set_xticks([0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9], minor=True)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="minor", length=1.8)

    # Nothing is clipped, and the reading near zero is still legible. Every interval fits
    # inside the limits, including the +44 s upper end at f = 0.10: the endpoint is read close
    # to the ceiling at the low fractions, where the curves are flat, so the estimate is
    # unstable there and that instability is part of what the sweep shows. Purely linear, those
    # two flares would spend four fifths of the panel and squeeze the -7 to +1 s region -- where
    # the sign change, the declared reading and every interval-versus-zero statement live --
    # Into a millimetre or two. The axis is therefore symmetric-log outside +/-10 s.
    low = min(float(b["lo"].min()) for b in table.values())
    high = max(float(b["hi"].max()) for b in table.values())
    ax.set_yscale("symlog", linthresh=SYMLOG_S, linscale=1.35)
    ax.set_ylim(low - 1.2, high + 4.0)
    ticks = [-10, -5, 0, 5, 10, 20, 40]
    ax.set_yticks(ticks)
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"{v:g}" for v in ticks])
    ax.set_yticks([-15, 15, 30], minor=True)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="minor", length=1.8)
    house_grid(ax)
    require_plain_tick_labels(ax)
    return {text: colour for _key, text, colour, _m, _d in CRIT_SERIES}


def prepare():
    """Everything both layouts draw, computed once, with every gate applied before any canvas.

    Panel (c) is gated before anything is drawn. The sweep re-derives every number it draws
    from the deposited curves through the release's own estimator and refuses to return if the
    declared-fraction endpoints (to 0.01 s), the bracketed sign change or its interpolated
    crossing (to 0.01 in f) move. Returns the sweep table, its checks, the sweep result and the
    long-form archive view -- the four things a renderer needs and the only things it gets, so a
    layout cannot reach past this function into the archives on its own.
    """
    table, checks, crit_result = _criterion_sweep()
    archive = _long_form()
    if archive["schema_version"] != 2:
        raise AssertionError(f"expected schema v2, got {archive['schema_version']}")
    if sorted(archive["reportable_cohorts"]) != ["mcsnn|F", "msnn|F"]:
        raise AssertionError(f"reportable cohorts moved: {archive['reportable_cohorts']}")
    return {"table": table, "checks": checks, "crit_result": crit_result, "archive": archive}


def _render(L, prep=None):
    """Draw one layout of the figure from a preparation. ``L`` is an entry of :data:`LAYOUTS`."""
    apply_style()
    prep = prepare() if prep is None else prep
    table, checks, crit_result = prep["table"], prep["checks"], prep["crit_result"]
    archive = prep["archive"]

    # Canvas held, type set for the reduction. At 6.3 in the emitted PDF was 6.10 in wide,
    # and a 7.0 in measure magnified it 1.15x: the 7.8 pt labels arrived at 9.0 pt while
    # every other figure was reduced. 7.23 in emits 7.03 in, which is very nearly its own
    # size in a 510 pt measure -- but the wide layout is placed in a 437.46 pt
    # text block, where the same page is reduced to 0.861x. The canvas is not changed for
    # that (see CANVAS_W_IN); the type is, so the page shows the house scale.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=L["canvas"])
    colour = {ITO: PALETTE["device"], EXPO: PALETTE["exponential"]}
    # The comparator'S lifetime leaves the key. At two panels the key had the whole measure and
    # "exponential, equal mean $\tau$ 23.43 s" fitted in one of two columns; with a third panel
    # to key beside it, that one entry set the width of the whole block. The value is in the
    # text, in the caption and in the equation that defines the comparator, none of which lose
    # it -- and it is the wording the compact layout uses, so a reader moving between
    # the two documents sees one key.
    label = {ITO: "measured ITO relaxation",
             EXPO: "exponential, equal mean $\\tau$"}
    ctl_style = {"state_cleared": ("state-cleared control", PALETTE["control"],
                                  (0, (4.0, 2.0))),
                 "probe_only": ("probe-only control", PALETTE["slate"],
                                (0, (1.0, 2.2)))}
    reported, spans, tops = {}, {}, []

    for col, (arch, name, dual_name) in enumerate(PANELS):
        ax = axes[col]
        dual = _archive_view(arch)
        if dual["cohort"] != "F" or dual["primary_comparator"] != EXPO:
            raise AssertionError(f"{dual_name} is not the finalized F comparison")
        delays = [float(v) for v in dual["delays_realised"]]
        seeds = list(dual["seeds"])
        floor, cp = float(dual["floor"]), float(dual["cp95"])
        # The band drawn here must be the one the controls were scored against: bounding them is
        # what it is for.
        _ctl = json.loads((_DATA / "substitution.json").read_text())["controls"]
        if (round(floor, 12), round(cp, 12)) != (round(float(_ctl["floor"]), 12),
                                                 round(float(_ctl["chance_bound"]), 12)):
            raise AssertionError(
                f"{arch}: the band drawn here ({floor}, {cp}) is not the one the controls "
                f"were scored against ({_ctl['floor']}, {_ctl['chance_bound']})")

        # ---- chance band: the upper one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound on the
        #      majority-class rate. A curve inside it is not a measurement.
        ax.axhspan(0.0, cp * 100.0, color=PALETTE["grid"], alpha=0.55, lw=0, zorder=0,
                   label="chance band (95% CP)")
        ax.axhline(cp * 100.0, color=PALETTE["guide"], lw=0.8, zorder=1)

        # ---- the two arms: every seed drawn, plus the seed mean ------------------
        curves, dmax, crit = {}, {}, {}
        legacy = _transient_legacy(archive, arch)
        for arm in (ITO, EXPO):
            acc = np.array([[dual["curves"][f"{s}|{arm}|{d}"][RULE]
                             for d in dual["delays_realised"]] for s in seeds]) * 100.0
            curves[arm] = acc
            # The two archives must agree on the same replay under the same rule
            for si, s in enumerate(seeds):
                for di, d in enumerate(delays):
                    got = dual["curves"][f"{s}|{arm}|{dual['delays_realised'][di]}"]
                    want = legacy[(s, arm, round(d, 4))]
                    if abs(got["legacy_1_over_n"] - want) > 1e-9:
                        raise AssertionError(
                            f"{arch} {arm} seed {s} D={d}: dual-tie legacy "
                            f"{got['legacy_1_over_n']} != archive {want}")
            estimated = [A.dmax_interp(delays, list(acc[si] / 100.0), floor, FRAC, cp=cp)
                         for si in range(len(seeds))]
            if any(censored for _, censored in estimated):
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"{arch} {arm}: a seed is censored at the grid edge, so its usable "
                    f"delay is a lower bound and must not be drawn as a measurement")
            dmax[arm] = np.array([v for v, _ in estimated])
            archived = np.array(dual["results"][RULE]["dmax"][arm], dtype=float)
            if not np.allclose(dmax[arm], archived, rtol=0, atol=1e-9):
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"{arch} {arm}: re-derived D_max {dmax[arm].tolist()} != archived "
                    f"{archived.tolist()}")
            crit[arm] = np.array([floor + FRAC * (A.iso_dec(list(acc[si] / 100.0))[0]
                                                  - floor) for si in range(len(seeds))])

            for si in range(len(seeds)):
                ax.plot(delays, acc[si], lw=0.6, color=colour[arm], alpha=0.32, zorder=2)
            ax.plot(delays, acc.mean(0), lw=L["mean_lw"], marker="o", ms=L["mean_ms"],
                    color=colour[arm], zorder=3, label=label[arm])
            ax.plot(dmax[arm], crit[arm] * 100.0, ls="none", marker="v", ms=L["dmax_ms"],
                    color=colour[arm], mec="white", mew=0.4, zorder=5)

        # ---- the endpoint this panel supports, re-derived from what is drawn -----
        delta = dmax[ITO] - dmax[EXPO]
        got = A.student_t_ci(delta)
        want = dual["results"][RULE]["delta_primary"]
        if not np.allclose(got, want, rtol=0, atol=1e-9):
            raise AssertionError(f"{arch}: Delta D_max {got} != archived {want}")
        if int((delta < 0).sum()) != int(dual["results"][RULE]["n_negative_primary"]):
            raise AssertionError(f"{arch}: sign concordance disagrees with the archive")
        reported[arch] = got

        # ---- the functional controls ------------------------------------------
        ctl = _controls(archive, arch)
        levels = {}
        for cond in ("state_cleared", "probe_only"):
            per_seed = ctl[cond]
            if sorted(per_seed) != seeds:
                raise AssertionError(f"{arch} {cond}: seeds {sorted(per_seed)} != {seeds}")
            # One hold each (the memory delay); the level is not a function of D, which the
            # gain-zero condition measures at all thirteen holds
            at = {s: sorted(v.items()) for s, v in per_seed.items()}
            if any(len(v) != 1 for v in at.values()):
                raise AssertionError(f"{arch} {cond}: expected one hold per seed, got {at}")
            levels[cond] = {s: v[0][1] for s, v in at.items()}
            where = {v[0][0] for v in at.values()}
            if len(where) != 1:
                raise AssertionError(f"{arch} {cond}: holds differ across seeds: {where}")
            hold = where.pop()
        gz = ctl["gain_zero"]
        for s in seeds:
            flat = sorted({round(v, 12) for v in gz[s].values()})
            if len(gz[s]) != len(delays) or len(flat) != 1:
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"{arch} gain_zero seed {s}: {len(gz[s])} holds, {len(flat)} distinct "
                    f"values -- the label-blind level is not measured flat in D")
            if abs(flat[0] - levels['state_cleared'][s]) > 1e-12 \
                    or abs(flat[0] - levels['probe_only'][s]) > 1e-12:
                raise AssertionError(f"{arch} seed {s}: the three zero-state reads differ")
        pooled = np.array([levels["state_cleared"][s] for s in seeds]) * 100.0
        if float(pooled.max()) > cp * 100.0:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"{arch}: a control clears the chance gate at {pooled.max():.2f}%")
        spans[arch] = (float(pooled.min()), float(pooled.max()))

        # The control levels are still read and still gated above -- the three zero-state
        # reads must agree per seed, the gain-zero level must be flat in D, and none may
        # clear the chance gate -- but they are NO longer drawn, and their entries leave the
        # key with them. Two horizontal dashes inside the chance band added a second grey
        # vocabulary to a panel whose subject is the two arms, and the levels they marked are
        # reported as numbers in the text, against the 12.53% bound. The band stays: a curve
        # inside it is not a measurement, and that has to be visible.
        for cond in ctl_style:
            _ = np.array([levels[cond][s] for s in seeds]) * 100.0

        # The tail is a disclosure, not decoration: at the three longest holds the mean of
        # every arm is inside the chance gate, so the curves do end label-blind, and every
        # D_max drawn is read far below them.
        tail = np.array([[curves[arm].mean(0)[di] for di in (-3, -2, -1)]
                         for arm in (ITO, EXPO)])
        if float(tail.max()) > cp * 100.0:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"{arch}: an arm mean is still above the chance gate at the three longest "
                f"holds ({tail.max():.2f}% > {cp * 100:.2f}%)")
        if float(max(dmax[ITO].max(), dmax[EXPO].max())) >= delays[-3]:
            raise AssertionError(f"{arch}: a D_max reaches the holds that sit in the band")

        ax.set_xlabel("evaluated delay $D$ (s)", fontsize=L["body"])
        if col == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel("accuracy (%)", fontsize=L["body"])
        # Set on the axis, not on the ticks that exist now: tick_params is remembered, so a
        # tick matplotlib creates later -- on a redraw at another dpi, say -- is created at
        # this size too. Setting each label object instead would leave those at 7.4 pt.
        ax.tick_params(axis="both", which="both", labelsize=L["tick"])
        tops.append(float(max(curves[ITO].max(), curves[EXPO].max())))
        if XSCALE == "symlog":
            ax.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=2.0, linscale=0.65)
            # Decade labels on a log axis, not the grid points: 226 s is where the data ends,
            # which the curve already shows. Four labels is also all this panel has room for --
            # at 8.6 pt on a 3.2 in panel, nine would nearly touch.
            ticks = [0, 1, 10, 100]
            ax.set_xticks(ticks)
            ax.set_xticklabels([f"{v:g}" for v in ticks])
            # A full LOG10 minor subdivision, generated and bounded by the axis. Every unit
            # of every decade that falls inside the axis -- 2-9, 20-90, and 200, which the
            # 250 s edge admits and 300 does not -- so 30 or 70 s can be located and not
            # only the labelled decades. The bound is XLIM_S rather than the last label:
            # Cutting at 100 would leave the region the three longest holds sit in
            # unsubdivided, which is exactly the region a reader is being asked to read as
            # label-blind. They carry gridlines but no labels, so the density costs no type.
            minor = [v for decade in (1, 10, 100)
                     for v in (np.arange(2, 10) * decade) if v <= XLIM_S]
            ax.set_xticks(minor, minor=True)
            ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="minor", length=1.8)
            # Faint minor gridlines at the decade subdivisions, so 20 or 40 s can be located
            # without labelling them. Drawn lighter and thinner than the decade grid that
            # house_grid lays down, and below the data.
            ax.grid(True, which="minor", axis="x", color=PALETTE["grid"], lw=0.4,
                    alpha=1.0)
            ax.set_xlim(0.0, XLIM_S)
            # No NullLocator: the minor ticks are chosen explicitly above, and a locator call
            # here would wipe the ticks the minor gridlines are drawn on.
        else:
            ax.set_xlim(-4.0, delays[-1] * 1.03)
        # y ticks pinned AT 20 points. Left automatic they are chosen against the axes size
        # in pixels, so the two panels are free to disagree -- 0/50/100 on one architecture
        # and 0/20/.../80 on the other -- which would break the one thing the shared y range
        # exists for. These are the five the automatic locator chose at the old type size.
        ax.set_yticks([0, 20, 40, 60, 80])
        ax.set_yticklabels([f"{v:g}" for v in (0, 20, 40, 60, 80)])
        panel(ax, "abc"[col], fontsize=L["title"])
        # The architecture name is subordinated to the panel letter. At the title size the
        # bold letter and the name claim their two ends of the panel and read as two titles
        # of equal weight; at the body size the letter stays the largest glyph in the panel,
        # which is the hierarchy the house style intends.
        ax.set_title(name, loc="right", fontsize=L["body"])
        house_grid(ax)
        require_plain_tick_labels(ax)

    # One y range for both accuracy PANELS, so they are read against each other rather than
    # against two different rulers; the ceilings differ by 8 points and the criterion levels
    # with them, which is part of the reading. not panel (c): its y axis is seconds of usable
    # delay, not per cent correct.
    for ax in axes[:2]:
        ax.set_ylim(0.0, max(tops) * 1.08)

    # ---- panel (c): the criterion sweep, from the gate above ---------------------
    crit_colours = _criterion_panel(axes[2], table, checks, L)
    panel(axes[2], "c", fontsize=L["title"])

    fig.tight_layout()

    # ---- Two keys, each over the panels it describes ----------------------------
    # One key for all three panels was tried first and is wrong twice over: four of its five
    # entries say nothing about (c), and adding (c)'s two series to it would put four
    # differently coloured line entries in one block whose reader has just been told that
    # colour means kernel. The arms key is therefore left-aligned on panel (a) and spans (a)
    # and (b); (c)'s key is right-aligned on (c). Both sit above the canvas, so neither can
    # cover data or a panel letter -- which is asserted below rather than assumed. Placed
    # after tight_layout because they read the final axes geometry: a figure legend is
    # invisible to tight_layout, so the order cannot be the other way round.
    found = dict(zip(*reversed(axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels())))
    order = [label[ITO], label[EXPO], "chance band (95% CP)"]
    handles = [found[text] for text in order]
    labels = list(order)
    handles.append(Line2D([], [], color=PALETTE["ink"], ls="none", marker="v",
                          ms=L["key_ms"],
                          mec="white", mew=0.4))
    labels.append(f"$D_{{\\max}}$ per seed at $f$ = {FRAC:g}")
    # Two by two, not three plus one. The two control entries left the key with the lines
    # they described, and four entries at ncol=3 wrap as three on the top row and a single
    # orphan below, which reads as an afterthought rather than as a key. ncol=2 fills both
    # rows and keeps the block inside the (a, b) span. The size is passed explicitly for the
    # same reason the tick labels are.
    left = compact_legend(fig, handles, labels, loc="lower left",
                          bbox_to_anchor=(axes[0].get_position().x0, 1.0),
                          ncol=2, max_chars=L["key_chars"], fontsize=L["tick"])

    found_c = dict(zip(*reversed(axes[2].get_legend_handles_labels())))
    order_c = [CRIT_SERIES[0][1], CRIT_SERIES[1][1], f"primary criterion $f$ = {FRAC:g} (c)"]
    right = compact_legend(fig, [found_c[text] for text in order_c], list(order_c),
                           loc="lower right",
                           bbox_to_anchor=(axes[2].get_position().x1, 1.0),
                           ncol=1, max_chars=L["key_chars"], fontsize=L["tick"])
    for text, colour_c in crit_colours.items():
        if text not in order_c:
            raise AssertionError(f"panel (c) drew {text!r}, which its key does not carry")

    # The two keys are one band above the axes, so they must not run into each other or into
    # anything on the canvas. Checked geometrically, at the drawn size.
    fig.canvas.draw()
    renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
    if Bbox.intersection(left.get_window_extent(renderer),
                         right.get_window_extent(renderer)) is not None:
        raise AssertionError("the two keys overlap: narrow a label or drop a column")
    for ax in axes:
        if legend_overlaps_data(ax, left) or legend_overlaps_data(ax, right):
            raise AssertionError("a key sits on the data")
        if legend_overlaps_furniture(ax, left) or legend_overlaps_furniture(ax, right):
            raise AssertionError("a key sits on a panel letter, an axis label or a tick")

    # ---- the two code paths must agree on the one number all three panels report --
    # (a) and (b) re-derive the endpoint from the curves they draw, through A.dmax_interp and
    # A.student_t_ci here; (c) reaches the same deposit through the release's experiment module,
    # which censors at the grid edge to NaN and summarises the resolved seeds. Two
    # implementations of one estimand on one archive: the declared-fraction reading has to be
    # the same number in both, and the triangles in (a, b) then sit on the guide in (c).
    for arch in ("msnn", "mcsnn"):
        here = reported[arch]
        there = checks[arch]["declared"][:3]
        if any(abs(float(g) - float(w)) > ATOL_S for g, w in zip(here, there)):
            raise AssertionError(
                f"{arch}: the curves' own Delta D_max {here} disagrees with the criterion "
                f"sweep's reading at f = {FRAC:g} {there}; the two paths have diverged")

    young, old = _state_age_span()
    caption_note(_figure_name(), "(a) TemporalMSNN, seeds 40-44; (b) TemporalMCSNN, seeds 30-34; "
                           "(c) both architectures, the same "
                           "five networks each and the same deposited curves, with the endpoint "
                           "read at every criterion fraction instead of only at the declared "
                           "one.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "D is the ADDITIONAL input-free hold, so D = 0 is zero additional hold "
                 "and not zero state age: the sample-dependent state the probe reads spans "
                 f"ages D + {young:g} s to D + {old:g} s, because eight write frames give "
                 "seven inter-frame intervals and the twelve probe ticks add twelve more. "
                 "It is a span, not one additive age.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "Thin lines are the five seeds, the marked line their mean, and each "
                 "triangle one seed's D_max at that seed's own criterion "
                 "floor + 0.75 (ceiling - floor), so the triangle's height IS the "
                 "criterion and its position IS D_max.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "The state-cleared and probe-only controls coincide to every archived "
                 "digit -- both are the same zero-state read -- and the gain-zero "
                 f"condition measures that level flat across all thirteen holds, read at "
                 f"D = {hold:g} s. None of the three is drawn: their levels are reported "
                 "in the text against the 12.53% Clopper-Pearson bound.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "Controls and arms are scored by the same primary membrane tie rule, so "
                 "the chance comparison is made under one rule throughout. Controls span "
                 f"{spans['msnn'][0]:.2f}-{spans['msnn'][1]:.2f}% (a) and "
                 f"{spans['mcsnn'][0]:.2f}-{spans['mcsnn'][1]:.2f}% (b) against the "
                 "12.53% Clopper-Pearson bound.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "At the three longest holds (128.1, 180.1 and 225.8 s) the mean of every "
                 "arm is inside the chance band, and every D_max drawn is read far below "
                 "them; the delay axis is symmetric-log below 2 s so that all thirteen "
                 "holds are shown.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "Delta D_max (ITO - equal-implemented-mean exponential, tau 23.4285 s), "
                 "membrane rule: "
                 f"{reported['msnn'][0]:.2f} s [{reported['msnn'][1]:.2f}, "
                 f"{reported['msnn'][2]:.2f}] (a) and {reported['mcsnn'][0]:.2f} s "
                 f"[{reported['mcsnn'][1]:.2f}, {reported['mcsnn'][2]:.2f}] (b), five seeds, "
                 "Student-t, 5/5 negative in both.")

    # ---- panel (c) ---------------------------------------------------------------
    dense, conv = checks["msnn"], checks["mcsnn"]
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "(c) Mean paired difference dD_max = D_max(measured ITO relaxation) - "
                 "D_max(exponential of the same implemented mean lifetime, tau = 23.4285 s) "
                 "against the criterion fraction f, read from the SAME deposited curves as (a) "
                 "and (b) under the primary membrane tie rule; whiskers are 95% Student-t "
                 "intervals over the five networks of each architecture, and the large marks on "
                 "the dashed guide are the two readings the text quotes.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "In (c) the series are architectures, not kernels: neither the device green "
                 "nor the exponential navy of (a) and (b) is reused, because every series in "
                 "(c) is already a difference between those two arms. The horizontal line at "
                 "zero is furniture, not a series.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "Negative values indicate shorter usable delay with the measured ITO "
                 "relaxation. At the declared criterion the difference is "
                 f"{dense['declared'][0]:.2f} s [{dense['declared'][1]:.2f}, "
                 f"{dense['declared'][2]:.2f}] in the dense network and "
                 f"{conv['declared'][0]:.2f} s [{conv['declared'][1]:.2f}, "
                 f"{conv['declared'][2]:.2f}] in the convolutional one, negative in all five "
                 "networks of each, and those are the same two numbers (a) and (b) report from "
                 "their own re-derivation.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 "The difference is negative and resolved for fractions at or above "
                 f"{conv['resolved_negative_from']:.2f} in the convolutional network and "
                 f"{dense['resolved_negative_from']:.2f} in the dense one, is unresolved "
                 "through the middle of the range, and turns positive below "
                 f"{conv['bracket'][1]:.2f} and {dense['bracket'][1]:.2f} respectively (mean "
                 f"crossings at f = {conv['crossed']:.2f} and {dense['crossed']:.2f} by linear "
                 "interpolation between the swept fractions), reaching a resolved positive "
                 f"value at {conv['resolved_positive_below']:.2f} and "
                 f"{dense['resolved_positive_below']:.2f}. The direction is therefore "
                 "criterion-dependent, which is a property of the estimator and not of the "
                 "material.")
    caption_note(_figure_name(),
                 f"In (c) the difference axis is symmetric-log outside +/-{SYMLOG_S:g} s, so "
                 "that the whole interval at every swept fraction is shown -- the endpoint is "
                 "read near the ceiling at low f, where the curves are flat, and the interval "
                 "there reaches +44 s -- without compressing the region in which the sign "
                 "change and the declared reading are read. No interval is clipped.")

    # R2: the caption carries the prose. The one sanctioned note is outside the axes and
    # annotate_outside() has already verified that it landed there.
    require_no_floating_text(fig)

    # ---- the canvas against the placement, and the printed floor ----------------
    # The floor is checked on the canvas width, which is the pessimistic reading: the page
    # LaTeX actually scales is the bbox='tight' crop, never wider than the canvas, so a
    # figure that clears the floor here clears it as emitted. Checked rather than asserted in
    # a comment, because the smallest glyph is whatever the drawing code left smallest, not
    # whatever this module set: a marker label or a shortened key entry added later would
    # move it without anyone noticing.
    smallest = smallest_pt(fig)
    placed_in = L["placed_pt"] / TEX_PT_PER_IN
    canvas_w = L["canvas"][0]
    printed = smallest * placed_in / canvas_w
    if printed < MIN_PRINTED_PT - 1e-9:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"the smallest glyph is {smallest:.2f} pt on a {canvas_w:.2f} in canvas, so "
            f"at the {L['placed_pt']:.2f} pt measure ({placed_in:.3f} in) it prints "
            f"at {printed:.2f} pt, under the {MIN_PRINTED_PT:.1f} pt house floor; the "
            f"widest canvas that clears it at this type size is "
            f"{size_for(placed_in * 25.4, base_fontsize=smallest):.2f} in")
    return fig, reported, spans, table, checks, crit_result


def build():
    """The wide layout: the registered geometry, type set for the reduction it is placed at."""
    return _render(LAYOUTS["wide"])


def build_compact():
    """The compact layout: the same figure at the house type sizes for a wider measure.

    Not a crop and not a second analysis. It shares :func:`prepare` with :func:`build`, so every
    gate has already run and every number drawn is the same object; what differs is in
    :data:`LAYOUTS`.
    """
    return _render(LAYOUTS["compact"])
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/plotting/\_intervention.py}
\index{tools/plotting/\_intervention.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""fig_intervention -- what the frozen all-layer networks need in order to classify after a delay.

The reading, in three columns:

  1. the intact network is far above chance and the fully cleared one is inside it;
  2. removing any single layer costs a large, resolved fraction of the accuracy;
  3. keeping any single layer recovers little of it.

A grid, not a row. The architectures have different layers, so architecture is a property of the
grid row, named once as that row's axis label, and each panel carries only short layer names in its
own gutter. In a one-row layout the label gutter is shared with the neighbouring panel, and long
labels spill into its data area.

Why three separate scales. Column 1 is an absolute accuracy. Column 2 is accuracy lost relative to
the intact network. Column 3 is accuracy recovered relative to the control in which the state was
never written. Three quantities against three references: on one axis equal lengths would mean
different things, and a single 0-100% axis compresses the left edge to the point of being
unreadable. Within a column the two rows share limits, so lengths are comparable where they
are commensurable and nowhere else.

One colour and no legend. Every mark in a panel is the same kind of thing, so hue would carry no
information; the column titles say what is measured and the row's axis label says whose network it
is.

Faint points are the individual networks, drawn because five is few enough that the spread should be
shown rather than summarised -- one sufficiency row is carried almost entirely by a single network,
which an interval alone would hide.

No data is recomputed: every value is read from the deposited per-seed records.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib as _pathlib

_DATA = _pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "data"

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = HERE / "fig_intervention.pdf"



from mnn_torch import estimators as A                                          # Noqa: E402
from .common import (PALETTE, apply_style, house_grid,             # noqa: E402
                                require_plain_tick_labels, smallest_pt)

D = "4.0725"
#: Colours inherited from ``frozen_substitution_delay``, with its meanings, not just its hues.
#: There the measured device
#: kernel is PALETTE["device"], the comparator is PALETTE["exponential"], the no-state controls are
#: PALETTE["control"], the chance band is PALETTE["grid"] at alpha 0.55 and its bound is
#: PALETTE["guide"]. This figure has no comparator, so the exponential colour is deliberately unused
#: rather than borrowed for something else; every mark that quantifies what the measured volatile
#: state contributes is DEVICE, every mark for a condition holding no state is CONTROL, and chance is
#: drawn exactly as that figure draws it, and per-network points reuse its per-seed alpha of 0.32.
DEVICE = PALETTE["device"]
CONTROL = PALETTE["control"]
BAND = PALETTE["grid"]
GUIDE = PALETTE["guide"]
INK = PALETTE["ink"]
GREY = PALETTE["control"]
RULE = PALETTE["grid"]
SEED_ALPHA = 0.32

ARCHES = ("mcsnn", "msnn")
ROWLAB = {"mcsnn": "TemporalMCSNN", "msnn": "TemporalMSNN"}
#: Short, because these sit in each panel's own gutter. `fc1` names different layers in the two
#: architectures, so the implementation name is resolved before a reader ever sees it.
LAYER = {"mcsnn": {"conv1": "conv1", "conv2": "conv2", "fc1": "output"},
         "msnn": {"fc1": "hidden", "fc2": "output"}}
#: Short enough to fit the panel: each is about 1.9 in wide, and a descriptive label runs past its
#: own axes into the neighbouring column. What each quantity is referenced to belongs in the
#: caption; the axis only has to distinguish the three.
COLTITLE = ("accuracy after delay (%)",
            "loss when cleared (pp)",
            "gain kept alone (pp)")


def load(arch):
    """The five per-network records for one architecture, from the all-layer archive."""
    doc = json.loads((_DATA / "all_volatile.json").read_text())
    recs = [r for r in doc["records"]["nmnist_all_layer"] if r.get("arch") == arch]
    recs.sort(key=lambda r: r["seed"])
    if len(recs) != 5 or any(r.get("calibration_failed") for r in recs):
        raise SystemExit(f"{arch}: expected five complete networks in the all-layer archive, "
                         f"found {len(recs)}")
    return recs


def ci(vals):
    m, lo, hi = A.student_t_ci(list(vals))
    return m * 100.0, lo * 100.0, hi * 100.0


def strip(ax, y, vals, colour=None, *, spread=0.13):
    """Faint per-network points, then the mean and its 95% interval drawn over them."""
    colour = colour or DEVICE
    v = np.asarray(vals, float) * 100.0
    off = (np.arange(v.size) - (v.size - 1) / 2.0) * (2.0 * spread / max(v.size - 1, 1))
    ax.scatter(v, np.full(v.size, y) + off, s=6.5, color=colour, alpha=SEED_ALPHA,
               linewidths=0, zorder=2)
    m, lo, hi = ci(vals)
    ax.plot([lo, hi], [y, y], color=colour, lw=1.5, solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=3)
    ax.plot([m], [y], marker="o", ms=4.6, color=colour, mec="white", mew=0.4, zorder=4)


def finish(ax, labels, *, xlim, bottom, xlabel=None, ylabel=None):
    ys = list(range(len(labels)))[::-1]
    ax.set_yticks(ys)
    ax.set_yticklabels(labels)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.8, len(labels) - 0.2)
    ax.set_xlim(*xlim)
    if xlabel:
        ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, labelpad=5)
    if not bottom:
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelbottom=False)
    house_grid(ax)
    ax.grid(False, axis="y")
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
    for side in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
    return ys


def build():
    apply_style()
    data = {a: load(a) for a in ARCHES}
    cp = data["mcsnn"][0]["cp95"] * 100.0
    floor = data["mcsnn"][0]["floor"] * 100.0

    def span(vals):
        lo, hi = min(vals + [0.0]), max(vals)
        m = 0.08 * (hi - lo)
        return lo - m, hi + m

    nec = [r["delta_necessity"][l] * 100.0 for a in ARCHES for r in data[a]
           for l in data[a][0]["layers"]]
    suf = [r["delta_sufficiency"][l] * 100.0 for a in ARCHES for r in data[a]
           for l in data[a][0]["layers"]]
    xlims = ((0.0, 100.0), span(nec), span(suf))

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7.18, 3.40))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 3, wspace=0.30, hspace=0.22,
                          left=0.140, right=0.995, top=0.915, bottom=0.140)
    axes = np.empty((2, 3), dtype=object)
    for i, arch in enumerate(ARCHES):
        recs, layers = data[arch], data[arch][0]["layers"]
        lab = [LAYER[arch][l] for l in layers]
        bottom = (i == len(ARCHES) - 1)

        ax = axes[i, 0] = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, 0])
        # The chance band exactly as ``frozen_substitution_delay`` draws it: grid fill,
        # guide-coloured bound
        ax.axvspan(0.0, cp, color=BAND, alpha=0.55, lw=0, zorder=0)
        ax.axvline(cp, color=GUIDE, lw=0.8, zorder=1)
        ax.plot([floor, floor], [-0.8, 1.2], color=GUIDE, lw=0.8, ls=(0, (2.4, 1.6)), zorder=1)
        ys = finish(ax, ["intact", "all cleared"], xlim=xlims[0], bottom=bottom,
                    xlabel=COLTITLE[0] if bottom else None, ylabel=ROWLAB[arch])
        strip(ax, ys[0], [r["accs"]["intact"][D] for r in recs], DEVICE)
        strip(ax, ys[1], [r["accs"]["cleared_all"][D] for r in recs], CONTROL)
        if i == 0:
            ax.annotate("chance", xy=(cp + 2.5, ys[1]), fontsize=6.6, color=GUIDE,
                        ha="left", va="center")

        for c, key in ((1, "delta_necessity"), (2, "delta_sufficiency")):
            ax = axes[i, c] = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, c])
            ax.axvline(0.0, color=RULE, lw=0.8, zorder=1)
            ys = finish(ax, lab, xlim=xlims[c], bottom=bottom,
                        xlabel=COLTITLE[c] if bottom else None)
            for y, l in zip(ys, layers):
                strip(ax, y, [r[key][l] for r in recs], DEVICE)

    for r, letters in enumerate(("abc", "def")):
        for c, letter in enumerate(letters):
            axes[r, c].set_title(letter, fontsize=8.6, loc="left", pad=3, color=INK,
                                 fontweight="bold")
    return fig, data, cp


def audit(fig, data, cp):
    """The three claims, checked against the plotted numbers before the file is written."""
    bad = []
    for arch, recs in data.items():
        if any(r["accs"]["cleared_all"][D] * 100.0 > cp for r in recs):
            bad.append(f"{arch}: a fully cleared network exceeds the chance bound")
        if not all(r["accs"]["intact"][D] * 100.0 > cp for r in recs):
            bad.append(f"{arch}: an intact network fails the chance bound")
        for l in recs[0]["layers"]:
            if not all(r["delta_necessity"][l] > 0 for r in recs):
                bad.append(f"{arch}: clearing {l} does not cost accuracy in every network")
            if max(r["accs"][f"only_{l}"][D] for r in recs) >= \
                    min(r["accs"]["intact"][D] for r in recs):
                bad.append(f"{arch}: keeping {l} alone reaches intact accuracy")
    for ax in fig.axes:
        require_plain_tick_labels(ax)
    return bad


def main():
    fig, data, cp = build()
    problems = audit(fig, data, cp)
    fig.savefig(OUT, bbox_inches="tight")
    w, h = fig.get_size_inches()
    print(f"  wrote {OUT.name}  canvas {w:.2f} x {h:.2f} in  smallest glyph "
          f"{smallest_pt(fig):.2f} pt")
    for arch, recs in data.items():
        print(f"  {arch}: intact {ci([r['accs']['intact'][D] for r in recs])[0]:.2f}%  "
              f"cleared {ci([r['accs']['cleared_all'][D] for r in recs])[0]:.2f}%  "
              f"layers {[LAYER[arch][l] for l in recs[0]['layers']]}")
    print("  " + ("all three claims verified against the plotted data" if not problems else
                  f"{len(problems)} PROBLEMS\n    " + "\n    ".join(problems)))
    return 1 if problems else 0
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/plotting/\_protocol.py}
\index{tools/plotting/\_protocol.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""fig_protocol -- what is trained, and what is swapped afterwards.

The one reading this figure must deliver. Panels (a) and (b) show the two networks with a
bracket spanning everything that is trained. Panel (c) shows the same chain with a bracket
spanning everything that is frozen, and exactly one block outside that bracket, marked as the
thing that is exchanged. A reader who looks only at the brackets should get the protocol.

Why this is a complete redraw, not an edit. The previous version drew neuron circles on axes
whose x and y scales differed by a factor of about 1.45 -- roughly 2.3 in across ten data units
against 2.1 in up six and a half -- so every ``Circle`` came out visibly oblong and the boxes
read as crude squares. Two things fix that class of defect at the source rather than by
adjusting numbers:

* ``set_aspect("equal")`` on every panel, with the coordinate ranges chosen to match the
  panel's physical aspect, so a circle is a circle and a square is a square;
* no round glyphs at all. Layers are rounded bars and synapses are rounded boxes, both drawn
  with ``FancyBboxPatch``, so nothing in the figure depends on an aspect ratio being right.

The visual grammar, held across all three panels
    tall thin rounded bar   a layer of units; its label is the layer width
    wide rounded box        a synapse; its label is the map it applies
    grey fill               ideal, non-volatile, and identical between the two replays
    GREEN                   the class-output layer, in every panel and in both of its states
    square bracket below    the span of a statement about training: "trained", or "frozen"
    green bracket above     a statement about the class-output layer: "ideal", or "swapped"

Green marks the same element throughout, not one of its states. The class-output layer is green
in all three panels, because it is one layer whose treatment changes rather than two different
components: ideal and non-volatile while the network is trained, volatile and exchanged
afterwards. Which of those two states applies is said by the bracket above it -- "ideal" in (a)
and (b), "swapped" in (c) -- so the colour carries identity and the bracket carries state.
Colouring it grey during training would make the trained output layer and the replayed one look
like unrelated blocks, hiding the fact that the mapping is onto the same layer.

Why the volatile element is last in every chain. It is the class-output layer in both networks
-- ``fc2`` 64->10 in the dense one and ``fc1`` 32->10 in the convolutional one -- so exactly one
fading state stands between the stimulus and the class decision. Drawing it first, upstream of
the hidden layer, would make the attribution unreadable.

And why no membrane is drawn decaying. Neuronal state is reset before every probe; that is what
leaves the volatile layer as the only surviving sample-dependent state. The decay profiles
attach to the volatile block and to nothing else.

NO data. The two profiles come from their closed forms, so the shapes compared are the real
ones: the measured stretched exponential, and the exponential of equal implemented mean
lifetime, 23.4285 s. No axis is numbered. The ITO measurement supplies the decay shape only;
the array and its static electrical model are SiOx, which the caption states.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib as _pathlib

_DATA = _pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "data"

from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, Rectangle

from .common import PALETTE, apply_style, smallest_pt

OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "fig_protocol.pdf"   # Not with_suffix(): this file is *_source.py

GREEN = PALETTE["device"]           # The volatile layer, and the measured decay
NAVY = PALETTE["exponential"]       # Exponential of equal implemented mean lifetime
INK = PALETTE["ink"]
GREY = PALETTE["control"]
FILL = "#eaeef2"                    # Ideal, non-volatile
FILL_V = "#e7f6f1"                  # Volatile
RULE = PALETTE["grid"]

TAU_KWW, BETA_KWW = 16.033, 0.6225
TAU_EXP = 23.4285                   # Implemented mean lifetime, not the analytic 23.0323

TITLE_PT, LABEL_PT, SMALL_PT = 8.6, 7.2, 6.8

#: Panel coordinate box. The panels are ~2.33 in wide, so at ten units across one unit is
#: 0.233 in and an equal-aspect panel 1.94 in tall spans 8.32 units. Both are set explicitly
#: and ``set_aspect("equal")`` enforces the correspondence.
XMAX, YMAX = 10.0, 8.32

BASE = 4.30                          # Vertical centre of every chain
BAR_W, BAR_H = 0.46, 2.05            # a layer
BOX_H = 1.44                         # a synapse


def bar(ax, x, label, *, colour=INK, fill=FILL):
    """A layer: tall thin rounded bar, labelled with its width underneath."""
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x, BASE - BAR_H / 2), BAR_W, BAR_H,
                                boxstyle="round,pad=0,rounding_size=0.16",
                                fc=fill, ec=colour, lw=0.9, zorder=4,
                                mutation_aspect=1.0))
    ax.text(x + BAR_W / 2, BASE - BAR_H / 2 - 0.30, label, fontsize=SMALL_PT, color=INK,
            ha="center", va="top")
    return x + BAR_W


def synapse(ax, x, w, top, bottom, *, green=False):
    """A synapse: wide rounded box, labelled with the map it applies.

    ``green`` marks the class-output layer, which is the same layer in all three panels.
    """
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x, BASE - BOX_H / 2), w, BOX_H,
                                boxstyle="round,pad=0,rounding_size=0.18",
                                fc=FILL_V if green else FILL, ec=GREEN if green else INK,
                                lw=1.5 if green else 0.9, zorder=4, mutation_aspect=1.0))
    for dy, txt in ((0.26, top), (-0.34, bottom)):
        ax.text(x + w / 2, BASE + dy, txt, fontsize=SMALL_PT,
                color=GREEN if green else INK, ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)
    return x + w


def link(ax, x0, x1, *, colour=INK):
    """The plain connector between blocks. Short, so it never carries a label."""
    ax.annotate("", xy=(x1, BASE), xytext=(x0, BASE),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=colour, lw=0.9,
                                shrinkA=0.0, shrinkB=0.0), zorder=3)


def bracket(ax, x0, x1, y, label, *, colour=INK, depth=0.28, pt=LABEL_PT, style=None):
    """A square bracket spanning ``x0``..``x1``, labelled below its centre.

    Drawn from line segments rather than an arrowstyle bracket, because the arrowstyle
    variants size their jaws in points and so change shape when the panel is resized, which is
    exactly the coupling this figure is trying to remove.
    """
    xm = 0.5 * (x0 + x1)
    ax.plot([x0, x0, x1, x1], [y + depth, y, y, y + depth], color=colour, lw=0.9,
            solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=3)
    ax.text(xm, y - 0.26, label, fontsize=pt, color=colour, ha="center", va="top",
            style=style or "normal", linespacing=1.25)


def bracket_above(ax, x0, x1, y, label, *, colour=GREEN, depth=0.28, pt=LABEL_PT,
                  style="italic"):
    """``bracket`` inverted: jaws point down at the blocks, label sits above.

    Used in the space between a panel title and its chain, so a statement about one block can
    be made without competing with the training bracket underneath.
    """
    xm = 0.5 * (x0 + x1)
    ax.plot([x0, x0, x1, x1], [y - depth, y, y, y - depth], color=colour, lw=0.9,
            solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=3)
    ax.text(xm, y + 0.24, label, fontsize=pt, color=colour, ha="center", va="bottom",
            style=style)


def frames(ax, x, n=8):
    """The eight ordered input frames, as an offset stack of plain squares."""
    s, dx, dy = 0.52, 0.105, 0.085
    # Centred on the chain. The stack's own height is (n-1)*dy + s, so it is centred from that
    # rather than anchored to the bar bottom, which is what left it sitting low against its
    # neighbours: the offsets accumulate upward, so a bottom anchor puts the stack's midline
    # below BASE by half the accumulated offset.
    y0 = BASE - ((n - 1) * dy + s) / 2.0
    for i in range(n):
        ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x + i * dx, y0 + i * dy), s, s, fc="white", ec=GREY,
                               lw=0.8, zorder=4 + i * 0.01))
    return x + (n - 1) * dx + s


def profile(t, kind):
    if kind == "kww":
        return np.exp(-((t / TAU_KWW) ** BETA_KWW))
    return np.exp(-t / TAU_EXP)


def cartridge(ax, x, y, w, h):
    """The two interchangeable decay profiles, in a rounded frame above the volatile block."""
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x, y), w, h,
                                boxstyle="round,pad=0,rounding_size=0.16",
                                fc="white", ec=GREY, lw=0.9, zorder=4,
                                mutation_aspect=1.0))
    px0, px1 = x + 0.30, x + w - 0.30
    py0, py1 = y + 0.26, y + h - 0.26
    t = np.linspace(0.0, 40.0, 300)
    for kind, colour, ls in (("kww", GREEN, "-"), ("exp", NAVY, (0, (3.6, 1.6)))):
        ax.plot(px0 + (px1 - px0) * t / 40.0, py0 + (py1 - py0) * profile(t, kind),
                color=colour, lw=1.5, ls=ls, zorder=5, solid_capstyle="round")
    ax.plot([px0, px0], [py0, py1], color=RULE, lw=0.7, zorder=4)
    ax.plot([px0, px1], [py0, py0], color=RULE, lw=0.7, zorder=4)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- panels --
def panel_a(ax):
    """The dense network, with a bracket over everything that is trained."""
    ax.set_title("a   TemporalMSNN pre-training", fontsize=TITLE_PT, loc="left",
                 pad=4, color=INK)
    x = 0.42
    x = bar(ax, x, "578")
    link(ax, x + 0.08, x + 0.52)
    x = synapse(ax, x + 0.60, 2.28, "dense", r"$578{\to}64$")
    link(ax, x + 0.08, x + 0.52)
    x = bar(ax, x + 0.60, "64")
    link(ax, x + 0.08, x + 0.52)
    out0 = x + 0.60
    x = synapse(ax, out0, 2.28, "output", r"$64{\to}10$", green=True)
    out1 = x
    link(ax, x + 0.08, x + 0.52)
    x = bar(ax, x + 0.60, "10")
    bracket(ax, 0.42, x, 2.28, "trained together\nno device, hold or probe", style="italic")
    bracket_above(ax, out0, out1, 6.20, "ideal")


def panel_b(ax):
    """The convolutional network, same grammar and the same bracket."""
    ax.set_title("b   TemporalMCSNN pre-training", fontsize=TITLE_PT, loc="left",
                 pad=4, color=INK)
    x = frames(ax, 0.34)
    ax.text(0.34 + 0.62, BASE - BAR_H / 2 - 0.30, "8 frames", fontsize=SMALL_PT, color=INK,
            ha="center", va="top")
    link(ax, x + 0.06, x + 0.44)
    x = synapse(ax, x + 0.50, 1.40, "conv", "4 ch")
    link(ax, x + 0.06, x + 0.40)
    x = synapse(ax, x + 0.46, 1.40, "conv", "8 ch")
    link(ax, x + 0.06, x + 0.40)
    x = bar(ax, x + 0.46, "32")
    link(ax, x + 0.06, x + 0.40)
    out0 = x + 0.46
    x = synapse(ax, out0, 1.82, "output", r"$32{\to}10$", green=True)
    out1 = x
    link(ax, x + 0.06, x + 0.40)
    x = bar(ax, x + 0.46, "10")
    bracket(ax, 0.34, x, 2.28, "trained together\nno device, hold or probe", style="italic")
    bracket_above(ax, out0, out1, 6.20, "ideal")


def panel_c(ax):
    """After training: one bracket for what is frozen, one block outside it for what is swapped."""
    ax.set_title("c   Kernel swap post-training", fontsize=TITLE_PT, loc="left",
                 pad=4, color=INK)
    x = 0.40
    x = bar(ax, x, "input")   # Either architecture's input: this panel is shared by both
    link(ax, x + 0.08, x + 0.52)
    x_enc0 = x + 0.60
    x = synapse(ax, x_enc0, 2.26, "encoder", "as trained")
    x_frozen_end = x
    link(ax, x + 0.08, x + 0.52)
    x_v0 = x + 0.60
    x = synapse(ax, x_v0, 2.72, "volatile", "output layer", green=True)
    x_v1 = x
    link(ax, x + 0.08, x + 0.52)
    x = bar(ax, x + 0.60, "10")

    # What is frozen, and what is not
    bracket(ax, 0.40, x_frozen_end, 2.28, "fixed")
    bracket(ax, x_v0, x_v1, 2.28, "swapped", colour=GREEN, style="italic")

    # The two profiles, installed into the block below them
    cartridge(ax, x_v0 - 0.62, 6.10, 3.96, 1.78)
    ax.annotate("", xy=(0.5 * (x_v0 + x_v1), BASE + BOX_H / 2 + 0.10),
                xytext=(0.5 * (x_v0 + x_v1), 6.02),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=GREY, lw=1.0,
                                linestyle=(0, (2.6, 1.7)), shrinkA=0.0, shrinkB=0.0),
                zorder=3)
    ax.text(x_v0 - 0.80, 7.36, "measured\ndecay", fontsize=SMALL_PT, color=GREEN,
            ha="right", va="center", linespacing=1.3)
    ax.text(x_v0 - 0.80, 6.36, "equal-mean\nexponential", fontsize=SMALL_PT, color=NAVY,
            ha="right", va="center", linespacing=1.3)


def build():
    apply_style()
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7.15, 2.42))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(1, 3, wspace=0.05, left=0.008, right=0.992, top=0.90, bottom=0.02)
    for i, fn in enumerate((panel_a, panel_b, panel_c)):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, i])
        ax.set_xlim(0, XMAX)
        ax.set_ylim(0, YMAX)
        ax.set_aspect("equal")          # a circle is a circle; a square is a square
        ax.axis("off")
        fn(ax)
    return fig


def audit(fig, *, pad_pt=1.0):
    """Overlapping labels, labels outside their panel, and labels crossing a block edge.

    Text extents depend on the font and the panel width, so they cannot be estimated while the
    coordinates are written -- a collision is invisible in the source and has to be measured on
    the rendered canvas. A label overlapping a block must be wholly inside it, or it is clipped.
    """
    fig.canvas.draw()
    r = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
    bad = []
    for pi, ax in enumerate(fig.axes, start=1):
        ab = ax.get_window_extent(renderer=r)
        boxes = [(t, t.get_window_extent(renderer=r)) for t in ax.texts
                 if t.get_text().strip()]
        for i in range(len(boxes)):
            ti, bi = boxes[i]
            for j in range(i + 1, len(boxes)):
                tj, bj = boxes[j]
                if bi.padded(pad_pt).overlaps(bj.padded(pad_pt)):
                    bad.append(f"panel {pi}: LABELS OVERLAP {ti.get_text()[:24]!r} <-> "
                               f"{tj.get_text()[:24]!r}")
        for t, b in boxes:
            if not (ab.containsx(b.x0) and ab.containsx(b.x1)):
                bad.append(f"panel {pi}: LABEL PAST SIDE EDGE {t.get_text()[:32]!r}")
            elif not (ab.containsy(b.y0) and ab.containsy(b.y1)):
                bad.append(f"panel {pi}: LABEL PAST TOP/BOTTOM {t.get_text()[:32]!r}")
        for p in ax.patches:
            pb = p.get_window_extent(renderer=r)
            if not (ab.containsx(pb.x0) and ab.containsx(pb.x1)
                    and ab.containsy(pb.y0) and ab.containsy(pb.y1)):
                bad.append(f"panel {pi}: BLOCK OUTSIDE PANEL {type(p).__name__}")
        for t, b in boxes:
            for p in ax.patches:
                pb = p.get_window_extent(renderer=r)
                if b.overlaps(pb) and not (pb.containsx(b.x0) and pb.containsx(b.x1)
                                           and pb.containsy(b.y0) and pb.containsy(b.y1)):
                    bad.append(f"panel {pi}: LABEL CROSSES A BLOCK EDGE "
                               f"{t.get_text()[:26]!r}")
                    break

    # Titles: left-aligned, so a long one runs off the canvas or into the next panel, and
    # neither shows up in the checks above because a title is not in ax.texts.
    #
    # It must be the left-title artist. ``set_title(loc="left")`` does not write ``ax.title``
    # -- that is the centre title, which stays empty here and reports zero width, so checking
    # it would pass any left title whatever its width. The left title lives on
    # ``ax._left_title``; it is private, so it is fetched defensively and the check states
    # loudly if it cannot be found rather than silently passing.
    fb = fig.get_window_extent(renderer=r)
    tb = []
    for i, ax in enumerate(fig.axes, start=1):
        art = getattr(ax, "_left_title", None) or ax.title
        if not art.get_text().strip():
            if ax.get_title(loc="left").strip():
                bad.append(f"panel {i}: TITLE CHECK CANNOT REACH THE TITLE ARTIST")
            continue
        tb.append((i, art, art.get_window_extent(renderer=r)))
    for i, t, b in tb:
        if b.x1 > fb.x1 or b.x0 < fb.x0:
            bad.append(f"panel {i}: TITLE RUNS OFF THE CANVAS {t.get_text()[:40]!r}")
        if b.y1 > fb.y1:
            bad.append(f"panel {i}: TITLE RUNS OFF THE TOP {t.get_text()[:40]!r}")
    for a in range(len(tb)):
        for c in range(a + 1, len(tb)):
            if tb[a][2].padded(1.0).overlaps(tb[c][2].padded(1.0)):
                bad.append(f"TITLES OVERLAP {tb[a][1].get_text()[:26]!r} <-> "
                           f"{tb[c][1].get_text()[:26]!r}")
    return bad


def main():
    fig = build()
    problems = audit(fig)
    fig.savefig(OUT)
    w, h = fig.get_size_inches()
    print(f"  wrote {OUT.name}   canvas {w:.2f} x {h:.2f} in   aspect equal on all panels")
    print(f"  smallest glyph {smallest_pt(fig):.2f} pt   "
          f"prints at {smallest_pt(fig) * (178.0 / 25.4) / w:.2f} pt at 178 mm")
    if problems:
        print(f"\n  {len(problems)} LAYOUT DEFECTS")
        for p in problems:
            print(f"    {p}")
    else:
        print("  layout clean")
    return 1 if problems else 0
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/plotting/\_schematic.py}
\index{tools/plotting/\_schematic.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""How the spiking neuron works: weighted inputs, and the membrane over time.

Two panels, in the same theme as the device and protocol figures: bold lowercase panel
letter then a sentence-case title, structure as rounded shapes with grey borders.

The theme is unchanged from the accepted version: bold lowercase panel letter then a
sentence-case title, structure as rounded shapes with grey borders, the element that holds
state given a green border and a pale green fill, which is how every figure here marks a
volatile layer, and physical panels carrying an L-shaped axis with no numbers.

Two things are fixed.

1. panel (b) now shares its time axis with the input spikes. Before, the membrane was drawn
   alone: every jump appeared without a visible cause, so the trace read as an arbitrary
   squiggle. The input spikes are now a row directly above it and the output spikes a row
   directly below, all three on one x-axis, so each jump lines up with the spike that caused
   it and each threshold crossing with the spike it emits. The arrivals are also spread out
   rather than packed, so a jump and the decay after it are separately visible.

2. No floating text anywhere. Every word is an axis label, a tick label or a panel title, so
   `require_no_floating_text` applies and is asserted. That removed four annotation phrases,
   the `x_i` and `w_i` symbols and the text inside the neuron: the caption carries what they
   said, the three input rows are distinguished by tick density and the three connections by
   line thickness, and the neuron is identified by the panel title and the caption.

Panel (a) draws the same events as panel (b), not a decorative substitute: the same three
input trains and the same output spikes, compressed onto the diagram. ``audit`` asserts the
counts match, so the two panels cannot drift apart.

What it draws, and what the model actually does. The training loop's neuron subtracts the
threshold on firing and has no refractory lockout, so there is no reset to a drawn V_reset and no
shaded refractory window: each crossing drops by exactly one threshold and continues from a state
clear of zero. The x-axis carries no units, because a timestep has no physical duration until the
measured relaxation is introduced.

NO randomness. The arrivals are written down, because this is a schematic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
from matplotlib.transforms import ScaledTranslation

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

from .common import (PALETTE, apply_style,                   # Noqa: E402
                                require_no_floating_text,
                                require_plain_tick_labels, smallest_pt)

OUT = None
PNG = None

#: The canvas is the placed width, so LaTeX scales it 1:1 and printed type equals set type.
#: The placement is \textwidth = 437.461 pt = 6.053 in (measured, not assumed). A 7.20 in
#: canvas at 0.95 textwidth scaled to 0.799 and printed this figure's 7.4 pt labels at 5.91 pt,
#: under the 7 pt house floor. The remedy is a narrower canvas at width=\textwidth, never a
#: larger font: printed size is fontsize * placed / canvas, so inflating the font and the
#: canvas together buys nothing.
PLACED_IN = 437.46112 / 72.27
MIN_PRINTED_PT = 7.0

#: How far a panel title sits right of its letter, in points, so both panels match.
TITLE_GAP_PT = 11.0
MIN_LETTER_GAP_PT = 1.5

DRIVE = PALETTE["exponential"]   # Input spikes, in the comparator colour
STATE = PALETTE["device"]        # The neuron and its membrane: what holds state
FILL = "#e4f5ef"                 # The pale green that fills a volatile layer
EDGE = PALETTE["grid"]           # Baselines and box borders
GUIDE = PALETTE["guide"]         # Threshold and connectors
INK = PALETTE["ink"]             # Output spikes and type

T = 32
V_TH = 1.0
LAM = 0.86                       # Per-step membrane decay factor
WEIGHTS = (0.40, 0.28, 0.16)     # Channel 0 the strongest

#: (timestep, channel). The pattern is the same three times, which is why it reads as a rule
#: rather than a squiggle: one or two single arrivals build the membrane up in visible steps,
#: a coincidence on all three channels then carries it over the threshold, and a long quiet
#: stretch lets it leak back down. A single arrival on the strongest channel contributes 0.40
#: against a threshold of 1, so only a coincidence can overshoot far enough for the
#: subtraction to be visible.
#:
#: The three crossings are deliberately not adjacent. Two consecutive crossings would
#: demonstrate the absence of a refractory lockout, but they cost more than they buy: at panel
#: (a)'s compressed scale the pair merges into one mark, so (a) shows two output spikes where
#: (b) shows three, and the doublet is then the busiest thing in (b). Evenly separated crossings
#: show three marks in both panels, and that the model has no refractory lockout is stated in
#: the caption rather than drawn.
ARRIVALS = [(2, 0), (6, 1),
            (9, 0), (9, 1), (9, 2),
            (14, 0), (17, 1),
            (18, 0), (18, 1), (18, 2),
            (23, 0),
            (27, 0), (27, 1), (27, 2)]


def trains():
    out = [np.zeros(T) for _ in WEIGHTS]
    for t, c in ARRIVALS:
        out[c][t] = 1.0
    return out


def integrate(tr):
    """Leaky integration, reset by subtraction, no refractory lockout.

    The polyline carries the pre-reset peak and then the post-reset value at the same
    timestep. Plotting the recorded state instead would never touch the threshold, because at
    a firing step it is already reduced by it, and the crossing would be invisible.
    """
    v, xs, ys, spikes = 0.0, [], [], []
    for t in range(T):
        v = LAM * v + sum(w * s[t] for w, s in zip(WEIGHTS, tr))
        xs.append(t); ys.append(v)
        if v > V_TH:
            v -= V_TH
            xs.append(t); ys.append(v)
            spikes.append(1.0)
        else:
            spikes.append(0.0)
    return np.array(xs, float), np.array(ys, float), np.array(spikes)


def l_axis(ax, *, left=True, bottom=True):
    """The physical-panel axis: no box, no numbers, no grid; ticks carry words or nothing."""
    for side in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_visible(left)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_visible(bottom)
    for side in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[side].set_color(INK)
        ax.spines[side].set_linewidth(0.8)
    ax.grid(False)
    ax.tick_params(length=0, pad=3)
    return ax


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Panel (a): the arrangement, drawn with no text at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def panel_a(ax, tr, spikes):
    ax.set_xlim(0.0, 9.90); ax.set_ylim(0, 6); ax.axis("off")
    rows = (4.50, 3.05, 1.60)
    thick = (2.0, 1.35, 0.85)                       # Thickness carries the weight
    # One timebase for the input rows and the output row. Given a shorter span than the
    # inputs, the output row bunched its three marks into the left fifth of its own baseline
    # and read as an afterthought. Both spans are SPAN wide, so a mark at the same timestep
    # sits at the same offset along either row.
    # Horizontal budget, rebalanced for the narrower canvas. At 6.05 in the box that had held
    # "neuron" comfortably at 7.20 in no longer did -- the word overflowed it by 0.08 units,
    # which the box-fit check caught. The box is wider and the stages after it shift right to
    # pay for it, so the input and output rows keep the same SPAN and therefore the same
    # Timebase.
    SPAN = 2.05
    BOX_W = 1.85
    x0, x1 = 0.58, 0.58 + SPAN                      # The input trains, clear of their labels
    conv = (5.30, 3.05)                             # Where the connections meet the neuron
    ox0, ox1 = conv[0] + BOX_W + 0.30, conv[0] + BOX_W + 0.30 + SPAN   # The output train

    for i, (y, w, train) in enumerate(zip(rows, thick, tr)):
        ax.plot([x0, x1], [y, y], color=EDGE, lw=1.0, zorder=1, solid_capstyle="round")
        for t in np.flatnonzero(train):
            ax.vlines(x0 + SPAN * (t + 0.5) / T, y - 0.36, y + 0.36,
                      color=DRIVE, lw=1.3, zorder=3)
        ax.text(x0 - 0.14, y, f"$x_{i + 1}$", color=INK, fontsize=7.8,
                ha="right", va="center")
        ax.annotate("", xy=conv, xytext=(x1 + 0.16, y),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=GUIDE, lw=w,
                                    shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))
        xm = (x1 + 0.16) + 0.52 * (conv[0] - x1 - 0.16)
        ax.text(xm, y + 0.52 * (conv[1] - y) + 0.28, f"$w_{i + 1}$", color=INK,
                fontsize=7.2, ha="center", va="bottom")

    # The neuron, given the highlight reserved for the element that holds state
    NEURON = (conv[0], 2.40, BOX_W, 1.30)           # x, y, w, h -- audited against its text
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch(NEURON[:2], NEURON[2], NEURON[3],
                                boxstyle="round,pad=0.0,rounding_size=0.24",
                                linewidth=1.5, edgecolor=STATE, facecolor=FILL, zorder=4))
    cx = NEURON[0] + NEURON[2] / 2
    for dy, word in ((0.26, "leaky"), (-0.24, "neuron")):
        ax.text(cx, 3.05 + dy, word, color=STATE, fontsize=7.8, ha="center", va="center",
                zorder=5, gid="neuron-word")
    ax._neuron_rect = NEURON
    ax.annotate("", xy=(ox0, 3.05), xytext=(NEURON[0] + NEURON[2] + 0.04, 3.05),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=GUIDE, lw=1.0,
                                mutation_scale=8, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))

    # The output train, on a grey baseline of its own exactly like the inputs
    ax.plot([ox0, ox1], [3.05, 3.05], color=EDGE, lw=1.0, zorder=1,
            solid_capstyle="round")
    for t in np.flatnonzero(spikes):
        ax.vlines(ox0 + SPAN * (t + 0.5) / T, 3.05 - 0.36, 3.05 + 0.36,
                  color=INK, lw=1.5, zorder=3)

    ax.text((x0 + x1) / 2, 5.38, "spike trains in", color=DRIVE, fontsize=7.4,
            ha="center", va="center")
    ax.text((ox0 + ox1) / 2, 3.92, "spikes out", color=INK, fontsize=7.4,
            ha="center", va="center")
    # "and one neuron sums them" was not true, and it undercut panel (b). The neuron sums its
    # weighted inputs within a step; across the window it leaks, v <- lam*v + sum(w x), so a
    # contribution decays from the step after it arrives. On these arrivals 4.280 of weighted
    # input goes in, 3.000 leaves as three thresholds, a sum would end at 1.280 and the neuron
    # ends at 0.080 -- the leak discards 94% of it. Unqualified, "sums" invites the reading
    # that panel (b) exists to refute.
    ax.text(4.95, 0.58, "at each step the neuron sums its weighted inputs",
            color=INK, fontsize=7.4, style="italic", ha="center", va="center")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Panel (b): input row, membrane, output row -- one shared time axis
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#: Every label in panel (b) is left-aligned here, in the shared data x of the three rows.
LABEL_X = -0.3

#: The time arrow's span, kept as a constant so the label centred on it and the audit that
#: checks the centring both read the same two numbers.
ARROW_X = (-0.6, T + 0.4)

#: What a label looks like follows what it names. A label on a grey guide line is grey and
#: italic, so it reads as part of the scaffolding; a label naming a quantity or a direction is
#: ink and upright, like the "membrane potential" axis label. ``audit`` asserts it, because
#: this is the kind of thing that drifts one label at a time.
#:      word -> (colour, style, size)
LABEL_STYLE = {"inputs":    (GUIDE, "italic", 7.4),
               "output":    (GUIDE, "italic", 7.4),
               "threshold": (GUIDE, "italic", 7.4),
               "time":      (INK, "normal", 7.8)}


def panel_b(fig, sub, tr, xs, ys, spikes):
    ax_in = fig.add_subplot(sub[0])
    ax_v = fig.add_subplot(sub[1], sharex=ax_in)
    ax_out = fig.add_subplot(sub[2], sharex=ax_in)

    # One convention for all four words: left-aligned at LABEL_X, just above the thing named,
    # which is how "threshold" already sat above its dashed line. As rotated y-axis labels
    # "inputs" and "output" sat in the left margin at a different x from "membrane potential",
    # because matplotlib places each label relative to its own axes and these differ in
    # height; moved to the right-hand end they lined up with each other but not with
    # "threshold". Anchoring every one of them to the same x settles it, and the margin holds
    # a single rotated label.
    for i, train in enumerate(tr):
        y = len(tr) - 1 - i
        ax_in.plot([-0.6, T - 0.4], [y, y], color=EDGE, lw=0.8, zorder=1)
        ax_in.vlines(np.flatnonzero(train), y - 0.34, y + 0.34, color=DRIVE, lw=1.2,
                     zorder=3)
    # "inputs" sits below the three rows it names, so the slack in this axes is below them
    # rather than above; the span is unchanged, so the rows are drawn the same size as before.
    ax_in.set_ylim(-1.90, len(tr) - 0.30)
    ax_in.set_yticks([])
    ax_in.text(LABEL_X, -0.44, "inputs", color=GUIDE, fontsize=7.4, style="italic",
               ha="left", va="top")
    l_axis(ax_in, left=False, bottom=False)
    ax_in.tick_params(axis="x", labelbottom=False)

    ax_v.plot([-0.6, T - 0.4], [V_TH, V_TH], color=GUIDE, lw=1.0, ls=(0, (3.4, 2.0)),
              zorder=1)
    ax_v.plot(xs, ys, color=STATE, lw=1.55, solid_joinstyle="round", zorder=3)
    ax_v.set_ylim(-0.06, float(ys.max()) * 1.10)
    # The one label inside panel (b), and it is there to fix a layout fault. As a y tick
    # label "threshold" widened the left margin by its own length and pushed the
    # "membrane potential" axis label across into panel (a). Sitting just above the dashed
    # line it names, in that line's own colour, it costs no margin at all -- and the band
    # above the threshold on the left is empty, because the membrane has not yet built up.
    ax_v.set_yticks([])
    ax_v.text(LABEL_X, V_TH + 0.045, "threshold", color=GUIDE, fontsize=7.4,
              style="italic", ha="left", va="bottom")
    ax_v.set_ylabel("membrane potential", fontsize=7.8, color=INK)
    l_axis(ax_v, bottom=False)
    ax_v.tick_params(axis="x", labelbottom=False)

    ax_out.plot([-0.6, T - 0.4], [0.0, 0.0], color=EDGE, lw=0.8, zorder=1)
    ax_out.vlines(np.flatnonzero(spikes), -0.40, 0.40, color=INK, lw=1.6, zorder=3)
    # Each label sits below the line it names, so this axes stacks four things downwards:
    # The grey baseline, "output", the time arrow, "time". Its height ratio and the canvas
    # height were raised to hold them without squeezing the membrane panel above.
    ax_out.set_ylim(-2.35, 0.55)
    ax_out.set_yticks([])
    ax_out.text(LABEL_X, -0.50, "output", color=GUIDE, fontsize=7.4, style="italic",
                ha="left", va="top")
    # The time axis is an arrow, as the physical panels draw their axes: a spine says "these are the limits
    # of the measurement", an arrow says "this direction is time", and nothing here is
    # Measured. The label sits at the arrow's head in grey italic, as on the physical panels.
    # The right margin held "inputs" and "output"; with every label on the left it is not
    # needed, and the rows get the width back
    ax_out.set_xlim(-1.0, T + 1.0)
    ax_out.set_xticks([])
    ax_out.annotate("", xy=(ARROW_X[1], -1.42), xytext=(ARROW_X[0], -1.42),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=INK, lw=0.8,
                                    mutation_scale=8, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))
    # "time" names the whole axis, not a point on it, so it is centred under the arrow rather
    # than left-anchored with the three guide labels. It is the one label in panel (b) that
    # deliberately leaves the LABEL_X anchor, and the audit checks it against the arrow's own
    # midpoint instead of against that anchor.
    ax_out.text(sum(ARROW_X) / 2.0, -1.52, "time", color=INK, fontsize=7.8,
                ha="center", va="top")
    l_axis(ax_out, left=False, bottom=False)
    return ax_in, ax_v, ax_out


def build():
    apply_style()
    tr = trains()
    xs, ys, spikes = integrate(tr)

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(PLACED_IN, 2.95))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(1, 2, width_ratios=(1.00, 1.26), wspace=0.30,
                          left=0.010, right=0.992, top=0.845, bottom=0.115)
    ax_a = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
    panel_a(ax_a, tr, spikes)
    sub = gs[0, 1].subgridspec(3, 1, height_ratios=(1.30, 3.10, 1.55), hspace=0.10)
    ax_in, ax_v, ax_out = panel_b(fig, sub, tr, xs, ys, spikes)

    # The title'S offset from its letter is in points, not axes fraction. As a fraction it was
    # the same number on two axes of different widths, so the gap differed between the panels
    # and panel (a)'s letter ran into its title. A ScaledTranslation in points gives both the
    # same gap whatever the canvas, which matters because the canvas changed size once already.
    for ax, letter, title in ((ax_a, "a", "one neuron, many weighted inputs"),
                              (ax_in, "b", "integrate, fire, subtract the threshold")):
        y = 1.10 if ax is ax_in else 1.045
        ax.text(0.0, y, letter, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.6, fontweight="bold",
                color=INK, ha="left", va="bottom")
        ax.text(0.0, y, title, fontsize=7.8, color=INK, ha="left", va="bottom",
                transform=ax.transAxes
                + ScaledTranslation(TITLE_GAP_PT / 72.0, 0.0, fig.dpi_scale_trans))
    return fig, tr, xs, ys, spikes, ax_a, ax_in


def audit(fig, tr, xs, ys, spikes, ax_a, ax_b_head):
    bad = []
    fired = np.flatnonzero(spikes)
    if fired.size < 2:
        bad.append(f"only {fired.size} threshold crossing(s): too few to read as a rule")
    if ys.max() <= V_TH:
        bad.append("the drawn trace never reaches the threshold, so no crossing is visible")
    drops = [float(ys[i] - ys[i + 1]) for i in range(len(ys) - 1)
             if abs(xs[i] - xs[i + 1]) < 1e-9]
    if not drops or max(abs(d - V_TH) for d in drops) > 1e-9:
        bad.append(f"a drawn reset is not exactly one threshold: {drops}")
    post = [float(ys[i + 1]) for i in range(len(ys) - 1) if abs(xs[i] - xs[i + 1]) < 1e-9]
    if max(post, default=0.0) < 0.15:
        bad.append(f"every post-spike value is near zero ({post}): reads as reset-to-zero")
    # Every crossing must be separated, so both panels draw the same number of visible marks and
    # the trace stays legible.
    if fired.size > 1 and int(np.diff(fired).min()) < 5:
        bad.append(f"crossings at {fired.tolist()} come within "
                   f"{int(np.diff(fired).min())} steps: they will merge into one mark at "
                   f"panel (a)'s compressed scale")
    if fired.size > 1 and int(np.diff(fired).max()) < 5:
        bad.append("no gap long enough for the leak to be visible between crossings")
    # Every jump in the membrane must coincide with an input spike, which is the whole point
    # of sharing the axis; a jump without one would be the squiggle this replaces
    any_in = np.clip(sum(tr), 0, 1)
    for t in range(1, T):
        i = np.flatnonzero(np.isclose(xs, t))[0]
        prev = ys[i - 1]
        if ys[i] > prev + 1e-9 and not any_in[t]:
            bad.append(f"the membrane rises at step {t} with no input spike there")
    # The two panels must draw the same events
    if [int(s.sum()) for s in tr] != [int(s.sum()) for s in trains()]:
        bad.append("panel (a) and panel (b) draw different input trains")
    placed = {t.get_text(): t for ax in fig.axes if ax is not ax_a for t in ax.texts
              if t.get_text() in LABEL_STYLE}
    if sorted(placed) != ["inputs", "output", "threshold", "time"]:
        bad.append(f"panel (b) labels present are {sorted(placed)}, not all four")
    # The three that name a line share one left anchor
    for name in ("inputs", "output", "threshold"):
        t = placed.get(name)
        if t is None:
            continue
        if round(float(t.get_position()[0]), 6) != round(LABEL_X, 6):
            bad.append(f"{name!r} sits at x {t.get_position()[0]:.3f}, off the {LABEL_X} "
                       f"anchor the other line labels share")
        if t.get_ha() != "left":
            bad.append(f"{name!r} is {t.get_ha()}-aligned, so a shared x does not align it")
    # "time" names the axis, so it is centred on the arrow instead
    t = placed.get("time")
    if t is not None:
        mid = sum(ARROW_X) / 2.0
        if abs(float(t.get_position()[0]) - mid) > 1e-6:
            bad.append(f"'time' sits at x {t.get_position()[0]:.3f}, not the arrow's midpoint "
                       f"{mid:.3f}")
        if t.get_ha() != "center":
            bad.append(f"'time' is {t.get_ha()}-aligned, so its x is not its centre")
    for ax in fig.axes:
        if ax is ax_a:
            continue
        for t in ax.texts:
            want = LABEL_STYLE.get(t.get_text())
            if want is None:
                continue
            got = (t.get_color(), t.get_style(), round(float(t.get_fontsize()), 2))
            if got != want:
