                bad.append(f"{t.get_text()!r} is drawn {got}, not the {want} its subject "
                           f"calls for")
    fig.canvas.draw()
    for ax in fig.axes:
        if ax is ax_a:
            continue
        inv, ren = ax.transData.inverted(), fig.canvas.get_renderer()
        for t in ax.texts:
            if t.get_text() not in LABEL_STYLE:
                continue
            (_, ty0), (_, ty1) = inv.transform(t.get_window_extent(ren))
            lo, hi = min(ty0, ty1), max(ty0, ty1)
            y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()
            if lo < min(y0, y1) or hi > max(y0, y1):
                bad.append(f"{t.get_text()!r} spans y {lo:.2f}-{hi:.2f}, outside the axes "
                           f"limits {y0:.2f}-{y1:.2f}: it is clipped")
            for other in ax.texts:
                if other is t or other.get_text() not in LABEL_STYLE:
                    continue
                (_, oy0), (_, oy1) = inv.transform(other.get_window_extent(ren))
                olo, ohi = min(oy0, oy1), max(oy0, oy1)
                if lo < ohi and olo < hi:
                    bad.append(f"{t.get_text()!r} and {other.get_text()!r} overlap "
                               f"vertically ({lo:.2f}-{hi:.2f} vs {olo:.2f}-{ohi:.2f})")
    # The letter must not touch its title, measured in points on the rendered canvas
    fig.canvas.draw()
    ren = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
    for ax, letter, title in ((ax_a, "a", "one neuron, many weighted inputs"),
                              (ax_b_head, "b", "integrate, fire, subtract the threshold")):
        got = {t.get_text(): t.get_window_extent(ren) for t in ax.texts
               if t.get_text() in (letter, title)}
        if len(got) == 2:
            gap_pt = (got[title].x0 - got[letter].x1) / fig.dpi * 72.0
            if gap_pt < MIN_LETTER_GAP_PT:
                bad.append(f"panel ({letter}) letter and title are {gap_pt:.2f} pt apart, "
                           f"under the {MIN_LETTER_GAP_PT} pt minimum")
    w_in = float(fig.get_size_inches()[0])
    if abs(w_in - PLACED_IN) > 0.02:
        bad.append(f"canvas is {w_in:.3f} in against a placed width of {PLACED_IN:.3f} in: "
                   f"LaTeX would scale type by {PLACED_IN / w_in:.3f}")
    printed = smallest_pt(fig) * PLACED_IN / w_in
    if printed < MIN_PRINTED_PT - 1e-9:
        bad.append(f"the smallest glyph prints at {printed:.2f} pt, under the "
                   f"{MIN_PRINTED_PT} pt floor")
    margin = [ax.get_ylabel() for ax in fig.axes if ax.get_ylabel()]
    if margin != ["membrane potential"]:
        bad.append(f"panel (b)'s left margin holds {margin}, not the membrane label alone: "
                   f"two labels there cannot share an x position")
    for ax in fig.axes:
        require_plain_tick_labels(ax)
    # The requirement is per panel, so the check is too. Panel (a) is a labelled diagram and
    # annotates freely, as both reference figures do. Panel (b) carries exactly one word,
    # "threshold", on the line it names; anything else there is the prose that was removed.
    # Text inside a box is measured, not eyeballed. A word rendered a hair wider than its
    # rounded box reads as a drawing error, and the width depends on the font, the canvas and
    # the placed size, so it cannot be judged from the source.
    fig.canvas.draw()
    x, y, bw, bh = ax_a._neuron_rect
    inv = ax_a.transData.inverted()
    for t in ax_a.texts:
        if t.get_gid() != "neuron-word":
            continue
        bb = inv.transform(t.get_window_extent(fig.canvas.get_renderer()))
        (tx0, ty0), (tx1, ty1) = bb
        if tx0 < x or tx1 > x + bw or ty0 < y or ty1 > y + bh:
            bad.append(f"{t.get_text()!r} spans x {tx0:.2f}-{tx1:.2f}, y {ty0:.2f}-{ty1:.2f} "
                       f"against a box of x {x:.2f}-{x + bw:.2f}, y {y:.2f}-{y + bh:.2f}")
    PANEL_B_WORDS = ("threshold", "inputs", "output", "time")
    titles = ("a", "b", "one neuron, many weighted inputs",
              "integrate, fire, subtract the threshold")
    for ax in fig.axes:
        if ax is ax_a:
            continue
        stray = [t.get_text() for t in ax.texts
                 if t.get_text().strip() and t.get_text() not in titles + PANEL_B_WORDS]
        if stray:
            bad.append(f"panel (b) carries floating text other than the threshold "
                       f"label: {stray}")
    require_no_floating_text(fig, allow=titles + PANEL_B_WORDS + tuple(
        t.get_text() for t in ax_a.texts))
    return bad


def main():
    fig, tr, xs, ys, spikes, ax_a, ax_b_head = build()
    problems = audit(fig, tr, xs, ys, spikes, ax_a, ax_b_head)
    fig.savefig(OUT, bbox_inches="tight")
    fig.savefig(PNG, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")
    w, h = fig.get_size_inches()
    fired = np.flatnonzero(spikes)
    post = [round(float(ys[i + 1]), 3) for i in range(len(ys) - 1)
            if abs(xs[i] - xs[i + 1]) < 1e-9]
    print(f"  canvas {w:.2f} x {h:.2f} in   smallest glyph {smallest_pt(fig):.2f} pt   "
          f"prints at {smallest_pt(fig) * PLACED_IN / w:.2f} pt at width=\\textwidth")
    print(f"  input ticks per channel {[int(s.sum()) for s in tr]}; "
          f"{len(ARRIVALS)} arrivals over {T} steps")
    print(f"  crossings at {fired.tolist()}   peak {ys.max():.3f} vs threshold {V_TH}")
    print(f"  post-spike values {post}  (all zero would be reset-to-zero)")
    print(f"  crossing separation min {int(np.diff(fired).min())} / max "
          f"{int(np.diff(fired).max())} steps (all must be >= 5 so no two marks merge)")
    print("  " + ("every assertion holds; no floating text" if not problems
                  else f"{len(problems)} PROBLEMS\n    " + "\n    ".join(problems)))
    return 1 if problems else 0
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/plotting/\_training\_curves.py}
\index{tools/plotting/\_training\_curves.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
"""Hardware-aware training of both architectures, as one four-panel figure.

Test loss and test accuracy per epoch, ideal conductance against the measured Poole--Frenkel
response, for the dense and the convolutional network.

Why one figure and not two. This replaces two separately produced plots that were stacked
inside one float, which carried two panel (a)s and two panel (b)s and whose height was fixed by
images that could not be edited. All four panels are drawn here, lettered a-d once, at a canvas
whose height is chosen rather than inherited.

The input is the deposited history. The per-epoch histories are in ``data/static.npz`` as
``acc_hist`` and ``loss_hist`` on ``(arch, condition, seed, epoch)``; the sidecar carries the
configuration and the final-epoch means. Nothing is re-run to draw this.

Validation is against the sidecar, and it is a gate, not a report. ``data/static.json`` records
``final_epoch_mean`` for all four cells, and this producer refuses to draw unless the arrays
reproduce all four within ``FINAL_TOL``. The hazard is concrete: a 6,000-sample run exists with
the same schema whose fc|ideal ends at 87.99 rather than 94.94, and it would otherwise appear
under this figure without complaint. The deposited values are read from the sidecar rather than
copied into this file, so the gate cannot drift from the archive it guards.

Bands are one population standard deviation over the three seeds, which is what the caption
claims; ``numpy.std`` with ``ddof=0`` is the population form and is used deliberately.

Colour is the house palette, with the meanings the other figures use: the ideal arm is the
abstract comparator (``exponential``), the measured device response is ``device``. That is the
same pairing the substitution panels use, so one mapping carries across the set.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from .common import (PALETTE, apply_style, house_grid,               # Noqa: E402
                     require_plain_tick_labels, smallest_pt)

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DATA = HERE.parent.parent / "data"

OUT = None
PNG = None

#: The canvas is the placed width, so a document scales it 1:1 and printed type equals set type.
PLACED_IN = 437.46112 / 72.27
MIN_PRINTED_PT = 7.0

IDEAL = PALETTE["exponential"]
DEVICE = PALETTE["device"]

ARCHS = (("fc", "TemporalMSNN, dense"), ("conv", "TemporalMCSNN, convolutional"))
CONDS = (("ideal", "ideal conductance", IDEAL),
         ("memristive_pf", "memristive (Poole--Frenkel)", DEVICE))

#: Percentage points. The deposit is a mean over the same three seeds, so the tolerance only
#: absorbs rounding, never a different campaign.
FINAL_TOL = 0.05


def _archive():
    z = np.load(DATA / "static.npz", allow_pickle=False)
    return z, json.loads((DATA / "static.json").read_text())


def load(_unused=None):
    """The deposited histories, the sidecar config, and the deposited final-epoch means."""
    z, side = _archive()
    archs = [str(x) for x in z["archs"]]
    conds = [str(x) for x in z["conditions"]]
    series = {}
    for ai, a_ in enumerate(archs):
        for ci, c_ in enumerate(conds):
            series[f"{a_}|{c_}"] = {"acc_hist": np.asarray(z["acc_hist"][ai, ci], float),
                                    "loss_hist": np.asarray(z["loss_hist"][ai, ci], float)}
    return side["config"], series, dict(side["final_epoch_mean"])


def check_deposit(series, deposited):
    """Refuse any history whose final-epoch means are not the deposited ones."""
    bad = []
    for key, want in sorted(deposited.items()):
        got = float(series[key]["acc_hist"][:, -1].mean())
        if abs(got - want) > FINAL_TOL:
            bad.append(f"{key}: final-epoch mean {got:.2f}% against the deposited "
                       f"{want:.2f}% (tolerance {FINAL_TOL})")
    return bad


def band(ax, hist, colour, label):
    """Mean over seeds with a one-population-standard-deviation band."""
    ep = np.arange(1, hist.shape[1] + 1)
    m, sd = hist.mean(axis=0), hist.std(axis=0, ddof=0)
    ax.fill_between(ep, m - sd, m + sd, color=colour, alpha=0.20, linewidth=0, zorder=2)
    ax.plot(ep, m, color=colour, lw=1.4, marker="o", ms=2.6, mec="white", mew=0.35,
            zorder=3, label=label)
    return ep


def build():
    """The figure. Refuses to draw a history the archive does not vouch for."""
    _config, series, deposited = load()
    mismatch = check_deposit(series, deposited)
    if mismatch:
        raise AssertionError("this history is not the deposited run:\n    "
                             + "\n    ".join(mismatch))
    apply_style()
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(PLACED_IN, 3.05))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, wspace=0.26, hspace=0.34,
                          left=0.088, right=0.988, top=0.945, bottom=0.105)
    axes, letters = [], "abcd"
    for r, (arch, _arch_name) in enumerate(ARCHS):
        for c, (field, ylab) in enumerate((("loss_hist", "test loss"),
                                           ("acc_hist", "test accuracy (\\%)"))):
            ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[r, c]); axes.append(ax)
            for cond, cond_name, colour in CONDS:
                band(ax, series[f"{arch}|{cond}"][field], colour, cond_name)
            ax.set_xlim(0.6, 12.4)
            ax.set_xticks([1, 4, 8, 12])
            ax.set_ylabel(ylab)
            if r == len(ARCHS) - 1:
                ax.set_xlabel("epoch")
            else:
                ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelbottom=False)
            if field == "acc_hist":
                ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
                ax.set_yticks([0, 25, 50, 75, 100])
            house_grid(ax)
            for side in ("top", "right"):
                ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
    # One legend, placed where there is room rather than where it is tidy. Centred above the
    # panels it sat on the second panel's letter, because the letters occupy that band too;
    # moved inside the axes, the letters landed on the curves, since the accuracy panels are
    # full exactly where a letter goes. The loss panel's upper right is the one corner empty in
    # every seed -- loss falls monotonically -- so the legend goes there.
    axes[0].legend(loc="upper right", frameon=False, fontsize=7.4, handlelength=1.6,
                   labelspacing=0.3, borderaxespad=0.2)
    for ax, letter in zip(axes, letters):
        ax.text(-0.015, 1.02, letter, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.6,
                fontweight="bold", color=PALETTE["ink"], ha="right", va="bottom")
    return fig, axes, series, deposited


def audit(fig, axes, series, deposited):
    bad = list(check_deposit(series, deposited))
    for key, rec in series.items():
        for field in ("acc_hist", "loss_hist"):
            h = rec[field]
            if h.shape[0] != 3:
                bad.append(f"{key}|{field}: {h.shape[0]} seeds, not the three the caption "
                           f"claims")
            if h.shape[1] != 12:
                bad.append(f"{key}|{field}: {h.shape[1]} epochs, not twelve")
            if not np.isfinite(h).all():
                bad.append(f"{key}|{field} holds non-finite values")
    if len({t.get_text() for ax in axes for t in ax.texts}) != 4:
        bad.append("the four panel letters are not exactly a, b, c, d")
    w_in = float(fig.get_size_inches()[0])
    if abs(w_in - PLACED_IN) > 0.02:
        bad.append(f"canvas {w_in:.3f} in against a placed width of {PLACED_IN:.3f} in")
    printed = smallest_pt(fig) * PLACED_IN / w_in
    if printed < MIN_PRINTED_PT - 1e-9:
        bad.append(f"smallest glyph prints at {printed:.2f} pt, under {MIN_PRINTED_PT} pt")
    for ax in axes:
        require_plain_tick_labels(ax)
    return bad


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                    help="validate the source against the deposit and draw nothing")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    config, series, deposited = load()
    print(f"  source {DATA / 'static.npz'}")
    print(f"  config epochs={config.get('epochs')} seeds={config.get('seeds')} "
          f"train_subset={config.get('train_subset')} test_subset={config.get('test_subset')}")
    print("  final-epoch mean accuracy, supplied against deposited:")
    for key, want in sorted(deposited.items()):
        got = float(series[key]["acc_hist"][:, -1].mean())
        print(f"    {key:24} {got:6.2f}%  vs {want:6.2f}%   "
              f"{'ok' if abs(got - want) <= FINAL_TOL else 'MISMATCH'}")
    mismatch = check_deposit(series, deposited)
    if mismatch:
        raise SystemExit("  REFUSING TO DRAW: this history is not the deposited run.\n    "
                         + "\n    ".join(mismatch))
    if a.dry_run:
        print("  --dry-run: validated, nothing drawn")
        return 0
    fig, axes, series, deposited = build()
    problems = audit(fig, axes, series, deposited)
    if problems:
        print(f"  {len(problems)} PROBLEMS\n    " + "\n    ".join(problems))
        return 1
    w, h = fig.get_size_inches()
    print(f"  drew the figure  canvas {w:.2f} x {h:.2f} in  smallest glyph "
          f"{smallest_pt(fig):.2f} pt")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
\end{Verbatim}
\subsection{tools/plotting/common.py}
\index{tools/plotting/common.py}
\begin{Verbatim}
r"""Figure style and figure I/O: the palette, the registry, and how a figure reaches disk.

Two groups. The style -- the validated palette, the ramps, the label rules and the house cycle.
And the I/O -- the figure registry, the canonical names, and the save-and-display path a notebook
uses so the picture it shows is the file it wrote.

One house style for every figure in this package.

This module is the single source of truth for colour, type, grid, panel letters and
legend placement. Every notebook in ``experiments/`` should import from here instead of
carrying its own private copy of the style block, so that one physical meaning keeps one
visual encoding across the whole figure set:

    From plotting.common import (PALETTE, apply_style, panel, compact_legend,
                                    legend_overlaps_data, size_for)
    apply_style()

Scope: **style only**. This module deliberately does not know about figure saving,
provenance, hashing or the ``OWNED``/``FIGURE_REPORT`` bookkeeping. The notebooks keep
their own ``finish()`` writers; nothing here replaces or wraps them, and nothing here
touches data, seeds or model parameters.

Legibility contract
-------------------
A figure is legible when its *printed* type is in a readable band, not when its
on-screen type looks right. The printed size of a glyph is

    effective_pt = fontsize_pt * placed_width_in / figsize_width_in

Because LaTeX scales the whole canvas to the width given in ``\includegraphics``. The
house target is nothing below 7 pt and nothing above about 11 pt at the placed width,
achieved by *sizing the canvas* (see :func:`size_for`), never by inflating fontsize.

Proportion contract, and why it is a *height* rule
--------------------------------------------------
Type is sized in proportion to the plot, not in absolute points. The reference proportion is
one em of axis-label type at 4.6% of the axes height (11 pt labels on a 6.2 x 4.3 in canvas
with one tall axes).

Two quantities are easy to confuse, and only one of them is free:

* the *printed* size ``P = fontsize * placed_in / canvas_in``, floored at 7 pt above;
* the *proportion* ``R = fontsize / (72 * canvas_width_in)``, i.e. what fraction of the
  figure's width one em occupies.

``P = 72 * R * placed_in``, so at a fixed placed width P and R are proportional: type
cannot be made a smaller fraction of the plot horizontally without printing smaller, and
the 7 pt floor is 2% away on this set. Reducing fontsize *and* the canvas width together
buys nothing at all -- R is unchanged.

Canvas **height** is the free lever. LaTeX scales by width, so making a canvas taller at
a fixed width leaves every printed glyph exactly where it was while the axes grow, which
is precisely the ratio the eye judges. The house target is therefore stated against the
axes height, not the width:

    One em of axis-label type <= EM_PER_AXES_HEIGHT (4.6%) of the axes height,

i.e. **at least ~2.4 in of axes height per row of panels** at the 7.8 pt house label
size (:func:`axes_height_for`). Most figures in this set sit at 1.9-2.1 in and are the
reason the type reads large; the remedy is a taller canvas and less text, never a bigger
font and never a narrower canvas. :func:`proportion_report` states the gap per panel.

House rules the helpers here mechanise
--------------------------------------
* No floating text inside an axes. Anything explanatory belongs in the caption:
  :func:`caption_note` records the moved sentence verbatim so nothing is lost,
  :func:`annotate_outside` is the only sanctioned on-canvas note, and
  :func:`require_no_floating_text` fails a figure that still carries one.
* No legend over data *or over the panel letter*: :func:`compact_legend` now avoids
  both, and refuses a framed legend inside an axes outright.
* No data and no colour in tick labels: :func:`require_plain_tick_labels`.
* The bright end of the ramp is capped for lines and markers (section 1b).
"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Palette. Semantic roles, not decoration: "device" is the same green in every
#    figure this package produces. Every data role is a sample of
#    one perceptually uniform purple-to-yellow ramp (the same ramp as section 1b); the
#    neutrals and the reference red are deliberately off that ramp, for the reasons
#    given below. Do not add a colour without a semantic role, and never let a series
#    fall back on Matplotlib's default C0-C3 cycle.
#
#    Three roles are exclusive, and one palette is not one system unless they hold:
#      "device"      names the device arm. Not a device-adjacent ablation, not a mouse
#                    group, not a criterion band, not "the first series".
#      "exponential" names an exponential comparator. Nothing else. A second condition
#                    of a device arm, a biological group and a second criterion are all
#                    not exponentials, and each had taken this navy.
#      "reference"   names chance, criterion, set-point and other reference lines. It is
#                    never a data series: a red interval in a forest of coloured
#                    intervals reads as the reference the data is measured against.
#    Everything else picks an accent. The accents are a shared pool with an example role
#    recorded beside each, not one exclusive owner: "teal" can be a fourth biological
#    group in one figure and a one-factor-removed device ablation in another, because
#    neither reading collides with the three exclusive roles above. Prefer an accent
#    adjacent in hue when a series belongs to the same family as one of the core three.
#
#    Why one ramp for the data roles. The ramp's lightness is monotone in its position,
#    so sampling the nine data roles at nine separated positions buys nine distinct
#    greys as well as nine distinct hues: the figures keep their identifications in a
#    greyscale print and for a colour-blind reader without a second encoding. The
#    positions below are 5.7-16 L* apart, at or above the separability band section 1b
#    uses for thin lines, and they are ordered so that roles which appear in the same figure
#    sit as far apart as the ramp allows:
#
#       Pos   role          hex       L*   heritage hue
#       0.06  reward        #431563   19   was light purple  -> dark purple
#       0.14  violet       *#423078   26   purple            -> purple
#       0.20  exponential  *#414487   32   navy              -> indigo (caption: "blue")
#       0.31  rose          #34618b   40   was pink          -> slate blue
#       0.42  linear       *#297d8d   48   mid blue          -> blue-teal
#       0.60  device       *#22a884   62   green             -> green (caption: "green")
#       0.68  teal          #46b96f   67   dark teal         -> green
#       0.765 copper        #6aca5a   74   was warm brown    -> yellow-green
#       0.85  gold         *#9bd746   80   amber             -> yellow-green
#     (* the roles that co-occur in nearly every figure; they take the widest gaps,
#      about 15 L* between each of device / linear / exponential.)
#    "teal" landing next to "device" is deliberate, not a collision: notebook 03 draws
#    the one-factor-removed device ablation in it, and adjacency is the reading.
#
#    The light end is capped at ramp position 0.85, and the cap is the point. The
#    uncapped ramp puts "gold" at 0.95 (L* 87), which is too bright for a mark:
#    at that lightness a 1.8 pt stroke, an open circle or a scatter marker has almost no
#    contrast against white paper, so the figure loses its identification where contrast is
#    already lowest. Lines and markers therefore stop at 0.85 (L* 80),
#    here and in :func:`sequential`; only colourbars and filled areas keep the full ramp
#    (section 1b), because a solid fill reads at any lightness.
#    What the cap costs, recorded so nobody "fixes" it back by pushing gold up again:
#    Three roles now share the 0.60-0.85 window, so the light-end gaps fall from about
#    8 L* to 5.7 / 6.1 / 6.0 -- at the bottom of the separability band, not below it. A
#    Figure that really does draw device, teal, copper and gold in one panel must add a
#    second encoding (marker or dash), and must not widen the window to get one back.
#    Even capped, the light end is the light end: give "copper" and "gold" the house
#    1.8 pt stroke, a filled marker or an ink edge, never a hairline.
#
#    Not on the ramp, on purpose:
#      "reference"  keeps #c0392b red, because it is furniture -- chance, criterion,
#                   set-point, S = 1 -- and must never read as a data series. A
#                   Viridis-like ramp contains no red, which makes red the one hue that
#                   cannot be mistaken for data in a figure whose data is all ramp;
#                   pulling reference onto the ramp would both destroy that distinction
#                   and duplicate a real series.
#      "grid", "ink", "control", "pale", "slate", "guide" stay neutral. Grid and ink are
#                   not data at all, and the greys name null controls, conventional
#                   baselines and annotated guides, where achromatic *is* the reading:
#                   The eye should find the coloured arms first. Note the one thing
#                   greyscale cannot separate: these greys sit at L* 53-67, inside the
#                   ramp's own mid range, so a greyscale reader tells "control" from
#                   "device" by line style and label, not by tone.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PALETTE = {
    # --- core: sampled from the house ramp (see the position table above) ------
    "device":      "#22a884",  # Measured / physical device: the SiOx trace itself
    "exponential": "#414487",  # Matched or abstract exponential comparator
    "linear":      "#297d8d",  # Linear Erlang sensitivity / linear-device arm
    "control":     "#9aa6b2",  # No-trace and other null controls (neutral, off-ramp)
    "reference":   "#c0392b",  # Chance, criterion, set-point, reference lines (off-ramp)
    "gold":        "#9bd746",  # Au / fill branch; secondary comparator (capped at 0.85)
    "ink":         "#2b2b2b",  # Single-series ink, text, double ablation (off-ramp)
    "grid":        "#c8d0d8",  # Grid lines (never a data colour) (off-ramp)
    # --- accents: same hex everywhere, one name each ---------------------------
    "violet":      "#423078",  # Global-scalar comparator, unsigned rule ablation
    "slate":       "#7f7f7f",  # Conventional pair-based R-stdp (neutral, off-ramp)
    "rose":        "#34618b",  # No-negative rule ablation
    "pale":        "#8d99a6",  # Shallow / elm control arms (neutral, off-ramp)
    "reward":      "#431563",  # Single-trial reward events
    "copper":      "#6aca5a",  # Third biological group (capped: was ramp 0.84)
    "teal":        "#46b96f",  # Fourth biological group (moved down to clear copper)
    "guide":       "#8a949f",  # Annotated guide lines that carry a legend entry
}

# Three rules this dict depends on:
#   * no key may be removed or renamed -- figures index it by name.
#   * the categorical palette stops at ramp 0.85 because its members are strokes and markers,
#     while SEQUENTIAL_STOPS / SEQUENTIAL_CMAP run to 1.00, where a colourbar and a filled area
#     still read. The two diverging at the top is deliberate, not an inconsistency to repair.
#   * accent names label ramp positions, not hues: "rose" is a slate blue and "copper" a
#     yellow-green. Choose an accent by the role recorded beside it, never by its name.

#: Default property cycle. Order is "most likely first series wins the device green".
HOUSE_CYCLE = [
    PALETTE[key] for key in
    ("device", "exponential", "gold", "reference", "linear", "control", "violet", "ink")
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. The one sequential ramp. A *categorical* palette cannot encode an ordered
#     physical quantity: a bias sweep, a fill-rate product or a retention ladder needs
#     a map whose lightness is monotone, so that "more" is visible as "darker" without
#     consulting the key. Rather than let each figure reach for an
#     off-palette Matplotlib colormap, the house declares exactly one such ramp: the
#     viridis-like purple-to-yellow ramp #440154 -> #414487 -> #2a788e -> #22a884 ->
#     #7ad151 -> #fde725, uniformly spaced, whose lightness climbs monotonically from
#     L* 15 to L* 91. It is the same ramp the categorical roles in section 1 are sampled
#     from, so a sequential panel and a categorical panel in one float are one system.
#
#     The consequence to respect: a ramp colour is therefore not proof that a mark is *not*
#     a data role. Keep the two readings apart within a figure by position and by key --
#     one panel ordered, the next categorical, and a caption that says which -- not by hue.
#
#     Position 0 is the darkest end and 1 the lightest, as the perceptual Matplotlib maps
#     have it.
def _mix(colour: str, target: str, fraction: float) -> tuple:
    """``colour`` moved ``fraction`` of the way toward ``target`` in sRGB.

    Kept as the house shade/tint helper: it is how a figure derives a lighter or darker
    variant of a palette colour (a retention tint of the device green, say) without
    inventing an off-palette hue.
    """
    start = mpl.colors.to_rgb(colour)
    end = mpl.colors.to_rgb(target)
    return tuple(a + fraction * (b - a) for a, b in zip(start, end))


#: (position, colour) stops of the house sequential ramp, dark end first. The stops are
#: uniform, because this ramp is already perceptually uniform: six evenly spaced samples
#: of the default :func:`sequential` window (now capped at 0.85) land 11-14 L* apart
#: (21.6, 35.3, 46.8, 57.9, 68.8, 79.5), and the full-range anchors below sit at L* 14.9,
#: 31.8, 46.8, 61.7, 76.3, 90.9 -- comfortably separable for thin lines at every level.
#: The stops keep the full range on purpose: they are what a colourbar and a filled area
#: are drawn from, and the cap is a line-and-marker rule (:data:`SEQUENTIAL_LINE_MAX`).
SEQUENTIAL_STOPS = (
    (0.00, "#440154"),   # Dark purple
    (0.20, "#414487"),   # Indigo   (= PALETTE["exponential"])
    (0.40, "#2a788e"),   # Teal
    (0.60, "#22a884"),   # Green    (= PALETTE["device"])
    (0.80, "#7ad151"),   # Yellow-green
    (1.00, "#fde725"),   # Yellow
)

#: The single house sequential colormap. Use it for every ordered quantity, whether it
#: is sampled discretely (:func:`sequential`) or shown as a colorbar.
SEQUENTIAL_CMAP = mpl.colors.LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "mrl_fill", list(SEQUENTIAL_STOPS), N=256)


#: The brightest ramp position a line or marker may take. Above this the ramp is lighter
#: than L* 80 and a stroke, an open circle or a scatter point loses its contrast against
#: white paper. Filled areas and colourbars are exempt: see :func:`sequential_fill`.
SEQUENTIAL_LINE_MAX = 0.85


def sequential(n: int, lo: float = 0.10, hi: float = SEQUENTIAL_LINE_MAX, *,
               clamp: bool = True) -> list:
    """``n`` ordered colours from :data:`SEQUENTIAL_CMAP`, sampled from ``lo`` to ``hi``.

    The default window trims both extremes, which keeps the darkest level off the ink
    used for text and the lightest level dark enough to read on white. Passing
    ``lo > hi`` reverses the ramp.

    ``clamp`` (default on) pulls whichever end is brighter back to
    :data:`SEQUENTIAL_LINE_MAX`, so an existing call site that asks for ``0.90`` or
    ``1.0`` still gets a stroke-safe light end. It *rescales* the window rather than
    clipping each position, because clipping would collapse the top two levels of a
    six-colour ladder onto one colour and silently destroy an identification. Pass
    ``clamp=False`` (or use :func:`sequential_fill`) for bars, bands and colourbars,
    where the full ramp reads well and the extra lightness is worth having.
    """
    if clamp:
        if lo >= hi:
            lo = min(lo, SEQUENTIAL_LINE_MAX)
        else:
            hi = min(hi, SEQUENTIAL_LINE_MAX)
    count = max(int(n), 1)
    if count == 1:
        positions = [lo]
    else:
        positions = [lo + (hi - lo) * i / (count - 1) for i in range(count)]
    return [SEQUENTIAL_CMAP(x) for x in positions]


def sequential_fill(n: int, lo: float = 0.10, hi: float = 0.98) -> list:
    """``n`` ordered colours for filled marks: bars, bands, patches, heat cells.

    Identical to :func:`sequential` with the light-end cap lifted. A solid fill carries
    its hue over a whole area instead of a one-pixel stroke, so the ramp's bright end is
    legible there. Never use this for a line, a marker edge or scatter.
    """
    return sequential(n, lo, hi, clamp=False)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. rcParams
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The type scale is compressed toward the floor, not slid down through it. A uniform shrink is
# not available: the smallest glyph on the tightest figure already prints at 7.25 pt, 3.5% above
# the 7 pt legibility floor, so scaling everything by 1.3x would print it at 5.6 pt. What is free
# is closing the gap between the largest and the smallest type, because the floor binds only on
# the smallest glyph actually drawn:
#
#     Role                       was    now    printed pt at the tightest placement
#     Panel letter / title       9.5 -> 8.6    8.31    (was 9.18)
#     axis label / body          8.5 -> 7.8    7.54    (was 8.21)
#     tick label                 8.0 -> 7.4    7.15    (was 7.73)
#     legend                     7.5 -> 7.4    7.15    (was 7.25)
#
# The legend, which was the binding glyph, moves 1.3%; the panel letter moves 9.5%. Type
# bulk falls visibly, the floor is cleared at every placed width in use (worst case
# 7.14 pt, in nb00's 0.49-linewidth panels on a 3.2 in canvas), and no figure has to be
# re-laid-out to survive the change. The floor now binds at ~2%; any further reduction has to
# come from canvas height and from less text on the canvas. See :func:`axes_height_for` and
# :func:`proportion_report`.

#: Body fontsize (rcParams["font.size"]): axis labels and any on-canvas text.
BASE_FONTSIZE = 7.8
#: Tick labels and legend entries -- the smallest type the house draws, and therefore the
#: glyph the 7 pt printed floor is measured on. Do not lower it without also shrinking the
#: canvas width, which would undo the proportion gain (see the docstring).
SMALL_FONTSIZE = 7.4
#: Panel letters, axes titles and figure titles.
PANEL_FONTSIZE = 8.6
#: Legibility band at the placed width, in points.
MIN_PT = 7.0
MAX_PT = 11.0
#: Proportion target: one em of axis-label type as a fraction of the axes height (11 pt on a
#: 3.35 in axes = 4.56%). Unlike the pt floor this one is free to satisfy -- see
#: :func:`axes_height_for`.
EM_PER_AXES_HEIGHT = 0.046
#: \linewidth of the target class (a4paper, 2.5 cm margins).
LINEWIDTH_MM = 160.0
MM_PER_IN = 25.4
LINEWIDTH_IN = LINEWIDTH_MM / MM_PER_IN  # 6.299 in

# DejaVu Sans is what every existing figure already renders in: it is Matplotlib's
# default sans-serif and the family notebook 01 declares explicitly. Naming it here
# pins the family without reflowing anything.
_FONT_STACK = ["DejaVu Sans", "Helvetica", "Arial", "sans-serif"]

STYLE = {
    # Canvas
    "figure.dpi": 120,
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "savefig.dpi": 400,          # ~2520 px across a 6.3 in canvas: print-grade
    "savefig.facecolor": "white",
    "savefig.bbox": "tight",
    "savefig.pad_inches": 0.02,
    # Type: one family, one scale, everywhere
    "font.family": "sans-serif",
    "font.sans-serif": _FONT_STACK,
    "mathtext.fontset": "dejavusans",
    "font.size": BASE_FONTSIZE,
    "axes.titlesize": PANEL_FONTSIZE,
    "axes.labelsize": BASE_FONTSIZE,
    "xtick.labelsize": SMALL_FONTSIZE,
    "ytick.labelsize": SMALL_FONTSIZE,
    "legend.fontsize": SMALL_FONTSIZE,
    "figure.titlesize": PANEL_FONTSIZE,
    "axes.titleweight": "normal",   # Panel() sets bold on the letter itself
    # Furniture pads: less white between the axes and its labels means more of the canvas
    # is the plot, which is the same proportion argument as the type scale and costs
    # nothing in legibility.
    "axes.labelpad": 2.5,
    "xtick.major.pad": 2.0,
    "ytick.major.pad": 2.0,
    "xtick.major.size": 3.0,
    "ytick.major.size": 3.0,
    "xtick.minor.size": 1.8,
    "ytick.minor.size": 1.8,
    # Grid on every axes, behind the data, in the palette grey
    "axes.grid": True,
    "axes.axisbelow": True,
    "grid.color": PALETTE["grid"],
    "grid.linewidth": 0.5,
    "grid.alpha": 1.0,
    "grid.linestyle": "-",
    # Frame and lines
    "axes.linewidth": 0.8,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "lines.linewidth": 1.8,
    "lines.solid_capstyle": "round",
    "xtick.direction": "out",
    "ytick.direction": "out",
    # Legends: no box, tight

    "legend.borderaxespad": 0.4,
    "legend.handlelength": 1.6,
    "legend.handletextpad": 0.5,
    "legend.columnspacing": 1.0,
    "legend.labelspacing": 0.35,
    # Never the default C0-C3 cycle
    "axes.prop_cycle": mpl.cycler(color=HOUSE_CYCLE),
}


def apply_style(**overrides) -> dict:
    """Install the house style into ``matplotlib.rcParams``.

    Call once, near the top of a notebook, before any figure is built. Keyword
    overrides are applied last and are intended for one-off needs (a poster dpi, a
    presentation fontsize); the figures here should not need any.

    Returns the dict that was applied, so a notebook can print or assert on it.
    """
    settings = dict(STYLE)
    settings.update(overrides)
    mpl.rcParams.update(settings)
    return settings


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Panel letters and the house grid
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def house_grid(ax: Axes) -> Axes:
    """Put the house grid on ``ax``, behind the data. Idempotent."""
    ax.grid(True, color=PALETTE["grid"], linewidth=0.5, alpha=1.0, linestyle="-")
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    return ax


def panel(ax: Axes, letter: str, *, fontsize: float = PANEL_FONTSIZE) -> Axes:
    """Label ``ax`` with a bare panel letter, and guarantee it carries a grid.

    The convention already adopted in notebooks 03 and 04: the letter *only*, left
    aligned, bold, set as the axes title. Descriptive text belongs in the caption,
    never on the canvas, so this function accepts no description argument.

    One bracketing for the whole figure set: ``"(a)"``, ``"(a) "`` and ``"a."`` all normalise
    to a bare ``a``. A figure that wants brackets has to call ``ax.set_title`` itself, and is
    then outside the house style.
    """
    text = str(letter).strip()
    if len(text) > 2 and text.startswith("(") and text.endswith(")"):
        text = text[1:-1].strip()
    text = text.rstrip(").").strip() if text.endswith((")", ".")) else text
    ax.set_title(text, loc="left", fontweight="bold", fontsize=fontsize)
    return house_grid(ax)

    "baseline (zero)":                  "zero",
    "± s.e.m. across mice":             "± s.e.m.",
    "sessions 4 … n−2 omitted": "sessions omitted",
    "one stimulus-code draw":           "one draw",
    "single trained layer":             "shallow",
    "deep, no homeostasis":             "deep, no homeo.",
    "deep + homeostasis":               "deep + homeo.",
    "no trace + same homeostasis":      "no trace + homeo.",
    "no trace, no homeostasis":         "double ablation",
}

#: Prefix -> compact label, for labels built with an f-string so their exact text
#: carries a run-dependent number. Longest prefix wins. The number belongs in the
#: caption or the text, not in the legend.
SHORTEN_PREFIX = {
    "structural ceiling":                   "structural ceiling",
    "depth-identification rule":            "depth rule",
    "outside the frozen grid":              "outside frozen grid",
    "chance (":                             "chance",
    "chance $":                             "chance",
    "criterion (":                          "criterion",
    "declared criterion (":                 "criterion",
    "origin fit":                           "origin fit",
    "95% CI,":                              "95% CI",
    "95% session bootstrap":                "95% CI",
    "shaded: 95% bootstrap":                "95% CI (shaded)",
    "confound":                             "confound lead",
    "reward (n=":                           "reward",
    "stochastic omission":                  "omission",
    "cumulative fraction":                  "cumulative fraction",
    "frequency within 5% of best":          "within 5% of best",
    "measured, crit.":                      "measured",
    "swept, crit.":                         "swept",
    "overlap,":                             "overlap",
}

#: Panel back-references that must survive the generic tail trim.
_PANEL_TAIL = {f"({letter})" for letter in "abcdefgh"} | {
    "(a, b)", "(a, c)", "(b, c)", "(a, b, c)"
}


def shorten(label: str, *, max_chars: int = 30) -> str:
    """Compact one legend label.

    Order of attack: exact :data:`SHORTEN` entry, then longest :data:`SHORTEN_PREFIX`
    match, then a generic trim that drops a trailing parenthetical gloss when the
    label is still longer than ``max_chars`` (panel back-references such as ``(a, c)``
    are kept). Labels that are already short are returned unchanged, and anything
    starting with ``_`` is left alone so Matplotlib's hidden-artist convention still
    works.
    """
    if not isinstance(label, str) or label.startswith("_"):
        return label
    if label in SHORTEN:
        return SHORTEN[label]
    for prefix in sorted(SHORTEN_PREFIX, key=len, reverse=True):
        if label.startswith(prefix):
            return SHORTEN_PREFIX[prefix]
    flat = label.replace("\n", " ")
    if len(flat) > max_chars and flat.endswith(")") and "(" in flat:
        head, _, tail = flat.rpartition("(")
        tail = "(" + tail
        if tail not in _PANEL_TAIL:
            trimmed = head.strip().rstrip(",")
            if trimmed:
                return trimmed
    return label


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Geometry: does a legend sit on top of the data?
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _renderer(fig: Figure):
    fig.canvas.draw()
    return fig.canvas.get_renderer()


def _inflate(bbox: Bbox, pad_px: float) -> Bbox:
    return Bbox.from_extents(bbox.x0 - pad_px, bbox.y0 - pad_px,
                             bbox.x1 + pad_px, bbox.y1 + pad_px)


def _segment_hits_rect(x0, y0, x1, y1, rect: Bbox) -> bool:
    """Liang-Barsky: does the segment (x0,y0)-(x1,y1) touch ``rect``?"""
    if not (math.isfinite(x0) and math.isfinite(y0)
            and math.isfinite(x1) and math.isfinite(y1)):
        return False
    dx, dy = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
    t0, t1 = 0.0, 1.0
    for p, q in ((-dx, x0 - rect.x0), (dx, rect.x1 - x0),
                 (-dy, y0 - rect.y0), (dy, rect.y1 - y0)):
        if p == 0:
            if q < 0:
                return False
            continue
        r = q / p
        if p < 0:
            if r > t1:
                return False
            t0 = max(t0, r)
        else:
            if r < t0:
                return False
            t1 = min(t1, r)
    return t0 <= t1


def _artist_hits(artist, rect: Bbox, ax_bbox: Bbox, renderer) -> bool:
    """True if ``artist``'s ink intersects ``rect`` (both in display coordinates)."""
    if not artist.get_visible():
        return False
    if isinstance(artist, Line2D):
        # Exact: test the drawn polyline and its markers, not the bounding box, so a
        # sparse series does not veto every legend position inside the axes.
        try:
            path = artist.get_path().transformed(artist.get_transform())
        except Exception:                                     # Pragma: no cover
            return False
        pts = path.vertices
        if len(pts) == 0:
            return False
        if len(pts) == 1:
            return bool(rect.contains(pts[0][0], pts[0][1]))
        for (xa, ya), (xb, yb) in zip(pts[:-1], pts[1:]):
            if _segment_hits_rect(xa, ya, xb, yb, rect):
                return True
        return False
    # Collections (scatter, fill_between bands, error bars) and patches: use the
    # display bounding box, clipped to the visible axes region. Conservative, which
    # is the right direction for a "no overlap" assertion.
    try:
        bbox = artist.get_window_extent(renderer)
    except Exception:                                         # Pragma: no cover
        return False
    if bbox is None or bbox.width <= 0 and bbox.height <= 0:
        return False
    clipped = Bbox.intersection(bbox, ax_bbox)
    if clipped is None:
        return False
    return Bbox.intersection(clipped, rect) is not None


def _data_artists(ax: Axes) -> list:
    skip = {ax.patch, ax.xaxis, ax.yaxis, ax.title}
    artists = []
    for artist in (list(ax.lines) + list(ax.collections) + list(ax.patches)
                   + list(ax.images)):
        if artist in skip or isinstance(artist, Legend):
            continue
        artists.append(artist)
    return artists


def overlapping_artists(ax: Axes, legend: Legend, *, pad_pt: float = 2.0) -> list:
    """Artists on ``ax`` whose ink intersects ``legend``'s box (display coords)."""
    fig = ax.get_figure()
    renderer = _renderer(fig)
    pad_px = pad_pt * fig.dpi / 72.0
    rect = _inflate(legend.get_window_extent(renderer), pad_px)
    ax_bbox = ax.get_window_extent(renderer)
    return [a for a in _data_artists(ax) if _artist_hits(a, rect, ax_bbox, renderer)]


def legend_overlaps_data(ax: Axes, legend: Legend, *, pad_pt: float = 2.0) -> bool:
    """Geometric check: does ``legend`` sit on top of any plotted ink on ``ax``?

    Compares the legend's window extent (inflated by ``pad_pt`` points of clearance)
    against every data artist's extent in display coordinates. Lines are tested
    segment-exactly; collections and patches by their clipped bounding box. Grid,
    spines, ticks, the axes background and other legends are excluded.

    Intended for use as an assertion in the figure notebooks::

        Leg = compact_legend(ax, *ax.get_legend_handles_labels())
        assert not legend_overlaps_data(ax, leg)
    """
    return bool(overlapping_artists(ax, legend, pad_pt=pad_pt))


def _annotation_texts(ax: Axes) -> list:
    """Free texts and annotations drawn on ``ax``, excluding the panel letter.

    The panel letter is the axes *title*, so it is not in ``ax.texts`` and cannot be
    reported here. Axis labels and tick labels belong to the axis, likewise.
    """
    return [artist for artist in ax.texts
            if artist.get_visible() and str(artist.get_text()).strip()]


def annotation_collisions(ax: Axes, *, pad_pt: float = 1.0) -> list:
    """``[(text, [data artists it sits on]), ...]`` for every annotation on ``ax``.

    Why this exists as well as :func:`legend_overlaps_data`: that function interrogates
    one :class:`~matplotlib.legend.Legend`, and a floating value label or a
    confidence-interval block is a :class:`~matplotlib.text.Text`. A figure can
    therefore pass ``assert not legend_overlaps_data(...)`` with every annotation
    bisected by a reference line -- which is exactly what ``fig_shallow_dms_fair``
    panel (b) did: three interval blocks each crossed by the black zero line, while the
    legend assertion passed and was taken as evidence of a clean layout. It was not
    evidence of anything about the annotations.

    Same exclusions as the legend check: grid lines, spines, ticks and the axes patch
    are not data, so a text sitting on the grid is not a collision. A text laid over a
    plotted line, marker, band or bar is.

    An opaque background box is *not* treated as a resolution. It hides the ink beneath,
    which fixes the appearance while leaving the reference line broken where it is being
    followed, so the fix is displacement and the check says so.
    """
    fig = ax.get_figure()
    renderer = _renderer(fig)
    pad_px = pad_pt * fig.dpi / 72.0
    ax_bbox = ax.get_window_extent(renderer)
    found = []
    for text in _annotation_texts(ax):
        try:
            rect = _inflate(text.get_window_extent(renderer), pad_px)
        except Exception:                                     # Pragma: no cover
            continue
        hits = [a for a in _data_artists(ax) if _artist_hits(a, rect, ax_bbox, renderer)]
        if hits:
            found.append((text, hits))
    return found


def annotations_overlap_data(ax: Axes, *, pad_pt: float = 1.0) -> bool:
    """Geometric check: does any annotation on ``ax`` sit on top of plotted ink?

    Intended as an assertion beside the legend one::

        Assert not annotations_overlap_data(axB), "CI blocks sit on the zero line"
    """
    return bool(annotation_collisions(ax, pad_pt=pad_pt))


def _title_texts(ax: Axes) -> list:
    """The three title artists of an axes: centre, left and right.

    ``panel()`` writes the letter with ``loc="left"``, which Matplotlib keeps in a
    *different* artist from ``ax.title`` -- so a check that looked only at ``ax.title``
    would silently pass every panel-letter collision in this figure set.
    """
    return [artist for artist in
            (ax.title, getattr(ax, "_left_title", None), getattr(ax, "_right_title", None))
            if artist is not None]


def _furniture_texts(ax: Axes) -> list:
    """The axes' own type: panel letter / title, axis labels, tick labels.

    Not data, but not free canvas either: a legend must not land on the bold panel letter.
    """
    items = _title_texts(ax) + [ax.xaxis.label, ax.yaxis.label]
    items += list(ax.get_xticklabels()) + list(ax.get_yticklabels())
    return [t for t in items if t is not None and t.get_visible()
            and str(t.get_text()).strip()]


def legend_overlaps_furniture(ax: Axes, legend: Legend, *,
                              pad_pt: float = 1.0) -> list:
    """Axes type that ``legend``'s box covers: the panel letter, a label, a tick label.

    :func:`legend_overlaps_data` deliberately excludes the title and the axis labels,
    because they are not data -- which let ``fig_kernel_identifiability`` (c) place a
    legend squarely on its capitalised panel letter and still pass every assertion the
    notebook made. This closes that hole, and :func:`compact_legend` consults it when it
    searches for a position.
    """
    fig = ax.get_figure()
    renderer = _renderer(fig)
    pad_px = pad_pt * fig.dpi / 72.0
    try:
        rect = _inflate(legend.get_window_extent(renderer), pad_px)
    except Exception:                                         # Pragma: no cover
        return []
    hits = []
    for text in _furniture_texts(ax):
        try:
            box = text.get_window_extent(renderer)
        except Exception:                                     # Pragma: no cover
            continue
        if Bbox.intersection(box, rect) is not None:
            hits.append(text)
    return hits


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Compact, non-overlapping legends
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#: Inside positions tried, in order, before the legend is pushed outside the axes.
_INSIDE_LOCS = ("upper left", "upper right", "lower left", "lower right",
                "center left", "center right", "upper center", "lower center")

_OUTSIDE = {
    "above": dict(loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.02, 1.0, 0.12),
                  mode="expand", borderaxespad=0.0),
    "below": dict(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, -0.16, 1.0, 0.12),
                  mode="expand", borderaxespad=0.0),
    "right": dict(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0),
                  borderaxespad=0.0),
}


def compact_legend(ax_or_fig, handles: Sequence | None = None,
                   labels: Iterable[str] | None = None, *,
                   where: str = "auto", max_chars: int = 30,
                   shorten_labels: bool = True, pad_pt: float = 2.0,
                   **kw) -> Legend:
    """Place a short legend where it cannot cover the data, and return it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ax_or_fig
        An :class:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes` or a :class:`~matplotlib.figure.Figure`. A
        figure-level legend is always outside every data region, so ``where`` is only
        consulted for an axes.
    handles, labels
        As :meth:`matplotlib.axes.Axes.legend`. If omitted, they are taken from the
        axes (or from every axes of the figure, de-duplicated by label).
    where
        ``"auto"`` (default) tries the inside positions in :data:`_INSIDE_LOCS` and
        keeps the first that both :func:`legend_overlaps_data` and
        :func:`legend_overlaps_furniture` report clean, falling back to outside-above;
        ``"above"``, ``"below"``, ``"right"`` force an outside placement; ``"inside"``
        keeps Matplotlib's own ``loc`` handling. Passing an explicit ``loc`` or
        ``bbox_to_anchor`` in ``kw`` also bypasses the search.
    max_chars, shorten_labels
        Label compaction via :func:`shorten`.

    Notes
    -----
    Long legends are laid out in columns automatically (``ncol`` up to 3) so that a
    legend pushed above or below an axes stays one or two lines deep.

    A framed legend may not sit inside an axes. ``frameon=True`` (or a ``facecolor`` /
    ``edgecolor`` that draws a patch) together with an inside placement raises, because a
    box floating over the data hides it. Put the legend outside (``where="below"`` /
    ``"right"``) and keep it frameless, which is the house default.
    Hiding data under an opaque box is not a fix; it is the same overlap, undisclosed.
    """
    is_fig = isinstance(ax_or_fig, Figure)
    fig = ax_or_fig if is_fig else ax_or_fig.get_figure()

    if handles is None or labels is None:
        if is_fig:
            found: dict[str, object] = {}
            for axes in fig.axes:
                for handle, label in zip(*axes.get_legend_handles_labels()):
                    found.setdefault(label, handle)
            labels = list(found)
            handles = [found[label] for label in labels]
        else:
            handles, labels = ax_or_fig.get_legend_handles_labels()
    labels = list(labels)
    handles = list(handles)
    if shorten_labels:
        labels = [shorten(label, max_chars=max_chars) for label in labels]

    kw.setdefault("frameon", False)
    if "ncol" not in kw and "ncols" not in kw:
        kw["ncol"] = 1 if len(labels) <= 3 else min(3, math.ceil(len(labels) / 2))

    explicit = "loc" in kw or "bbox_to_anchor" in kw

    if is_fig:
        placement = dict(loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0))
        if explicit:
            placement = {}
        return fig.legend(handles, labels, **{**placement, **kw})

    ax = ax_or_fig
    framed = bool(kw.get("frameon")) or "facecolor" in kw or "edgecolor" in kw
    inside = where in ("auto", "inside") and where not in _OUTSIDE
    if framed and inside:
        raise ValueError(
            "a framed legend may not sit inside an axes: pass where='below' or "
            "where='right' to put the key outside the data, or drop frameon/facecolor "
            "and keep the frameless house legend")

    if explicit or where == "inside":
        return ax.legend(handles, labels, **kw)
    if where in _OUTSIDE:
        return ax.legend(handles, labels, **{**_OUTSIDE[where], **kw})
    if where != "auto":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown where={where!r}")

    for loc in _INSIDE_LOCS:
        legend = ax.legend(handles, labels, loc=loc, **kw)
        if (not legend_overlaps_data(ax, legend, pad_pt=pad_pt)
                and not legend_overlaps_furniture(ax, legend)):
            return legend
        legend.remove()
    # Nothing inside is clean: go outside, where overlap is impossible by construction.
    return ax.legend(handles, labels, **{**_OUTSIDE["above"], **kw})


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6b. No floating text inside an axes -- and nowhere for a caveat to be lost
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No free-floating sentence inside an axes: on-canvas prose competes with the data, gets no
# typographic hierarchy, cannot be copy-edited with the surrounding text, and is the
# first thing a journal's production step mangles.
#
# The rule has a half that matters more than the deletion. Most of those sentences are
# disclosures -- "criterion 0.75 markers ...", "n = 2 reads, |V| = 1 mV, preamp-free",
# "the dashed and dotted no-trace controls coincide". A caveat deleted from a figure and
# written nowhere is a loss of disclosure, which is the one thing this paper cannot
# Afford. :func:`caption_note` is therefore the sanctioned way to remove one: it returns
# the sentence verbatim and records it against the figure, so the notebook prints an
# explicit "move these into the caption" list at the end of a run and the caption can
# absorb them word for word.
CAPTION_NOTES: dict = {}


def caption_note(figure: str, sentence: str) -> str:
    """Record ``sentence`` as text removed from ``figure``'s canvas, and return it.

    Use it at the site of the deletion, so the record cannot drift from the figure::

        # Was ax.annotate("n = 2 reads, |V| = 1 mV, preamp-free", ...)
        caption_note("fig_fieldfree_trace.png", "n = 2 reads, |V| = 1 mV, preamp-free")

    The return value is the sentence unchanged, which lets a cell keep it in a variable
    it prints, asserts on, or writes into a provenance sidecar. Duplicates are ignored so
    a re-executed cell does not multiply the list.
    """
    text = str(sentence).strip()
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("refusing to record an empty caption note")
    notes = CAPTION_NOTES.setdefault(str(figure), [])
    if text not in notes:
        notes.append(text)
    return text


def caption_notes_report(figures: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Printable "these sentences must appear in the caption" list.

    Call it once at the end of a notebook (or per figure) and print the result, so the
    moved text leaves a trace in the executed record as well as in the caption.
    """
    names = list(CAPTION_NOTES) if figures is None else list(figures)
    lines = []
    for name in names:
        for note in CAPTION_NOTES.get(name, []):
            lines.append(f"  {name}: {note}")
    if not lines:
        return "no text was moved off a canvas in this run"
    return ("text removed from the canvas -- it must appear in the caption, "
            "unsoftened:\n" + "\n".join(lines))


def floating_texts(ax: Axes, *, allow: Iterable[str] = ()) -> list:
    """Free :class:`~matplotlib.text.Text` artists drawn inside ``ax``'s frame.

    Axis labels, tick labels and the panel letter belong to the axis or the title and are
    not reported. Anything else placed within the axes rectangle is a floating note, no
    matter which coordinate system positioned it, including a label whose only content is
    a number and one hidden behind an opaque ``bbox``.

    ``allow`` exempts exact strings, for the rare label that is genuinely part of the
    encoding (a curve's inline name where a legend would be worse). Use it sparingly and
    say why at the call site; an explanation, a caveat or a statistic is never in it.
    """
    exempt = {str(item).strip() for item in allow}
    fig = ax.get_figure()
    renderer = _renderer(fig)
    frame = ax.get_window_extent(renderer)
    found = []
    for text in _annotation_texts(ax):
        if str(text.get_text()).strip() in exempt:
            continue
        try:
            box = text.get_window_extent(renderer)
        except Exception:                                     # Pragma: no cover
            continue
        if Bbox.intersection(box, frame) is not None:
            found.append(text)
    return found


def require_no_floating_text(target, *, allow: Iterable[str] = ()) -> None:
    """Raise if any axes of ``target`` (an Axes or a Figure) carries floating text.

    Intended as an assertion beside the legend and annotation ones::

        require_no_floating_text(fig)   # R2: the caption carries the prose

    The message names the offending strings, so the fix is a copy-paste into
    :func:`caption_note` and then the caption.
    """
    axes = target.axes if isinstance(target, Figure) else [target]
    offenders = []
    for ax in axes:
        for text in floating_texts(ax, allow=allow):
            offenders.append(str(text.get_text()).replace("\n", " ").strip())
    if offenders:
        listed = "; ".join(f"{item!r}" for item in offenders)
        raise ValueError(
            f"{len(offenders)} floating text(s) inside the axes: {listed}. Move each one "
            f"into the caption via caption_note(figure, sentence), or place it outside "
            f"the axes with annotate_outside().")


#: Where :func:`annotate_outside` may put a note, in axes-fraction coordinates.
_OUTSIDE_NOTE = {
    "below": dict(xy=(0.0, -0.20), ha="left", va="top"),
    "below right": dict(xy=(1.0, -0.20), ha="right", va="top"),
    "above": dict(xy=(0.0, 1.04), ha="left", va="bottom"),
    "above right": dict(xy=(1.0, 1.04), ha="right", va="bottom"),
}


def annotate_outside(ax: Axes, text: str, *, where: str = "below",
                     fontsize: float = SMALL_FONTSIZE, color: str | None = None,
                     **kw):
    """Place a short note strictly outside ``ax``, and verify that it landed there.

    The one sanctioned on-canvas note, for the case a sentence must be adjacent to a
    specific panel rather than in a shared caption (a unit convention, a "shaded: 95%
    CI" gloss). It is checked, not trusted: if the drawn text intersects the axes frame
    the call raises, so a note cannot creep back over the data as a layout changes.

    Prefer :func:`caption_note` plus the caption. A note here still costs canvas height,
    which is the resource the proportion target needs (see :func:`axes_height_for`).
    """
    if where not in _OUTSIDE_NOTE:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown where={where!r}; use one of {sorted(_OUTSIDE_NOTE)}")
    spec = dict(_OUTSIDE_NOTE[where])
    xy = spec.pop("xy")
    artist = ax.annotate(str(text), xy, xycoords="axes fraction",
                         fontsize=fontsize,
                         color=PALETTE["ink"] if color is None else color,
                         **{**spec, **kw})
    fig = ax.get_figure()
    renderer = _renderer(fig)
    if Bbox.intersection(artist.get_window_extent(renderer),
                         ax.get_window_extent(renderer)) is not None:
        artist.remove()
        raise ValueError(
            f"annotate_outside({where!r}) landed inside the axes: give the note more "
            f"clearance, shorten it, or move it to the caption with caption_note()")
    return artist


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6c. Tick labels are an axis, not a legend
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#: Substrings that make a categorical tick label a smuggled legend entry or statistic.
_TICK_DATA_MARKERS = ("%", "=", "[", "±", "s.d.", "sd ", "n=", "n =")


def tick_label_defects(ax: Axes, *, allow: Iterable[str] = ()) -> list:
    """``[(axis, label, reason), ...]`` for tick labels that carry data or colour.

    Two defects, both of which make the axis do a legend's job and neither of which survives a
    greyscale print:

    ``carries data``
        a categorical tick label with a statistic inside it --
        ``fig_model_selection``'s ``linear Erlang k=3 (91.1% best)``. The name belongs on
        the axis and the number belongs in the panel, the caption or a second panel.
    ``coloured``
        a tick label tinted to match its series, as in ``fig_probselect`` (b). Colour on
        an axis reads as a category encoding that the axis does not have; the series
        colour belongs to the mark and to the legend.

    A numeric tick label is never reported for its digits: only the substrings in
    :data:`_TICK_DATA_MARKERS` count, and a label is "coloured" only when it differs from
    the rcParams tick colour. ``allow`` exempts exact strings, for a condition name that
    happens to contain a parameter value (``$\\beta = 1$`` identifies an arm; ``(91.1%
    best)`` reports a result -- the first is an axis, the second is not).
    """
    exempt = {str(item).strip() for item in allow}
    default = mpl.colors.to_rgba(mpl.rcParams.get("text.color", "black"))
    found = []
    for name, labels, tick_colour in (
            ("x", ax.get_xticklabels(),
             mpl.colors.to_rgba(mpl.rcParams.get("xtick.labelcolor", "inherit")
                                if mpl.rcParams.get("xtick.labelcolor", "inherit")
                                != "inherit" else mpl.rcParams.get("xtick.color", "black"))),
            ("y", ax.get_yticklabels(),
             mpl.colors.to_rgba(mpl.rcParams.get("ytick.labelcolor", "inherit")
                                if mpl.rcParams.get("ytick.labelcolor", "inherit")
                                != "inherit" else mpl.rcParams.get("ytick.color", "black")))):
        for label in labels:
            text = str(label.get_text()).strip()
            if not text or text in exempt:
                continue
            if any(marker in text for marker in _TICK_DATA_MARKERS):
                found.append((name, text, "carries data"))
            colour = mpl.colors.to_rgba(label.get_color())
            if colour not in (default, tick_colour):
                found.append((name, text, "coloured"))
    return found


def require_plain_tick_labels(ax: Axes, *, allow: Iterable[str] = ()) -> None:
    """Raise if ``ax`` has a tick label carrying a statistic or a series colour."""
    defects = tick_label_defects(ax, allow=allow)
    if defects:
        listed = "; ".join(f"{axis}: {text!r} ({why})" for axis, text, why in defects)
        raise ValueError(
            f"tick labels are doing a legend's job -- {listed}. Put the number in the "
            f"panel or the caption and give the series its colour on the mark.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6d. The proportion target: type against the axes height
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def axes_height_for(fontsize_pt: float = BASE_FONTSIZE,
                    em_fraction: float = EM_PER_AXES_HEIGHT) -> float:
    """Axes height, in inches, at which ``fontsize_pt`` reads like the ITO reference.

        axes_height_in = fontsize_pt / 72 / em_fraction

    At the house label size this is ``7.8 / 72 / 0.046 = 2.36 in`` of axes height per row
    of panels -- so a single-row full-width figure wants roughly a 3.3-3.5 in canvas once
    the x-label and an outside legend are paid for, where this set used 2.9 in and read as
    too text-heavy. Unlike :func:`size_for`, nothing here trades against the 7 pt printed
    floor: LaTeX scales a figure by its width, so height is free.
    """
    if fontsize_pt <= 0 or em_fraction <= 0:
        raise ValueError("fontsize_pt and em_fraction must be positive")
    return fontsize_pt / 72.0 / em_fraction


def proportion_report(fig: Figure, *, em_fraction: float = EM_PER_AXES_HEIGHT) -> str:
    """One line per axes: is its type small in proportion to its plot?

    Reports one em of the axes' own label type as a percentage of its drawn height, the
    target, and the height the axes would need to meet it. A guideline, not a gate: the
    remedy is a taller canvas, which the figure cell owns, and a hard failure here would
    only tempt someone to shrink the type through the 7 pt floor instead.
    """
    fig.canvas.draw()
    renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
    lines = []
    for index, ax in enumerate(fig.axes):
        height_in = ax.get_window_extent(renderer).height / fig.dpi
        if height_in <= 0:
            continue
        size = float(ax.xaxis.label.get_fontsize())
        fraction = (size / 72.0) / height_in
        want = axes_height_for(size, em_fraction)
        flag = "ok  " if fraction <= em_fraction else "TALL"
        titles = [str(t.get_text()).strip() for t in _title_texts(ax)]
        letter = next((t for t in titles if t), f"#{index}")[:4]
        lines.append(f"  {flag} panel {letter:<4s} {size:.1f} pt em = "
                     f"{100 * fraction:.1f}% of a {height_in:.2f} in axes "
                     f"(target {100 * em_fraction:.1f}%, wants {want:.2f} in)")
    return ("proportion (one em of label type against the axes height):\n"
            + "\n".join(lines) if lines else "no axes to report on")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. The legibility arithmetic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def effective_pt(fontsize_pt: float, placed_mm: float, figsize_width_in: float) -> float:
    """Printed size of ``fontsize_pt`` when the canvas is scaled to ``placed_mm``.

        effective_pt = fontsize_pt * (placed_mm / 25.4) / figsize_width_in
    """
    return fontsize_pt * (placed_mm / MM_PER_IN) / figsize_width_in


def smallest_pt(fig: Figure) -> float:
    """Smallest fontsize actually drawn in ``fig``, in points.

    Use this to state the legibility arithmetic honestly: the binding constraint is
    the smallest glyph on the canvas (usually a legend entry or a tick label, both
    :data:`SMALL_FONTSIZE` = 7.4 pt in the house style), not ``rcParams["font.size"]``.
    """
    sizes = []
    for text in fig.findobj(mpl.text.Text):
        if not text.get_visible():
            continue
        if not str(text.get_text()).strip():
            continue
        sizes.append(float(text.get_fontsize()))
    return min(sizes) if sizes else float(mpl.rcParams["font.size"])


def size_for(placed_mm: float, min_pt: float = MIN_PT,
             base_fontsize: float = BASE_FONTSIZE) -> float:
    """Widest canvas, in inches, that still prints ``base_fontsize`` at ``min_pt``.

    Derivation
    ----------
    LaTeX scales the saved canvas so that its width becomes the placed width, so every
    glyph is scaled by the same factor ``placed_width_in / figsize_width_in``:

        effective_pt = base_fontsize * placed_width_in / figsize_width_in

    Requiring ``effective_pt >= min_pt`` and solving for the canvas width gives

        figsize_width_in <= base_fontsize * placed_width_in / min_pt

    Which is what this function returns. For a full-width figure
    (``width=\\linewidth`` = 160 mm = 6.299 in) with the house body size 7.8 pt and a
    7 pt floor::

        size_for(160.0) = 7.8 * 6.299 / 7 = 7.02 in

    Pass ``base_fontsize`` = the *smallest* size on the canvas (see
    :func:`smallest_pt`): 7.4 pt for tick labels and legend entries, which tightens the
    same example to ``7.4 * 6.299 / 7 = 6.66 in``. For a fractional placement,
    multiply the line width first, e.g. ``size_for(0.92 * 160.0)``.

    An oversized canvas is how printed type collapses: at 7.8 pt on an 18 in canvas placed at
    6.3 in, ``7.8 * 6.299 / 18 = 2.73 pt``.

    This function bounds the canvas width only, and it is the *width* that trades against
    legibility. Height is governed by :func:`axes_height_for`, which does not compete with
    it: a figure may be as tall as the page allows at no cost in printed type.
    """
    if placed_mm <= 0:
        raise ValueError("placed_mm must be positive")
    if min_pt <= 0:
        raise ValueError("min_pt must be positive")
    return base_fontsize * (placed_mm / MM_PER_IN) / min_pt


def size_bounds(placed_mm: float, min_pt: float = MIN_PT, max_pt: float = MAX_PT,
                base_fontsize: float = BASE_FONTSIZE) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """``(narrowest, widest)`` canvas width in inches for the ``[min_pt, max_pt]`` band.

    The lower bound comes from the ceiling (type must not print *larger* than
    ``max_pt``), the upper bound from :func:`size_for`. For a full-width figure at
    7.8 pt: ``(4.47, 7.02)`` in.
    """
    widest = size_for(placed_mm, min_pt, base_fontsize)
    narrowest = base_fontsize * (placed_mm / MM_PER_IN) / max_pt
    return narrowest, widest


# ============================================================================
# Figure registry and I/O
# ============================================================================
# The figure registry, and the one call a notebook cell makes.
#
# Why this exists. A notebook cell must do three things -- render, display exactly
# once, and (when saving is on) write the same object to ``figures/`` -- and it must
# do them in one statement. Two statements would echo the second one's return value
# and, with the inline backend, emit the figure a second time:
#
#     Fig = static.iv_sweeps()      # 1 inline image
#     save_figure(fig, "fig1_iv-sweeps") # ... and a second one, from the echoed path
#
# Measured, not assumed: of the five plausible cell forms, only assignment without an
# echo yields exactly one image. :func:`render` collapses the three jobs into one such
# Assignment.
#
# Why A registry. ``figures/<name>.pdf`` has to match what the notebook displayed. If
# each cell spelled its own filename, the notebook would be the only record of that
# mapping and a typo would be undetectable. Here the mapping is data, and it is also the
# shipped inventory: :data:`FIGURES` names every figure the release contains, and the
# build compares the saved set against it and refuses any difference in either direction.
#
# Saving is off by default (``MNN_SAVE_FIGURES``). Rendering is cheap and safe;
# writing files is not something a reader running the archive profile out of
# curiosity should trigger.

import os
from pathlib import Path

from mnn_torch import archives as paths

__all__ = ["FIGURES", "FINDINGS", "figure_dir", "saving_enabled", "render", "canonical_name",
           "render_and_display", "finding", "INLINE_DPI", "SAVE_DPI"]

#: Publication resolution for the raster fallback. The canonical output is PDF --
#: vector, so dpi is irrelevant to it -- but a PNG is written alongside when a
#: caller asks for one, and 300 dpi is what the geometry assumed.
SAVE_DPI = 300

#: Resolution of the copy a notebook embeds, which is not the resolution of anything
#: written to disk: the canonical PDF is vector and the optional PNG carries
#: :data:`SAVE_DPI`. It is separate because the committed notebooks are part of the
#: release and are size-capped, and 26 figures rastered at the house style's 120 dpi
#: display setting put them over that cap. Point sizes scale with dpi, so the embedded
#: image is the same picture, in fewer bytes. The house style is vendored and must not
#: be edited to achieve this.
INLINE_DPI = 100

#: every figure the release ships: ``(module, function) -> canonical stem``.
#:
#: ``(module, producer) -> output stem``. A stem says what the figure is; nothing here records
#: where any of them was ever placed. This is also the inventory: the package ships exactly these.
FIGURES = {
    # ---- 01_static ------------------------------------------------------
    ("static", "snn_schematic"): "snn_schematic_vector",
    ("static", "msnn_architecture"): "msnn_architecture",
    ("static", "iv_sweeps"): "siox_state_sweeps",
    ("static", "iv_nonlinearity"): "siox_pf_nonlinearity",
    ("static", "training_curves"): "training_curves",
    # ---- 02_retention ---------------------------------------------------
    ("retention", "physics_to_kernel"): "volatile_synapse_origin",
    ("retention", "device_to_primitive"): "ito_kernel_derivation",
    ("retention", "device_to_primitive_compact"): "ito_kernel_derivation_compact",
    # ---- 03_spiking -----------------------------------------------------
    ("spiking", "pretrain_map_freeze"): "pretrain_map_freeze",
    ("spiking", "frozen_substitution"): "frozen_substitution_delay",
    ("spiking", "frozen_substitution_compact"): "frozen_substitution_delay_compact",
    ("spiking", "intervention"): "allvolatile_intervention",
}

#: the two ``_compact`` entries are layouts, not analyses. Each reads the same preparation as
#: the wide figure beside it and differs only in presentation, so a number cannot disagree
#: between the pair. They are registered separately because the inventory is by output name and
#: a layout that ships must be accountable like any other figure.


#: What each figure shows, in numbers the archive holds.
#:
#: One entry per figure that reports a measurement, keyed exactly as :data:`FIGURES`. Each is a
#: sentence with named fields and the quantity each field is computed from, so the sentence is
#: filled from the archives when the cell runs. A finding written as prose would be a second,
#: unchecked copy of a number.
#:
#: Schematics have no entry. They encode no measurement, so there is nothing for an archive to
#: vouch for, and a sentence under one would be interpretation of a drawing.
FINDINGS = {
    ("static", "iv_sweeps"):
        ("The device was measured at {n_measured:.0f} conductance states, of which "
         "{n_screened:.0f} passed screening; the sweeps below are those states.",
         {"n_measured": "device.n_states_measured", "n_screened": "device.n_states_screened"}),
    ("static", "iv_nonlinearity"):
        ("The conduction model is fitted over the {n_screened:.0f} screened states, so the "
         "nonlinearity drawn here is a property of the screened set and not of a single state.",
         {"n_screened": "device.n_states_screened"}),
    ("static", "training_curves"):
        ("At the last epoch the dense network reaches {fc_ideal:.2f}% with an ideal conductance "
         "and {fc_pf:.2f}% with the measured response; the convolutional network reaches "
         "{conv_ideal:.2f}% and {conv_pf:.2f}%. The nonideality costs {fc_gap:.2f} and "
         "{conv_gap:.2f} points respectively.",
         {"fc_ideal": "static.final_accuracy.fc.ideal",
          "fc_pf": "static.final_accuracy.fc.memristive_pf",
          "conv_ideal": "static.final_accuracy.conv.ideal",
          "conv_pf": "static.final_accuracy.conv.memristive_pf"}),
    ("retention", "physics_to_kernel"):
        ("The measured relaxation is fitted at a scale of {tau:.3f} s and an exponent of "
         "{beta:.4f}. The exponent is below unity, so the fraction of the remaining state lost "
         "per unit time falls as the state ages, which a single time constant cannot express.",
         {"tau": "kernel.tau", "beta": "kernel.beta"}),
    ("retention", "device_to_primitive"):
        ("The kernel decomposes into {n_modes:.0f} nonzero modes spanning {tau_min:.3f} to "
         "{tau_max:.2f} s, reconstructing the fitted shape at a fidelity of {fidelity:.6f}. Its "
         "analytic mean lifetime is {analytic:.3f} s and the implemented one {implemented:.3f} s.",
         {"n_modes": "kernel.n_modes_nonzero", "tau_min": "kernel.mode_tau_min",
          "tau_max": "kernel.mode_tau_max", "fidelity": "kernel.fidelity",
          "analytic": "kernel.analytic_mean", "implemented": "kernel.implemented_mean"}),
    ("spiking", "frozen_substitution"):
        ("Substituting an exponential of the same implemented mean lifetime changes usable "
         "delay by {msnn:.3f} s [{msnn_lo:.3f}, {msnn_hi:.3f}] in the dense network and "
         "{mcsnn:.3f} s [{mcsnn_lo:.3f}, {mcsnn_hi:.3f}] in the convolutional one, with "
         "{msnn_n:.0f} and {mcsnn_n:.0f} of five networks negative. Equal mean lifetime "
         "therefore does not give equal task memory.",
         {"msnn": "substitution.dmax_difference.msnn.membrane.mean",
          "msnn_lo": "substitution.dmax_difference.msnn.membrane.ci95_low",
          "msnn_hi": "substitution.dmax_difference.msnn.membrane.ci95_high",
          "msnn_n": "substitution.dmax_difference.msnn.membrane.n_negative",
          "mcsnn": "substitution.dmax_difference.mcsnn.membrane.mean",
          "mcsnn_lo": "substitution.dmax_difference.mcsnn.membrane.ci95_low",
